# gamelab

gamelab drives the real game with exact key timelines, records it, and measures what happened. It started as the way MapleHelper's combo timing was measured: which way she jumped and threw, and whether the game ignored a key. A regular attack locks out jumps and attacks for about 730 ms. Quick taps right after takeoff were missed about 6% of the time.

On top of that it hunts on its own: it finds her and the monsters on screen, places them on the map, plans routes and fights, and sweeps a map platform by platform.

## Layers

The code is organized like a self-driving car's stack. Each layer is a package, and a layer only imports the layers below it (`tests/test_architecture.py` checks this).

```
  behavior      what to do next: the hunter (the agent), fights, looting, tours
     |
     +-- attack       which monster, from where, and how                    [pure decisions]
     +-- control      decisions turned into keys: actions, one move, a route; the key player
     +-- motion       motion planning, A to B: physics, routes, chained key timelines   [pure]
     +-- localization where she, the monsters and the drops are on the map (mined map data)
     +-- perception   pixels to what's on screen (no map knowledge)

  ui            the live mini-map window (reads telemetry)
  sim           an offline game: the stack runs against it with no game and no keys
  analysis      measuring combos and her movement in recordings
  shared        paths, screen geometry, left and right (directions), telemetry, the game window, screen capture,
                gamelab's few pieces in C (native), Python's garbage collections timed (gcstats), who plays and her
                profile (character, classes: Characters)
```

| Package | Does | Main pieces | May import |
|---|---|---|---|
| `perception` | Pixels to what's on screen, in half-size screen px | `Eyes` (the only door to pixels): `look` gives an `Observation` (her name tag, HP/MP, the ground under her, her minimap dot and other players', ropes, her EXP number and the box it's read from); `monsters`, `items`, `bar`, `refind` and `heading` (which way she faces, off her picture: `Heading`) answer questions about a look's frame; `messages` (the pickup log's rows) and `chat_line` (the message bar's game line: `perception.messages`, The top of a rope) read the service's whole frame. `MobDetector`, `LootDetector`, `NameTag`, `LieDetectorSpotter`; `exp_number` (her EXP number read, glyph by glyph); `deaths` (a monster's death seen: the game data's die1 frames where a track's feet are, `DeathWatch`: Her kill's monster); `frames` (the game as the screen shows it, for the continuous feed, never brought to the front) | shared |
| `localization` | Where things are on the map, in map units | `mapdata` (the map from the game's own data), `pose` (her position from the minimap dot, refined by ropes or her platform's end; the `Camera`), `Scene` (a look placed on the map), `Monster`/`MonsterTrack`/`Tracker` (monsters seen, told apart from look to look, and where they can be next), `Players` (other players, by their minimap dots), `Senses` (every look goes through it; its sweep searches the screen a slice a look), `Memory` (the monsters she has seen anywhere, kept across looks: Her memory of the monsters), `gains` (what each EXP gain was: the kills its size names, by kind; her EXP a minute off the number); the continuous feed: `tracking` (monsters followed frame by frame: ids, deaths and who killed them, her kill bound at her gain to the monster her attack took: Her kill's monster), `worldstate` (the feed's step, a frame at a time, every monster with its track's id), `feed` (its child process, the stack's side of it, and `SyncFeed` for the simulator) | perception |
| `motion` | Getting from A to B | `body` (how the game moves her: the client's movement step by step, from its own Physics.img), `physics` (jumps, falls and walking, measured), `route` (every move between platforms; Dijkstra; the ways a trip may choose among: Route diversity), `flow` (several moves chained into one key timeline, hopping monsters) | localization |
| `attack` | Which monster, from where, how | `reach` (where a star hits, and what an attack from a jump can pick), `stance` (throw, jump-throw, jump back, step away, close in), `spots` (where to stand to shoot a platform), `danger` (how badly she can be touched at a place: the monsters seen and the spawn points, by game data) | perception (monster names), localization, motion |
| `control` | Keys out | `Actions` (her key plans: throws, walking, pick-up, potions), `Mover` (one move, closed loop), `Navigator` (a route: chains, glances, cut-offs, replans), `client` (plans to the key player), `player` (the key player itself), `alarm`, `lie_recorder` (the Lie Detector's cycle recorded), `rolling` (the game's last 5 minutes kept: The rolling recording), `recording` (that recording kept by the perception service, from its own frames) | perception, localization, motion |
| `behavior` | What to do next | `Hunter` (the agent: senses, actions, a looter, her vitals and health), `fight` (`clear`, `kill`, fighting on the way), `Looter` (sweeps, mop-ups, drops remembered), `Tour`, `probe` (the in-game probes of what a star hits, and their scorer), `PetCare` (her pet fed), `retreat` (on the Lie Detector, away to a safe place within 10 s; and at the safety stop), `safety` (her HP staying low ends the hunt: No resting; under her profile's hits of the map's largest touch, in HP: The safety stop in HP), `darts` (her presses taking no MP and killing nothing for long end it: Out of darts; the game's refusals don't count: The top of a rope) | all of the above |
| `ui` | The mini-map window | `MapView` (draws a state; pure), `State` (the latest record per topic), sources (live, replay, a planned route), `MapWindow` | localization, motion, attack |
| `sim` | An offline game, and the offline checks | `World` (her body, monsters, kills, drops), `FakeEyes`, `FakePlayer` (the Lie Detector too: `alarm_at`), 43 scenarios on Tree Dungeon, golden traces; the harness and its baselines; `replay` (her recordings through any commit's perception, scored against labels: Replaying the recordings) | everything but ui |
| `analysis` | Combo tests and her movement on recordings; how her routes are used | `track`, `scroll`, `analyze`, `calibration`, `recordings`, `physics_check` (her tracked movement against the physics models), `coverage` (each route move planned, taken and missed, and why the others lose: Route coverage), `respawn` (how soon a platform she empties has a monster again, how long drops lie, how full the platforms are, from the telemetry: Respawns and drop life) | perception, motion, control |

How a look becomes keys:

```
Eyes.look -> Observation -> Senses.look -> Scene ─┬─> attack.stance ─────────────> Actions ─┐
   (perception)            (localization)         └─> motion.route / flow -> Navigator / Mover ─┴─> client -> player -> the game
                                         after each look: the hunter's vitals (EXP gains, HP), her heading off the frame (Actions.see) and telemetry
```

The loops live in `behavior/fight.py` (a fight), `control/navigator.py` (a route) and `behavior/tour.py` (a sweep).

## How the keys get to the game

MapleStory runs as administrator, and Windows blocks key presses from normal programs into admin windows. So one small process, the **player** (`control/player.py`), runs elevated, and everything else runs normally and talks to it through files in `gamelab/lab/`. It reads plans (JSON) from `lab/inbox`, presses keys only while the game is in front, records the game window if asked, and writes results to `lab/outbox`. `control/client.py` hands it plans and waits for the results; `control/timeline.py` runs MapleHelper's own combo code on a virtual clock, so tests play exactly what the helper plays.

What keeps the player safe:
- **No code from plans:** it runs no code it receives; plans are data.
- **Any key, and clicks inside the game** (since 2026-10-23, at the user's request: the key bindings window, `\`, needs a click on Confirm to save a change): it presses any key `config.toml` can name (`player.ALL_KEYS`) and both mouse buttons (`lbutton`, `rbutton` events; `act`'s `click@X,Y` and `rclick@X,Y`), and moves the pointer only inside the game window. Until then it pressed only her bound keys, `\` and Esc, never Enter, and never clicked.
- **Game in front only:** it stops pressing keys if the game leaves the foreground.
- **Fixed at start:** it loads its code and key list once, when it starts, and loads as little of gamelab as it can (a test checks).
- **Stops itself:** it exits when `lab/STOP` appears or after 24 idle hours (3 until 2026-10-23: the user asked that it not be exited proactively, since starting it again needs their UAC click; not while it records a Lie Detector), and after a Lie Detector once you've cleared it (below).
- **Plans can be cut short:** when `lab/inbox/<plan id>.cancel` appears, it stops pressing and lets go of every key it holds. A plan it hasn't started yet can be withdrawn: it renames each plan as it takes it, so the client can tell. The navigator uses this when she's hit or off course mid-plan.
- **Plans can be queued:** a plan can say how long it lasts (`end_ms`), so the next one starts the moment it ends. Keys are still all released between plans.
- **Stops on the Lie Detector:** the player checks the game screen 4 times a second, idle or not. It recognizes the countdown window (yellow "LIE DETECTOR" title), the mouse mini-game's notice 10 s before it, the mouse mini-game ("The Lie Detector Mini-game: use the mouse to follow the fading figure"), the image quiz's warning 30 s before it, the image quiz ("Click all matching images"), and the Truth Booth that a failed test sends her to (the notice and the quiz since 2026-10-25: below). When one appears, it:
  1. stops all input within about 10 ms, mid-move included, and lets go of any keys and mouse buttons a plan held: from then on that's all that goes out, so none stays held;
  2. writes `lab/ALARM.json` first, then saves a screenshot (once, exiting mid-save left neither);
  3. pages whoever is at the PC with alert sounds and a Windows notification that doesn't take focus from the game, even when `ALARM.json` can't be written (the disk full: it had raised before the paging, and nobody was told);
  4. records the whole cycle: every frame it grabs until the Lie Detector has been off the screen for a minute (see The Lie Detector's recordings);
  5. stays up, locked: every plan is answered with the Lie Detector error, but for the two kinds below (her pet's food, her retreat's moves). Once you have run `python -m gamelab clear-alarm` and the Lie Detector has been off the screen for a minute (`lie_recorder.END_S`), it stops (its log says so, then "player stopped"), and plans are taken again only once you start it again (`player --elevate`, your UAC click), as when it shut down at the alarm. Until then it goes on watching: a new Lie Detector is paged and recorded as the first. Until 2026-10-24 it shut down at once, its watchdog with it, so nothing it saved showed the Lie Detector being answered. It doesn't take plans again by itself: then `clear-alarm`, an ordinary command any program can run, would be all that stood between the keys and a Lie Detector the spotter can't see (the figure tracking, below), and starting it again is the step only a person at the PC takes. So `clear-alarm` refuses while the recording is still going (exit code 3), and the alarm cleared anyway (its file deleted) is raised again, and paged, at the next sight of the Lie Detector. An `ALARM.json` that couldn't be written keeps it up and locked until it's stopped: nothing could then tell that a person cleared it.

  It never tries to answer the test, and never moves her by itself (it knows neither the map nor where she is). While it's up it sends step 1's letting go, and only two kinds of plan, each only as its kind says (`player.alarm_refusal`; since 2026-10-24, the user, after a Lie Detector failed over Chrome Remote Desktop's lag and the alarm then kept her pet from being fed: "just stop any in-progress hunt when this happens, don't block pet feeding", and "On a lie detector you should move to a safe place, within 10s"). A plan says its kind (`client.send(kind=...)`, `alarm.PLAN_KINDS`):
  - **`pet_food`**: one tap of her pet food key (`config.toml` `pet_food`, U) and nothing else, the whole plan over within 200 ms of its start (`player.TAP_MAX_MS`: its key down and up, its `end_ms`; a food planned later, or lasting longer, would hold the player meanwhile, her retreat's moves and its stop once the alarm is cleared waiting behind it): no other key, no mouse, no resize, no recording; 3 in any minute at most (`alarm.PET_FOOD_PER_MIN`; a food is due every 75 s or so at the most often). The pet food key with anything else is refused.
  - **`retreat`**: her moves alone (her arrows, jump, up and down: walking, jumping, climbing, dropping), every key it presses let go by its end, no mouse; for 12 s after the sighting (`alarm.RETREAT_WINDOW_S`; when it was seen is the alarm Event's, `player.Alarm.at`), a plan still running then cut there and its keys let go, and none taken after. Either kind starts within 200 ms (its `lead_ms`; a plan's lead was bounded only by the frames it records). Who sends it, and why it's 12 s: On the Lie Detector, below.

  Neither is ever brought to the front (whoever is at the PC is answering the test), each is logged ("Lie Detector alarm up: her pet's food ...", "... her retreat's plan ...", "... refused ..."), and any other plan is refused as before, by the client already (exit code 3). The two kinds get past the client's check of `ALARM.json` (the player decides), so the player holds them to these rules with the file up too when its own watchdog hasn't seen the Lie Detector (`watch --lie-detector` raised it), a retreat's 12 s counted from the file's `at` ("Lie Detector alarm up (its file's; this player hasn't seen it): ..."); until a review on 2026-10-24 such a plan played as any, the game brought to the front. A plan running when the Lie Detector is seen stops at once whatever its kind; one refused raises `client.LieDetectorAlarm` with why, also when the alarm file isn't written yet. The alarm, its recording, `clear-alarm` and the player's stop and start again are as they were. Until you run `clear-alarm`, every command that sends keys or brings the game to the front refuses to run (exit code 3), including starting the player again and `probe run` (`spot`, `minimap`, `sim`, `map --offline`, `probe list`, `probe score` and the recording tools still run). A player started again takes no plan before its watchdog's first look at the game, so a Lie Detector still on screen (the Truth Booth) is seen before any key, and it stops if its watchdog does (nothing would see one). A plan waiting on the game's window (a resize, the game brought to the front) stops there when the Lie Detector is seen meanwhile, before the game is brought forward: those waits weren't watched, the keys' own are. When Claude is driving gamelab, it also pushes the alert to your phone.

  On 2026-10-18 the mini-game form wasn't known yet. It went unanswered, and she was sent to the Truth Booth (entry count 1). It has been recognized since then.

  **The notice and the image quiz (since 2026-10-25).** The two mini-games of 23:51 and 00:55 that night were each announced 10 s ahead by a box at the bottom right ("The mini-game will start soon. Go to a safe place before the game begins."), and at 00:28 a new test came: a see-through box, "Question in 30 seconds / Answer within 10 seconds", counting down, then "Click all matching images" with three pictures and a Confirm button, 10 s to answer. The player alarmed only at the board, so the hunt attacked through both notices, and the quiz went by unseen, the hunt going on (the user answered all three). At 1920x1080 the board's template had caught the notice, just (0.80 against 0.8: the 2026-10-19 and 21 alarms were notices); at the game's own 1366x768 it scored 0.75. Each of the three now has its own half-size template (`perception.lie_detector.HALF_SIZE`: `mini-game notice`, `quiz warning`, `quiz`), cut from the rolling recorder's frames of that night. Replayed through the spotter, every saved frame of 2026-10-19 to 25 (12,548; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/report-1025`): the alarm comes at the first frame of each notice (23:51:19.0, 00:55:00.6) and of the quiz's warning (00:27:58.0), 10 s and 30 s before the test, and on no frame but a Lie Detector's. Each is told for what it is (`ALARM.json`'s `form`, the log's "LIE DETECTOR seen (quiz warning)", the page: "MapleStory image quiz in 30 s"), and everything else is as for any form: input stopped, her retreat, the recording, the part before it. Not known: whether the quiz's warning always gives 30 s and the quiz always 10 (the template is its second line, "Answer within 10 seconds"), whether other quizzes have another title, how the see-through box reads over a bright map (both were seen only on Tree Dungeon), and what an unanswered quiz does.

## On the Lie Detector: the hunt stops, she retreats, her pet is still fed (from 2026-10-24)

**The hunt stops at once.** From the sighting the player refuses the hunt's plans: the one running is cut (its keys let go within about 10 ms) and its result raises `client.LieDetectorAlarm`; a hunt that is only looking for a while (waiting for respawns, standing on a spot, standing by) stops at its next look, as every look of the hunter (`Hunter.look`), every pass of a navigator's trip and her pet care in a hunt (`Hunter.feed_pet_if_due`) check the alarm first. `hunt kill`, `hunt clear`, `nav`, `tour`, `tour --loop` and `probe run` then retreat (below), and stop with the Lie Detector's message and exit code 3, as before; `combo`, `lock`, `act`, `do` and the other commands that only press keys stop as before, with no retreat.

**Her retreat** (`behavior/retreat.py`, `retreat.on_alarm` around each of those commands' hunt): the hunt that was running moves her to a safe place within 10 s of the sighting (`alarm.RETREAT_S`), because it has the map, the danger model and the navigator; with no hunt running nothing moves her, and the player only raises the alarm and records. Live on 2026-10-24 and 25, seen at the board, she was on platform 25 at 3.4 s and 3.0 s; seen at the mini-game's notice or the quiz's warning (since 2026-10-25), her 10 s are over before the test begins. Her retreat counts from the alarm's `at` (`ALARM.json`, `time.time()` at the sighting; added for it):
- **Where to** (`retreat.choose`): of the safe places she gets to in time, by the route planner's time stretched for her looks and stops on the way (`trip_s`: 1.5 times it and 0.6 s), the nearest safe platform (`MapModel.safe`) or place the danger model rates safe enough (`attack.danger`: 1% of her HP at most, `SAFE_DANGER`, with every spawn point's monster at its point and with the look's monsters; on a map where no kind counts, as on the first, only a safe platform), if it's near (`NEAR_S`, 6 s by `trip_s`); else the quickest to get to of those and the ropes as safe (positioning's rope model, `attack.ropes`: from any platform she gets to, at its safest height; she regains no HP on a rope, so only when no safe platform is near); with none in time, the safest place she gets to, or where she is if that's it. On a safe place already, she stays, a rope as safe too (`retreat.safe_rope`: her dot still over three looks by a rope, its danger as a rope's in `choose`), where the hunt waits out monsters (rule 9); off a rope that isn't, at once. Until a review on 2026-10-24 she always got off a rope first, after the navigator's 2 s look until she stood still: in the simulator, off the rope at -8 (its danger 0) and across the map, 9.2 s after the sighting.
- **How**: her moves alone, as the navigator plans them avoiding monsters (`navigator.AVOID`, never a fight; the quickest way; a monster in the way of a move waited out where she can stand, or gone round, as on any trip: a hurry that did neither, tried first, took her through 18% more touches on the floor in the simulator for no more of her on a safe place at 10 s, review 2026-10-24), every plan of kind `retreat` (`Actions.moves_only`: her arrows, jump, up and down; no attack, pick-up or pet food, and no mouse: the mover's nudge of the pointer, for a tooltip over the minimap, sends nothing), each go given its trip's time and 1.5 s, and another from where she is if a touch knocked her back or a rope was missed (3 at most, `TRIES`) while the 10 s have time for one. No potion or pet food on the way: her pet's care stops with the hunt (the babysitter goes on: below).
- **What it says**: "LIE DETECTOR: retreat to platform 25 (a safe platform; 1.5 s by route, danger 0.000), 0.8 s after it was seen; her moves only, no mouse", then "LIE DETECTOR: retreat over (arrived): on platform 25 at x 260, 2.8 s after it was seen" (or how it stopped: "timeout", "not on the rope", the player's refusal past 12 s), and telemetry `event`s of kind `retreat`.
- **In the simulator** (`sim.fakes.FakePlayer.alarm_at`: the player sees it then, refusing as the real one does, `player.alarm_refusal` itself; scenarios `loop_tree_lie_detector`, `_28` and `_23`; `tests/test_retreat.py`): the hunt loop on Tree Dungeon, the Lie Detector seen at 40, 75, 110 or 150 s, seeds 1-12. Shooting 23 from 24, as live: on a safe place 10 s after the sighting in 47 of 48 runs (onto 25, 2.3 s after it at the median, 4.7 at p90). Hunting the whole map, mostly its floor (33) among its Green Mushrooms: 39 of 47 (83%), most onto the rope at 146 from 32 or onto 28 (no monster reaches it, though it isn't `MapModel.safe`), the rest knocked back on the way by the Greens on 32 and 30 (28 is the planner's 4.3 s from the floor, which took 5-12 s among them: past `NEAR_S`, so the rope comes first). In every run nothing but her moves went out after the sighting, and a retreat's plan past 12 s was refused (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/ldpet/sweep.py`, after the review's fixes of 2026-10-24).
- **With the feed and the attack choice, and grinding** (work/integrate-3 rebased onto it, 2026-10-25): `tour --loop --grind` runs inside `on_alarm` as `tour --loop` does, and grinding (`behavior.grind.Grind`, a `Hunt`) stops at the alarm as the hunt loop does. With the feed, the default, the hunt notices it at its next look or pass as before (her looks still go through `Hunter.look`, her trips' passes through `Navigator._pass`); her retreat's looks come from the feed as any trip's, and its reactions cut a retreat's chain for a monster coming into its way with `client.cancel` (no key plan: the player takes it with the alarm up) before the next chain of kind `retreat`. Her retreat's actions (`moves_only`) have no Lucky Seven key and throw nothing, so the attack choice has nothing to decide there. Scenarios `feed_loop_tree_lie_detector` (as `tour --loop` runs by default from 28, the Lie Detector seen at 110 s: the feed, the attack choice, Lucky Seven costing MP, group 0's walls stopping her) and `loop_tree_lie_detector_grind` (as `tour --loop --grind` does, from 23, at 75 s): of seeds 1-12, 11 and 12 are on a safe place 10 s after the sighting with the monsters' bars read empty as before 2026-10-25 (Perception: Monster HP bars), 12 and 12 with them read; the retreat began within 0.22 s of it on every seed of the first, and within 0.59 s on 11 of the second (on seed 11 she was resting on 25, a safe platform, and the rest's next look came 5.0 s on: she stayed). In the default world, with only her group's walls, a touch knocked her out of the map before the sighting on 2 and 3 of the seeds (a simulator effect, as `loop_tree_run`'s). `tests/test_retreat.py`'s sweep from the floor's crowd (seeds 1-8, seen at 40, 75, 110 and 150 s) now runs with the feed, as `tour --loop` does by default: 24 of 29 on a safe place at 10 s (27 of 32 at master's head without it). **Without the feed** (`--no-feed`, and the simulator's default) the hunt loop sweeps the screen a slice a look (`hunt.SWEEP`, Her memory of the monsters), and there it was 15 of 32 (37 of 62 over seeds 1-16), against 28 of 29 with `hunt.SWEEP` off: the retreat is the same (the sweep is off by then), but the hunt before it had her on the floor more often at the sighting (38 of 61 runs against 30 of 61) and hit just before it more often (14 against 8), and from the same places her retreat fared worse (the floor and 32: 20 of 38 against 23 of 30). Not fixed; the test said so (a strict xfail) until her jumps' attacks were weighed and her jump throws turned in the air (2026-10-25, Attacks from her jumps): since then 26 of 32 without the feed, 28 of 32 with it (none out of the map), 32 of 32 shooting 23 from 24, the hunt before the sighting gone otherwise; with the review's fixes (her body clear of a monster above over a jump in place, a jump forward's landing however it goes, the ground's reach capped 60 above her again), 24 of 31 without the feed, 28 of 29 with it (three runs out of the map before the sighting), 32 of 32 shooting 23 from 24; with the ground's reach above 60 on again by the user's choice (`reach.UP_BY_SEARCH`), 25 of 32 without the feed, 28 of 29 with it (three out), 30 of 32 shooting 23 from 24; the sweep's cost isn't measured apart again. The feed leaves the sweep out of the looks it serves, so live it applies only while the feed rests or is gone.
- **Not done**: the retreat isn't tried in game; it doesn't know her HP (a retreat at 10% HP goes as one at 90%); its numbers (`SLACK`, `NEAR_S`, `SAFE_DANGER`) are the simulator's; a hunt standing still on looks that fail their checks (`LookLost`: Capture checks) doesn't notice the alarm until they pass, by when the 10 s are usually over (then "too late": she stays). When the alarm is noticed from a look rather than a plan, up to a pass's time (about 0.4 s) has gone by.

**Her pet is still fed.** The pet babysitter (`pet --every 1`) goes on through the alarm: its food (`Actions.feed_pet`, kind `pet_food`) by the fullness it follows in time (`behavior/pet.py`), never a read of her Character Info until the alarm is cleared (the read double-clicks her, and you may be answering the test with the mouse); a pet never read yet gets a food once 2 h have passed since the last, as when the panel can't be read. A food the player refuses (more than 3 a minute) or doesn't answer (the player stopped) is said and tried again at the next follow, where it used to end the command. Once you've cleared the alarm, the player stops as before (a minute after the Lie Detector's last sight), and the babysitter's foods wait for it to be started again.

**To put it live** (the player loads its code once: the running one keeps the old rules until it's started again): with the Lie Detector answered and off the screen for a minute, `python -m gamelab clear-alarm`; the running player stops by itself a minute after the Lie Detector's last sight (its log ends "player stopped"; `python -m gamelab stop` if not); then `python -m gamelab player --elevate` (your UAC click). Its log's first line says "with it seen: a tap of 'u' for her pet, 3 a minute, and her retreat's moves for 12 s; nothing else". A `pet --every 1` already running keeps the code it started with (it would end at the next Lie Detector): start it again too (no UAC).

**To check in game**, at the next Lie Detector (explore only: no attacks; a hunt running only when attack tests are allowed again): `pet --every 1` running, its foods go on ("pet fullness: about N"; the player's log "Lie Detector alarm up: her pet's food"), and no Character Info opens; with a hunt running, it stops at once, she moves to a safe place within 10 s by its log and the minimap, and nothing presses after 12 s; nothing moves the mouse while you answer. At the mini-game's notice or the quiz's warning (a player started since 2026-10-25: its log's "LIE DETECTOR seen (mini-game notice)" or "(quiz warning)"), all that within a second of the box showing, and she's on her safe place before the board or the quiz; `ALARM.json` says the `form`, the page names it, and the recording's folder has `before/`.

## No resting: the safety stop (from 2026-10-26)

(Its rule, 65% of her HP for 2 s, went on 2026-10-28: The safety stop in HP, below. What it does at the stop is as here.)

The user, on 2026-10-26, after the review of parts A and B found a touch standing her up from the chair and her waiting out the rest's 120 s with her HP flat (24% of the hunt loop's rests in the harness: Found offline): "Just remove the sit recover hp functionality, it's no longer needed". Her pet drinks her potions (live on 2026-10-25, 6 HP potions in 11 minutes, about 250 HP each, under 70%).

**Her HP:** her HP number when it was read at its last change (`Scene.hp_of`, a glance's state's `hp_of`), else her bar's share less a px (`BAR_SLACK`, 1/104) times her max HP; her max HP not read, everything in shares of her bar. 10 s of looks with the number never read is said once ("her HP number not read in 10 s of looks ...: the safety stop goes by her HP bar, under 50% of her HP bar (her max HP not read yet)": the perception service not restarted on this code, or a client size it reads none at, such as the stretched 1920x1080), where nothing hunts (`nav`): a command that hunts hunts nothing without it (`HpNotRead`).

**The debounce:** under it on 2 readings (`LOOKS`) 0.25 s apart at least by her HP number (`DEBOUNCE_EXACT_S`: her pet's potion lands 0.04-0.20 s after a touch), 0.6 s by her bar or with a potion key of her own (`DEBOUNCE_S`: the bar's settling, 0.37 s; her own drink waits for a health check and her key: the first map's simulator, whose stack binds one, stopped at 0.3 s with her HP number drawn before her key's potion landed); a reading at or over it starts again; under one touch (`FLOOR_TOUCHES`) 2 readings in a row (`FLOOR_LOOKS`) stop it then. Its readings are her looks and her glances (`Hunter._vitals`, `Hunter._glanced`), and it's raised at the reading it's due at (`Hunter._stop_now`; `STOP_ON_LOOK`), once a hunt has asked after her health and not while she retreats; an HP read 0 after a higher one isn't believed until the next look reads it too (`Hunter._doubt_hp`), as before.

**`--low-hp`** overrides it: 1 or under a share of her max HP, over 1 HP. A potion key of her own (`--potion-hp`, none bound live) caps it five points under its threshold, as before. ## Her stat window read: her W.DEF at a hunt's start (from 2026-10-28)

The user, 2026-10-28 ~18:20, on a first run with no touches kept (her DEF not known, so the safety stop's reserve took DEF 0, the most a touch can take: 453 HP of 840 on Tree Dungeon at level 28, until 8 touches were kept and fitted): "You can open character stats panel to check the defense". So a hunt opens her stat window at its start, reads her W.DEF and what else it shows, and closes it: the reserve and the positioning model take its DEF from then on (her touches only check it), and the stat window's read is kept in her stats file.

**When** (`behavior/statcheck.py`, `StatCheck.due`): at a hunting command's start (`hunt`, `tour`, `probe run`: `gamelab.__main__._hunter`, `Hunter.read_stats`), after her chat box's collapse (the section before), after her max HP is read off her HUD (and if it isn't in 5 s, the window's max HP is taken before `HpNotRead` would be raised, where something bears it out: below), when her DEF isn't known from the window this session (`bootstrap.HerStats.window_due`):
- no stat window read yet;
- read at another level than hers now ("her W.DEF 111 read at level 28; she's level 29 now");
- read in another session (the perception service's run, its pid, as the read kept it) or over 3 h ago (`SESSION_S`: she's played by hand between the bot's runs, and her gear changed between 10-26 and 10-28);
- her newest 8 touches since the read not fitting it (fewer than 80%: "her gear changed?");
- over the DEF her last 40 touches fit, with fewer than 8 since the read to bear it out (below).

Each of these but a level-up in the run also means the kept W.DEF isn't her DEF now (`HerStats.window_doubt`, below): it's a check until it's read again.

And only:
- with the reader calibrated on this client (`lab/stat_window.json`, written by the live capture below). Without it nothing is sent, and the log says once: "her stat window not read: its reader not calibrated on this client yet: run `python -m gamelab stats --read --record` once, the game up and her somewhere quiet";
- with her stats key known and safe (`stats_key`). The key is ABILITY's in her remembered key bindings (control.keymap's `lab/keybindings-<her id>.json`, its `functions`, once work/attack-key-2 is merged). Otherwise it's S, ABILITY's in her key bindings of 2026-10-28. It's refused, and said, where it's one of her own keys, Esc, the backslash or maplehelper's hotkeys, or where her remembered bindings have ABILITY on no key;
- twice a run at the most (`READS_MAX`): the start's, and one after a level-up in the hunt loop (`StatCheck.level_up`: "her level 26 now, her W.DEF read at level 25: her stat window again at a quiet moment in the hunt").

**How** (`StatCheck.run`; each step is said in the log, and a telemetry event 'stat_window' is sent at the end):
1. *A quiet moment*: `keycheck.unquiet` (on a platform, not on a rope nor at its top, untouched for 0.45 s, no monster within 250), and her still over two looks 0.3 s apart, within 3 s. A monster within 250 puts it off at once: nothing moves her for it, and standing there it would come to her. Every look asks the safety stop, as the key check's do.
2. *A frame first*. A client not at 1366x768 gets nothing sent (the window is read at that size). A window open already is read as it is, then closed.
3. *The mouse and the key*. The mouse moves off where the window opens: (1100, 300), or the first of (1300, 420), (120, 420), (683, 60) clear of the calibrated panels by 16 px. A pointer over a value draws its tooltip (Detail's toolTipDelay 500 ms). Her stats key is tapped, then frames are taken 0.6, 1.0 and 2.0 s after it until a panel is found. Not found: the frame is compared with the one from before the key where the calibration has the Main panel. If 85% of its px haven't changed by 48 levels, it didn't open, and nothing more is sent. Otherwise it may be open.
4. *DETAIL*. Her W.DEF is on the DETAIL panel. If no panel found holds W.DEF's cell, its button gets one click at its centre (Main/button:detail, (122, 256) of the Main panel, 47 x 18; or where a live calibration read "DETAIL"). This is the only click sent. Then the mouse goes off again, and frames are taken 0.4 and 1.0 s later until the panel shows. If it doesn't, the Main panel's values are read without W.DEF ("partly").
5. *The read*: both panels, one frame (`perception.stat_window.read`). A second frame is read only if W.DEF's cell read no number. The frame is kept (`lab/shots/statwindow_<time>.png`).
6. *Closed*. Her stats key again (it toggles the window), then frames 0.6 and 1.0 s later. If both still show it, Esc, and once more the same way. Esc is never sent with no panel seen: with nothing open, Esc opens the game's MENU.

It **may be open** when it isn't seen closed after her stats key and two Escs, or there's no frame to tell by. Then `StatWindowStop` is raised (a HuntStop: in a hunt her retreat, said in capitals and paged "close it with S or Esc"; exit code 7; at a start nothing is hunted, said and paged the same). With the Lie Detector alarm up the player refuses its keys, as every plan's (`client.LieDetectorAlarm`); a window that may be open then is said and paged ("STAT WINDOW: her stat window may still be open in the game: close it with S or Esc"). Only her stats key, mouse moves, one click and Esc go out: nothing that attacks or moves her.

**Put off** (not quiet): in the hunt loop (`tour --loop`, `--grind`) it's raised again (`StatsDue`, from `Hunter.health_check`) at the first quiet look 5 s or more later, 6 times at the most (`DEFERS_MAX`). Elsewhere (`hunt kill`, a plain `tour`, `probe run`) it isn't read this run.

**What the read gives** (`Hunter._stats_read`), each checked before it's taken (below):
- *Her W.DEF*: hers (`HerStats.see_window`), kept in `lab/her_stats.json` with her level, the session, when, and the rest of the read (`WINDOW_KEEPS`). Her touches check it; her measured touches raise her reserve past it where the game hits harder, as before.
- *Her max HP*: only if her HUD's number hasn't read, and only where her HUD's as her stats file last kept it is the same, or her HP bar bears it out (under full, its share within 5 points of the window's cur / max).
- *Her level*: only where nothing has read it.
- *Her max MP*: her casts are reckoned at it (`Hunter.max_mp`, `Attacks.max_mp`), where her MP bar bears it out or it's within x1.25 of what they were reckoned at. config.toml's `[character] mp` (623) was used until then; live at level 28 it's 679. Said.
- *SPEED and JUMP*: said where they differ from config.toml's, which plan her moves (physics is loaded once, so they aren't taken).
- *ATTACK, ACCURACY, EVASION, MAGIC, MAGIC DEF., STR/DEX/INT/LUK*: kept and shown by `gamelab stats`. Nothing is modelled from them yet. Her MISS chance would need the monsters' EVA and the game's hit formula; the reserve takes every touch as landing, whatever her AVOID.

**Checked before it's taken** (after the review of 2026-10-28, which found a misread taken as read and a stale read kept governing):
- *Her HUD*: the window's level and max HP are her HUD's in game. Where both are read and either differs, none of the read is taken: "her stat window's read not taken: it says level 26, her HUD's LV. digits 25 (a misread?); her DEF as it was, ...". The capture tool (below) doesn't calibrate on such a read either.
- *Its range*: a W.DEF outside 0-400 (`DEF_TOP`, the fit's own range) is no read: not kept, her DEF as it was, said. An OCR's "711" for 111 had put the reserve at 117 HP of 840 with no touches kept, and "1111" at 21.
- *Her touches* (`HerStats.window_doubt`): her newest 8 touches since the read fitting it under 80% take it back (their fit, else the prior, said). With fewer than 8 since, a W.DEF over what her last 40 touches fit (and under 80% of them fitting it) isn't her DEF either: her touches' fit is, until 8 since the read bear it out. A 171 read for 111 with her 40 level-28 touches kept: her DEF stays 106.5-115.25, the reserve 387. A W.DEF under what her touches fit is taken: the lower is the safe side (a touch takes more of her), and gear taken off shows as that.
- *A read kept from before this run* is her DEF only if it was read in this run's session of the perception service (`HerStats(session=...)`, the feed's pid), at her first level this run, and under 3 h before it started. Else it's a check, and her DEF is her touches' fit or the prior, said in the start line ("DEF 59.75-64.75 (fitted to 40 of her last 40 touches; her stat window's not taken: her W.DEF 111 read 48.0 h ago (over 3 h))"). So a run whose read doesn't happen (put off at a plain `hunt`'s start, six put-offs, no calibration, S opening nothing) runs on the evidence, not the old read. A read made in the run stays hers over a level-up in it (the same gear), and is read again.
- *Its max HP and MP*: above. With no touches kept and nothing read off her HUD to check by, a W.DEF in range is taken as read (the user's first run: 453 -> 366 at W.DEF 111).

In the log, at a quiet start in the simulator: "her stat window: main at (560, 150)", "her stat window: DETAIL open (a click on its button)", "her stat window: closed (S)", "her stat window: W.DEF 75, level 25, HP 774/774, MP 623/623, ATTACK 60~75, ACC 85, AVOID 27, ... (2.6 s; sent mouse, s, click DETAIL, s)", then "the safety stop now under 393 HP of 774 (51%: 3 Horny Mushroom touches of 131) (was 453 HP of 774 (59%: 3 Horny Mushroom touches of 151)): her DEF 75 (her stat window's W.DEF, read ...)". Live at level 28, if it reads W.DEF 111 (her touches fit 106.5-115.25 there), a Horny Mushroom's top is 122: with no touches kept, 3 x 122 = 366 of 840 from the start, not 453; with her measured 122 (5% over: 129), 387 as before.

**The reader** (`perception/stat_window.py`). The client's windows are the newer UI the copy's `UI/UI_000.wz` holds (its KEY BINDINGS window matched the live one to the pixel), and its stat window is `CharacterStat.img`:
- *The panels*: CHARACTER STAT (Main/backgrnd, 185 x 281) and the DETAIL panel (Detail/backgrnd, 187 x 223; backgrnd2 is the same but for its left 4 columns, which are left out of the match).
- *The cells*: each value in a light cell (225, 223, 213) around its vector. `CELLS` is measured off the pictures (`cells_of`); HP, MP and the four stats are cut short of their AP buttons.
- *Found* (`find`): the picture with its value cells, the AP box and buttons masked out (what's drawn there changes). It's tried within 4 px of where it was last seen first, else at half size over the whole frame, then to the px. The fit is in levels² a channel, 400 at the most: 0 pasted with any values, about 50 as a JPEG, 12,000-18,600 at the best place on a frame without it. About 0.1 s for both panels on a frame without them.
- *Read*: each panel's value column goes to the OCR in one call (maplehelper.ocr's shared RapidOCR, enlarged x2), each row taken for the cell its centre falls in. The value is parsed: "840 / 840" is (cur, max), "60 ~ 75" is (lo, hi), "119%" and "25 (20+5)" give their first number.
- *Numbers*: on frames drawn from the copy's pictures (`compose`) the real OCR reads every value (`--slow`: W.DEF 111, level 28, HP 840/840, MP 138/679, ATTACK 60~75), 1.9 s with its models' load. The window's own text in the game's font (NotoSansKRMedium, in Font_000.wz as raw data) isn't seen yet.

**The calibration: a single live capture.** `python -m gamelab stats --read --record --map 10002073` (`_stats_recorded`) sends her stats key, mouse moves, one click on DETAIL if its panel doesn't open with the window (`--no-click`: none), and her stats key or Esc to close it. Each plan is recorded at 15 frames a second into `lab/shots/statwindow-<time>/`, with a report. Step by step:
1. A frame before. The client not at 1366x768, or the window open already: nothing sent.
2. Her stats key, recorded 1.5 s (one more frame a second later if none showed it). Each frame is looked at for the game data's pictures, and a calibration's own if there's one.
3. *Not found by them*: the last frame against the one before (`changed_boxes`: rectangles of 100 x 100 px or more, 40% of them changed) tells a window that opened from nothing. Nothing: "nothing opened after S ...: S may not be ABILITY in her key bindings (`gamelab keys --read`); nothing more sent". A window: it's cut from the frame as a template (`calibrate`). Its value cells are found by their labels with the OCR (`layout`: LEVEL, HP, WEAPON DEF., ACCURACY, EVASION and the rest, the value from the label's right end to the next label on its row or the window's edge, "DETAIL" the button's place), masked out of it, and saved under `lab/stat_window/`.
4. The DETAIL panel not open with it: one click on DETAIL, recorded 1.2 s. A live calibration without that panel cuts it from what opened since the click.
5. The last frame is read with the OCR.
6. Closed: her stats key, recorded 1.2 s; Esc only if the two frames at its end still show it, and so once more. A window not found by any pictures counts as closed once the frame is back to the one from before.
7. Seen and closed, and its level and max HP her HUD's (else "not calibrated: its read says ..."): the calibration is saved (`lab/stat_window.json`: "copy", the game data's pictures matched, or "live"; where each panel opened; whether DETAIL opened with the window; the key; the frames' folder), and her W.DEF is kept in her stats file (checked as a hunt's read is).
- Anything raised after her stats key went out (a crash, the Lie Detector) says "HER STAT WINDOW MAY BE OPEN IN THE GAME: close it with S or Esc", writes the report with the error, and raises on. As first built, the frames' truth (`res.get("frames") or []` on the numpy array the player hands back, as `keys --record` before 4c4bfa0) crashed it right after S, the window left open and nothing said.
8. Not calibrated: it says to run `python -m gamelab stats --calibrate <open.png> --before <before.png>` (`--box x0,y0,x1,y1` for each panel where the frames' difference doesn't find them), which sets the reader up from the saved frame offline (`_stats_calibrate`).

`gamelab stats --read` runs the hunt's own flow (the quiet moment; `--anywhere` waits for none) whatever her stats file says. `gamelab stats` alone prints the calibration and the window's other values as kept.

**The simulator** (`sim/world.py`, `sim/fakes.py`):
- *The window*: her stats key S toggles her stat window (`Realism.stat_key`; None: ABILITY on no key, nothing opens), drawn from the game data's pictures with her stats (`FakeEyes._capture`: `stat_window.compose` at `DRAW_AT`, its values `FakeEyes.stat_values`: her HUD's level and HP, the character's MP and DEF, the rest the thief's as near as known).
- *DETAIL and closing*: the DETAIL panel opens by a left click on its button (`FakePlayer` passes a click with where the plan's last mouse move put the pointer: `World.click`), or with the window (`Realism.stat_detail`). Esc closes it as it closes the KEY BINDINGS window; `Realism.stat_stuck`: nothing closes it.
- *Reading*: found by the real `find`, its text read by a stand-in for the OCR that says what was drawn where (`FakeEyes.stat_ocr`: only for crops of frames it drew).
- *No calibration by default*: the simulator's lab has none, so no other scenario opens it; the 34 Tree goldens are as they were.
- *Its own scenarios*: `loop_tree_stat_window` (a quiet start: S, DETAIL, S, closed 2.6 s in, her DEF 75 from the window, the reserve 453 -> 393) and `loop_tree_stat_window_put_off` (a Green and a Horny Mushroom within 250 at the start: put off at once, raised again by the hunt loop at its first quiet look at 6.7 s, read and closed by 9.2 s, the same keys). Their goldens are recorded.

**Tests:**
- `tests/test_stat_window.py`: the pictures and cells against the game data; found where pasted whatever the values, as a JPEG, near the last place and anywhere, nowhere on a frame without it; both panels read in one OCR call each; parsing; read_wdef; the calibration kept and read back; calibrated off the game data, and off a "newer" window (recoloured, labels read by a stand-in OCR, found again moved 40 px); a label and its value on one row; the real OCR with `--slow`, on a drawn window and on a recoloured one by its labels.
- `tests/test_statcheck.py` in the simulator: the flow S, DETAIL, S and the reserve 453 -> 393; DETAIL open with it (no click); a key that opens nothing (no Esc); a window that won't close (S, Esc, Esc, `StatWindowStop`); not calibrated (nothing sent, said once); put off near a monster at once; another client size; the Lie Detector halfway, and during her stats key's own plan (said and paged); the safety stop at its looks; what the read gives (max HP, max MP, SPEED); a read her HUD disagrees with (none of it taken); its max HP and MP only where borne out (8840 / 8840 and 6790 / 6790 at full aren't); the level-up re-read in the hunt loop; a window that won't close in the hunt loop (her retreat, paged once).
- `tests/test_statcheck.py` offline: her stats key from her remembered bindings, else S, and the refusals; `window_due`; `_hunter`'s order (her max HP, then the window; the window's max HP before `HpNotRead`); the capture tool on a stand-in game answering as `client.wait` does (one numpy array of frames): calibrated off the game data, DETAIL with it, `--no-click`, stuck once and for good, nothing opening, another size, open already, a newer window calibrated off its labels, stopped halfway (may be open, the error raised on), a read her HUD disagrees with (not calibrated).
- `tests/test_bootstrap.py`: a misread W.DEF ("711" and "1111" refused; 171 over her touches' fit not her DEF; 111 with no touches taken); touches since the read taking it back; a stale read kept (48 h, another session, another level) a check, and a read in the run kept over its level-up. `tests/test_keycheck.py`: the Lie Detector during the backslash's own plan, said and paged.

**To check in game** (supervised; the perception service and the player as for any command; her standing on a platform with no monster within 250, e.g. Tree Dungeon's 23):
1. `python -m gamelab stats --read --record --map 10002073`. It should print "seen open by the game data's pictures: main at (x, y) (fit ...)" (the fit near 0), click DETAIL if needed, then "her stat window: W.DEF ..., level 28, HP 840/840, MP .../679, ...", "read and closed (S)" and "calibrated: ...". Look at `lab/shots/statwindow-<time>/open.png` and `detail.png` against the game, and at `report.json` (each frame's fits; when it opened and closed).
   - If it says "a window opened ... that the game data's pictures don't match: calibrating from its labels": check that the cut panels' cells (in `lab/stat_window.json`) are on the values.
   - If it says "not calibrated: run `python -m gamelab stats --calibrate ...`": send the frames (`open.png`, `before.png`), so the boxes can be given.
2. `python -m gamelab stats`: her DEF 111 or so "(her stat window's W.DEF, read ...)", and the window's other values.
3. `python -m gamelab tour --loop --grind --map 10002073`: the start line's DEF "(her stat window's W.DEF, read ...)", and right after it "her stat window not read: her DEF ... this session's" (read by step 1 in the same session of the perception service, under 3 h before). In another session the start line says the kept read isn't taken ("her stat window's not taken: ... read in another session"), then S, DETAIL, S and "the safety stop now under ... : her DEF ... (her stat window's W.DEF ...)". It should be closed in the game, with nothing pressed in it. If it says "her stat window's read not taken: it says ...", send `lab/shots/statwindow_<time>.png`.

**Not done:** the bottom bar's stat button as another way in (ABILITY on no key: not opened, said); her MISS chance from ACC and her dodge from AVOID; SPEED and JUMP taken for her moves (said only); the window's own picture and font, never seen live: the capture above is the first look.

## Out of darts: the hunt stops (from 2026-10-26)

The user, at 01:28 on 2026-10-26, during the grind of 01:04: "stop, you run out of darts"; the bot kept pressing for nothing. Her last cast that took MP was keyed at 01:28:16.80 (her bar 37 -> 35 px of 104, shown at 17.11); every press after it took none, 23 of them over 20 s on platform 24 at a Horny Mushroom 100-150 off whose bar read 0.26 throughout, until she went for her drops at 01:28:38 and the user stopped the hunt (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/grind-0104.log`, `lab/telemetry/20261026-010352-tour.jsonl`, the perception service's `20261025-210747-perceive.jsonl`). No frame of it was kept (the rolling recording is saved only when asked), so what the game shows then, if anything, isn't known. Her dart count is never on screen while she hunts: it's in her inventory's Use tab (a window a hunt never opens; a quick slot holding the stars would show a number, and none does), so there's no warning before they run out: not built.

**What else takes no MP.** Her Lucky Seven presses take no MP with her darts too: 10-15% of them live (Found offline: Lucky Seven presses that took no MP), mostly one or two in a row, and 5-9 in a row (counted as below) 14 times in the 79 minutes of the five live hunts of 2026-10-25 23:43 to 2026-10-26 01:28, never more (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/norest/darts/count.py`). Two of those runs are on the frames the Lie Detector recordings kept (`lab/lie_detector/20261026-002509/before`, 00:23:19-28, and `20261026-010145/before`, 00:58:19-26): a Green Mushroom (and a Snail) standing on her at platform 24's right end, which the looks didn't find, and every press a swipe of her claw at it, 18-24 damage or MISS over it, her MP 172-175/623 on the HUD unchanged for 10 s, the green dead after 9 presses on it. Up close the Lucky Seven key swipes, as the attack key does, and takes no MP. Of the 14, 9 ended in such a kill (7 greens, 233 HP: 8-9 presses; 2 Horny Mushrooms, wounded before), the others in her casts taking MP again (the monster gone, or she stepped away) or her MP read under her pet's warning. A Horny Mushroom standing on her whole would take longer: 403 HP, defence 10.

**The stop** (`behavior/darts.py`: `DartWatch`, `OutOfDarts`): a stretch is her Lucky Seven presses (their keys: `Attacks.on_throw`) since her bar last showed a cast's MP (2 px under its highest read since: a cast is 14 MP, 2.3 px), a drink of her pet's (4 px over it), a read under 5 px (her pet's warning: it can't tell) or a kill of hers (her EXP told of it; a party share names none and doesn't count); of its presses, those her bar has had 0.55 s to show count, and not those keyed in a gap of 2 s in the reads (looks failing: the game perhaps not in front, her keys not reaching it; a trip between fights, with no press, doesn't end the stretch). Every look's MP bar feeds it, whoever took the look (`Attacks.on_look`, and the glance before a key). A stretch of `presses_for` the map stops the hunt, raised where her health is asked after at every look (`Hunter.health_check`, after the safety stop), once: 20 on Tree Dungeon (`PRESSES`), twice and more the 9 the hunts with her darts had at the most (11 with the perception service's 10 reads a second merged in, as the review counted). On a map whose toughest monster takes more of her swipes standing on her than a Horny Mushroom does (`swipes`: 21 damage a press, misses in, as the greens took them live, less its defence, x 100 / (PDDamage + 100); a Horny Mushroom 21.1), as many times more (West Rocky Mountain II's Axe Stump, 23.0: 22). ## The regular attack's key checked: doubted after 5 presses without effect, her stars, the game's key bindings read (from 2026-10-28)

The user had moved the regular attack off Ctrl in their own play and hadn't put it back before handing over (live, 2026-10-28 00:30, Tree Dungeon: `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/grind-1028-0030.log`, `lab/telemetry/20261028-003049-tour.jsonl`), so the bot's regular attack presses did nothing: at 00:31:14-00:31:33 she pressed it about 20 times at one Horny Mushroom at 28/403 HP ("the regular attack: horny-mushroom ~28/403 HP; finishing it"), its bar 9% throughout; from 00:33:00 regular attacks killed again (the key put back by then). Nothing noticed. The user's chosen fix: "I'd rather use another way to fix this, 1. Throw 5 times before doubting the key error 2. Check if star has run out 3. Open keyboard config (\\) to check the key configuration and see if attack button is different, and fix things."

**The doubt** (`behavior/keycheck.py`: `RegularWatch`, fed by `Attacks` at every throw and every look, whoever takes it). A regular press is judged at the first look 0.6 s or more after its key (`attacks.LANDS_S`), 2.0 s at the latest (`JUDGE_BY_S`: live the first sign of an effect came 0.25-1.27 s after the key, p10-p90, 1.52 at the most, of 135 regular presses with one), and only one that should show what it did: at a target (its kind's HP known, not dying), from the ground or from a jump (`JUMPS_JUDGED`: as designed a jump throw's was left out, and in the simulator with the game's Attack moved the doubt then never came in 3 of 12 runs, 110-250 useless regular presses each, 70-80% of them jump throws at a monster she couldn't finish; judged, the live runs have 4 more effects and no more presses without one), not on a rope or at its top (the game refuses those), no touch on her from 0.45 s before its key to its look (`KNOCK_S`), its target's bar believable before it (between empty and full: hurt, not dying) or none up (unhurt: `UNHURT_JUDGED`, from the review; a monster shows its bar once it's hit, so with the regular attack alone and its key wrong no press was ever judged: in the review's simulator runs 283 and 258 useless presses and no doubt), a bar missed in one look taken as the one seen on that monster in the 3 s before (`BAR_MEMORY_S`: at 00:31:14.7 the Horny Mushroom at 9% read with no bar between two reads of it at 9%), and its target in her regular attack's reach at its key's look and at the judging one (`regular_reach`: the star's, 50 inside `reach.STAR_RANGE`, walls and floors stopping it, monsters above her as far as the star's search reaches, and no other monster nearer that way that her star or her claw takes first, the look's or one the watch saw in the last 1.8 s and the look didn't find (`_in_front`, `RegularWatch.hidden`, `HIDDEN_S`: under its damage numbers; `loop_tree_ore_waits` doubted with her keys right, its stars taking a Horny Mushroom so hidden in front of the target; live it passes over 6 presses with her keys right, 2 of them without effect); a wand's box for the magician. Live 8 of 8 presses at a monster 67-89 above her and 131-269 ahead took effect, so the review's simulator run that doubted with her keys right at a Horny Mushroom 90 above her and 232 ahead, none of 6 stars taking it, is the simulator's own geometry; keeping to the 60 above and below measured as hits cost the doubt in 1 of the 12 sweep runs with the Attack moved and caught nothing live). It took **no effect** when that monster is seen again alive with a believable bar as high as before (`BAR_STEP`/2, 0.015, under it at the most; one higher than its own was is another monster's, and waited past), or still with no bar up in two looks 0.3 s apart if it had none (`UNHURT_AGAIN_S`: a bar missed once isn't none), no kill of hers placed on it and no EXP gain naming its kind from 0.15 s after the key (`SHOWS_S`); an **effect** when its bar is lower (or one is up where there was none), a kill of hers is placed on it or a gain names its kind (a party share names none: it isn't one). An effect a Lucky Seven cast at it keyed after the press could have made is the cast's: the press is passed over, as every press not judged is (neither counted nor ending a run). Its target is followed look to look by the feed's track, else by kind and place (`seen_again`), else as the one of its kind on its platform it can have walked to since it was last seen (120 units a second: a look between that missed it). Five no-effects in a row (`DOUBT_PRESSES`) are the doubt: "THE REGULAR ATTACK TOOK NO EFFECT 5 TIMES IN A ROW (horny-mushroom, its bar 9% throughout, 00:31:15.0-00:31:19.3: in reach, untouched, each judged 1.3 s after its key): checking her stars, then the game's key bindings", and a telemetry event `key_doubt`. Her regular presses are held from then (Lucky Seven at a target instead while she has the MP for a cast, else no throw, and none at nothing: `Attacks.key` says None, `Actions.throw` sends nothing).

**In the hunt loop** (`tour --loop`, `--grind`, which is what runs live) the doubt raises `KeyDoubt` where her health is asked after (`Hunter.health_check`), and `Hunt.run` runs the check (`Hunter.check_keys`) as it stands still for a look that failed its checks: its clocks paused over it, the next pass from where she is. Every look of the check asks the safety stop as `health_check` would (the HP watch's due: until the review a check could hold it off for about 34 s). Elsewhere (`hunt kill`, `hunt clear`, `nav`, a plain `tour`, `probe run`) there's no check: her regular presses stay held for the run and whoever is at the PC is paged to run `gamelab keys --read`.

**The check** (`KeyCheck.run`; reordered by the review of 2026-10-28):
1. *Where*: no monster within 250 of her (and 120 up or down: `PLACE_CLEAR`, `hunter.PET_CLEAR`) in a look, she stays; else away to a safe place as on the Lie Detector (`retreat.away`, "KEY CHECK: retreat to platform 25 (a safe platform; ...)", 10 s at most, her moves alone), and a look after it: one still near puts the check off (below).
2. *Her stars* (the thief's: her profile's ammo, "throwing stars"; a magician's regular attack is her wand, nothing to run out of: "her stars: none to run out of"). A Lucky Seven cast that took MP since the doubt's first press (`DartWatch.mp_shown_at`, its bar 2 px under the stretch's highest) says she has them (at 00:31 her casts took MP at 00:31:11-13 and 00:31:20). Else, with the MP for a cast and a step, her Lucky Seven key and a monster in reach, none within the claw's reach and 50 more of her either way (up close the key swipes, no MP whatever her stars; until the review only the way she cast was looked at), her on a platform, not on a rope nor at its top (`DartWatch.roped`, `at_top`: the game refuses casts there), up to 5 casts in 10 s (`STAR_CASTS`, `STAR_TEST_MAX_S`): one whose MP shows on her bar 0.55 s after its key, or that lowers its target's bar (or puts one up) within 1.3 s, says she has them ("her stars: the test's cast 2 took MP: she has them"); a touch on her ends the test ("not known (touched during the test, after 1 cast(s))"); 5 that took no MP and hurt nothing say her stars **may be out**, which isn't the stop: live her casts take no MP with her stars in her bag 5-9 in a row (Out of darts: a monster on her unseen, the key swiping it), and the review counted 7-8 in a row under the test's own conditions on 2026-10-26 (21:32:34, 23:13:46, 23:32:51: `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/akey/review-correctness/casts_mp.py`), where the test as built would have stopped the hunt. So out of darts stays its own watch's: the test's casts are counted in its stretch like any Lucky Seven press, and `OutOfDarts` comes from the test only if that's due (20 presses on Tree Dungeon); else "her stars: MAYBE OUT (5 test casts took no MP and hurt nothing; ...): out of darts' own watch stops the hunt at 20 Lucky Seven presses in a row without MP", and ATTACK found on her key (4.) turns the regular attack off for the run. Without the MP, or with no monster to cast at, it isn't known.
3. *A quiet moment*: right before the backslash a look with her on a platform (not on a rope, not at its top), untouched for 0.45 s, no monster within 250, and two looks 0.3 s apart with her where she was (`unquiet`, `QUIET_LOOK_S`); one more retreat if a monster's near; none within 3 s (`QUIET_S`): the check is **put off** ("ATTACK KEY: the key check put off (green-mushroom near her still after the retreat (arrived)): her regular presses held; again at a quiet moment (1 of 3)"), her regular presses held, and `health_check` raises its doubt again at the first look 5 s or more later that `unquiet` passes (`DEFER_GAP_S`, `RegularWatch.again`; "the key check put off: a quiet moment now"); put off a 4th time, no more regular attacks this run, paged (`DEFERS_MAX`). Until the review the window could open with a monster on her: nothing looked again after the retreat or the stars' test.
4. *The window* (`KeyCheck._window`): a frame first (the client not at 1366x768: nothing sent at all, not read; until the review the backslash went out and Esc never did), the mouse moved off where it opens (1100, 300: a pointer over a cell hides it, and over a preset page draws that page as "checked"), a frame (open already: read, no backslash), the backslash tapped, frames 0.6, 1.0 and 2.0 s after it until it's seen open (`SETTLE_S`, `AGAIN_S`, `LATE_S`: its opening isn't measured live yet), by its whole title or its name alone with the rest off the frame (`keybindings.find_part`). Seen, its frame is kept (`lab/shots/keybindings_<time>.png`, 3 a run); Esc, frames 0.6 and 1.0 s later, Esc once more only if both still show it (a window slow to close isn't sent a second Esc, which would open the MENU), and so once more. **Remembered** (`keymap.remember`, `at_start`). Every read of the window that can be followed is saved for the character who plays (`lab/keybindings-<character>.json`: her keys as followed, when, the frame it was read off in `lab/shots`, the preset, the whole map, config.toml's keys then, and the game's Attack on no key if it was), by the check and by `gamelab keys --read`. A command's keys at its start are those (`control.timeline.her_setup`, `__main__._hunter`; config.toml's [keys] stay the first default only), and the log says which: "her keys: the key bindings read off the game's window at 2026-10-28 16:05:12 (keybindings-thief.json, from keybindings_20261028-160512.png); not config.toml's: JUMP ALT -> C", "her keys: config.toml [keys]"; with the game's Attack on no key remembered, that's said, and the regular attack is tried again on its key (5 presses without effect doubt it again: since the review, below; until then it was off from the start of every later run, with nothing to doubt it again). A remembered file that doesn't hold keys as they can be (a name config.toml can't name, her arrows, jump or attack on none, two on one key, one of NEVER, her moves or pet food not as the alarm's allowance takes them) is left out, said ("config.toml [keys] (keybindings-thief.json left out: two of hers on one key)"); config.toml's [keys] changed since it was read is said too, and `gamelab keys --forget` drops it. `gamelab keys` says which keys are in use. `pet --every` reads it again before each follow and follows a change (a hunt that followed her pet food elsewhere since it started). maplehelper's own app (`python -m maplehelper`, the combos jump_throw, back_off, hop_back and jump_back_shot that press her jump and attack keys) takes the thief's file too (`config.followed`, said in its banner; `--config-keys` for config.toml's).

**The player's allowance with the Lie Detector's alarm up** (`control/alarm.py`: `AlarmKeys`; `control/player.py`). The player is a separate, elevated process that reads config.toml once at its start. Her moves' and pet food's keys in use are written for it (`keymap.publish`, `lab/alarm_keys.json`: those six fields and nothing else) at every command's start and whenever the hunt follows them, and the player reads that file again whenever it changes (its size or modification time, at each plan of the alarm's two kinds). What goes with the alarm up stays what it was, her retreat's moves for 12 s and a tap of her pet food a few times a minute, only by the keys they're on now: the file can't name any other of her keys, a key config.toml can't name, Esc, the backslash, Enter, Tab, Backspace, a digit or maplehelper's hotkeys, two moves on one key or her pet food on a move's; a file that does is left out, said once in the player's log, and config.toml's keys stand (`tests/test_alarm.py`: her followed jump and pet food let through, her old jump, attack, Lucky Seven, pick-up, old pet food key and the mouse refused, each kind of bad file left out, a change read without a restart). Since the review (below), a key of the file's that config.toml has for another of hers that isn't let through with the alarm up (her attack, Lucky Seven, potions, pick-up, chair, sit) is on no key with the alarm up: neither it nor config.toml's own for that field (the game may have either on something else), said in the player's log ("pet_food 'ctrl' is config.toml's attack: not let through with the alarm up"). **The player must be started again once** (`player --elevate`, the user's UAC click) for this code; after that a followed key needs no restart. Until it is, a player of the old code refuses her retreat's followed moves and a followed pet food tap with the alarm up (it allows only config.toml's).

**To check in game** (no attack; only the backslash, Esc and a mouse move; with the user at the PC, not within 50 minutes of a Lie Detector):
1. Start the player again (`python -m gamelab player --elevate`, the user's UAC click: its allowance reads `lab/alarm_keys.json` from this code on), the perception service running, the game in front at 1366x768, her on a safe platform with no monster near, nothing else running.
2. `python -m gamelab keys`: "her keys: config.toml [keys]" and her keys (no binding remembered yet).
3. `python -m gamelab keys --read --map 10002073`: as before (ATTACK on CTRL, preset 2, read and closed), and now "her keys as the game has them: as she has them" with her Lucky Seven on SHIFT, PET FOOD on U and THE GREEN RELAXER on D in the map's line, and "remembered in ...keybindings-thief.json". `lab/alarm_keys.json` then has her moves and U; the player's log says nothing new (the same keys as config.toml's).
4. `python -m gamelab keys` again: "her keys: the key bindings read off the game's window at ...". Then `python -m gamelab keys --forget` (config.toml's again), or keep it.
5. Later, supervised: move JUMP to C in the window by hand (an unused preset, or put it back after), run `keys --read`: "JUMP ALT -> C", remembered; `tour --loop` then starts with "not config.toml's: JUMP ALT -> C" and jumps with C. Put JUMP back on Alt, `keys --read` again (or `keys --forget`).

Rebased onto master 73394ba (her touches as her popups, the safety stop in HP, her stats from perception, the goldens on a pool): the conflicts in `hunter.py`, `navigator.py`, `scene.py`, `fakes.py`, `scenarios.py` and `__main__.py` merged with both sides kept (a touch that took HP tells the casts' watch too, as it tells the regular one; a chain cut by a touch is `TOUCHED`'s; a command that hunts sets her keys up, then waits for her max HP). The numbers in the paragraphs above are the build's, before it; as rebased and fixed, the scenarios' are in their docstrings and below. Every finding was checked against the code, its probe run again on it:

1. *A key taken off with nothing else moved went on being pressed* (PICK UP on no key, the game's QUEST on Z: Z 174-786 times a 4-minute run). Her keys are followed whenever the window read's differ from hers (`keymap.changes`), not only when one moved: her pick-up, chair or sit on no key now aren't pressed any more ("the misses were something else; nothing moved; pick up on no key: not pressed any more"), remembered so.
2. *Out of darts' stop was dropped when the check before it found Attack moved or on no key* (its `fired` kept: never due again that run). The stop is raised after ATTACK is followed (or turned off) and paged, unless her Lucky Seven itself moved; her Lucky Seven moved restarts out of darts' stretch (`DartWatch.followed`) whatever else moved.
3. *Her pet food key was never doubted* (a stale remembered PET FOOD fed nothing; the fullness followed rose 30 a food all the same). `behavior/pet.py`: at a check her pet's fullness is read after each food, and 2 in a row that didn't raise it (`FOOD_DOUBT`) are the doubt ("HER PET FOOD TOOK NO EFFECT 2 TIMES IN A ROW (its key U; her pet's fullness 40 -> 40 -> 40, read after each): out of Pet Food, or her pet food key another in the game's Key Bindings?"): no third tap, paged ("MapleStory: her pet food"), that key not tapped for 30 minutes (`FOOD_DOUBT_WAIT_S`), then a check again. A pet food key that's neither config.toml's nor read off the window this run (`Hunter._pet_key_trusted`) isn't fed by blind: a food due is a check (read, fed, read again), waited for while no read can be made and the fullness followed is 20 or more (`BLIND_BELOW`); one whose food a check saw take goes by blind for 2 hours (`VERIFIED_S`: the babysitter runs beside the user's own play). In the hunt loop the doubt is a "pet" doubt (`Hunter._pet_doubted`): the window read, PET FOOD followed where the game has it, or "PET FOOD ON U AS CONFIGURED ...: out of Pet Food?".
4. *A stale remembered arrow was never put right and came back at every start* (MOVE RIGHT remembered on E, the game's on Right: 0 of 12 put right). A doubt that gets no check (outside the hunt loop, none within a check's gap, no quiet moment `DEFERS_MAX` times, the window not read) tells her hunter (`Hunter.keys_doubted`): if her keys in use are a remembered binding's otherwise than config.toml's for what the doubt is about (a moves doubt her arrows, jump, up and down; casts her Lucky Seven and arrows; regular her attack; pet her pet food; a stall any) and no read this run had them, the binding is marked (`keymap.suspect`), said, and the next command starts with config.toml's [keys] ("config.toml [keys] (keybindings-thief.json, read at ..., left out: doubted at ... and not checked, a moves doubt not checked (not in the hunt loop: no check): RIGHT RIGHT -> E; `gamelab keys --read` reads the game's)"); maplehelper's app leaves it out too; a read writes it again, unmarked. And a retreat for a check that timed out (an arrow on another key can do that: the review's seed 2) has the run's later checks wait for a quiet moment where she is (`KeyCheck.no_retreat`). In the simulator (`fix/sim/stale2.py`, the review's runs of `loop_tree_remembered_keys` with a stale remembered key, 2-minute hunts): MOVE RIGHT on E, 12 seeds: still not put right within the run (its doubts came after the hunt, 165-235 s, or were put off: the build's weak case, above), but marked in 12 of 12, so the next start takes config.toml's [keys] (the review: 0 of 12, the stale E at every start); JUMP on C, 6 seeds: 3 followed in the run, 1 marked, 2 with no doubt at all (the stale C carries on there: 28 and 45 kills, few jumps needed); Lucky Seven on A: 6 of 6 followed (out of darts due, the check first); PET FOOD on I: 6 of 6 followed in the run, 12-32 s in (her pet's first check fed nothing twice: the pet doubt, the window read, PET FOOD on U). Not built: the file expiring unless a read confirms it, or a read at every start (the backslash at each start; the user's call).

A MISS counts from 0.5 s after the key (`MISS_FROM_S`, the star's release at 0.52 s: it was 0.15, a damage's earliest on its target's bar, which is the server's) by its popup's first sighting (`_first_seen`: its sightings 0.5 s apart at the most near where it was), and one the other attack keyed at that monster 0.5-1.6 s before it was first seen could have made, before or after the press, is left out: the press is judged by its target's bar as without it (it was passed over only for a cast keyed after the press). Once a run for each kind ("(not in the hunt loop: no check here; paged already this run)"). ## The top of a rope: on the rope, not on the platform; the game's refusals (from 2026-10-27)

On 2026-10-26 out of darts stopped three grinds on Tree Dungeon with her stars in her bag (22:58:32, 23:11:49, 23:12:42; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/grind-2240.log`, the tour's and the perception service's telemetry, and the service's own 15 fps recording of the last 90 s, which the first stop saved: `lab/recent/20261026-225844-out-of-darts`). Each time the same (the diagnosis: `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/rope/diag`):
1. a climb up the rope at x 111 (rope 4, from 19 to 18) went past a Green Mushroom walking on 18 ("NO_WAIT: climb -> 18 past a green-mushroom regardless");
2. it touched her near the top (22:58:08.596, 47 under it, 0.22 s before the plan had her there); `Navigator._watch` cut the chain on the HP drop and let go of every key, up too;
3. the game doesn't knock her off a rope (she stayed on after 11 of 11 hits on ropes on 10-25 and 10-26), so she hung about 30 under 18's surface;
4. her dot snapped onto 18 (`Localizer.where_dot`: up to 33 under a platform, DOT_SNAP_LIFT 25 and FEET_BELOW 8; her dot (101.3, -861.1), 31 under it), and she was placed standing on 18 at x 113.3 for 25.4 s, by the hunt and the perception service alike; her name tag is at x 771 on the rope and standing at its top, and the camera keeps her feet at screen y 489 either way;

Two jump_ups from 18 "ended on platform 18 instead of platform 17": a jump on a rope with no arrow does nothing.
