## The Lie Detector's recordings

Since 2026-10-24 the player's watchdog records each Lie Detector's whole cycle (`control/lie_recorder.py`): the user asked for it, as the player's logs stopped at the alarm and none showed them answering it. Only the player records (`watch --lie-detector` raises the alarm and pages, as before, and records nothing). Since 2026-11-01 it keeps no pictures (the user: "stop keeping the 4fps recording and only use the unified recorder's 15fps video saving"): its index and summary only, the cycle's video being the rolling recorder's alarm clip, 15 a second and lossless, written once this recording's summary says the cycle is over (The rolling recording: Each alarm's own clip). Nothing of the mouse or the keyboard is recorded, and the watchdog never touches the game. One folder a cycle, `lab/lie_detector/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>/`, named for when it was first seen:
- **`index.jsonl`**: a line a look: `t` (s since the first sight) and the look's frame number `i` (the YOLO shadow's check of it comes back with it), the spotter's `scores` for each form (match / threshold, 1 = seen) and `seen`; or, with the game window gone or minimized, `game` ("no window", "minimized") and no frame. Such a grab doesn't count as the Lie Detector gone: it may have been up behind. With another window over some of the game (`window.shows`: its middle and near each corner), the grab is still checked for the Lie Detector, as it always was (it can show round that window; a picture of it shown over the game, its screenshot in a viewer, is taken for it too), but it gets no frame number (the YOLO shadow doesn't check it) and it counts as gone: `game` "covered", with the `scores` and `seen` of what was on top. (Minimized, the game's client area isn't 0×0 but 432×54, so the watchdog now asks Windows whether it's minimized, where it grabbed whatever was at that spot.) When the disk is too far behind to take a line, it's dropped, and the next line's `dropped_before` says how many.
- **`summary.json`**, when it ends: `first_seen`, `last_seen` and `seen_s`; `duration_s`; the `grabs` (looks); `not_showing` (by why); `forms` (each form seen, when it first and last showed and in how many frames); `truth_booth` and `outcome` (as far as the picture tells: "answered" if it went away without the Truth Booth showing, "sent to the Truth Booth", or "unknown" if it was still up when the recording ended); `end` ("gone", "cap", or "stopped": the player stopped); the alarm's screenshot; the `window`'s size; and `dropped`.

**YOLO shadow.** During a cycle started by the template spotter, the player also runs the local YOLO11n checkpoint (`assets/lie_detector_patterns.pt`, GPU 0 when CUDA is available, CPU otherwise) on the game's frames, on a thread of its own (`ShadowWorker`, `control/player.py`), never in the watchdog's looks. Its first check used to run in the look of the first sighting, and loaded torch, ultralytics and the model there: 5.0 s for the import and 3.9 s for the model and a first check on an idle PC, about 16 s live. The 21:02 recording of 2026-10-24 has frame 0, then nothing until 16.1 s, by when the Truth Booth showed: the whole mouse mini-game was lost, and the alarm waited as long. Now the player loads it when it starts and checks a blank frame once (its log: "the YOLO shadow is ready: loaded and a first check in N s, off the watch"; one that can't be loaded is turned off, the Lie Detector watched and recorded as ever). The watchdog hands it each frame of a cycle and grabs on; when it's free it checks the newest one handed it (4 a second at most; the others go unchecked). Its check comes back late, as a line of its own in the index after its frame's: the frame's `t` and `i`, its `shadow` score (the patterns found / 4), `seen`, `late` (s after the grab) and `suggestions`: every detected pattern's `box`, pointer-location `center` and `confidence`, in original frame pixels. These are detections, not a claim that YOLO knows the fading target or correct answer. Nothing moves the pointer or sends a key. Four or more detections at confidence 0.5 mark `yolo patterns` seen at that frame, and keep the cycle going through active pattern play after the notice disappears, as a sight of the Lie Detector there would: the minute without it starts after that frame, an alarm cleared since that frame is raised again, and the cycle's end waits for the shadow's check of a frame of that minute, 30 s at most (`SHADOW_WAIT_S`: a check that hangs holds up neither the end nor the player's stop). YOLO alone cannot start a cycle or an alarm. `summary.json`'s `shadow` counts its `checks` and `suggestions`, says how late the latest came back (`late_max_s`) and how many were `lost` (the disk too far behind). A YOLO failure is logged and leaves the template alarm and frame recording working. In `tests/test_lie_yolo.py` a shadow that takes 10 s a check leaves the frames coming 4 a second. To check at the next Lie Detector: frames 4 a second from 0 s, with no gap after the first but the paging's 1.2 s, and the shadow's lines a fraction of a second `late`.

**When it ends.** Once the game has shown no Lie Detector for a minute (`END_S`), the same minute the player waits, its alarm cleared, before it stops. The template spotter knows the mouse mini-game's notice; the YOLO shadow now recognizes active pattern boards too (its sight counted at the frame it checked, however late it comes back). The minute still has to outlast the count and tracking when neither sees a known form, the moment between the countdown and Violettas' windows, and a frame or two missed in a flicker. The first full recordings will show whether that tail needs changing. At the latest, recording stops 10 minutes after the first sight (`CAP_S`): the longest cycle seen is a test left unanswered and the Truth Booth it sends her to, then the minute, about 8 minutes. A cycle that runs on past it goes on unrecorded, the player locked, and no second recording starts until it's over.

**Off the alarm's path.** The watchdog sets the alarm Event first, then writes `ALARM.json` and its screenshot and pages, as before, and only then starts the recording, with the look it saw. The paging's beeps take about 1.2 s, so the second look comes that much after the first. The index is written on a thread of its own behind a queue of 16 looks (4 s), and old recordings deleted on another: a slow or full disk never holds up a look, nor does the YOLO shadow, on a thread of its own too; nothing that goes wrong in a look, the recording or the log stops the watchdog (each is logged the first time and every 1,000th). The watchdog now looks 4 times a second from the start of each look. It used to wait 0.25 s after each, which with the look's own 70 ms made 3.10 a second on a 1366×768 frame (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/ld/rate_measure.py`), 4.00 now; recording a Lie Detector screen, 4.00 a second with nothing dropped (`rate_recording.py`). That's about a third more of the check's time: 0.26 of a core at 65 ms a check, where it was 0.20.

**Disk.** When a recording starts, the oldest others are deleted until they take at most 10 GB (`KEEP_BYTES`), never the one being written. A recording's own index is small since its frames went (2026-11-01; about 175 MB a cycle answered when its JPEGs were kept). The Lie Detector came about an hour apart at the most often (00:47, 01:58 and 02:54 on 2026-10-19): that's two days of play without a break, weeks of evenings, where the telemetry's 2 GB keep 4 days of `watch`. `lab-usage` counts them, with what the next would delete, and `clear-alarm` refuses while the recording is still going, and says how the last one ended. The player's log has a line when one starts and when it ends (its looks, how long, the forms, the outcome). With the rolling recorder running, each cycle's folder also has the 5 minutes before it (`before/`, about 650 MB at 1366×768: The rolling recording), and they count: about 0.65 GB a cycle, 15 of them in the 10 GB. The recorder prunes the folder itself each time it writes a part, to the same 10 GB with the parts counted and the cycle under way spared (`Recorder._prune_lie`), as the player counts them only from that day's code on (`lie_recorder.size_of` counts a recording's folders since; before, its files only): an older player, elevated and restarted only with the user's click, would hold some 58 cycles of 0.8 GB, 37 GB, with 32 GB free on D: that evening.

**To check in game**, when the next Lie Detector comes (explore-only first: the player only watches it):
- Within two seconds of the alarm (after the paging's beeps), `lab/lie_detector/<time>/` appears and the player's log says "LIE DETECTOR seen", then "recording the Lie Detector"; the player keeps running, where it used to shut down.
- Answer it. Once it's gone, the log says "Lie Detector recording ended (gone): N looks over S s". `summary.json` should have about 4 looks a second (`grabs`), the forms you saw with their times, `outcome` "answered" (or the Truth Booth), `end` "gone" and `window` [1366, 768]; the alarm's clip (`lab/alarm_clips/<time>-lie-detector-...`, written about 10 s after the cycle ends) should show you answering it. The mini-game notice's last `seen` in the index and the clip say how long the tracking took: `END_S` should outlast it with room (if the tracking ended within seconds of the recording, `END_S` goes up).
- `clear-alarm` before that minute is out refuses (exit code 3), saying the recording is still going; after it, it clears the alarm and says how the recording ended, and the player's log says "... the player stops", then "player stopped". Start it again (`player --elevate`); then `hunt look`, or `act 100` (no keys), runs. With a window over the game meanwhile (the terminal), the index has `"game": "covered"` lines for those looks, and they count toward the end.
- `spot --image` on its first frame should say it's on screen; the alarm's screenshot goes with the others in `tests/fixtures/lie_detector`.

## The rolling recording

Since 2026-10-24 a recorder keeps the game's last 5 minutes, 10 frames a second, so that what led up to a moment can be saved after it (`control/rolling.py`). The user asked for it at 21:50 that evening: something had popped up in the game wanting an answer within 10 s, and nothing recorded it (the player's Lie Detector check knew only the countdown, the mouse mini-game and the Truth Booth, and records once it has seen one of them). It was most likely the image quiz, which the player knows since 2026-10-25, with its warning and the mini-game's notice: their alarms are saved as any (below). `python -m gamelab recorder` runs it, at below-normal priority, all the time, hunts too: the babysitter keeps it running. It reads the screen only: no keys, no clicks, and it never brings the game forward.

**In the perception service** (from 2026-10-26; `control/recording.py`). The user: "The recording should probably just take frames from within the same perception process to have a rolling window copy of things in memory, match fps or fps/2." So `gamelab perceive` keeps it now, from its own frames, and `gamelab recorder` is what runs where it can't (below); what's kept, saved and said is as below, the same folders, files and status.
- *15 frames a second* (`FPS`: every other of the service's 30): the frame loop hands a frame over as it makes its state (`Service._emit` to `Recording.saw`: the picture by reference, its number and run), picked on the frames' own times by a token bucket (15 tokens a second, 2 at most, a frame taken with one: `BURST`), into a queue of 8 that's never waited on (past it a frame is dropped, counted). With the frame loop slower than 15 a second, as many as it makes, less its swing from second to second (no second gets more than 15): on the replays' real frame times (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/cadence_rules.py`, 77 runs), a loop at 12-14 a second kept 11.6-13.2, at 25-30 a second 15.0. (First built with a due grid, a frame every 1/15 s 16 ms early at most: 0.1-0.2 a second fewer; the review measured 78-94% of a loop at 12-16 a second kept, where the code said every frame.)
- *Never fewer than the old recorder's 10 a second* (`FLOOR_FPS`): with the frame loop under it (a crowd, without the native pieces of work/perceive-native: 11.7% of the hunts' 10 s status lines of 2026-10-25 and 26 said 7-10 frames a second; on the replays, on a busy machine, 10-50% of the seconds of the crowd), fewer than 10 of its frames in the last second, the recording takes its moments itself, 15 a second, as the recorder did (`Recorder.tick`: the window looked at, grabbed with mss, looked at again), until the loop gives 12 a second over 2 s (`FLOOR_BACK_FPS`); the loop's frames meanwhile only counted (one of its own between two of the loop's would make the second late). Said in the log every 10 minutes at most, counted in the status (`floor_moments`, `floor_times`). The recorder kept a median of 10 and never fewer than 9 in a second (the hunts before the Lie Detectors of 00:25 and 01:01). Its picture is the frame's own, which the capture never writes over while it's held (`perception.frames.Pictures`), never the shared memory's slot (encoding from one crashed the service once, an access violation, as a new run unmapped it).
- *Each kept as its difference from the one before* (`rolling.pack_diff`: uint8, wrapping round; zstd at level 1 as before), a whole frame every second (`KEY_EVERY_S`), after a gap, at another size or where another moment came between: a chain, which the ring lets go whole once its last moment is out, a save starts at a whole frame of (a save of N s holds up to a second more), and a part is decoded chain by chain as it's written (`rolling.decode`), each frame exactly as shown (the tests: bit for bit; the long run below: 3,069 frames of 3,069 the very frame fed). What it takes: on the lossless frames of the alarm clip of 01:02 (10 a second, consecutive; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/diff_rule.py`), the hunting before the alarm 265-375 KB a frame, the Lie Detector's dialog 122, 4-7 ms of CPU; so 5 minutes of hunting at 15 a second take 1.1-1.6 GB, 0.5 answering a Lie Detector. The replays' frames (`before/`'s, JPEG: their noise compresses worse) took 378 KB a frame in a crowd (the numbers review: 1.27 GiB after 300 s at 11.6 a second kept, about 1.6 at 15) and 624 on the quiet ones (about 2.7 GiB at 15). The floor's own grabs are whole frames, 350-480 KB (2 GB for 5 minutes of them). The cap is 4 GB as before. A difference comes out bigger than the whole frame on a camera pan (the review: 23% of the clip's pairs; 86% of one 10 s stretch of it), but keeping those whole instead saved only 3-5% (356 KB a frame against 375 on that stretch) for 65% more CPU (both packed: 10.9 ms against 6.6), so it isn't done.
- *Only frames of the game:* those the frame loop found showing it wholly, in front, uncovered and where its window is (the service's checks, at the recorder's grid), less one whose capture doesn't line up with the window (framecheck's `offset`), and none with another program's window over any of the game: with the recording on, the service's screen frames ask `window.over` too, just before the shot and again just after it, as the recorder asked around its grabs (`ScreenFrames.cover_check`, `Frame.over`: the grid's points miss a notification between them and a window clicks pass through; the review showed such a frame kept, where the recorder's check said "covered"). Since 2026-11-01 such a frame is kept as it is, the boxes of the client those windows were over noted with it (`Frame.over_boxes`: `frames.cover`, before the shot and after it; `Item.over`, `Item.covered`), the window named in the log; over all of the game, or where its boxes aren't known, a gap ("covered"), as every such frame was until then. One never asked (`over` None) isn't taken. What perception reads is as before. The walk up the z-order keeps Python's lock through its calls (`frames._over`: the same answer as `window.over`'s): 0.077 ms with the 44 windows above the window in front on this PC, 0.47 with all 277 (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/above_front.py`, `over_same.py`), two a frame. While the frame loop has none to give for 0.25 s (`OWN_AFTER_S`, 0.5 as first built: the game not on screen, the client another size, the picture drawn off it, the capture stalled or failing, the loop itself stalled), the recording takes its moments itself as for the floor: whatever the recorder kept, at any client size, it keeps.
- *Its index* has each frame's `seq` and `run` (the state's number and the service's run), so a frame joins what perception made of it; its summary the frames' `sources`; its status file says where its frames come from (`recorder --status`: "its frames: the perception service's frames, 15 a second asked", the frames taken, dropped, late and covered, its own grabs and those for the floor), and what it still has to write (`pending_clips`, `saves_waiting`: the babysitter's to read).
- *Saves* (an alarm's `before/` and clip, `save-recent`) are written by the saver's thread and 4 writers (2 while a command hunts) at the lowest thread priority (`WRITER_PRIORITY`; Perception at one pace), each writer a chain at a time: 120 s of a hunt in about 12 s. Since the reviews of 2026-10-26 each part is written by a process of its own (`rolling.write_part_apart`, `control/partwriter.py`: below normal priority, its threads at the lowest, as the recorder's process wrote them; in the service only if it fails): written in the service a save shared its Python lock with the frame loop, whose steps then waited 19-21 ms (median) against 1, against 3-4 written apart (Perception at one pace: After the reviews).
- *One recorder at a time* (the recorders' mutex): with `gamelab recorder` running the service doesn't record, tries every 10 s, and says it waits (`lab/recorder/waiting.json`); the babysitter (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/babysit3.ps1`) stops the old recorder when it sees that, once it has nothing left to write (no Lie Detector alarm up or begun in the last 5 minutes, no `save-recent` asked or being written, its status's `pending_clips` and `saves_waiting` at 0), and starts it when no recording runs (the service down, of the code before, or `perceive --no-record`). `perceive --no-record`: the service without it.
- *What it can't:* outlive the service. A service that ends (its watchdog, a crash, a restart) loses the 5 minutes it held; the next starts empty, where the recorder ran on through the service's restarts.

- **Only the game, what's over it noted.** A frame is kept when the screen shows the game's client area: its window there and not minimized, wholly on the monitors, with the window where it was. Another program's window over part of it leaves the frame as grabbed, with the boxes of the client it covered noted (since 2026-11-01, the user: "keep the frame if it's only partially covered ... save metadata on what part was covered by other window": until then a frame with any window over any of the game, or the game not in front, was a gap, and on 2026-10-29 seven Lie Detectors' clips, 00:29 to 09:30, kept no frame at all, "covered" 50-70 s each, while the player's 4 a second grabbed them). What's over it is asked before each grab and again after it, up the z-order (`window.overs`; `GameWindow.over`: the boxes, cut to the client); a game wholly under such windows is a gap ("covered"). Up the z-order means every window above the game that's shown (visible, not minimized, not cloaked: a window on another virtual desktop isn't) and whose box as drawn (DWM's, without Windows 10's invisible borders) meets the client area: points alone missed a window over the client's left 8 px, a 200×150 box between them and a 300×100 notification (the review's, on the real client area), and an overlay clicks pass through isn't found at a point at all. The game's own windows are left out. Its log names the window over the game (its class and box, not its title): "recording, another window over part of the game (by ...)", or "not recording: covered (by ...)". Otherwise the moment is a gap, and why ("no window", "minimized", "off the screen", "covered", "moved", "capture failed"). Any client size is recorded.
- **In memory, losslessly** (since 2026-10-25, the user asked). A frame's BGR pixels are kept zstd-compressed at level 1 (`pack`: OpenCV drops the alpha, Python 3.14's `compression.zstd` packs; zlib on an older Python), exactly as grabbed. On six 1366×768 frames saved losslessly (three scenes, a calibration shot, two Lie Detector boards; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch` `lossless.py`, `ringbench.py`): 757 KB a frame (381-1163) packed in 9.5 ms from the grabbed BGRA; 3,000 of them, 5 minutes, 2.2 GB (3.4 at the busiest). Not PNG: as big, and 55 ms a frame at its fastest; WebP lossless 502 KB in 667 ms. They take at most 4 GB (`MAX_BYTES`, the PC has 32): past it the oldest go before they're 5 minutes old (at 1920×1080, twice the pixels, about 4 minutes at the busiest), counted in the status as `trimmed`. A part is encoded as it's written, on 4 threads (`ENCODERS`): JPEG at quality 75 with full-resolution colour (`JPEG_PARAMS`: the player's Lie Detector recordings' settings until they stopped keeping frames, 2026-11-01; `spot --image` sees on one what the watchdog would have) for `before/` and `save-recent`, PNG for each alarm's clip (below): 5 minutes as JPEG in about 10 s (36 s of CPU, 741 MB), a clip's 70 s as PNG in about 14 s (44 s of CPU, 556 MB). Until then frames were kept as JPEG at those settings: on the 85 distinct saved 1366×768 game frames (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/rolling/jpeg_measure2.py`) 221 KB a frame (47-307), 33.0 dB, 4.0 ms to encode, 650 MB for 5 minutes (a 712 MB process), at most 1 GB. In memory and not in a ring of files on D: because 10 frames a second are 2.2 MB/s, about 190 GB a day written, for frames almost never kept.
- **Captured with mss, not DXGI** (until 2026-10-26; since then the service's frames, its duplication's, and mss for its own moments: In the perception service, above). Windows limits the duplications of a monitor: with `watch` and `pet` running, two more opened and a third failed (DuplicateOutput 0x887A0022, DXGI_ERROR_NOT_CURRENTLY_AVAILABLE; `capture_bench.py`, 2026-10-24). A recorder holding one all the time would leave a hunt's looks and its feed one fewer, and one that can't open falls back to mss for `capture.RETRY_S` (10 s of 17 ms looks instead of 2 ms). mss holds no duplication (the player's watchdog grabs with it too). On the game's box, 5 s of 10 grabs a second each, nothing kept: DXGI 2.6-4.9 ms a grab (median) and 1.9-4.7 ms of CPU; mss 14-25 ms (it waits for the compositor's next frame; p90 25-35) and 5.3-6.6 ms of CPU, alone or with two others grabbing at once. (Since 2026-10-25 the commands hold one duplication between them, the perception service's, where `watch`, `pet` and a hunt held one each: the recorder stays on mss.)
- **Its cost** (`loop_bench.py`, the PC 66% busy with other work): a frame takes 22-32 ms from the first look at the window to its JPEG (median; mss's wait the most of it), and 12.7-14.3 ms of CPU, everything counted (the grab 6.7, the JPEG 4-6, the two looks at the window 0.5, measured before `window.over`; its walk up the z-order adds 0.1 ms a look, 0.66 in the review's run, 39 windows above the game): 0.13-0.14 of a core, at below-normal priority. Kept losslessly since 2026-10-25, a frame's packing takes 9.5 ms against the JPEG's 4-6: about 0.17 of a core, not measured in the live loop yet. While the game isn't showing it only looks at the window (0.02 ms a moment when the game isn't in front).
- **Saved on demand.** `save-recent [--seconds N] [--name NAME]` asks the running recorder through its inbox (`lab/recorder/inbox/<id>.json`; it looks every moment, renames the request `.taken` and answers in `lab/recorder/outbox/<id>.json`) to save its last N s (300 by default: all it keeps) to `lab/recent/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>[-name]/`, and prints the folder last. The frames are those the ring held when it took the request, written on a thread of their own (5 minutes in about 10 s, encoded to JPEG as they're written; nothing waits for them). With no recorder running (its status file, `lab/recorder/status.json`, missing, saying it stopped, or older than 30 s), or none taking the request within 3 s (withdrawn then), it says so, exit code 1. When one is saved, the oldest others go until they take 5 GB (`RECENT_KEEP_BYTES`, about 8 of 5 minutes).
- **Saved on a Lie Detector alarm.** At an `ALARM.json` with a time it hasn't seen (looked for every 0.5 s), what it holds then, and what comes in the alarm's first 5 s (`BEFORE_TAIL_S`: the player writes the alarm, pages for about 1.2 s, then starts its recording), goes into that recording's folder as `before/`: the 5 minutes before the Lie Detector and its first seconds again. It's written with its clip (below), once the cycle is over, 10 s after the Lie Detector's last sight (since 2026-11-01, the user: "no more 60s, save all recordings you need at the 10s mark"; a minute after the alarm until then), so that encoding its frames (about 10 s on 4 threads) doesn't run beside the grabs while the Lie Detector is up (the user asked, 2026-10-25; it was written as the player's recording began). What the ring held at the alarm is held meanwhile. Before it's written, the Lie Detector's recordings are pruned to their 10 GB, the parts before counted (The Lie Detector's recordings: Disk). Its summary has the alarm and `alarm_t`, the alarm's moment in it (ALARM.json's time of writing). With no recording of the player's begun within 20 s of the alarm (the player not running, or `watch --lie-detector` raised it), the part goes to `lab/recent/<time>-lie-detector[-<form>]/` (`-quiz-warning`: the alarm's `form`, when it says one). An alarm already up when the recorder starts isn't saved (it holds nothing yet).
- **Each alarm's own clip** (since 2026-10-25, the user: "a 2nd line of defense"; since 2026-11-01 the Lie Detector's only video): from 10 s before the alarm (`CLIP_BEFORE_S`; the alarm's moment as for `before/`, ALARM.json's time of writing) to 10 s after the cycle's last sight (`CLIP_TAIL_S`: the player's recording's summary, its `last_seen` from the folder's time), in `lab/alarm_clips/<time>-lie-detector[-<form>]/`. It's written as soon as the cycle is over (`Recorder.cycle_end`: the player's recording summed up, the Lie Detector gone for `END_S`, 10 s), then the part before it: the user, 2026-11-01: "no more 60s, save all recordings you need at the 10s mark" (until then it ran 60 s after the alarm, and nothing was saved before). With no recording of the player's within 20 s of the alarm (the player not running, `watch --lie-detector` raised it), the cycle ends when the alarm is cleared. At most 3 minutes after the alarm (`CLIP_MAX_S`: a cycle sent to the Truth Booth runs on, a minimized game keeps the watchdog's cycle going; its moments are held meanwhile, at most about 0.9 GB). A recorder that stops before then writes what it has (`cut_short` true in its summary). Its moments are held by the clip as they come, so a ring that loses them first (its cap, at a bigger window) loses none of the clip's. Lossless: PNG (`00000.png` ...; `format` "png" in its summary), each frame exactly as grabbed. Its summary has `kind` "the alarm's clip", the `alarm`, `alarm_t` (10 s, the alarm's moment in it), `asked` (from -10 to how far after the alarm it went), `player_recording` (the recording it followed) and `cut_short`. About 8 MB a second at 1366x768; the oldest go past 30 GB (`CLIPS_KEEP_BYTES`; 5 GB until the user asked for 30, making room on D:, which had 27 GB free), counted by `lab-usage`. A recorder started since then is needed (the babysitter starts it again within 5 s of its process ending). A Lie Detector answered and then covered, or the game sent behind other windows, still gets its whole clip 10 s after its last sight: the watchdog counts covered looks toward the end (the frames of those 10 s are gaps where the game is wholly covered).
- **A saved part**: `00000.jpg` ...; `index.jsonl`, a line a frame (`i`, `file`, `t` s from the part's first moment, `at` the clock time, and, where other programs' windows were over part of the game, `over`, the boxes of the client they covered, and `covered`, their share) and a line a gap (the moments in a row with no frame for one reason: `gap`, `t` and `until`, `ticks`); `summary.json` (`kind`, `from`, `to`, `seconds`, `ticks`, `frames`, `part_covered_frames`, `bytes`, the `gaps` in s by why, `fps`, `jpeg_quality`, the `window`'s size).
- **To look at one**, `sheet FOLDER`: a contact sheet of a frame a second, a quarter size, labelled with the clock time (`sheet.png` in the folder; `--every`, `--shrink`, `--start` and `--end` in s; 2 s for a minute's). `sheet FOLDER --video`: an mp4 playing in real time (`video.mp4`), a gap a grey card saying why, the clock time at the top left. It's OpenCV's own MPEG-4 Part 2 (its build has no H.264): about 30 dB, the HUD's text legible; a minute of the saved frames was 10 MB and took 18 s to write (`video_bench.py`). Both read the Lie Detector's recordings as well.
- **How it's doing**: `recorder --status` prints its status file: whether the game shows, what it keeps (s, frames, MB, gaps), and over the last 5 s its frames a second, ms a frame, CPU a frame and share of a core; its saves. Its log says when the game starts and stops showing, each save, and every 10 minutes what it keeps and costs. One recorder runs at a time (a named mutex: a second says so and exits). A moment that goes wrong (a grab that fails: the desktop locked, a UAC prompt) is a gap, logged the first time and every 1,000th; nothing stops it but Ctrl+C or its process ending, and with it what it holds.
- **Where it runs**: from a checkout whose `gamelab/lab` is the player's, as the alarm, the Lie Detector's recordings and the inbox are in it: the main checkout, or a live worktree (their `lab` is the main checkout's, through a junction) that has `control/rolling.py`. `save-recent` and `recorder --status` are run from any of those.

**To check in game** (nothing it does sends a key; since 2026-10-26 in the service: Perception at one pace, To put it live):
- `recorder --status` says "running" and, with the game in front, "the game on screen: recording", about 10 frames a second and about 0.13 of a core; with another window over part of the game, "recording, another window over part of the game (by ...)"; over all of it, "not recording: covered", and the gaps count up. After 5 minutes it keeps 300 s, about 2.2 GB at 1366×768 (650 MB before the frames were kept losslessly), with nothing `trimmed`. Task Manager: the python running `gamelab recorder` at below-normal priority, about 2.3 GB (the ring's 2.2 and the rest, as the JPEG ring's 650 MB were a 712 MB process; not seen live yet).
- Put another window over part of the game for a few seconds, then `save-recent --seconds 30 --name check`: the folder has about 300 frames, those with the window over part of the game as they were grabbed, the window's box in their index lines (`over`, `covered`).
- During a hunt, its capture should stay DXGI (no "falls back to mss" in its log) and the feed's frames a second as before; the game's frame rate as before (`check` on a recording made with the recorder running). mss copies with CAPTUREBLT, which on some PCs makes the Windows pointer flicker as it copies: the game draws its own pointer, but look for it over the desktop.
- At the next Lie Detector, `lab/lie_detector/<time>/before/` and `lab/alarm_clips/<time>-lie-detector-...` appear about 10 s after its last sight (the cycle's end): `before/` about 4,500 frames, its `alarm_t` about 300, the frames before it showing what came up; the clip from 10 s before the alarm to that end.

## Use

From the repo root, in the `maplehelper` conda env:

```bash
python -m gamelab player --elevate
python -m gamelab calibrate
python -m gamelab combo jump_back_shot --runs 4 --chain 8
python -m gamelab stop
```

1. `player --elevate` starts the player. Approve the UAC prompt.
2. `calibrate` finds her on screen and keeps her name tag's template. Stand her on flat, textured ground, such as a girder, with nothing around. The recordings (`--record`, `do`, `combo`, `lock`) are cropped around her name tag where it is when they start, found with that template (`calibration.crop_now`): calibrate's own crop is kept while her tag is within 40 px of where it put it, and used, with a warning, only when the tag isn't found. (On 2026-10-21 the 16 runs of a sweep of `act --record` were cropped from a calibration she had walked away from, and none had her.)
3. `combo` plays the combo, here 4 runs of 8 shots in a row, and reports every jump and throw.
4. `stop` shuts the player down.

Other commands (`python -m gamelab -h` lists them all):

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `hunt look` | What she sees now: her map position, HP/MP, room to walk on her platform, her EXP number as read, the monsters in her shooting band with their platform, whether a star reaches them (or is stopped by a wall of her foothold group: "behind a wall"; by a floor, her own for one below her: "a floor in the way"; or the attack takes one first whose star is: "behind one whose star is stopped"), which way they face and the template that matched, and the drops on every platform in view (annotated `lab/hunt_look.png`: each monster's feet as a dot, with an arrow the way it faces); sends no keys |
| `hunt clear --ground 17 --kills 6` | Shoot the monsters on platform 17 (and any on hers), looting kills that fall on her platform |
| `hunt kill --near -200` | Kill one monster (the one closest to that many map units away) and loot it |
| `hunt shots` | Hits and misses of every throw logged so far, by how far above or below her the target was. `lab/shots2.jsonl` also keeps her x, the target's x, her foothold group, whether a wall of it stood in the way, every monster in front of her at the throw and at the first look after it that placed her (about when the attack picked its target, timed from the key), and the target's HP bar at every look until the throw was scored. A bar drop or a kill is a throw's only if no other throw's damage can have shown then: from 0.47 s after its key (the star's release) to 0.3 s past when it was due (with its flight), as the game may show it at either and the simulator shows it at the release. Else the throw stays undecided. `lab/shots.jsonl`, logged until 2026-10-20, made every throw in flight at a kill a hit |
| `probe list`, `probe run NAME`, `probe score` | The in-game probes of what a star hits (see Probes to run): what each settles, running one, and weighing each question's two answers on their log, `lab/probe_geometry.jsonl` (`list` and `score` send no keys) |
| `map`, `map --offline` | The map's platforms and her position on them (`lab/shots/map_<id>.png`); sends no keys |
| `nav 35`, `nav 35 --fight` | Go to platform 35; with `--fight`, shoot monsters on the way instead of avoiding them |
| `nav --walk 15 --seed 1 --map 10002073` | Movement only: random trips to the QA walk's platforms (7-33 on Tree Dungeon) for 15 minutes in one navigator (`behavior.walk`), the rolling recording saved every 270 s, then parked on 27 at x 77; the Lie Detector's or a stop's retreat ends it (Evading) |
| `nav 17 --avoid climb` | A kind of move the route takes only if nothing else gets there (each costs 20 times as much): from 23, the two rope hops instead of the climb past its end |
| `nav 3 --ways 3`, `tour --loop --ways 3` | Each trip chooses among the 3 best distinct ways to where it's going, by a softmax over their times, not only the quickest (`route.ROUTES`; off by default: in the simulator as much EXP, and fewer of her drops picked up; see Route diversity; not tried in game) |
| `tour --loop --camp --ground-tie 0.1` | Of the grounds within 10% of the best's score, the one she left longest ago goes next (`hunt.GROUND_TIE`; off by default: nothing in the simulator measures it; see Route diversity; not tried in game) |
| `tour --stops 3 --kills 5` | A hunting sweep of the map, then standing by on a safe platform |
| `tour --loop --minutes 20` | The hunt loop instead of the sweep's stops, grinding (below) by default: one decision after every look, for 20 minutes, then standing by on a safe platform |
| `tour --loop --camp` | The hunt loop hunting one ground at a time (`docs/hunt-modes.md`): the best of the value map, waiting there for its respawns and leaving by its rate; the default until 2026-10-27 |
| `tour --loop --grind` | The hunt loop going round the map in a loop of stops chosen by EXP a minute, pulled to the monsters she sees, shooting what comes into reach on the way and leaving a stop as soon as staying gives less than going on, instead of hunting one ground at a time (`behavior/grind.py`; see Grinding; the default with `--loop` since 2026-10-27, `--grind` still taken) |
| `patrol [FILE] [--map M]` | Grinding's view of a map (its stops, the loop it would take, camping's best), and with a recorded run, the next stop grinding would have taken every few seconds along it, and why; no game, no keys |
| `memory FILE --out OUT` | Her memory of the monsters run again on a recorded run (its looks' monsters and what each searched, her kills from its 'kill' events): what it held, and a copy of the run with its 'memory' records for `minimap --replay OUT`; no game, no keys |
| `tour --low-hp 0.5`, `hunt clear --low-hp 0.5` | The safety stop's threshold: her HP under it for 2 s ends the hunt, she goes to a safe place and you're paged (default 0.65, five points under her pet's warning; under 25% two looks in a row too; see No resting: the safety stop). `tour --rest-below` and `--rest-avoid` are gone, with the rests (2026-10-26). Out of darts ends a hunt the same way, by itself (exit code 5; see Out of darts) |
| `minimap` | The live mini-map, following the run in progress: a window beside the game, and the same as a web page for a phone on the same Wi-Fi; see below |
| `minimap --window-only`, `minimap --web-only` | Just one of the two (`web` is short for `minimap --web-only`) |
| `minimap --replay FILE`, `minimap --plan 36 2` | Replay a recorded run, or show the route between two platforms; no game needed |
| `sim SCENARIO --speed 4` | Run the stack offline on the simulator, recorded for the mini-map; `sim list` names the scenarios |
| `do walk left 150`, `do climb_rope 300`, `do pick_up 2`, `do stand_up` | Run one move from `maplehelper/actions.py` in the game, recorded (`do rest`, on the chair for HP, went on 2026-10-26) |
| `act right*800 alt 500 @960,540 --record` | Ad-hoc steps: `KEY` tap, `KEY*MS` hold, `KEY+`/`KEY-` press/release, `MS` wait, `@X,Y` move the mouse |
| `combo NAME --regular-attack` | A combo test, throwing with the plain attack key (no MP) |
| `track RECORDING`, `sheet RECORDING --around-her`, `check RECORDING`, `list` | Her path through a recording; a zoomed contact sheet; whether keys went out on time and the game kept a steady frame rate; saved recordings |
| `sheet FOLDER`, `sheet FOLDER --video` | A recording kept as JPEG frames (`save-recent`'s, the part before a Lie Detector, a Lie Detector's): a contact sheet of a frame a second, or an mp4 playing in real time, its gaps shown (see The rolling recording); no game |
| `lock attack 700 740 780` | Whether a jump that many ms after an attack goes through |
| `snap` | Screenshot of the game in `lab/shots/snap.png` (commands save their pictures in `lab/shots`: the lab's own screenshots are test data) |
| `spot`, `spot --image FILE` | Whether the Lie Detector is on screen now (or in a screenshot); sends no keys |
| `bench-look [FILES]`, `bench-look --live --n 100` | Each stage of a look timed (median, p90, fastest): on saved screenshots, 1920×1080 or 1366×768 (by default 17 1920×1080 ones in `lab`; `--shrink 1366x768` times them shrunk to the game's own size, `--look-scale 1` or `2` with full- or half-size looks), or on the game as it is on screen (`--capture dxgi` or `mss`: how; by default as config.toml says). Also counted: looks that didn't find her name tag near where it was, and ropes on the whole screen that the search where the map's ropes can show missed. Live it refuses unless the game is in front already, and never brings it forward; sends no keys |
| `bodies`, `bodies FILES --recordings NAMES`, `bodies --tracks FILES` | Where the monster detector puts monsters, offline: their feet against the surface of the platform each is put on, on saved screenshots where she stands (by default bench-look's), by the matched template's origin and by its bottom; and on recordings with the camera still (by default `stand_snail` and `walk_snail`), how far their x strays from frame to frame, whether they face the way they move, how often their pose (the matched template's frame) is what they do, walking or standing, by cut-outs and sprites, and how fast each kind walks. `--tracks` reads `watch`'s telemetry instead: each track's velocity against how far its x went by the next record, for those standing and those walking. No game, no keys |
| `heading FRAMES`, `heading --learn left FRAMES`, `heading --seed --fresh --learn left FRAMES` | Which way she faces on saved frames (her picture above her name tag against her pictures: see Her heading), and with `--learn`, frames whose facing you know teach her pictures (`lab/heading_1366x768.npz`; with `--seed`, the seed in `gamelab/assets` that stands in until she has her own; `--fresh` drops them first; `--tags TAGS` takes her tag where a study put it, not where a look finds it). Offline: no game, no keys |
| `bench-paste`, `bench-paste FILES --map 10004021` | A map's monsters (each kind with a colour gate) and its drops (Perception: drops of each map), the game's own pictures drawn onto frames of the game at its own 1366×768 as the game draws them (alpha blended, at known places; by default the three in `tests/fixtures/native`, every frame of each kind both ways twice), looked for there and on the same scenes stretched to 1920×1080 as the window stretched them: how many the whole screen's search found and a fight's band around each, where against where they were drawn (map units), their scores, as which frame and facing, what was found that wasn't drawn (in the scenes and on the frames as they are), and how long each search took; then re-finds: each monster found, drawn where it stood as a frame it may show next (itself, its pose's next, standing to walking or back, a flinch) and looked for again as the feed does, with the fallback to the kind's whole set and without; `--full-step-1` also searches with step 1 at full size (as before the search went coarse to fine). See Screen size. No game, no keys |
| `learn-colours FRAMES --map 10002073` | A map's background colours from saved frames of it (any window size, or folders of them), for its monsters with no hand-made colour test: kept in `assets/backgrounds/<map id>.npz`, from which the map's detector learns their gates (see Perception: learned gates); offline, no keys |
| `bench-capture --n 100` | A look's capture and a glance's timed through DXGI and through mss, on the game's window as it is on screen (or the screen's top-left 1920×1080 without the game), and whether the two see the same pixels; never brings anything forward; sends no keys |
| `perceive`, `perceive --map 10002073`, `perceive --frames DIR` | The perception service (see The perception service): the game looked at every frame at all times by one process, its latest state handed to every command and published for the mini-map (`lab/telemetry/<time>-perceive.jsonl`); waits for the game window, never sends a key nor brings the game forward; one at a time on the PC (a second says so and ends); the babysitter keeps it running, and a command starts it if none runs. `--frames`: saved frames instead of the game, offline, at a pipe of its own (commands reach it with `GAMELAB_PERCEIVE=saved`); it ends itself if its frame loop hangs 10 s, for another to be started |
| `watch`, `watch --minutes 10 --lie-detector`, `watch --heading` | What the perception service sees, on the console every 10 s: its frames a second, the monsters followed, their deaths and whose, her EXP, who's attached (a viewer of it: no keys, the game never brought forward; it starts the service if none runs); with `--lie-detector` it also checks the service's frame for the Lie Detector twice a second and pages whoever is at the PC; with `--heading` it says which way she faces off every frame |
| `nav 35`, `tour --loop`, `hunt clear`, `pet --every 1` | Every look and glance is the perception service's latest state (since 2026-10-25; `--feed`/`--no-feed` and `--sweep` are gone): the command attaches as a client (the hunting commands send keys and tell her throws, `pet` sends keys; `hunt look`, `map` and `watch` only look), and at its end says what it had of it (states, times none came in time, connections) |
| `coverage tour-game loop-game --live` | How often each move of the map's routes was planned, taken and missed in saved harness runs and the live telemetry, her time on each platform, and the moves never taken with their cost gap and why they lost; a picture of the map with them (`lab/coverage_<map>.png`); with `--ways 3`, how often trips choosing among 3 ways would have gone through each move. See Route coverage. No game, no keys |
| `respawn`, `respawn FILES` | How soon after a kill that empties a platform a monster is seen there again, how long a drop lies before it's gone without her picking it up, and how full the platforms monsters spawn on were while in view, from the live telemetry (or the files given), as survival estimates over censored observations (Kaplan-Meier: n, the median and its 95% interval, the share left at 5 s to 180 s), against the map's own spawn fields in the game data. See Respawns and drop life. No game, no keys |
| `lab-usage`, `lab-usage --prune-telemetry` | What gamelab keeps under `gamelab/lab`, by kind (recordings, the Lie Detector's recordings, `save-recent`'s, the alarms' clips, screenshots, telemetry, harness runs, golden traces, the player's inbox and outbox, the rest), and the telemetry and recordings due to go; deletes nothing, unless `--prune-telemetry`: then the telemetry a run starting now would (see Memory and disk) |
| `recorder`, `recorder --status` | The rolling recording: the game's window 10 times a second, the last 5 minutes kept in memory, saved into a Lie Detector's recording at its alarm and by `save-recent` (see The rolling recording); `--status` says how the running one is doing. Reads the screen only, keeps nothing of another window, sends no keys; the babysitter keeps it running |
| `save-recent`, `save-recent --seconds 60 --name popup` | The running recorder's last 5 minutes (or 60 s) saved to `lab/recent/<time>[-name]/`; prints the folder |
| `clear-alarm` | After you've answered a Lie Detector yourself and it has been off the screen for a minute: lets gamelab run again (refused while its recording is still going, exit code 3); a running player then stops, and `player --elevate` starts it again |
| `pet`, `pet --every 1`, `pet --read` | Her pet kept fed (`behavior/pet.py`): its fullness read once off her Character Info (a double-click on her, then Esc) and followed in time, a Pet Food when it's low; `--every 1` follows it every minute until stopped, counting only time the game is there; `--read` reads it now. With the Lie Detector alarm up it goes on: foods by the fullness followed (the player takes them then, 3 a minute at most), no read until the alarm is cleared (On the Lie Detector). With `--every`, while the client is another size or the game draws off it, it waits, sending nothing (Behavior: Her pet) |
| `keys --read`, `keys --read --record`, `keys --frame FILES` | The game's KEY BINDINGS window read (`perception/keybindings.py`): which key Attack, her regular attack, is on against config.toml's, the preset in use, what every key does. `--read` opens it with the backslash (the mouse moved off it first), reads it, closes it with Esc only once it's seen open (with nothing open Esc opens the game's MENU), and again only once it's seen still open, as the hunt's check does after a doubt (a client not at 1366x768: nothing sent; a window not read: why, and nothing of where Attack is); `--record` records its opening and closing at 15 frames a second into `lab/shots/keybindings-<time>/` with a report; `--frame` reads saved 1366x768 frames and sends nothing. A window read live has her keys followed to where it shows them and remembered for her next runs (`lab/keybindings-<her>.json`, her moves' and pet food's in `lab/alarm_keys.json` for the player); `keys` alone says which keys are in use, `keys --forget` drops the remembered ones (config.toml's [keys] from the next start). Nothing else is sent; with the Lie Detector alarm up, nothing (see The regular attack's key checked, Her keys followed) |
| `stats`, `stats --frame FILE`, `stats --read [--record] [--no-click] [--anywhere]`, `stats --calibrate FRAME [--before FRAME] [--box X0,Y0,X1,Y1 ...]` | Her stats as perception has them (`behavior/bootstrap.py`): her DEF (her stat window's W.DEF if read, else fitted to her kept touches, `lab/touches.jsonl`), her max HP and level as last read (a hunt reads them again from her HUD: these aren't used for it), the DEF her kept touches fit now, the stat window's calibration and its other values as kept; `--frame` reads her W.DEF off a saved 1366x768 frame with her stat window's DETAIL open (`perception/stat_window.py`) and keeps it in `lab/her_stats.json` (offline). Live (the player running): `--read` opens it as a hunt's start does (her stats key, a click on DETAIL, her stats key or Esc: nothing that attacks or moves her; the reader calibrated first), `--read --record` the calibrating capture (recorded into `lab/shots/statwindow-<time>`, writes `lab/stat_window.json`); `--calibrate` sets the reader up from a saved live frame (offline). (Her stat window read) |

**On another map** every command that reads the map takes `--map` (by default the first, Thicket Around the Beach II, 10000012): West Rocky Mountain II is `--map 10004021`, Tree Dungeon, Forest Up North II `--map 10002073` (`hunt look --map 10002073`, `nav 8 --x 137 --map 10002073`, `tour --loop --minutes 10 --map 10002073`, `watch --map 10002073`). Offline, the simulator's scenarios carry their map (`sim nav_tree_bottom_to_top --speed 4`, `sim loop_rocky_bridge`), and the harness and the coverage report take `--map` (Offline: the simulator; In game, on each map, for what's known and what to check there first).

`hunt kill`, `hunt clear`, `nav`, `tour` and `probe run` bring the game to the front before their first look and wait up to 3 s for it to come (`__main__.FRONT_WAIT_S`); with `hunt look` and `map`, a game minimized is restored and brought forward first, before its window's size is taken (`_game_geometry`): the player refuses every plan while another window is in front, and a look captures whatever is. Windows doesn't always let a program bring another window forward; then the command says which window is in front and stops before it looks or sends anything: click on the game and run it again. (On 2026-10-21 at 01:01:30 a tour's first looks captured the Claude window for 2.5 s and its first plan was refused, "game not in front"; `window.bring_to_front` had been called and quietly done nothing. It now also switches to the game as Alt+Tab does if it hasn't come half way through the wait: `window.SWITCH_FALLBACK`, not tried in game yet.)

## The mini-map

`python -m gamelab minimap` opens a window that draws the map from the game data, and on it what the stack sees and plans, as it happens (it also serves the same as a web page for a phone: see "On a phone" below):

- **Localization:** her position (yellow; a magenta ring when placed from the minimap dot because her name tag is hidden) with the way she faces and her trail, HP and MP, and how her position was worked out (rope, edge or dot).
- **Perception:** the monsters in the last look (its band, and what perception follows off it: `Scene.swept`; until 2026-10-25 a slice of the sweep), coloured by kind, with their HP bars once hit; the monsters she remembers (rings of their kind's colour where each was seen last, fading over 20 s, broken once looks covering their place have missed them; a red cross where one was killed, a dim one where one was forgotten: Her memory of the monsters); the drops seen on the ground (yellow), and those remembered for later (hollow squares); other players where their minimap dots put them (dots ringed dark, in their markers' colours: anyone red, her party orange, a guild lavender, a buddy cyan), and how many there are under the map.
- **Prediction:** where each monster can be in the next second, as the move planner sees it (red bars).
- **Motion planning:** the planned route (cyan: arcs for jumps, arrows for climbs and drops) and the chain of moves in the running key plan (magenta: where she runs, and where each move lands).
- **Attack:** where a star reaches from her (the band either side, brighter on the side she faces, cut short at a wall of her foothold group whose outer face looks at her), the monsters the last throw aimed at (red rings), and the fight's last decision.
- **The tour:** its stops in order, the current one, the spot she shoots it from, the safe platforms (teal) and the hunting grounds (bright green). Below the map, the latest log lines.
- **The hunt loop** (`tour --loop`): the grounds visited, the current one and its spot; under the map, the rule that decided the last step, the objective, her EXP rate on this ground and the rate to beat elsewhere; on it, the piles in its drop store (hers bright, others' dim, expected ones small, urgent ones red).

**On a phone:** `minimap` also serves the same picture as a web page, for a phone on the same Wi-Fi, from the same process (no administrator rights; closing the window stops it too). `--window-only` starts just the window, and `--web-only` (or `python -m gamelab web`) just the page. If the page's port is taken, the window still opens (`--port` picks another). It prints two addresses: one for this computer, and one for the phone (opened on the computer, the page also shows a QR code of it). Each address ends in a key that changes every time, so nobody else on the network can watch; `--key WORD` keeps it the same, so a bookmark keeps working. The page shows the map, either the part around her (the default on a phone) or the whole of it, with HP and MP, the hunt loop's rule, objective and rates, the fight, the moves, her position and the latest log lines, as they happen. A replay (`--replay FILE`) gets buttons to pause, change the speed and jump 10 s (the page and the window each play it with their own controls). The first time, Windows may ask whether Python may accept connections: allow it on private networks. `--host 127.0.0.1` serves this computer only. Like the window, it only reads the telemetry: it sends no keys and never touches the game.

The server pushes the run's records to the page as they're written (Server-Sent Events, standard library only), and the page draws the map itself on a canvas, layer for layer as the window does, with the window's colours, reach and map (`/map.json`, from `render.py`). Her position is drawn 100 ms behind the run's clock, gliding between her positions (they come every 67 ms while she moves; ones more than 0.6 s apart aren't glided between), and the page follows a replay's pause and speed. It used to fetch the text every 400 ms and then a 40 KB picture of the map: 1.6 pictures a second, 280 ms old on average and up to 540 ms on this computer, showing 43% of her positions, for 45-70 KB/s. Measured offline on 2026-10-20 with the same live tour written again at its own pace (45 s, on 127.0.0.1):

- Every one of her 174 positions reached a client reading the stream (a Python script, on the same computer), 22-23 ms after it was written on average (p99 39-41 ms, at most 39-50; three runs).
- 2.0 KB/s, plus a snapshot of 3-10 KB when a page connects and the map (6 KB) once.
- The whole process (the server, the script writing the run again and the clients reading it) used 0.1-0.2% of a core, and 0.2-0.4% with three clients.
- In the desktop app's browser (Chromium, 3 device px per CSS px), the page drew at 60 frames a second, 0.2 ms a frame (p90 0.3 ms, at most 0.6), and only when something moved. Following the same run there for 60 s, the records reached the page 20 ms after they were written (p90 37 ms, at most 46, by the browser's own clock, which is this computer's), and its `?debug=1` corner said 22 ms (p90 37, at most 47).
- After the server was stopped and started again under an open page, the page had the new server's snapshot within a second of it starting.

A phone that was locked, or had the page in the background, catches up by itself. iOS Safari can leave a stream open but dead after the screen was locked, so the server pings every 5 s, and the page opens the stream again when nothing came for 12.5 s, or when it's shown again after more than 6 s of quiet; every connection starts with a full snapshot. Past 16 open streams the oldest ends (a phone gone from the Wi-Fi leaves one open until a write to it fails), and its page says so and waits to be shown again or reloaded, rather than come back and end the next oldest. Add `&debug=1` to the address for a corner with the frame rate, the drawing time, messages and KB a second, reconnects, how late the records come (p50 and p90 over the last 5 s; Wi-Fi adds about half the round trip shown next to it), and how long ago the newest record was written. That last isn't a delay: between moves she's looked at only a few times a second, so in five recorded live tours the newest record was over 250 ms old 30-58% of the time, with no network at all. Her position is drawn another 100 ms behind, to glide. `&delay=0` draws her where she was last seen instead of gliding. `/frame.jpg` (the map as a JPEG, `?view=her` around her) and `/state.json` (the text) are still served for a quick look, but the page doesn't use them. WebRTC was left out: the server would need aiortc and FFmpeg's libraries, for a stream of 2 KB/s on a home network. Not tried on an iPhone yet.

Hunting commands (`hunt clear`/`kill`, `nav`, `tour`) record what they see and plan to `lab/telemetry/<time>-<command>.jsonl` (`gamelab/telemetry.py`). The window follows the newest of those files, so it can be opened before or during a run. A run past 64 MB goes on in a new part, `<time>-<command>-part2.jsonl` and so on, which starts with the run's session record marked as the continuation of the part before (see Memory and disk); the window goes on into it. Live, the window never takes focus from the game: the player only presses keys while the game is in front, and screen captures see whatever is on top. So it goes beside the game window when the screen has room, and clicks on it don't activate it. A replay (`--replay FILE`, also last night's `lab/sweep_track.json`) is an ordinary window: space pauses, + and - change the speed, and the arrow keys jump 10 s.

## Offline: the simulator and golden traces

`gamelab/sim` is a small game that the whole stack runs against, with no game and no key player. `FakeEyes` answers perception's questions from a simulated world (monsters with where their feet are, which way they face and whether they walk, stand or flinch, as the templates tell; her EXP number drawn with the game's glyphs, for the stack to read), and `FakePlayer` runs key plans on it on a fake clock. Her body moves as the engine moves her (`motion/body.py`, below, which the planner's constants come from): the game sees each key a measured lag after it goes out, an arrow speeds her up and letting go brakes her, a jump gets the kick, the opposite arrow brakes her in the air, and an attack stops her landing; she climbs as measured. Monsters walk their platforms as fast as the game data says (see Localization), touch her (what a touch takes, and how often she evades it, by the monster's kind: below), are pushed back by hits, die from stars, give EXP and drop loot. An attack picks its target when it starts, about 65 ms after its key, from where she is then (as in game; see Attack): on the ground the claw stabs the nearest monster whose body its stance's box reaches, else the star goes to a monster the star's search picks, band by band; from a jump, to the nearest whose body reaches into the attack's area (with `world.AIR_PICK = 'v83'`, as from the ground, from where she is then; from 2026-10-27 by the star's search alone, `AIR_PICK` 'search', with the noise fitted to the live jump throws: Clearance and slopes). Each picks by the bodies, whatever the terrain; then the line to a star's pick alone is checked, and stopped, the attack hits nothing (Attack: what stops a star). The bodies are as tall as the game data has them walking (taller for 0.6 s after a hit, while they flinch). So her jump-throws go over snails as they do in game, and from the ground a star goes over a monster right under her. 86 scenarios cover navigation (every kind of move, a rope jumped at past a platform's end, two rope hops, the basin's right side up, off a rope with nothing at its top, monsters in the way, fighting on the way, cut-off plans, a walk-off and a jump onto 14 right after a kill in a world that swallows arrows pressed too soon after an attack, a climb then a step back and two jumps with the lags spread, two time-outs pinned), single moves, fights (a snail cornering her on a short platform too, a step wall between her and the monsters), kills, mop-ups, a full inventory, tours and rests (with and without the fighting escort), the hunt loop (`loop_*`: the basin, a spot off the ground, leaving an empty ground, lull loot, a rest, 8 minutes end to end, the game's errors, another player, finishing what she hurt, shooting 21 from 22, a valuable drop at once, a pile on the way), the in-game probes (`probe_*`: the window's top from 13, the step wall from 4 from the ground and jumping back, jump throws at a snail), and the continuous feed (`feed_*`: twins of five of those with her looks from a feed; see Continuous perception).

**On the other maps** (from 2026-10-24). A scenario says which map it's on (`Scenario.map_id`), and the simulator plays her as she is there (`scenarios.HER`): on the first map at level 19 (HP 642, her potions on a key), as its 86 golden traces were recorded (its scenarios and traces gone since 2026-10-31; the harness still runs there); on West Rocky Mountain II at level 23 (HP 730) and on Tree Dungeon, Forest Up North II at level 25 (HP 774, MP 623, her stars as the HP bars read them: `world.LEVEL_25`, level 24's HP 752 until 2026-10-26), with her keys from 2026-10-23 and her pet drinking her potions. On those two a touch takes HP by meowdb's formula at DEF 75 (`world.Her.defence`; a share of PADamage on the first map, as fitted), a kind the first map hasn't takes as many stars as its HP and defence need (`world.hits_of`), and a hit pushes a monster back only from its `pushed` damage in the game data (`world.PUSH_BY_DAMAGE`; any damage pushes the first map's four). What isn't known of the game there the world runs either way (`world.Realism`: `sides`, the map's platforms' ends or HeavenClient's 25 units in from its footholds; `zero_walls`, the walls of foothold group 0 stopping her whatever her group; `rope_reach`, 95 or HeavenClient's 82), and other players can camp (`Realism.camps`: each kills the monsters of its kinds on the platforms it hunts soon after they show). Up held at a portal ends the run (`world.SimLeftMap`), as a fall out of the map does: on the ground or in the air, from 100 above it to 25 below and 25 either side, as HeavenClient takes one (`mapdata.PORTAL_BOX`; whether the game takes one in the air isn't known). The fake eyes keep a camera that can't move across a map narrower than the view, and on a map whose minimap picture is taller than its window show other players' dots only in the rows the window scrolls to. Since 2026-10-31 all 42 scenarios are on Tree Dungeon (`*_tree_*`; In game, on Tree Dungeon): the first map's 75 and West Rocky Mountain II's 15 went with those maps' tests, the bot playing only Tree Dungeon.

**Its monsters** (`sim/world.py`) are as the game data has them where it has them (`Mob/<id>.img`, cached in `gamedata/data/out/mobs`; without it, the flat values from before):
- **A touch takes HP by the monster's touch damage:** 0.68 of its PADamage (snail 3, slime 13, pig 15, Orange Mushroom 17) of her 642 HP (her HP bar), give or take 70%. That is 1.6% on average for a pig, 1.4% for a slime, 1.8% for an Orange Mushroom and 0.3% for a snail, where every touch took 1.4%. It's fitted to `lab/hits.jsonl`: 100 hits on the grounds where only pigs and slimes spawn (the basin and 21) took 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 px of the 147 px bar 30, 32, 28, 9 and 1 times (2.19 px, 9.6 HP, on average), and the fit has 26, 33, 30, 9 and 0 (and 2 too small to show). How the game takes her defence off isn't known, and no touch by a snail or an Orange Mushroom alone was logged.
- **She evades a touch with a chance inversely proportional to the monster's accuracy** (acc: snail 33, slime 53, pig 54, Orange Mushroom 62; the form MapleStory's dodge rule is usually given in, unmeasured), fitted to the 13 touches logged hopping over pigs (7 MISS): a pig's half the time, a slime's 51%, an Orange Mushroom's 44%, a snail's 82%, where every kind's was half. In the harness she evades 50.5% (loop) and 52.5% (tour) of all touches.
- **A monster touches her by the box of the frame it shows** (its lt/rb in the game data: none of this map's monsters has an attack of its own, so the client hurts by the body), walking, standing, or flinching for 0.6 s after a hit (its hit1 frame), turned the way it faces. Before, every monster was its kind's half width either side and as tall as its first walking frame. A walking slime is in the air for 400 of its 1,050 ms, 10-17 units up and up to 66 tall (40-44 on the ground), so a hop over it has to clear that; a walking pig is 4 units up and 47 tall for 300 of its 500 ms; an Orange Mushroom reaches 36 behind it and 27 in front standing, and 67 tall for 120 ms of its walk. An attack still picks its target by the old bodies (`World.top`: each kind as tall as it walks, as the decisions' `reach.body_of` has it): by its frames a pig standing 60 below her (38-40 tall) would be picked from the ground only from 171 units sideways, not 151, and by a jump's area (its floor 19 below her feet, `reach.AREA_DOWN`) not at all, where in game pigs 60 below were hit (see Found offline).

Unhurt, a monster walks its own way, wherever she is. Her hit (a star's or a swipe's landing, killing it or not) starts its chase for 3-4 minutes (`AGGRO_S`: the v83 client's `Mob::chase`, `targettime = 180000 + rand(60000)` ms, in HeavenClient's rewrite of it from the client's code), and each hit of hers starts it anew, its way decided again at her (`Mob::chase`). Chasing, it decides every 0.72-1.17 s (`CHASE_THINK_MS`, the client's think timer: 8-13 of its 90 ms AI steps) which way to walk: at her, or on the way it chose while she's within 100 across (`AGGRO_PASS`), so it walks on past her 100 units and up to a decision's walk more before turning back, and where its platform's end turned it by her, back to that end (`Mob::think` keeps the way it chose; until 2026-10-31 it went on the way the end sent it); it never stands, walks at its walk speed (`info/chaseSpeed` only counts for a kind with a chase animation, and none of Tree Dungeon's or the first map's kinds has one, nor `info/firstAttack`, a chase on sight), along its own platform at her x wherever she is (turning at its ends, as its walks do), after a hit's flinch first; dead, she's chased no more. Back after its death, it walks its own way.
