- `python -m gamelab sim tour_tree_run --speed 4` runs a scenario and records it for the mini-map: open `python -m gamelab minimap` first to watch it as it happens.
- `python -m gamelab.analysis.physics_check` replays her recorded movement (18 recordings, or the 6 kept as test fixtures) through the physics models and prints how far each is off (see Motion planning).
- `python -m gamelab.sim.golden check` reruns every scenario and compares it with the golden trace recorded earlier: every key plan, log line and result. A refactor that leaves those byte-identical hasn't changed what she does. `record` rewrites the traces (after an intended change). Both take `--jobs N`, the scenarios on a pool of N processes, the same traces and output (Checking a change). The traces hold map data, so they stay in `lab/golden` (git-ignored): a branch worked on in a worktree of its own re-records them in its own `lab`, so once it's merged, `record` is run in the main checkout too (with the feed's searches off the frame loop, the route track and the other players together, 32 of master's 86: the other players' and her EXP number's 27 and the five `feed_*`; Found offline).

**Set-ups, not lucky seeds** (from 2026-10-31). A scenario whose checks are her reaction to an event sets the event up, rather than keeping a seed that happens to bring it, so that a change to the world's draws (the chase, the server's respawn: every run re-rolled) can't take the event away: the map's monsters of a kind hurt at the start (`Realism.hurt`, ((kind, share), ...): their bars up, back whole once killed; a Green Mushroom to finish with the regular attack, for her attack key's doubt: `loop_tree_grind_attack_key` and its three twins), her start where the event comes (the Lie Detector seen 2 s after she starts on the floor, or just under 28), or the monsters on the platforms that make it certain (her runs right with no monster near: monsters up the tower only). Each such scenario's docstring says how, and on how many of seeds 1-13 it meets its checks; it meets them on its own seed with the chase off and on the old respawn clock too. Every Tree Dungeon scenario classified (an event, an outcome, a set-piece), with the proposal for the outcomes (a pass rate over seeds against master's, as `ab` does): D:/MapleHelper-scratch/sim-setups/classification.md.

The move into the layers above was checked this way: all 50 traces stayed identical, apart from two counters that were never read (`Report.out_of_reach`, `Hunter.skipped`), which were removed.

**Comparing policies** (`python -m gamelab.sim.harness`): `run POLICY` hunts 20 simulated minutes on each of 10 world seeds (`tour`, `loop`, or `loop-grind`; `loop-avoid` until 2026-10-26), and `compare BASE CAND` applies the bar seed by seed: more EXP a minute on 8 of 10 seeds and none more than 10% worse, at least the drops share, no more HP lost, no death, no fall out of the map, no stop (the safety stop, out of darts: from 2026-10-26 a run a stop ended counts as a death does, and its time ends with her retreat after it: `alive_s`, the idle stretches). What a run gave is read from the simulated world, not from her own reports. Preset `game` adds the game's errors (27.5% of stars miss, hit monsters hidden for 1-3 s, 10% of looks miss a monster, her lags spread as measured, 60% of taps of 50 ms or less lost), arrows pressed while an attack plays swallowed as in game (`Realism.lock_arrows`: pressed less than 0.72 s after the key, seen only 0.77 s after it if still held, else never; the noisy scenarios have it too), 60% of spawns filled, another player killing a monster every 25 s (hunting one place at a time, its dot on the minimap: see Other players), and 60 potions (not monsters' poses read wrong, `Noise.pose_wrong`, which no preset has yet); `game-drops` has the drops seen in game, `game-air` jump throws missing a snail close by as often as in game (`Noise.air_snail`), `game-sparse` 15% of the spawns filled (the coverage test's world: Route coverage), each `game` otherwise, the arrows swallowed too; `plain` is the simulator's own crowded world; `--think 1` also charges the stack's real computing time to the clock (those runs aren't repeatable). `--costs measured` makes the simulator's looks as fast as they're measured after the profiling pass of Where the time goes (a look placing her 20 ms with its frame's wait and copy, her band 24 more, the whole screen 84, a strip of drops 8; as step 5 measured them, 24, 32, 122 and 8), not the 100 ms they were coded at; `--feed` takes her looks and glances from a continuous feed; `--ways 3` has her trips choose among 3 ways (Route diversity). (`rests`, comparing trips to rest at low HP with and without `--rest-avoid`, went with the rests on 2026-10-26.) Each run also counts her trips from the stack's log (`nav`: plans cut short by a hit and off the path, replans, misses and the falls among them, her glances), and `compare` shows their totals. Runs are saved in `lab/harness` (git-ignored), each with a tally of her moves for the coverage report (3-7 KB a run).

On the new maps: `--map 10004021` (West Rocky Mountain II) and `--map 10002073` (Tree Dungeon, Forest Up North II) hunt there with her as she is there, from their own starting places, saved as `POLICY-PRESET-MAP`; `compare` refuses runs of two maps. `--world NAME` (again for another) switches on what isn't known: `zero-walls`, `client-sides`, `client-reach`, `touch-share` (a touch a share of PADamage, not the formula), `no-evade`, `red-potion` (her potions heal a Red Potion's 100 HP, not 30% of her HP), `client-body` (her body for the world's touches the client's, 22 either side and 65 tall as the stack plans by, `motion/bodies.py`, not the simulator's 15 x 55), `near-misses` (the detector's misses as live on 2026-10-25, `world.NEAR_SEEN` on her platform by how near her, `OFF_SEEN` off it: Cutting her touches), `spawn-fade` and `spawn-fade-wide` (a monster back at its spawn point fading in, found as late as live finds it with the spawn watch or as the whole screen alone did: `world.SPAWN_FOUND`, `SPAWN_FOUND_WIDE`; Spawns seen as they fade in), and how she plays: `lucky-seven` (her attacks as Lucky Seven's thrown live, `tour --loop --skill`: 3 of the simulator's stars a cast, `world.LUCKY_SEVEN`, so a Horny Mushroom dies in about 4 throws and a Green in 3, as live, not 12 and 7), saved as suffixes. Each run also keeps the seconds she was hunting (`alive_s`: rates a minute alive, where a death would drag a rate over the horizon down), the touches by a monster just back at its spawn point (`fresh_hurt`: within `world.FRESH_S`, 1.5 s, of its respawn) the time the hunt loop waited for respawns and the HP lost then (`wait_s`, `wait_hp_lost`: its rules 'wait' and 'lull loot'), and the time she was on the move and the touches that hurt and HP lost then (`trip_s`, `trip_hurt`, `trip_hp_lost`: a chain's or a lone move's start to its end), and from 2026-10-26 on her stays for drops (`pile_s`, `pile_hurt`, `pile_hp_lost`), off her trips (`stand_hurt`, `stand_hp_lost`), her knocks off a platform (`knock_falls`, `knock_fall_dy`), her pet's potions (`pet_potions`; her MP items `mp_potions`) and her Lucky Seven casts whose stars hit nothing (`casts_nothing`). `--grounds 23` (saved as `-g23`) has the policy hunt only those grounds, as the live hunt loop of 2026-10-24 hunted 23 alone. Presets `crowd`, `crowd-17` and `crowd-slow` are Tree Dungeon's alone: the other players the crowding study saw, camping (`harness.TREE_CAMPS`), every spawn filled, respawns at 8.8 s, 17 s (the live median on 23) or 30 s, other players' dots under hers unseen. `ropes` counts the hunt loop's waits on a rope. The policy `loop-hp50` (the hunt loop resting under half her HP) went with the rests on 2026-10-26. A run that goes through a portal keeps `left_map_at` and fails the bar as a fall does. The coverage report reads either map's runs (`coverage RUN --map M`; the first map's own questions, platform 12 and the rope hops, only there).

**Master's side once** (from 2026-10-28): `run ... --cache` keeps a commit's seeds and reads them after, `cached ... --sha master` reads master's without running anything, `ab` runs a candidate against them (12 seeds, more only while a headline difference isn't told from nothing), `spot` runs a saved run's seed or two again: Checking a change.

**Soak runs** (`python -m gamelab.sim.soak`): the stack kept going for minutes on saved frames or in the simulator, to see whether its memory grows (see Memory and disk).

**The stack's own computing** (`python -m gamelab.sim.latency loop|tour [--seeds 5] [--minutes 10] [--profile FILE]`): the harness's hunts, with every stretch of the stack's computing between two of its calls to the game (a look, a key plan, a sleep) timed with the real clock, by the call that ended it, and not charged to the fake clock, so the runs are the harness's own. What a look's answer waits for before her next keys go out is the "before a key plan" row; in game it comes on top of the look itself (see Where the time goes).

Tests can't press keys, page anyone or write under `gamelab/lab` (`tests/conftest.py` stops them), and the simulator refuses to run unless its fakes are in place. The tests, the golden traces, the harness and the simulator's latency and soak runs take her stats as measured (SPEED 119.2, JUMP 100), not as `config.toml` `[character]` has them (`physics.FIXED_STATS`), so editing those for her gear changes nothing they check: with SPEED 125 in the file, 16 tests failed and every golden trace changed.

## Checking a change: the goldens on a pool, master's baseline cached, `ab` and spot checks (from 2026-10-28)

The user, 2026-10-28, on workflows that run long (measured from the agents' transcripts, 60-70% of their agent-hours went to waiting on harness tables, replays and benches, tests and goldens, and every stage ran master's side of its comparisons again): "Smaller simulator tables first; Reviewers spot-check instead of re-running everything; Run the goldens in parallel; Reuse master's baseline numbers". All of it is offline, and every job still starts through `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/cpu/hunt/bg_quiet.cmd`, one job of 2 workers while the user plays.

**The order to check a change in.**
1. Targeted tests while working, the fast suite before a commit.
2. The goldens of the map worked on, on a pool: `python -m gamelab.sim.golden check NAMES --jobs 2` (4 with the game down). Tree Dungeon's 30: 411 s in one process, 265 s on 2, 135 s on 4, the same output to the byte each (30 of 30 match; the PC busy beside them, CPUs 12-23 at Idle); at the review, 607 s in one process and 152 s on 4, the same to the byte, and after the rebase onto master 4558f61 its 34 (the regular attack's key check's four with them) 153 s on 4, 34 of 34 match.
3. The smallest harness table that answers the question, against master's cached baseline, master's side never run again: `python -m gamelab.sim.harness ab loop --map 10002073 --preset crowd --attack choice --costs measured --world zero-walls --world near-misses --world walkers --minutes 5 --jobs 2 [--metric close_s]` (and `loop-grind`): 12 seeds of 5 minutes; 24, then 48, only while a headline difference isn't told from nothing.
4. A perception change for her: her recordings replayed through the branch and scored against their labels beside master's cached dumps, `python -m gamelab.sim.replay run --out RUN` then `score --dumps RUN --base master` (Replaying the recordings).
5. A review reads the author's saved runs and `ab`'s report and spot-checks them: `python -m gamelab.sim.harness spot NAME --seeds 3,9` runs two of the author's seeds again (each the same to the digit, or the keys that differ), `cached ... --sha master` shows master's table without running anything. A whole table again only where a spot check fails.

**The goldens on a pool** (`golden check|record [names] --jobs N [--folder DIR]`; `golden.ran`, `run_one`, `_ready`, `_run_in_worker`). Each scenario runs on a `ProcessPoolExecutor` worker made ready as the command makes itself (the environment it restarted itself with, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and her stats fixed, inherited; the scenarios imported and every map they're on loaded), exactly as in one process, and its trace comes back as the JSON `record` writes. The longest go first, by their recorded traces' size; each is given back in the order the names were given as soon as it and those before it are done, so what's printed is in that order (what a worker's run prints is printed in its place), the exit codes are as before, and `check`'s output is the same to the byte whatever N. Default 1: in the command's own process, as it always was. `--folder DIR` writes (record) or reads (check) the traces there instead of `lab/golden`. Proof (master 0e14114 with only this change, a frozen copy: `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/fastchecks/golden`, gproof.sh): all 105 recorded scenarios (Tree Dungeon's 30, the first map's 75), `check` with 1, 2 and 4 processes gave the same output to the byte (30 match; the first map's 75 differ, as on master, where they aren't checked: recorded before the feed), and `record` into three scratch folders with 1, 2 and 4 the 105 traces the same to the byte (Tree's 30 also the same as `lab/golden`'s). Times for the 105, with other workflows' jobs on the same CPUs (12-23, Idle): `check` 1,065 s in one process, 433 s on 2, 232 s on 4; `record` 1,204, 538, 215 s.

**The baseline cache** (`gamelab/sim/baseline.py`; the harness's `run ... --cache`, `cached`, `compare` on a cache's folder). The results, a seed a file (the dict `run_one` gives), go under `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/baselines/harness/<code>/<key>/seed-NNN.json` (`GAMELAB_BASELINES` moves it), with `meta.json` beside them saying what the key covers and which commit ran them first. Only deterministic results are kept: a run with `--think` or `--think-clock` (this computer's computing charged to the clock) isn't cached. *The code* (`code_id`) is a commit's: a SHA-1 of its tree under `gamelab/`, `gamedata/`, `maplehelper/` and `config.toml` (each file's mode, blob and path, the Markdown aside), so commits that change only tests or READMEs share a baseline (master went 0e14114 -> 98f9181 while this was built, the capture's test and README alone: its baseline is 0e14114's, read at once). Only while the checkout's code is as committed (`git status` there: no change staged or not, no untracked file; files git ignores, such as `lab`, `build` and `gamedata/data`, aside); a checkout with changes runs everything and keeps nothing (`cache: not used: ...`). A hash of the working tree would be as safe, but a checkout being worked on changes with every edit, so it would keep runs nobody reads again; what's asked for again is a commit's ("master"). *The key* covers every argument of `run_one` but the seed (bound with its defaults: policy, preset, minutes, think, costs, ways, map, the worlds in their order, grounds and attack always; an argument a later commit adds only off its default, so a new switch left off keeps the keys before it and still pairs a base with a candidate), the game data's stamp (every file under `gamedata/data` by path, size and mtime: it isn't in git), Python's version and the installed packages' a run imports (numpy, OpenCV, Pillow, mss: `baseline.PACKAGES`, each distribution that could give the module, so both of the OpenCV wheels this env has; `tests/test_baseline.py` fails if a run of the standard command or of the first map imports any other), the `GAMELAB_*` environment as it resolves (`gamelab_env`: the character played and whether her stats are fixed, `character.active_id`; the GPU mode, `native.gpu_mode`, from `GAMELAB_GPU` or the checkout's `lab/GPU`; any other `GAMELAB_*` variable as set, none of which changes a run today, kept to be safe; `GAMELAB_BASELINES` and `GAMELAB_BASE_FILL`, where the cache is and who fills it, aside: `GAMELAB_CHARACTER` unset or `thief`, `GAMELAB_GPU` unset or `0`, are one key) and the scheme's `FORMAT` (2 from the review: 1 had numpy's version alone and the `GAMELAB_*` variables as set, so `GAMELAB_BASE_FILL` or `GAMELAB_GPU=0` split the cache and `GAMELAB_CHARACTER=thief` failed `ab`, and an OpenCV or Pillow upgrade went unseen). The DLLs' compiler isn't in it: they're built `/fp:precise` to give Python's answers to the bit (`native.FLAGS`), which their tests check. A seed is kept as it ends (its file renamed into place whole), and only if the checkout is still as committed then, so a run cut short keeps what it finished. `run ... --cache` reads the seeds the code has and runs only the others; `cached POLICY [options] --sha master` reads them without running anything, as a table, saved as a run (`NAME@sha7`) for `compare`, which also takes a cache's folder or a `.json` file. Not for: timing benches (`sim.latency`, `bench-look`, `bench-capture`, the service's frame rates, `--think`: what they measure is the computer), and a checkout with changes.

Proof (the two standard commands below; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/fastchecks/harness`: hproof.sh, same.py). For both: master's 12-seed fill and the same command again, every seed read from the cache, saved the same run to the byte; master run without the cache in one process (no pool) on seeds 1-3, each the same to the byte as the cache's file (written by a pool of 2); the branch as committed with `--cache`, run and then read, the same to the byte, and its seeds 1-3 the same as master's files to the byte, under the same key from both checkouts (e2390ed2bff7ff71, fc999d4c91260fee); `spot` of master's saved grinding seeds 5 and 12 with the branch: the same to the digit. A 12-seed table without the cache took 178 s (the hunt loop) and 245 s (grinding) on 2 workers, with it 2 s each.

**The base checkout** (`D:/MapleHelper/.claude/worktrees/ov-base`: a detached HEAD at master, set up as `ov-search` is: `gamedata/data/copy` and `out` junctioned to the main checkout's, its own `lab` with the main lab's top-level files, `golden/`, `heading/` and `shots/` copied, the DLLs built; never edited, never deleted: its junctions lead into `D:/MapleHelper/gamedata`). `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/baselines/base.py [--ref master] -- run POLICY [options] --seeds N --jobs J` moves it to master's latest (or `--ref`'s commit: `git checkout --detach`), builds the DLLs again if their sources changed (`native.build`, a no-op otherwise), and runs the command line there with the cache. It holds a lock while it does (`baselines/ov-base.lock`, let go by the OS when it ends), so a second fill waits rather than move the checkout under the first's runs, and it refuses a checkout that isn't as committed. Until this branch is on master, master's harness has no `--cache`: `base.py` runs master's own `harness.main` (its parser, table and save, its `run_one` on its own pool) with its `run_many` through the cache's code (`baselines/lib/baseline.py`, a copy of this branch's `baseline.py`: the same keys). Once master has `--cache`, it runs `python -m gamelab.sim.harness ... --cache` there instead.

**`ab`** (`python -m gamelab.sim.harness ab POLICY [run's options] [--base master] [--metric KEY ...] [--seeds 12] [--max-seeds 48] [--jobs N] [--fill FILE]`; `difference`, `ab_next`, `HEADLINE`). This checkout (the candidate) against the base commit's cached seeds, paired seed by seed: 12 seeds; 24, then 48, only while a headline difference is within 2 standard errors of the paired differences and not zero, or has too few seeds to tell. 'Zero' is every seed the same to the digit (its value, or its having none), not a mean difference of 0: a death moved from seed 7 to seed 3, +4 touches on one seed and -4 on another, or +30 EXP a minute and -30, is 'within 2 se' and takes more seeds (until the review, a zero mean read 'zero' and stopped `ab` at 12 seeds); under 2 seeds with a value on both sides (`mp_per_kill` with one kill each) is 'too few', which takes more seeds too and is said as unsettled if `ab` stops at the most. A `--metric` that no seed's result has on either side (the whole dotted path: `landings.trip.neer`, `hurts`) is refused after the first seeds, exit 2, with the names nearest it, rather than read as a zero; one only the candidate's results have (a metric the change adds) is taken, its base's 0 where it's a nested count. The headline metrics are EXP a minute, touches, deaths, falls out of the map or through a portal, stops, and each `--metric` (a result's key, dotted for nested ones: `nav.misses`, `landings.trip.near`). Each step prints its table (base, candidate, the mean difference, as a share, its se, t, and 'zero', 'too few', 'beyond 2 se' or 'within 2 se'), then the seeds it takes next and why, or why it stopped; then the bar (`compare`), shown only, and both sides saved (NAME and NAME-base). The base's missing seeds are run by the filler in the base's own checkout (`--fill`, `GAMELAB_BASE_FILL`, else `baselines/base.py`, handed the base's commit and the environment the base's key resolved, `baseline.filler_env`: `GAMELAB_CHARACTER` and `GAMELAB_GPU` said outright, so a candidate with a `lab/GPU` file, or run with `GAMELAB_CHARACTER=thief`, gets the base's seeds where it then reads them; `base.py` keeps that environment); the candidate's here, cached while its code is as committed. On this branch (nothing she does changed) against master: every difference zero at 12 seeds, stopped there (230 s and 207 s: master's 12 read, 9 of the candidate's run, 3 read from its own cache). With `fight.UNSEEN_PRICE` 0 (left uncommitted: a candidate with changes, nothing of it cached), grinding: at 12 seeds EXP a minute -0.7% (se 6.6%), touches +6.8% (t 1.3), close_s +8.3% (t 1.1), hurt +10.6% (t 1.6), all within 2 se: 24 (master's 13-24 run by `base.py` as asked); at 24 -5.3% (t -1.4) and the rest within 2 se: 48; at 48 EXP -2.2% (se 2.4%), touches +4.6% (t 1.5), close_s +6.3% (t 1.7), hurt +2.9% (t 0.9), deaths, falls and stops zero: "stopped at 48 seeds (1-48): 48 seeds, the most (--max-seeds); still within 2 se: exp_per_min, touches, close_s, hurt" (1,852 s, master's 36 seeds included).

**`spot`** (`python -m gamelab.sim.harness spot RUN [--seeds 3,9] [--jobs N]`): a saved run's seeds (by default its first and its last; RUN a name, a `.json` file or a cache's folder) run again here with the arguments each result records, each "the same to the digit" or the keys that differ and how (exit 1). Two seeds of 5 minutes: 58 s on 2 workers.

**What's cached** (2026-10-28, master 0e14114 = 98f9181's code, `7a8990e8f962`): the land-clear standard commands (Tree, preset `crowd`, `--attack choice`, `--costs measured`, `--world zero-walls --world near-misses --world walkers`, 5 minutes), the hunt loop and grinding, seeds 1-48 each (`cached ... --sha master --seeds 48` reads one in 2 s); keys 3db72c7a2f022f5e (the hunt loop) and 96491aec58059698 (grinding), FORMAT 2: run again under the new key by `base.py` after the review, each of the 96 files the same to the byte as FORMAT 1's (e2390ed2bff7ff71, fc999d4c91260fee, then deleted). Master moved on to 4558f61 meanwhile (the regular attack's key check: `sim/world.py`, `fakes.py`, `scenarios.py`; code `95d85864786f`), a new code with no seeds of its own: its seeds 1-12 of both commands were filled by `base.py` (`ab`'s first step, 324 s on 4 workers; 13-48 are filled when an `ab` asks for them), each of the 24 the same to the byte as 98f9181's, and `--base 98f9181` still reads the 48 of before.

**Replays** (the perception identity checks: the states on a recording as saved, stamped 30 a second, held 3x). pfast's canon dumps them (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pfast/tools/ident.py dump --checkout --folder --drops on|off [--hold N] [--range A:B]`, `pfast/review-numbers/ident30.py` stamped 30 a second; `ident.py compare A B`), and `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/baselines/replay.py dump [--ref master] [--lab-of CHECKOUT] --folder BEFORE --drops on|off [--hold N] [--fps 30] [--range A:B]` keeps master's: `baselines/replay/<code>/<the tools' hash>/<recording>_<drops>[_hN][_f30][_rA-B]_l<lab>.jsonl.gz` with a `.json` of what it's of (the frames' stamp checked when read), made in the base checkout under the same lock the first time, its path printed after (`where`: the path, or "not cached"). `<lab>` is a hash of the dumping checkout's lab inputs, the git-ignored files there that perception reads and `code_id` can't see (`replay.LAB_INPUTS`: her calibration and name tags, each window size's, `lab/character.json`, another character's under `characters/`; each by its content, or as absent: an audit of a dump's opened files found `calibration_1366x768.json`, `character.json`, `tag_template_1366x768.npy` and `tag_template_full_1366x768.npy`; her heading pictures are the hunter's, not read). Each dump runs under an audit hook (`baselines/labread.py`) and is kept only if every lab file it opened is one of those and none changed while it ran. `replay.py compare MASTER CANDIDATE` runs `ident.py compare` once the two dumps' lab inputs are seen to be the same (from a dump's `.json`, or for one made by `ident.py` itself, from the checkout its first line names, as that lab is now), and refuses otherwise (exit 2, the files that differ; `--any-lab` compares anyway): after a recalibration, or a candidate whose lab copies are newer than ov-base's, master's dump is made on the candidate's with `--lab-of` (ov-base's own saved to `baselines/lab-saved/` first). `replay.py lab CHECKOUT` shows a checkout's lab inputs and their hash. Master's (0e14114 = 98f9181's code, `GAMELAB_GPU=0`) are cached for both Lie Detectors' `before/` (00:25, 01:01) and 23:15's, drops on and off as saved, and stamped 30 a second: 9 dumps of 3,048-4,551 frames, 123-190 s each to make and 1 s to find after, each with 0 frames differing from master 301e78e's (the GPU merge's, `wide10/gpu/ident/master_*`), so those stand for today's master too. They were made before the lab key and given it after (lab `337d2b7e`, the same in the main checkout, ov-base and ov-fast): ov-base's lab inputs were made (13:22) and last written (10-23) before the first of them (14:44), so they're the files each read; one made again with the lab key and the audit, from nothing, has 0 frames differing from its keyed copy. Held 3x isn't cached yet: `replay.py dump ... --hold 3` makes it once. kplace's `replay.py` (a hunt's recording with her throws told from its telemetry) is a different recipe and isn't wrapped: its master dumps (`sfast/merge/rep-ov-search.jsonl.gz`, `r2310 --range 0:400 --no-throws`) are reused by naming them, as gpu-merge's verify.sh does.

**Found on the way**: `bg_quiet.cmd` doesn't pass on its command's exit code (`start /b /wait` leaves cmd's own 0: a script exiting 3 through it gives 0), so the workflows' `echo "exit $?"` after it have always said 0. An `exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%` after its `start` line passes it on (tried on a copy; the file itself left as it is). The exit codes of `golden --jobs` were taken without it (tests/test_golden.py).

## Replaying the recordings: her own frames through any commit's perception, scored against labels (from 2026-11-02)

The simulator can't play the magician (P41 of the 2026-11-02 analyses: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/rec-analysis/plans), so a perception change for her is checked on her own frames: the three lossless recordings of RiceBaby grinding Tree Dungeon on master 40ba190 that night (R1 00:10:57-00:14:57, 3,601 frames; R2 00:37:01-00:42:02, 4,515; R3 00:46:40-00:51:41, 4,512; 1366x768 PNG at 15 a second, 6.6 GB in D:/MapleHelper-scratch/golden-clips, kept as fixtures by the user's word), with the run's telemetry and logs beside them. Until now each analysis rebuilt the replay by hand (spawn-fade's `replay_rec.py`, the lenses' `replay.py`s, none of them telling her throws). The kit (ROADMAP item 5) is `gamelab/sim/replay.py`, `replay_run.py` and `replay_score.py`, in the simulator's layer beside the harness and its baselines (the analysis layer may import neither localization nor sim: tests/test_architecture.py):

```
python -m gamelab.sim.replay run [R1 R2 R3] [--root DIR | --commit REF] [--out DIR] [--range A:B] [--unpaced] [--jobs 3]
python -m gamelab.sim.replay cached [CLIPS] [--commit master] [--where]     a commit's dumps, made once, read after
python -m gamelab.sim.replay score [CLIPS] [--dumps RUN_DIR] [--base master] [--json FILE]
python -m gamelab.sim.replay check A B                                     two dumps the same to the byte?
python -m gamelab.sim.replay bench [CLIPS] --base REF [--range A:B] [--rounds 1]   pass times, side by side
python -m gamelab.sim.replay feed R2                                       what the run's records tell the step
```

Every one that runs frames goes through the CPU rule's wrapper as any harness job (heavy.sh / `bg_quiet.cmd`): a replay takes about a core and a half while it runs.

**What `run` runs** (`replay_run.py`, a child process per recording run as a script by its path, so the tree it's given is the `gamelab` it imports): what `service.screen_world` builds for the live service, with the saved frames for its screen (`analysis.bench.SavedEyes`: the same Eyes, its captures handed over): the map's monster detector for the game's own 1366x768, her name tag's template from her calibration, the minimap's picture, Senses with her Shape (`GAMELAB_CHARACTER=magician`) and the look band `perceive` uses, the world step on the service's schedule; then as `Service._tune` has it while the tour was attached (it was through every frame of the three: their perceive.log): the hunt's schedule and her throws known. OpenCV on one thread, Windows' timers at 1 ms, the GPU off (`GAMELAB_GPU=0`, as the baselines' replays: the GPU's answers are the same to the bit). Each frame is handed over at its own time in the recording (15 a second, the next read from disk in the slack after the pass); `--unpaced` runs them back to back. The tree: this checkout as it is, another (`--root`), or a commit (`--commit`: `git archive` of its `gamelab/`, `gamedata/`, `maplehelper/` and `config.toml` under the cache's `trees/<code>-<lab>/`, with this checkout's DLLs (named by their sources' hash: a source that differs is built there) and this checkout's lab inputs, so both sides of a comparison read the same; the game data read from D:/MapleHelper's, read only).

**The clock and the feed** (`clock`, `feed`). The frames are stamped in wall time (summary.json's `from`, local UTC-8, and index.jsonl's `t`); the service's telemetry names frame times on its own `time.monotonic` (a victim's gain, a touch's popup); the hunt's records are wall time at their emission. The one offset that puts the service's frame times on frames is 1793544509.301 s on all three (R1 73 of 76 within 2 ms of a frame, R2 106 of 107, R3 79 of 81), and the step runs on the service's own clock (frame 0 at `t0`), so the times it makes read against the live ones directly. What the service took from outside: her throws, each told before the first frame shown after its tour `attack` record went (when the service heard of it; its key `TURN_S` 80 ms later where her keys had her facing the other way, as `Actions.throw` taps the arrow first: 23, 46 and 39 of 80, 139 and 119), its side from the fight's `stance` record just before it (all 338: none needed her target's side of her), and the drops the hunt asked for (each tour `scene` that looked at drops: an ask on the last frame shown 12 ms before it, her platform's or every one in view as the look was wide; 319, 487, 501 asks). Not told: throws told again the other way by a frame (`hunter._retell`: no `retold` event in the whole hour, so none to tell).

**Live's events, reproduced** (master's code, unpaced, against the perceive telemetry over the frames: `recfix/replay/scripts/fidelity.py`): every gain bound to the same monster first (kind, x within 15, platform): R1 45 of 45, R2 69 of 69, R3 51 of 51; let-gos 7 of 7, 12 of 12, 10 of 11; touches 21, 26 and 24, each at the same popup time to the millisecond; deaths of hers 45, 68, 45 (live 47, 69, 46) and others' 5, 18, 69 (live 4, 18, 71); and the spawn watch's onsets the analyses' replays had, the same point and frame: R2 92 of 92, R3 105 of 105, R1 47 (the analysis's 30 newborns given out, all 30, and 17 more: 15 re-finds of a newborn reported 5-7 frames before, 2 the late find of a birth under her name tag, each a real newborn on recfix/replay/sheets/r1_onsets_a,b.png).

**The dump** (one gzip JSON line a frame, mtime 0, so the same lines are the same bytes; a head line with `t0` and the feed's hash, an end line with the step's, tracker's and spawn watch's counts): her place, view and bars, the state's monsters (kind, place, track, alpha, facing, bar, box, score, picture), the tracks (state, kind, place, alpha, how first seen, bar, gain, cause), the events (with their data and time), the players, the spawn watch's sightings before the hand-over, the whole screen's raw detections, the drops asked for, and what the eyes or senses logged: 0.28-0.41 MB a recording. The pass's times (the real clock's) go in a side file, never in the dump, with the lab files the run opened.

**The labels** (`tests/fixtures/recordings/<clip>/labels-v1.json`, 26-35 KB each, in git where no cleanup of the scratch drive can lose them; the frames stay in golden-clips, named by path; built by `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/recfix/replay/scripts/build_labels.py` from the analyses' verified lists and master's replay):

|---|---|

**`cached`**: a commit's dumps (master's by default) under `<GAMELAB_REPLAYS, else the baselines' root>/recordings/<code 12>/<key 16>/` with `key.json` (what it's of) and the side file, as the harness's baselines are kept: `code` the commit's `code_id` (sim.baseline: its tree under `gamelab/`, `gamedata/`, `maplehelper/`, `config.toml`, Markdown aside), `key` a hash of everything else a dump depends on: `replay_run.py`'s own source, the feed, the lab inputs (`LAB_INPUTS` by content: who plays, her calibration and name tags, her stat window's place, her plate and pose models, the map's art; a dump that opened any other lab file isn't kept), the `GAMELAB_*` environment, Python's and the packages' versions, the recording's frames and the range. **`bench`**: pass times only from runs made side by side, the base and the tree alternated (base, tree, tree, base a round) on the same frames, paced, one at a time; never against a cached dump's times (the machine isn't the same between them).

A fix that binds better than master's last binding there reads as wrong on `all`; `strong` (64: die1 with a binding agreeing, the R1 lenses' 7, 7 by eye) is the one to trust. ## Route coverage

`python -m gamelab coverage RUN... [--live]` (`analysis/coverage.py`; offline, no keys) reads saved harness runs and, with `--live`, the live telemetry (`lab/telemetry`, but the simulator's files), and says for each move of the route graph (its kind, platforms and where it starts: `jump 32->29 @536`) how often it was planned (every route record, replans too), taken (set off on, in a chain or made alone) and missed (she ended elsewhere, not from a hit), with where she ended instead (a chain hit on the way that still ended where it was to made every move; one a hit left elsewhere is a hit's); for each platform her visits and time (look to look, 5 s at most); the trips by how they ended, those that timed out before she set off apart; the tour's stops (its sweep's: the hunt loop's 'tour' records are its grounds) and the hunt loop's grounds. Which move of a chain missed is read from where she was seen standing in between: her looks and glances on a platform's surface (within 6 units) twice in a row, against the platforms the chain goes through. Each harness run keeps a tally of its own telemetry for it (`analysis.coverage.tally`, 3-7 KB a run; runs saved before 2026-10-21's evening have none). `--text FILE` writes the report, and each set of runs gets a picture of the map (`lab/coverage_<map>.png`, then `-2`, `-3`: taken in green, thicker the more often; planned but never taken in yellow; never planned in red).

For each move never taken: the least gap from the best route through it to the route chosen, by the planner's own times (no random weights, no penalties), on the plans that could have made it (but those that kept a ground off or avoided a monster); on how many of them it was within 35% of the chosen (the most the navigator's weights, 1 to 1.35 a move a trip, can make up); and why it lost: **replanned** (planned, but replanned before she got to it, or the trip over), **weights** (cheaper than the route chosen: the weights drew the other), **penalty** (cheaper, but its route went onto a ground the trip kept off, or through a move a monster was in the way of), **ground** (the quickest way between two places on the map, but no trip went between them), or **cost** (the quickest between no two places: from every 60 units along each platform to every other platform). A move flow can't chain from where it starts (no takeoff passing `Flow.sure_takeoff`'s room) is named too: none on this map. Platform 12 and 23 -> 17 by the two rope hops get their own lines, with how often the weights would have sent her that way (`coverage.drawn`: the planner's own search under 40 draws of the weights a plan).

The live telemetry so far was all planned on older graphs, and its routes don't say where they were planned from: each route's moves are put on today's of the same kind and platforms that start nearest (1,941 of them more than 3 units off, the takeoffs since placed for room), its start is the look before it, its misses are read from the navigator's log lines ("ended on ... instead of"), and a move cheaper on today's graph than the route chosen then reads **then** (not in that graph, or the weights). From now on the navigator records both (Control: A route, what it records).

What it found (2026-10-21; the harness's preset `game`, 10 seeds of 20 minutes, and the 72 live files of 2026-10-19 to 21; the same harness runs as the branch's start, seed for seed: the tally only reads the telemetry the run captured anyway):
- **The graph:** 204 moves. 13 are the quickest way between no two places on the map: the 6 rope climb-downs, all 3 rope jumps (the hops 23 -> 17, 6 -> 16 by 798's rope, 3 -> 9 by 723's), and 4 that another move beats by 0.07-0.40 s. Flow chains every other move from where it starts (no takeoff fails `Flow.sure_takeoff`'s room); the 10 climb-downs and rope jumps the mover makes alone.
- **Used:** the tour planned 104 of the 204 and took 98 (478 moves, 11 missed, 42 a hit's); the hunt loop 51 and 45 (166, 3, 26). Live, 121 of today's moves were taken (1,412 moves, 88 missed: the jump 32 -> 29 26 times of 83, into the basin; 29 -> 28 8 of 73; 16 -> 14 7 of 56, onto 25; 19 -> 18 7 of 66, onto 24 and 26). 55 moves weren't taken in any of the three.
- **The simulator's hunts hardly leave the basin.** The hunt loop spends 87.5% of its time on 36 and takes up 36 as its ground 12 times in 10 runs, 4 twice, 2 and 17 once; over 20 seeds no move of a route got her onto 2, 7, 12, 20 or 21 (she was on 12 and 21 only where two runs start, `harness.START_AT`, and on 2 after jump throws from 4). Live, 17.4% of the time was on 36, and the loop's grounds were 4 (24 times), 36 (20), 17 (16) and 1 (6). The tour spends 51.5% on 36, and the escort's fights there eat its trips: 59 of its 246 trips timed out, 28 of them before she set off (no route planned: bursts on the way and fights in her way until the stop's 90 s ran out), so its sweep's far stops come late or never (over 30 seeds it got onto 7 on 2 and 35 on 3). Live, 8 of 573 trips timed out. Whether the game's basin is as busy as the simulator's (60% of its 8 spawns filled, 8 s respawns) was for the respawns' measurement: it isn't. In game the basin had a monster at 12% of its spawn points while in view, and none 45% of the time, against 27% and 7% in the simulator by the same report, and a platform she emptied was mostly still empty 12.56 s later (80%), where in the simulator about half had a monster back within 5 s (Respawns and drop life).
- **Never taken, by why:** the tour's 106: ground 72, penalty 18 (its spots' trips keep off the ground they shoot), cost 10, replanned 6; the loop's 159: ground 137, cost 13, replanned 6, weights 3. Most moves lose to where the trips go, not to their cost.
- **Platform 12** (2 pigs and an Orange Mushroom): the tour stopped at it 6 times of 70 (7 moves onto it, 1.1% of its time); the hunt loop never made it a ground, in the simulator or live (live, 2 visits and one move onto it in 3 days). Through 12 on the way elsewhere was slower for every trip the runs made: the tour's at best +3.1 s (+149%), none within 35%; the loop's +0.8 s (+15%), 3 of 133 plans within 35%; and the weights would have sent her through it on none. On today's graph the live trips' ends had a route through 12 within 35% of the one chosen on 205 of 684 plans, but the weights would send her through it on about 1 of them: each move's weight is drawn on its own, so over the long left side they average out (as found before: Found offline, Ropes in mid-air, route variety). So in the harness it's the ground choice: hardly a trip goes where a way through 12 is close (none of the tour's 219 plans, 3 of the loop's 133), and she goes onto 12 only to hunt 12 itself, which the hunt loop never does. Live it's the weights: a way through 12 was within reach on 205 plans, and the weights almost never draw it (Route diversity: why her routes were fixed).
- **23 -> 17 by two rope hops** (`rope_jump 23->17 @959`): in the graph since the ropes in mid-air (2026-10-21, 09:40), after the last live run (01:52), so live it wasn't there to take, nor the climb past 23's end. In the harness it was never planned: 4.49 s with its risk (0.5 s, a guess), against 3.15 for the climb past 23's end, +1.1 s (+29%) from where the quickest routes leave 23 (x 903), so it's the quickest way nowhere (cost). The weights make that up only when the climb's draw is 1.28 times the hops' or more: on 1.2% of the trips from 23 at x 903 (2.5% from x 866, by its left end; 0.2% from 959). Over the tour's 226 plans that could have made it, the weights would have sent her by the hops on 0.6 (the climb was taken 24 times; in the loop 0.0 and 3); the live trips' ends, on today's graph, 1.2 of 685. That it was never taken in these runs is what its cost predicts: to be taken it needs a lower cost or a diversity setting (Route diversity: `--ways 3`, which takes them on about 1 in 10 of the trips from there, from x 930 or less), or `nav 17 --avoid climb`.
- **The regression test** (`tests/test_coverage.py`): in the harness's own world it's the fights in the basin that decide which platforms she gets to, so the test runs in preset `game-sparse` (`game` with 15% of the spawns filled): the tour and the hunt loop on seeds 1-5, 10 minutes each, between them get her onto every platform monsters spawn on (16), each by 2 runs of the 10 or more (12 by 2, 35 by 3). Of the first 16 seeds, every 4 in a row do (13 of 13), every 3 in a row 13 of 14. 9.5 s, the runs in worker processes as the harness's.

To check in game: the first live run with the new records, by `coverage --live`: its routes should count as planned on today's graph (none "older"), its misses fall on the moves her dot shows (the verdicts the navigator's own now), and a chain hit on the way that still got her there count as made. The hops' own check stays as it was (Found offline: Ropes in mid-air).

## Respawns and drop life

`python -m gamelab respawn [FILES...] [--text FILE]` (`analysis/respawn.py`; offline, no keys) reads the live telemetry (`lab/telemetry`, but the simulator's files), or the files given, and measures three things, each time as a survival estimate over censored observations (Kaplan-Meier; its median's 95% interval Brookmeyer and Crowley's, the share left at 5 s to 180 s with its interval on the log-log scale; a time is given only where 5 or more were still followed):
- **Respawn:** from a kill (her 'kill' events, and the deaths the continuous feed saw, 'died': `watch`'s, hers and others', and from late on 2026-10-21 a hunt's with `--feed`, others' only) that empties its platform until a monster is seen there again. An episode starts only if the kill's monster was seen there in the 3 s before (a kill placed on the wrong monster would start one on a platform empty long since) and the looks after it, from 1.5 s on (a kill is seen dying for up to 1.26 s), see the platform empty twice, 0.5 s apart. A monster seen there then (or another kill there) ends it at the midpoint between that look and the last that saw the platform empty, if they're 2 s apart at most. A longer gap between the looks covering the platform, whether the next sees a monster or not (she was away: a monster may have come back and been killed by someone else meanwhile, and the telemetry has others' kills only from the feed), the end of the run or 180 s censors it at the last empty look. (The report first went on with an episode across a gap when the look after it saw the platform empty again, as if it had been empty all along, though the method said otherwise: 34 of the 77 live episodes spanned such a gap, of up to 111 s, and its "past a minute" rested on that unwatched time. Found in review on 2026-10-21.) One seen first with an HP bar is one she had hurt, hidden for a while under its damage numbers, and drops the episode. 'Lone' episodes had no other kill on the platform in the 15 s before: with a respawn per spawn point, an earlier kill's monster coming back first cuts the time short.
- **Drop life:** each drop, told apart by its kind and where it lies (within 8 units: from one look to the next within a second, 76% of the live drops seen again were within a unit of where they'd been, 89% within two), from the kill of hers it lies by (within 60 units and 20 s before it was first seen; else from when it was first seen, its age then unknown) until two looks 1.5 s apart that looked for drops where it lies, with her standing, her inventory not full and no other drop over it (drops drawn over one another are found as one), see it gone: an event if she wasn't by it since it was last seen (within 25 units, or her walk from one look to the next over it: the looter walks over a row of piles pressing pick-up with no look in between), else picked up (censored). It's followed only until the next kill by it (another kill's drops land where it lies, and one of its kind there would be taken for it), and what's then seen where it lay is neither it nor a new drop until the spot is seen empty. Other players take drops too, once they're no longer the killer's, and nothing in the telemetry tells that from a drop vanishing: the estimate is a lower bound of the game's drop life.
- **How full:** for each platform monsters spawn on, over the looks that covered it (each counted until the next look, 1 s at most), the monsters seen on it against its spawn points, and how much of the time none was. Detection misses a monster now and then, and her kills keep down the ones she hunts.

A look sees a platform empty only if it searched for monsters with her standing (from mid-jump the band and the screen are up to 77 units higher than her platform puts them) and all of the platform in the area searched: her band (140 above her feet to 75 below, a monster's body 60 tall held in it), or the whole screen above the bottom bar and clear of the minimap, less 40 units at the screen's sides. A monster seen on it in any look that searched with her standing is one there. **From 2026-10-21's evening each scene record says so itself:** whether the look searched for monsters (`searched`) and on the whole screen (`wide`), where it looked for drops (`looked`: platform, map x from, to), the map the screen showed above the bottom bar (`view`) and whether she stood (her `grounded`); `watch`'s records carry where its last search for drops looked. That's about 90 bytes a look (16-23% more per scene record in the simulator's runs; about 0.7 MB an hour of hunting on its 4.2). Before, the report infers them: a look searched if it saw a monster, if the hunt loop's 'monsters' record or a fight's 'stance' followed it, in a probe's run off a trip (a probe looks for minutes, every look searching), or in `watch`; it was wide if it saw a monster off her band or drops off her platform, in a probe that looks wide, or in `watch`; she stood if her name tag was seen on her platform's surface, not within 1.3 s of a fight's jump (in the live hunt loops, of the looks after a jump stance whose look before saw 2 drops or more on her platform, 104 of 130 saw none 0.9-1.1 s after it, 13 of 23 at 1.2 s: in the air); the hunt loop's own looks that saw a drop on her platform looked for drops all along it. The rest (the navigator's looks for her landing, the looter's, the rests') say nothing, and the screen is put by the camera's model (`pose.Camera`).

**The game's own data** has no respawn time for this map: its 48 spawn points (life entries: 9 snails, 12 slimes, 18 pigs, 9 Orange Mushrooms) all have `mobTime` 0, its info `mobRate` 1.0 and no `createMobInterval`. No map of the 306 in the client's data has `createMobInterval`; of the spawn points of the 196 with monsters, 4,794 have `mobTime` 0, 2,512 none, and 341 a time of 1 s to 3 hours (timed spawns). The respawn's timing is the server's.

**MeowDB's stated model** for MapleStory Classic (its pages of maps 010003111, The Murky Swamp II, and 010000012, this one, read 2026-10-21): one respawn tick every 7.56 s for every map the server has loaded; after a monster dies its spawn point waits a cooldown (5 s, or for timed spawns the map's `mobTime`) and the monster comes back on the next tick. A map holds at most 75% of its spawn points' monsters with one player there, 5% more for each other player, all of them from 6: here about 36 of 48 solo. The map's mob rate isn't applied to those figures, which it gives as its reading of the closed beta. By it a spawn point's monster is back 5-12.56 s after it dies (8.8 s on average), while the map is under its cap.

What it found (2026-10-21; the 72 live files of 2026-10-19 to 21: 14,869 looks placing her, 469 kills of hers, every look's coverage inferred; no other player's kill is in them, the one `watch` file being a minute long):
- **A platform she empties mostly stays empty while she watches it.** 77 episodes, each followed while the looks covering its platform came 2 s apart at most: 12 seen back, all within 10.8 s (2.5-10.8 s after the kill). Not back by 5 s: 90% (95% 81-95%, 55 still followed); by 8 s: 83% (71-90%, 39); by 12.56 s: 80% (67-88%, 23); by 30 s: 80% (11 followed); fewer than 5 were watched to 60 s, the longest 79 s. The 36 lone ones: 91% not back by 12.56 s (70-98%, 13 followed). The median isn't reached. How much that leans on the 2 s: censored only at gaps over 5 s, 83% weren't back by 12.56 s (34 followed) and 80% by 60 s (5); taking the unwatched time as empty, as the report first did, 83% by 12.56 s (46) and 81% by 60 s (15). So about four in five aren't back by 12.56 s, whichever way; that they stay empty past a minute only the unwatched time said. By platform: 4 (shot from 3) 6 of 20 back (2.5-10.8 s), followed to 70 s; the basin 3 of 14 (2.5-4.0 s), the rest followed only to 13.4 s, as she left; 3 (one snail; she stood on it, shooting 4) 1 of 15 (7.3 s), followed only to 12.9 s; 18 and 21 none of 7 each, followed to 79 and 71 s; 17 1 of 6; 20 1 of 4; 22 none of 3. Of the 469 kills, 350 didn't empty their platform, 26 had it out of view after, 9 had no monster of theirs seen there just before, 7 were a hurt one coming out from under its damage numbers. Whether she stood by the platform's spawn points can't say why: 69 episodes had her within 150 units of one at the kill (12 back), 8 didn't (none back, followed to 49 s).
- **The simulator refills within seconds** (the same report on 8 runs of preset `game`, the hunt loop and the tour on seeds 1-4, 10 minutes each, the records saying what each look searched): 22 episodes, 11 seen back at 3.0-8.8 s, the other 11 followed only 2.5-6.3 s (she left, or a gap in the looks): 52% not back by 5 s (95% 26-72%, 6 still followed), against the game's 90% (81-95%); on the basin 6 of 10 back at 3.0-4.2 s (an earlier kill's monster comes back first), on 31 (one snail's) 4 of 9 at 3.8-8.8 s, the sooner ones after a kill whose event came seconds after the death (a kill's event comes at the look that saw her EXP go up: in the simulator 0.53 s at the median, 1.8 s at the 90th percentile, and a quarter of its kill events had no death of their kind there in the 5 s before). Read as the older telemetry is (everything inferred), the same runs give the same picture (21 episodes, 12 seen back at 2.6-8.8 s, the rest followed only to 5.2 s; the median 3.8 s). `tests/test_respawn.py` has a pig alone in the basin back 7.6 s after its kill's event, 8 s after it died. (Before the gap rule: 14 of 22 back. The messages of commits 299e9e7 and 4906f4d have every one back by 8.8 s: 8 were followed only to 2.5-6.3 s.)
- **So neither the simulator's 8 s at the spawn point nor MeowDB's 5-12.56 s fits the game's platforms after she empties them**, as far as 12.56 s: by MeowDB's model every spawn point's monster would be back by then, while the map is under its cap. MeowDB's cap would fit: with the map at it, a respawn goes to some free spawn point of the map, not the one she freed (her platform's chance a few in the dozens free), and other players' kills elsewhere bring monsters to platforms nobody hunts. That isn't settled, and how full the platforms were (below) would put the cap well under 75%.
- **How full:** 26% of the spawn points of the platforms in view had a monster, over 4,523 s of platforms covered (her kills included). The basin 12% (0.99 monsters of 8, none 45% of the time; the simulator's, by the same report, 27% and 7%), 12 17% (0.52 of 3, none 72%: a run of the probe top-60 watched it from 13 for 5 minutes and never had one in range), 4 22%, 17 19%, 18 28%, 21 35%, 2 40%; the one-snail platforms 20 93%, 33 72%, 22 64%, 31 45%, and 3 8% (she stood on it). The simulator's preset `game` fills 60% of the spawn points, and its monsters come back where they were.
- **Drop life isn't settled: longer than a minute.** 337 drops followed (235 hers, 102 found), 10 seen gone without her by them (hers at 4-10 s, found at 0-77 s); 141 lost from view, 139 followed only until a kill by them, 47 picked up. Still lying at 60 s: 95% (89-97%, 7 followed that long), and none was followed past 88 s: she picks hers up within seconds, and where she hunts the next kill lands by the rest. The early ones gone may be other players' takes, or the detector's. In the simulator, where every drop lies 180 s, the same report saw 21 of 481 drops gone, at 2-187 s, and the basin's kills cut most short (316): a hunt's telemetry can't measure it.
- **The constants stay:** `hunt.RESPAWN` and `world.RESPAWN` 8 s, `hunt.DROP_LIFE` 90 s (`looting.DROPS_LAST`) and `world.DROP_LIFE` 180 s, their comments saying what was measured. RESPAWN's value isn't measured (the median isn't reached) and neither is the game's way (a delay, or a cap): another value would be another guess, and in the simulator, whose monsters do come back in 8 s, any shorter wait would only lose. It decides a fair share of the hunt loop: in the live hunt loops (4,135 s), rule 8 (lull loot, a kill due back) held 6.2% of the time and rule 9 (wait) 5.3%, and 20 of their 43 departures from a ground were "nothing left here, and nothing due back", RESPAWN + 2 s and the 3 s to confirm after her last kill there. The drop life is over a minute, as both values are.

To check in game (the report runs on any telemetry): the next hunt loop or tour with `--feed` (`tour --loop --minutes 20 --feed`), by `respawn` on its file, now with every look saying what it searched and the feed's deaths of others' kills recorded ('died'): whether a platform she empties, watched without a gap, stays empty past 12.56 s as here (80% not back), or has a monster back within it (MeowDB's respawn at a spawn point); and how many of the platforms she empties someone else empties first (others' kills on them). If it stays empty, RESPAWN's wait (rules 8 and 9, and the fast exit's "due back") isn't worth its time in game, and the simulator needs the game's refill (MeowDB's cap, say) before the harness can weigh a shorter one. A hunt watches a platform only while she's near it, so for longer: `watch --minutes 20` (it sends no keys) while she, played by hand, clears a platform in full view (12 from 13, or 21 from 22) and stands still 3 minutes, twice, and `respawn` on its file: the feed records every death ('died', hers and others'), so each clearing is an episode watched throughout, and the other platforms in view say whether monsters come back elsewhere meanwhile (a cap). In the same watch, one kill's drops left lying on a quiet platform in view (a snail's on 22 or 20) and not picked up for 4 minutes: when they go is the drop life, which no hunt has left a drop long enough to show.

**Tree Dungeon's respawn, measured (2026-10-29: the map's tick, a chance at each, a cap).** From the perception service's own telemetry (`lab/telemetry/*-perceive*.jsonl` of 2026-10-28 and 29: 10 files, about 16 hours, every look searching the whole screen; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/respawn`: `extract.py`, `period.py`, `ticks_an.py` and the tables' scripts beside them). A birth is a new track at a spawn point of its kind (within 60 units, on its platform), its platform in view the 1.5 s before (no gap over 2 s), its kind's count there up from 1 s before to 1 s after, no death of its kind within 100 units in the 1.5 s before (a dying monster found again): 9,957 of them. A free point is one of a platform's points of a kind over its monsters of that kind then (live and hidden tracks), counted at each tick while all the platform stayed in view from 2 s before to 1.5 s after.

| | measured |
|---|---|
| the map's tick | every 7.115 s (fitted on each stretch of looks: 7.09-7.13 s); 73-95% of the births within 0.6 s of a tick by stretch (the rest the detector's lag, or a phase reset); the births' pairwise gaps peak at 0, 7.1, 14.1, 21.1, 28.4, 35.4 s |
| a free point at a tick, in view | gets a monster 0.27 of the time (5,775 births in 21,285 free point-ticks; 487 more births in full groups: the count's own misses) |
| ... by the time since the point's last death | 0.22 within 2 s, 0.28-0.32 at 2-30 s, 0.23-0.25 at 30-120 s, 0.17 past 2 minutes: no cooldown, no clock of its own |
| ... by her distance | 0.20 within 100 units of her, 0.25-0.29 farther: no keeping out of her way |
| ... by the free points in view | 0.24-0.28 with 1 to 9 free: each on its own, not a number a tick shared out |
| ... by the other players on the map | nobody else for a minute: 0.023 (11 births in 486 free point-ticks, each within two ticks of a kill of hers: the cap); nobody in the look 0.06-0.15; up to one a look: 0.10-0.17; more: 0.26-0.31 |
| ... by her kills in the tick before | 0.26 with none, 0.27-0.29 with 1-2, 0.31 with 3 or more |
| ... by 5 minutes, 2026-10-29 | 0.25-0.35 every 10 minutes of the night's grinds (2.4-4.9 others a look); in the afternoon 0.40 at 15:55, 0.08-0.16 at 16:05-16:30, 0.03 at 16:35, none at 16:40 (0.1 others a look), 0.31 at 16:45 |
| the map's count | when 26 or more of its 31 points were seen within 30 s, 0.32-0.47 monsters a point (0.69 at the most) |
| 16:39-16:44 | the top's 12 points and 3 of the middle's free 4 to 9 minutes, in view at every stop she made: no birth in 38 ticks, no death, nobody else on the map; the map then held 14 monsters at the most |
| in view or out of it | of the free points she left, net back after 7-15 s out of view 0.32, 15-60 s 0.43-0.46, 1-10 minutes 0.43-0.53; in view all along 0.41, 0.46-0.48, 0.49-0.53 (net of her kills there): the same, no spawning only out of sight |
| other players' kills | 77% of the deaths seen (2,825 hers, 9,391 others'); in her grinds 35-65%, at night others killing 1.5-3 times what she did |

So the game respawns on the map's clock (MeowDB's 7.56 s tick, at 7.115), each free point's monster back with a chance at each tick, whenever it died, as long as the map is under its cap (MeowDB: 75% of its points with one player, 5% more for each other; here, alone, 14 of 31 at the most): with nobody else killing, a point she empties stays empty until something dies somewhere, her own kills too (the alone row counted by look over all ten files, as the review of 2026-10-29 did, `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/respawn/fix/alone_all.py`: first counted by tick it had 0 births in 154 free point-ticks, but its ticks were placed only among births, few when she's alone). Not per point, nothing for 5 s and then n x 12.8 s (the belief's until then), not 8 s after each death (the simulator's). Grinding learns the rate (Grinding: the belief); the simulator has it as `--world tick-respawn` (`Realism.respawn_tick`) and `--world solo` (nobody else).

**... against the server's own rule (2026-10-30: the map fills itself to its cap).** The client has no spawn logic: it shows the monsters the server sends. The nearest thing to the server's code is OrionAlpha (github.com/EricSoftTM/OrionAlpha, KMS-1.23: `LifePool.init`, `tryCreateMob`; a replica of Nexon's early Korean server): a pass at least every 7 s spawns the cap less the monsters alive at spawn points drawn at random (each at most once a pass); the cap is the map's area times its `mobRate` (one monster in 128,000 square px of its footholds' box, 1 to 40, doubled only with more players than half of it); a point with `mobTime` 0 has no cooldown, only no monster within 100 px; one with a `mobTime` holds one monster, back 1.3-2 times it after it dies. MeowDB's model (a global 7.56 s tick, a 5 s cooldown, 75% of the points with one player and 5% more a player) is its own reading of the closed beta. Checked on 40 hours of Tree Dungeon's telemetry (19 files of 2026-10-28 to 30, 85,187 point-passes at 11,187 fitted passes; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/respawn-orion`, RESULTS.txt and the scripts beside it):

| | measured | OrionAlpha |
|---|---|---|
| the pass | 88% of the births within -0.8..+1.0 s of the fitted 7.115 s ticks | 7 s at the least, at the server's update: fits (MeowDB's 7.56 doesn't) |
| what comes back | with her alone (13 minutes of 40 hours) only what she killed: 10-29 16:37-16:46, 16 of 16 births 1.2-5.8 s after a kill of hers (by accident ~3e-4); 16:39-16:44, no kill, 17-19 free points watched 5 minutes, no birth (a chance for each free point, even 2.5% a tick, expects ~18) | the cap less the alive: fits |
| the cap | with her alone the parts she saw held 11-15 (0.35-0.5 a point: the 24 points she saw 0-7, the bottom's 7 about 8 at its next look, after others were back); with others 0.39-0.55 a point at every count of players, 1 to 6+: counts of what was in view, the whole map never seen without a kill between | 22 here (0.71 a point): more than was seen, but what wasn't seen isn't known; no rise with players: fits (MeowDB's 75%-100%: neither) |
| a point with a monster near it | first read as no rule: births beside a monster already there, 0.12-0.21 a pass against 0.20-0.27 farther (seen monsters only), and the clips at 08:26:04 on 10-30 and 20:40:24 on 10-29. Retracted on 2026-10-31 (the user's catch): frame by frame both clips' newcomers faded in at platform 15's other Horny Mushroom point, 115 px from the monster there, outside its box; the detector credited a newborn to the point nearest where it was first tracked, after it had walked, and a spawn tracked once fading in and again solid reads as a new monster beside one there. Nothing seen against the box (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/respawn-orion/RESULTS.txt`, 6) | no monster within 100 px of the point, across and up or down: kept (the user, 2026-10-31: "I feel the orionalpha's rule actually holds") |

So the respawn is the map's: every ~7.1 s it spawns its cap less what's alive, at points drawn at random among the clear ones (no monster within 100 px across and up or down, nor a point taken before it in that pass), whoever else is there. The cap is the server's formula (`MapModel.mob_cap`: the map's area times its `mobRate`; Tree Dungeon II 22, Thicket Around the Beach II 26, West Rocky Mountain II 23, 10002072 27, 10002074 20): the counts above are of the parts of the map she saw, and the map was never seen whole without a kill between (hers or another's), so how many it held isn't known (the user, 2026-10-30: "Let's use the formula, the issue with your approach is that we don't know how many mobs are on the map at any given time"; it was 0.42 of the spawn points, 13 of 31, from those counts, for a few hours). A point's 0.27 a tick (above) is what died over the map since the pass before, over the free points: with others killing it's about that; alone it's her own kills, back at one of the free points each, mostly those she has just emptied (at the cap 22 of Tree Dungeon's 31 points are held, about 9 free), and where nobody kills stays held. The simulator's every world is this from 2026-10-31 (the user: "Use the tick default everywhere"; `--world clock-respawn` the per-monster clock as before, `tick-respawn` kept as a name; five set-piece scenarios on their monsters' own clock, `scenarios._CLOCK`, and ten re-seeded; until then only `--world tick-respawn`, from 2026-10-30 (`Realism.respawn_tick`, `respawn_cap` None: the formula's, by the players there, a share of the points still a knob; a point drawn only with no monster within 100 units of it, `world.SPAWN_CLEAR`; until then each free point's monster back with a chance of 0.27 a tick, a cap of 0.45 of the points and 0.05 more for each other player)); grinding's belief too (Grinding: the belief). Not settled: whether the game's cap is the formula's (22 here, where the parts she saw held 11-15 with her alone: a count of the whole map with nobody killing would tell); whether a kill with the map at its cap brings a pass at once (OrionAlpha keeps no pass time while the map is full) or waits for the tick, 14 births alone can't tell.

**With the chase** (merged onto master's aggro, 2026-10-31: both every world's). Against master's golden traces (aggro, each monster back on its own clock), Tree Dungeon's 42: 32 changed; summed, touches 1,333 -> 700, kills 947 -> 640, EXP 27,685 -> 21,411 (the map at its cap, 22 of its 31 points, a kill back only at a clear point). Re-seeded where a scenario's event no longer came, each noted (`fight_step_wall`, `loop_tree_23_near_misses`, `loop_tree_ore_waits`, `loop_tree_grind_arrow_key`, `loop_tree_grind_lucky_seven_key`, `loop_lull_loot`, `loop_rival`); the heading tests' knocks on their monsters' own clock. `loop_tree_run` failed: of seeds 1-13 none met it, 8 going up the tower among its Horny Mushrooms and 5 knocked out past its walls, where the server's respawn alone met it on 5 (6 up the tower, 2 out) and the chase alone on 7. Looked into the same day, two faults found: the hunt loop's check that a look covers a ground (`hunt._covers_ground`) went by where drops were looked for (`Scene.looked`), a strip at a time since the drops' rotation (`worldstate.DROPS_EVERY_S`), so no ground was ever covered, "nothing left here" never came, and she left an empty ground on her patience alone for the one she'd just left, every 4-5 s (seeds 3, 6, 9): now by where monsters were searched (`Scene.searched_x`: the frame's breadth where its rows take in the ground's level); and the simulator let her fall past the tower's walls off a floating platform's end (seeds 2, 5, 10, 12, 13, mostly 24's right end, at the wall), where live her measured place in the air along them is the wall's x (351 times; 3 past it by the body cue's spread; never anything outside, with 7,031 placements within 20 of 24's right end): group 0's walls stop her by default now (`Realism.zero_walls`; `--world own-walls` the old way). With both, of seeds 1-13 none falls out, every run 23-31 kills and 726-878 EXP, and 3 meet all of it; the other 10 hunt a tower ground a while (7, 10 or 19) by its EXP for its danger, standing on 10 or shooting 19 from 20 (1-2 hurting touches there on seeds 5 and 6, against 10-13 on 23). On its seed 1 it meets all of it again (under the goldens' settings and two other hash seeds), no longer expected to fail; its "not up the tower" was written when the floor alone, every point full and each back 8 s after its kill, paid most. The slow tests (`--slow`), not run on the two merges: 10 of them failed for them and pass again, the probes' targets on the old walk and clock (tests/test_probe.py's `_targets_as_measured`, as the probe scenarios'), `nav_fight_basin` re-seeded and `loop_run`'s floor 45 kills (46-69 on seeds 1-13); the 6 failing before them fail still (`nav_fight_across_runs_out`, `tour_hunt_basin` and 4 of test_probe's).

## Route diversity

With `--ways N` (`nav`, `tour`, `tour --loop`, and the harness's `run` and `coverage`; `route.ROUTES`, 1 by default) each trip chooses among the N best distinct ways to where it's going, not only the quickest. It still weighs every move's cost by a random 1 to 1.35 (`route.NOISE`, kept through its replans), so near-equal variants take turns (the basin's two ropes, a drop or a walk-off, which takeoff). Then, at its first plan:
- **The ways** (`Planner.alternatives`): the quickest, then the best route through each other move (to where it starts, the move, and on from where it lands: one search out from her and one back from where she's going, as road maps find alternatives through a via node), cheapest first, none more than 35% dearer than the quickest (`route.STRETCH`), none onto a platform twice, and none through a move of the quickest (with no random weights a tie gave one, from 0 at x 1290 to 18 through walk_off 0->1 at no cost more, and `through` that move gave back the quickest itself: 7 of 978 ways offered on random trips, none with the weights). A way is the platforms it goes through and the rope each move takes: another takeoff, or a jump for a walk-off between the same two platforms, is the same way, which the weights vary. From 23 by its right end (x 903) to 17 the planner offers the climb past the end at 1040's rope (3.79 s) and the two rope hops off 959's (4.87 s, +29%); from 19 to 3, the way by 18, 16, 14 and 6 (13.0 s) and the one up the map's left side through 12 (16.0 s, +23%).
- **The choice** (`route.chances`, `choose`): a softmax over their times, a way dearer than the quickest by 10% of its time weighing 1/e of it (`route.TEMPERATURE`). By their times alone the hops are taken 5.5% of the time from x 903, and 10% with the weights drawn as well; the way through 12 from 19, 9%. A way through a move she hasn't set off on for 2 minutes (`route.STALE_S`; the navigator's memory, since it began), one the quickest doesn't make, has a chance of 20% at least (`route.FLOOR`; such ways get half the chances at most between them).
- **Kept to:** replanned, the trip goes the way it chose (`Planner.through` its move) until she has set off on that move, unless from where she is that costs more than the quickest by more than any way offered could (35% of the quickest's time when it chose: a share of what's left dropped the hops at the end of a trip from 35 in the first runs), she is past the move (on a platform the way reaches from it on: she got there another way), or the way from there would take her back (onto a platform twice, or onto one she has set off from since it chose that the quickest from there doesn't go onto: knocked back below one, the quickest goes over it again too). Without those two (found in review on 2026-10-21), a trip from 34 to 2 that chose the hops and got onto 17 by the climb past 23's end instead was sent from 17 down to 23 to hop back up, and from 14 walked back off onto 17 for it; replanned at the landings of the quickest route on random trips that chose another way, 186 of 1,240 replans that kept the way went back onto a platform she had been on, none of 889 now. In the harness neither changed a run (the 80 runs with 3 ways below): only 29 replans there kept a way chosen, none past its move or going back; they're for the misses and knocks of the game. The hunt loop's objectives keep their trips' choice, as they keep their weights. A chain the next one is planned on the move from counts its moves as made: before that, from 9, having walked off 5 on the way through 12 from 19 to 3, she jumped back onto 5 to walk off it again (14.2 s flown, 17.1 with the loop).
- **Not in a hurry:** a trip with a deadline goes the quickest way (`go(vary=False)`): the tour's trips for drops and to rest, the hunt loop's for piles.
- The route record of a trip's first plan has the ways it chose among, each way's move, cost and chance, and which it took (`ways`, `chose`); the log says which when it isn't the quickest ("of 3 ways, the one through drop 12->21 (+5%, chance 27%)").
- Computing (`sim.latency`, the tour on 5 seeds of 10 minutes): before a key plan the 99th percentile was 1.98 ms with 3 ways and 1.99 with one, at most 10.5 ms and 3.6 (a trip's first plan, the two searches: 6-8 ms on this map; a replan while its move is still ahead, 2-3 ms).

**Why her routes were fixed.** What step 1's coverage report left to settle, looking for a modelling error first:
- *Not a move's cost.* The hops cost about what the simulator flies them in: from 23 at x 900, 4.89 s with their risk (0.5 s, a guess) against 5.05 flown, and the climb past 23's end 3.81 against 3.93, 1.1 s apart both ways (with no monsters and no noise, the hops chosen by hand). Through 12 the planner is, if anything, on 12's side: 19 -> 3 by 18 and 16 is 13.0 s by the planner and 10.5 flown, up through 12 16.0 and 14.2.
- *Not a move left out by its margins:* every move flow can chain passes `Flow.sure_takeoff` from where it starts (Route coverage).
- *Not the rate rule:* 12 is a poor ground by the spawn data (12.3 EXP a visit; the basin 30, 17 19.5) and by what visits gave live (13.7 EXP a visit over 9; the basin 59.5 over 31, 4 61.0 over 21). Live it was among the hunting grounds (its EXP a second 19% of the basin's, where the cut is 15%) and lost on its value.
- *The weights:* the navigator's comment had each trip's weights let routes within about 35% of the quickest take turns. But a route's draws average out (the mean of n has a spread of 0.35 / sqrt(12 n)), so ways 12% or more apart never swapped, and on today's graph the weights would have sent the 342 live trips of 2026-10-19 to 21 (their first plans) through 12 on 1.1, where 71 had a way through it within reach, and by the hops on 0.3 of 29. Those, and the hunt loop's grounds (which follow their value), kept her ways fixed; the choice among whole ways is for the first.

Its seeds 1, 2, 4 and 10 had no choice of way and came out the same.

- **EXP a minute is the same** on every setting, within 2% either way (standard errors 0.9-1.7%). **Fewer of her drops are picked up** on every one, by 0.6-3.3 points (each 0.3-2 standard errors; with `--ways 3` 1.5 ± 1.2 in the tour and 2.2 ± 1.9 in the loop, and their worth a minute down too). Not the trips for drops: before those went the quickest way, 3 ways cost the tour 1.0 point and the loop 2.5. HP lost is the same or a little lower (0.03-0.14 bars).
- **Her moves widen in the tour:** 5 more distinct moves over the 40 runs and 2.2 more a run, 0.5 more spawn platforms a run, 5 points less of her time on the basin, half again as many moves onto 12, and the hops 4 times for 1. Of the tour's 183 trips that chose (the trips to its stops: those for drops and to rest go the quickest way), 104 had one way within 35%, 79 two or three, and 28 took another than the quickest; the hops were offered on 14, chosen on 3 and made all 3. The hunt loop hardly leaves the basin (31 of 40 runs hunt it alone, where the simulator's monsters come back in 8 s: Respawns and drop life), so 11 of its 40 seeds had no choice of way at all and came out the same as with one way: 79 trips chose, 25 took another way, and of 3 that chose the hops 2 ended in position (a rule called for her) before 23.
- **None passes the bar** on seeds 1-10: in the tour EXP is better on 5-7 of 10 seeds, the worst 16-26% down, and fewer of her drops picked up with each setting; in the hunt loop 2-4 of 10, as 4 of the 10 come out the same (no choice of way), and so can't pass with any route setting. So `ROUTES` stays 1: diversity is a setting to turn on (`--ways 3`), with the defaults the harness had for it (temperature 0.1, the floor 0.2 after 2 minutes, the noise 0.35). (Before the fix to chains followed on, and with the trips for drops choosing too, 3 ways with no floor gave the tour -1.6% ± 1.3% and the loop +1.5% ± 1.4%: that much the noise moves it.)
