- Tour: moves taken 127 -> 132 of 204, never taken 77 -> 72; platform 12: 45 -> 67 visits, 1.6% -> 2.1% of her time, 48 -> 71 moves onto it (29 -> 27 stops at it); through it on the way elsewhere at best 0.04 s quicker than the route chosen (13 x 70 -> 4), within 35% on 15 of 1,063 plans, and the choice would send her through it on 2.5 (the weights 0.9). The hops: planned 5 -> 16, taken 1 -> 4, the climb 83 -> 67.
- Hunt loop: moves taken 84 -> 96, never taken 120 -> 108, spawn platforms reached 15 -> 16 of 16 (7 too); 12 hardly (7 -> 5 visits, 2 moves onto it both); the hops planned 0 -> 12, taken 0 -> 2.
- Live (the 685 plans of 2026-10-19 to 21 on today's graph, each counted as a choice, as the weights' were in Route coverage): through 12 on 13.4 for 1.2, by the hops 25.7 for 1.2. Counting each trip's first plan only (its choice; replans keep it): through 12 on 5.2 of 342 trips for 1.1, by the hops 6.3 for 0.3, before the floor (by which the hops, stale until she has made them, are taken 20% of the time they're offered).

**Ties between grounds** (`hunt.GROUND_TIE`, 0 by default): of the grounds whose score (EXP a second, travel included, varied by 0.75-1.25) is within that share of the best, the one she left longest ago, or never got to, is next. At 0.25 the harness's hunt loops (40 seeds) were the same to the key as with 0, and at 0.1 with 3 ways as 3 ways alone: 31 of the 40 runs take up one ground, the basin, for the whole run. (Grounds she never got to all rank first and equal, so the best of them goes, and in the harness she seldom gets past the basin.) Live, by the value map, 17 and 1 were within 3% of each other from the basin and from 3 (4 ahead of both), and her grounds already varied (4 24 times, 36 20, 17 16, 1 6). Nothing measures it: off, and `tour --loop --ground-tie 0.1` turns it on for a run.

To check in game (none of this has been played):
- `tour --loop --minutes 20 --ways 3`, then `coverage --live`: the route records' `chose` (the first plan of each trip that chooses) show the choice working and the ways it takes, and whether those trips take about what the planner gives them (dearer by their margin: through 12 from 19, 3 s); and no route replanned after a miss or a knock should go back onto a platform she has left (the route records' `from` against the moves before). One run can't measure the rates: in the simulator a 20-minute run has 4-5 trips that choose in the tour and 2 in the loop (15% and 32% of them took another way than the quickest); live, at the 342 trips of 105 minutes of 2026-10-19 to 21, a 20-minute run would go through 12 on about 1 trip and by the hops on about 1. Several runs, against as many without `--ways`, would show whether she picks up as many of her drops (in the simulator 1.5-2.2 points fewer).
- The hops: whether she makes them is `nav 17 --avoid climb` from 23 (Found offline, Ropes in mid-air). How often `--ways 3` takes them: `nav 17 --ways 3` from 23 at x 930 or less, each a fresh navigator, so no floor: about 10% of the time (by the planner's chances over 2,000 draws of the weights: 11% from x 870, 10% from 903, 9% from 930, 8% from 950, 3% from 981, where with no weights there's only the one way), so about 20 tries to see them twice (none in 20: 12%).
- `tour --loop --minutes 20 --ground-tie 0.1` against a run without it: whether she alternates between 17 and 1 (within 3% of each other from the basin and from 3) rather than taking the same one each time.
- If the game agrees, `route.ROUTES` 3 could be the default.

## Perception

| Piece | Does |
|---|---|
| `mobs.py` | Finds snails, slimes, pigs and Orange Mushrooms, and any other kind with a colour gate learned for its map (below). It matches each monster's body-colour silhouette first, then checks the best spots with masked colour templates. The matches run on 6 threads, OpenCV letting go of Python's lock while it matches; which spots get checked doesn't depend on what the checks find, so they're all picked first, and the answers are the same as on one thread, in the same order. 21.6 ms for the fight's band around her and 76 ms for the whole screen (medians on the 17 bench frames), against 92 and 350 on one thread. What step 1 does after each match (windows with too little colour out, the peaks picked) is done in C (`gamelab/native.c`, called through ctypes, which lets go of Python's lock for it): in numpy it held the lock, so the threads took turns at it, 18 of the band's 34 ms (33.5 and 120 ms before it, timed back to back). The C does numpy's arithmetic in numpy's order, so the answers are the same to the bit (on all 31 saved 1920×1080 screenshots, and tests compare them on made-up ones); it's built with MSVC 2022's Build Tools the first time it's needed (`python -m gamelab.native` builds it now; see Motion planning), and without them the search runs in numpy as before (`bench-look` says which). More than 6 threads still don't help: the colour tests before the matches are numpy's. The first pass ignores windows with almost none of the monster's colour (summed from one integral image per kind): their normalised score is noise that can reach a perfect 1.0. The frame is also cut to an even size so the half-size mask is an exact shrink. An odd size (the fight's band was 151 rows) smeared faint colour into blank windows. In the basin, those fake matches took all 12 checks per monster type, so the fight never saw the snails and pigs at her level while a whole-screen look did. That's likely also why one pass over the whole screen once missed three slimes in plain view; whole-screen looks still go band by band. A monster found says which template matched it, and so what that template knows (`sprites.py`): where its feet are, which way it faces (the game's sprites face left; flipped, right) and its pose (standing, walking, flinching). It's placed where its feet are, not at its picture's middle and bottom: a sprite's origin is up to 8.5 units off its picture's middle, a slime's hop frames end 10-17 units above its feet, and the cut-outs were cut off anywhere from 9.5 units above the feet to 16 below. On 15 saved frames where she stands (`bodies`), monsters' feet came out -1.4 to +2.5 units from the surface they stand on (18 of them; sprites +1.4 on average), against -8.5 to +16.4 by the picture's bottom, and +7.7 for a pig on platform 26 480 units above her, whose hop frame matched best though its picture's bottom sat on the surface (the walking frames scored 0.83-0.88 against 0.91); on two recordings with the camera still, a snail's x strayed from a straight line by 1.5 and 1.6 units (rms; at most 4.8 and 5.2) against 2.4 and 3.5 (at most 13.4 and 9.8), when it jumped between a sprite and an off-centre cut-out. The way it faced was the way it moved in 192 of the 199 stretches of 0.6 s where it walked (the misses at turns). For the continuous feed a monster seen before is re-found 16 px around where it should be (`refind`): with the template that matched it last, 0.69 ms, else with its kind's templates in that window, 3.4 ms; on the 17 saved frames 84 of 84 were re-found where they were, and 84 of 84 moved 8 px. At the game's own 1366x768 the search is coarse to fine: step 1 at this scale, step 2 at full size around each place with several frames a place (see Screen size). Since 2026-10-27 step 1 is all in C (`gamelab/search.c`: the shrink, the colour tests, each silhouette scored exactly where the cover test keeps a window, the peaks and the places) and the gate's and checks' matches go in a few calls: a crowd's whole screen 115 ms of CPU on one thread to 20 (about 22 since the reviews: where OpenCV's noise could decide, those shapes master's way), master's answers (A cheaper whole screen). |
| `sprites.py` | Templates for the monsters on the current map, made from the game's own sprites (every stand, move and hit frame) at their on-screen size, with what the game data says of each frame (`index.json`: its origin, the point that stands on the monster's feet, its body's box, its head, how long it shows). They're added to the screenshot cut-outs in `assets/mobs/`, which still catch monsters half hidden in plants. Each cut-out is matched once against its kind's sprites, both ways (`cutouts.json`): all 11 matched a frame at 0.86-0.98 (the other way round 0.29-0.52), which gives where their monster's feet are and which way it faces; under 0.85 a cut-out would stand on its middle and bottom instead. The four pig cut-outs are all the hop frame cut off 9.5 units above the feet, and three slime cut-outs reach 14-16 units below them (grass). Built on first use and kept with the other extracted data (git-ignored). At the game's own 1366x768 the templates are the game's pictures as they are, alpha and all (`sprites_x1`), and the cut-outs aren't used (see Screen size). |
| `spawns.py` | Monsters fading in at their spawn points (`SpawnWatch`, from 2026-11-01): every spawn point in view on every frame whose view was registered on it, the frame against the map's own art there (localization.mapart: nothing learned), a blend of the point's kind's first pictures (stand/0, move/0, both ways, its feet within 4 units of the point) fitted exactly, a newborn where its alpha is 0.02 or more, 1 - R2 0.008 or less and the residual 1.5 colour levels or less; each newborn then followed in its stand, move and hit1 pictures until the whole screen finds it, its alpha in each sighting (`Mob.fading`). The sums in C (`gamelab/spawns.c`, integer, the same as numpy's). No false positive on the 153,474 labelled point-frames of Tree Dungeon's lossless clips; 229 of the 233 newborns whose start shows found at their first visible frame (the median), 7 frames sooner than the whole screen. Of record, master's frame step against this one's on every usable recording (92 minutes): the whole screen's detections unchanged on every frame, none of the 1,477 sightings false, all 233 reported at frame 0 at the median (master 7, 469 ms), the pass 1.1 ms longer at the median (11.7 against 10.6). After the review: a newborn's first sighting at alpha 0.8 at most (`A_START`), Tree Dungeon alone (`MEASURED` by map), points past the screen's top or sides looked at in what shows, a picture fading out followed no further, the hand-over by kind, a newborn never on the track of the one before it at its point; no false positive on any recording, every negative an onset could start from 14 times off the rule or more on the clips (5.2 under a 20% shade), the pass 1.7 ms longer at the median. See Spawns seen as they fade in. |
| `loot.py`, `drops.py` | Finds drops on the ground: what the map's monsters drop (on the first map Squishy Liquid, Slime Bubble, Leather, Pig's Head, Pig's Ribbon, Orange Mushroom Cap, Snail Shell; another map's from `drops.py`, below), the potions monsters this level drop (Red, Orange, White and Blue Potion), and bronze and gold mesos (3 spinning frames each; a coin found says which it is, `Item.coin`: their amount picks it). Templates are the game's own item pictures at their on-screen size, scaled by their opaque pixels only. A spot counts when the masked template matches (0.6) and its colours differ from the template's by at most 24 on average, checked where the picture covers whole pixels. The sea and island backdrop matched the Blue Potion's shape at 0.60-0.63, and UI buttons the White Potion's; they differed by 27-57, real drops by 12-19. Only a strip just above each platform is searched (drops lie on the ground), on 8 threads (3 since 2026-10-26: CPU), every strip's templates at once: 6.0 ms for her platform, 54 for every platform in view (medians on the 30 saved screenshots that place her, with and without mesos only), against 8.5 and 89 strip by strip on 4 threads, with the same drops in all 120 searches. On 110 saved frames it found all 18 drops and nothing else. Drops lay on the ground about 2 s after her EXP went up, and monsters are drawn in front of them. At the game's own 1366x768 the templates are the game's pictures as they are, and the shapes are matched on brightness alone, the colours checked as here (see Screen size). |
| `nametag.py` | Her name tag, matched at full resolution (at half size the score swings between ~0.6 and ~0.9). Of the good matches in the play area, the one nearest where she was wins: her name also shows in the minimap, the bottom bar and the party list. A look searches within 240 px across and 120 down of where she was found last first: 3.4 ms, against 37 for the whole play area (`bench-look`, 17 saved frames, the same answers on all of them). The whole play area is searched when she isn't there (a warp, the tag hidden), and every 30th look anyway, so a wrong match can't stick. Since 2026-10-26 (CPU) a look searches within 80 px across and 40 down first (1.6 ms; then the 240 and 120). |
| `plate.py`, `poses.py` | Her name plate's exact colours counted where her tag's gray match isn't sure, and her body by her poses where her plate doesn't show (from 2026-10-29; their inner loops in C, `gamelab/locate.c`; the service's from 2026-10-30, `localization/locate.py`): Her place by her plate and her body, Her place from the scene. |
| `exp_number.py` | Her EXP number read, glyph by glyph, by drawing the game's own glyphs as the game draws them and keeping a reading only when every cell is clearly its glyph and the percent fits her level's requirement (see Her EXP number): all 32 saved frames and 19 saved crops of the bar read right, 8.6 ms a reading, only when the number changes. |
| `hp_number.py` | Her HP number, "[624/840]", read as her EXP number is (the same glyphs and exact path: `exp_number.Layout`), whenever its box changes: her HP and max HP in HP for the safety stop (The safety stop in HP). |
| `hud.py` | HP and MP from the bar colours; her EXP number, which only changes when she gains EXP (read only then); a monster's HP bar (its frame matched above the monster, its green rows read: Monster HP bars, below; 0.5 ms at 1366x768, 0.8 at half size of 1920x1080); the purple MISS or damage numbers when a monster touches her. |
| `minimap.py`, `terrain.py` | Her yellow minimap dot, and other players' (see Other players); the ground under her; ropes and ladders on screen. Ropes are looked for only where the map's ropes can show: Senses hands perception the columns, 52 px either side of where her dot puts each (`ROPE_PAD`: all a rope can be off and still place her). 4.2 ms a look, against 31.4 for the whole screen with the rope colour test in numpy as before (in OpenCV now: the same pixels, checked on every colour; the whole screen 19) and 8.4 before each column was copied out of the screen for its colour test (OpenCV split a column viewed in place 8 times slower) and the shapes were made only in the box around the rope colour's pixels (58% of a column) and connected only around what was left of them (9%): the same ropes on all 31 saved 1920×1080 screenshots, over the whole screen and in random columns, and on 3,000 made-up strips. On 17 saved frames the ropes seen were 0-20 px from where her dot put them, and the same as on the whole screen. |
| `lie_detector.py` | The Lie Detector's six forms (see above). A check of the screen takes 64.5 ms (the player's, 4 times a second, about 3 until 2026-10-24: The Lie Detector's recordings; 73.6 before its capture was turned into a picture of its own and the title's yellow tested in OpenCV, with the same scores). Most of it is matching the title's letters (about 35 ms) and the two half-size forms (about 19). The notice and the quiz's two forms (2026-10-25) add about 9 ms each, whatever a template's size: on a 1366x768 frame with the PC busy, 99-103 ms a check against 75-78 without them, about 0.4 of a core at 4 a second. Since 2026-10-26 the watchdog's looks match each form only around where it has always shown, 7 looks in 8, on a frame of the game's own size with its picture where it belongs (`near`, 11 ms; CPU). |

**Monster HP bars** (`hud.hp_bar`, from 2026-10-25). The bar a monster shows once it's hurt, as the game draws it at
1366x768 (game px; the saved frames and the rolling recorder's clips of 2026-10-24 and 25): a white frame 50 x 8 between
two black ones, and inside the fill, 46 x 4: three rows green (0, 255, 0) for the HP left over a red one (170, 0, 0),
then the latest damage, red fading to dark red, and the HP lost black; its frame's top-left 25 left of the monster's
centre and 29 above its picture's top on 567 of the 575 bars paired with a mushroom the detector found within 6 px (25
above on 6 Horny Mushrooms, 33 once, 26 left once; 3 more bars of the clips sat 10-13 px right of the nearest Horny
Mushroom found, perhaps over one it missed, and read only for the search's 14 px either side; at 1920x1080 the pigs'
25-30 game px above, the slimes', whose pictures change height as they bounce, 0-30). A party member's bar over a player
is the same filled red, and a monster's as it dies all red and black.
- **Why every bar read empty:** the reader took the longest run of pure green, black and dark red in a row above the
  monster for the fill. At 1366x768 the black frame outside the white one is 52 px of pure black, longer than the
  fill's 48: of 567 labelled bars 488 read 0 and 64 none (the run read was the black frame on 375 of the 503 read, the
  black rows inside on 53, the red row under the green on 49), and the scenery's 1-px black outlines read as empty bars
  over 267 of 2207 monsters with none. At half size of 1920x1080 the black rows blend into the white or not by where the
  bar falls in a look's px: 111 of 162 bars of the first map's recordings read 0 (and live on 2026-10-21 a third of the
  bars read 0). The simulator drew a bar of its own, grey around green and black, which read right.
- **Now** the bar is found by its frame: the frame's least colour (white high; the black frames and the fill, green, red
  or black, all low) matched against the bar's (`TM_CCOEFF_NORMED`, 0.75: at 1366x768 0.75-1.0 on the 805 bars found
  in the frames, 3 of them under 0.78, and 0.73 at most around a monster with none, a margin of only 0.02; at half size
  of 1920x1080 0.86 and up on the bars, 0.62 at most around none), drawn at the look's scale for each place a game px
  can fall in a px (quarters across, halves down: `_bar_frames`), around where it's expected from the monster (14 game
  px either side, 12 above, 31 below). Of the places matching about as well as the best (0.1), the nearest is read (the
  frame slid along its own long rows matches less well: a slime's slid 7 half-size px matched 0.81 against 0.99,
  nearer, and read 0.97 for 0.74). The HP
  left is green from the left to the last green column (green over red and blue by 60, blue under half of it: a vine's
  mint green over a bar isn't, a glow's yellow tint is), whatever covers the rest of its rows (a damage number over the
  frame's top, sparkles, the red of the latest damage), its blended edge at half size counted by how green it is. If
  what's after the green isn't red or black (little green and blue in all four rows) something covers the end, and
  it's read halfway along that to the first red or black after it (on the clips 0.45, 0.73 and 0.47, where the next
  frame without the cover read 0.46, 0.72 and 0.50). No green: None.
- **Measured** on the labelled bars (`tests/fixtures/hp_bars`, a bar over each monster the detector found, its fill
  counted by pixel): at 1366x768 564 of 565 with the end in view within half a px (0.001 off on average; before 0.540,
  487 read 0, 63 none), 1 of 1 with the end covered within the range it's in, the 408 monsters without one of their own
  none (before 47 read empty); at half size of 1920x1080 161 of 162 within a px (0.003; before 0.518, 111 read 0, 15
  none), 16 of 16 with the end covered, none of the 131 monsters without one (before 3). Two labels were put right on
  review: a full bar whose end a vine covers (its mint green counted as green) is 38 of 46 px green, the HP lost's black
  after it, as in the frames either side; a pig's bar under a damage number's purple halo, labelled with no green, is
  0.675 green. 0.5 ms a monster at 1366x768, 0.8 ms at half size (0.2 before). Since 2026-10-28 (test data,
  `tests/testdata.py`) the 1366x768 clips are gone, pruned from `lab/recent` by the rolling recorder: the test checks the
  3 frames left in `lab/shots` (2 bars within half a px, 4 monsters with none) and skips the rest saying they need a new
  capture; and Tree Dungeon's 24 frames of 2026-10-28, whose 118 monsters have no bar (she didn't attack, and the bar
  over a monster others hit isn't shown to her; 18 flinching or dying under their hits, damage numbers and skills over
  many): none read. The 1920x1080 frames are the set `hp_bars_1920x1080` (the recordings' labelled frames and the 9
  screenshots, copied out of `gamelab/lab`).
- **In the simulator** the bars are drawn as the game draws them (`hud.draw_hp_bar`, at the half-size look's blend), and
  `--world bars-empty` (`Realism.bars_empty`) reads every bar up as empty, as live did before.

**Monsters with no hand-made colour test: learned gates** (from 2026-10-24; `perception/gates.py`, `mobs.py`,
`sprites.learn_background`, `learn-colours`). Step 1 looks for a kind only where its body's colour is, and the first
map's four kinds have that test written by hand (`mobs.PALETTES`). The next maps' monsters weren't looked for at all,
and by hand their tests would be hard to write: West Rocky Mountain II's stumps are browns like its rock, and Tree
Dungeon's mushrooms stand in a green forest, a Green Mushroom's cap pale green and a Horny Mushroom's grey-blue over the
same beige stem. Now a kind without one gets a gate learned from data:
- **Its colours** are its own pictures' pixels as step 1 sees them (the game's sprites shrunk to step 1's scale, as the
  detector makes them, at either window size), as drawn and blended toward the fog's white (`gates.FOG_ALPHAS`, 0.7 and
  0.4: West Rocky Mountain II's drifting fog; at 1920x1080 half size on 2026-10-23, red snails under it went from 48 to
  53 of 57 found with the blends). Tree Dungeon has no fog, and they cost nothing there: without them its gates took
  half as much of its background (0.76% for the two kinds together, against 1.63%) and a Horny Mushroom of the 17 in
  plain view was missed.
- **The background's** are the play area of saved frames of the map (above the HUD) at step 1's scale, with the
  monsters on them cut out (`sprites.learn_background`): they're found with gates learned against the frames as they
  are, monsters and all, then again with gates learned without the ones found, each one's picture cut out 6 game px
  around (`CUT_PAD`, `CUT_ROUNDS`).
- A colour, binned 5 bits a channel (32,768 colours), is the kind's where its share of the kind's pixels (as drawn or
  any blend) is 5 times its share of the background's or more (`gates.RATIO`). On West Rocky Mountain II's labelled
  frames (below) ratios of 3, 5, 8 and 12 found 55, 56, 56 and 57 of the 58 in plain view at 1366x768, but 164, 167, 164
  and 137 of the 203 on its 1920x1080 frames shrunk to that size; each stump's gate took about 5.5%, 4.2%, 3.2% and 2.2%
  of the background.
- `python -m gamelab learn-colours --map ID FRAMES` (saved frames of the map at any window size, or folders of them)
  keeps a map's background counts in `assets/backgrounds/<map id>.npz` (in git: 23 and 28 KB; the frames stay out of
  it), and the map's detector learns its gates from them as it's made (`sprites.detector_for`); with none kept for a
  map, its kinds without a hand-made test aren't looked for, as before. So the next map onboards the same way: its
  sprites are built from the game data on first use, a few frames of it are saved, and `learn-colours` is run once.
  Tree Dungeon's came from its 20 frames (53 monsters cut out; its gates take 0.98% and 1.22% of its background),
  West Rocky Mountain II's from its 133 frames at 1920x1080 and 31 at 1366x768 (667 cut out; each stump's gate takes
  3.8-4.4%, the Red Snail's 0.4%).

Everything below goes for the learned kinds only: the first map's four, their tests, templates and searches are as they
were, and the 86 golden traces are byte-identical.
- **One lookup a pixel:** each colour bin's byte has a bit for each learned kind (`gates.Gates`), so step 1 bins each
  pixel once and looks it up once for all of them (1.5-1.8 ms a band at 1366x768, on one thread).
- **The whole screen's bands overlap by the tallest picture** and step 2's slack (an Axe Stump's flinch is 93 game px
  tall, a band's overlap 43 at 1366x768), so one standing across a band's edge is whole in the next band. The bands
  are every kind's, so on a map with learned kinds the first map's kinds go by them too (on the first map, with none,
  they're as they were): on Tree Dungeon they overlap by the mushrooms' 56 rows and 9, and of 927 slimes drawn standing
  on its footholds (any frame of theirs, both ways, on its 19 frames from 28) the whole screen's search found 923, all
  117 on platform 30, whose surface lies on a band's edge (59 of 82 there with the bands as they were, in the map's
  study); overlapping by the slime's hop frame and the slack (93 rows), 925.
- **The fine gate tries a place's first two templates** (`mobs.GATE_TRIES`), not only its first. A stump's frames'
  silhouettes match a blob of its colour about alike, its flinch frame's (the largest) most often best, and gated with
  it a place failed where its own frame, the place's second or third, would have passed: on West Rocky Mountain II's
  1366x768 frames the places of Stumps and Axe Stumps in plain view scored 0.29-0.46 with the flinch frame and 0.67-0.77
  with their own (then 0.94-1.00 at full size). Gated with the first alone, 53 of the 58 in plain view were found (143
  of the 203 on the 1920x1080 frames shrunk), in 91 ms a whole screen; with the first two, 56 (167), in 106.
- **Kinds of one shape are searched as one** (`MobDetector.units`, `SAME_SHAPE` 0.9 of the larger picture's pixels in
  common, set on their feet): Horny and Green Mushroom are one sprite with two caps (95%), Stump and Dark Stump one in
  two colours (100%). They're searched by their gates together, with one silhouette a frame for both kinds (half step
  1's matches for the mushrooms), one set of places, and at each place step 2 checks each kind's picture side by side,
  the better kept. Searched apart, each kind made a place at the same monster and gated and checked it there, and a
  look where only one kind's gate fired there could have named a Green Mushroom a Horny one: the other kind's picture
  scores 0.82-0.92 on a mushroom (median 0.895, on the labels), where `THRESHOLD` is 0.6. Together, Tree Dungeon's whole
  screen took 65 ms against 81 apart (2026-10-24, alternating), finding the same; West Rocky Mountain II's 106 against
  110, finding 56 of the 58 in plain view against 57 (and 167 of the 203 on the frames shrunk, against 170).
- **An Axe Stump by its axe:** a Stump's picture matches the stump that is all of an Axe Stump but its axe about as well
  as the Axe Stump's own picture does (0.94 and 0.94 on most), so by the score alone 10 of the 40 Axe Stumps in plain
  view were taken for Stumps. A monster found as a kind that shares its body with one searched apart (`twins`: 80% of
  the larger picture's pixels in common; an Axe Stump and a Stump 85%, a Red Snail inside a Stump 32-38%) is checked as
  those at its feet (`mobs._pick_kind`): a picture with parts of its own (10% of its pixels outside the others', an Axe
  Stump's axe 15%) is the monster's only where those parts alone match 0.6 (`OWN_MATCH`), and then over the pictures it
  holds; otherwise the best score. On the 1920x1080 frames (shrunk, and at half size) an Axe Stump's axe matched
  0.83-0.97 on 39 of the 40 in plain view (one at 0.25), its place on a Stump or a Dark Stump -0.6 to 0.70 (one at 0.70,
  the next 0.52).
- **A track is re-found as its own kind only** (`MobDetector.refind`, `_its_kind`; at the game's own size). A monster
  followed is re-found with the picture that matched it last, and a kind's picture fits a monster of a kind that shares
  its body nearly as well. At each labelled mushroom and stump of the 1366x768 frames whose frame the labels give, the
  other kinds' pictures of it, re-found there, scored over `THRESHOLD` on all but 4: a Horny Mushroom's 0.79-0.90 on the
  Greens (median 0.895), a Green's 0.72-0.92 on the Hornies (0.912), a Dark Stump's 0.84-0.98 on the Stumps and Axe
  Stumps (0.979), a Stump's 0.86-1.00 on the Axe Stumps (1.00: its picture is all of theirs but the axe) and an Axe
  Stump's 0.66-0.89 on the Stumps (0.807). So the other kind's track re-found 52 of the 55 mushrooms and 115 of the 116
  re-finds asked of the stumps: a Horny's track would have gone on on a Green walking past or standing where it died.
  Now a monster re-found as such a kind is checked side by side with the other kinds' pictures of its frame, set on its
  feet, as a search tells them (`_pick_kind`), and isn't re-found where another kind's is the monster's: 0 of the 55
  and 0 of the 116, its own kind's track re-finding 53 of the 55 and 58 of the 58 as before (the two not re-found, a
  Horny standing on the chat box's border, its feet on row 700). The other kinds' pictures are matched where they lie
  on the monster's, not searched around, in numpy (`mobs._score`: OpenCV's masked score to 1e-9, 0.1 ms a picture,
  where OpenCV takes 0.73 for one place and 1.1-1.5 for 4 px around): the check takes 0.40 ms a mushroom and 0.85 a
  stump (medians on one thread, with other work sharing the CPU), where matched as a search does they took 1.36 and
  4.49. Where one kind's picture lies on another's is worked out once (`MobDetector.aligned`: the shift, 2 px at most,
  at which their masks overlap most, `mobs.ALIGN`): an Axe Stump's move/1 and move/3 lie a px across from a Stump's set
  on their origins, and checked there, 27 of the 40 Axe Stumps failed their axe's test. A track turned away goes on to
  its kind's whole set in the window, as one not found does (18-23 ms here), until it's taken for hidden (0.3 s,
  `tracking.MISSING_S`). From one labelled frame of a run to the next, each monster of these kinds the whole screen's
  search found re-found where it was: on Tree Dungeon 15 on their kind with the check and without; on West Rocky
  Mountain II 14 on their kind either way, and without the check an Axe Stump's track on a Stump and a Stump's on an
  Axe Stump too. `bench-look`'s feed step (her place and the monsters re-found), with the check and without it in
  turn, twice, with other work loading the CPU (its medians a third over the table's below): Tree Dungeon 33.9 and 34.2
  ms against 32.1 and 32.7, West Rocky Mountain II 36.9 and 37.8 against 33.4 and 30.3. At 1920x1080 half size
  re-finds go as they did: there the axe's test failed on 3 of the 81 Axe Stumps drawn and re-found as their next frame
  (`bench-paste`). The axe's test is worked out by `_score` in the search too: the same on every labelled frame, in the
  table below.

**The HUD's top** (`screen.Geometry.hud_top`). Monsters and drops are looked for above the HUD, and `HUD_TOP` (0.88 of
the height) put it at row 675 at 1366x768, where the chat box starts at row 700 (its dark border, from x 283 to 1080,
on every 1366x768 frame of both maps; at 1920x1080 at screen row 984-985, game row 700.2). At 1366x768 the search now
goes down to row 700 (`HUD_TOP_GAME`), and so do her band, the re-finds' bounds, the drops' strips and the view a scene
records: on Tree Dungeon those 25 rows hold platforms 31 and 32 seen from 28 (the Horny Mushroom on 31 stands half under
the chat bar there, its feet at rows 701-718, and still isn't looked for). At 1920x1080 it's as it was (the simulator
draws its world at that size, and the scenes it records go by it; the game isn't run at that size any more). Searching
the 25 rows more cost nothing measurable: the first map's whole screen took 89-98 ms either way (`bench-look --shrink
1366x768`, two runs each).

**On the labelled frames** (whole-screen searches; a monster counts as found where one is within 10 game px of its
feet; in plain view: not hidden, flinching, spawning, dying, faded, in fog or behind vines):

|---|---|---|---|---|
| labelled (in the rows searched); in plain view | 78 (57); 44 | 116; 58 | 287; 203 | 287; 203 |
| the background learned on | the other run of frames (14 or 6) | the 91 1920x1080 frames not labelled | those 91 and the 31 at 1366x768 | the same |
| found in plain view | 44 of 44 (Horny 17, Green 27) | 56 of 58 (Axe Stump 40 of 40, Stump 16 of 18) | 172 of 203 (Stump 55 of 67, Dark Stump 28 of 39, Axe Stump 35 of 40, Red Snail 54 of 57) | 167 of 203 (52, 27, 36, 52) |
| ... of all of them | 53 of 57 | 71 of 116 | 175 of 287 | 169 of 287 |
| of the wrong kind | none | none in plain view (1 of the others: a body facing right under an axe drawn facing left, labelled unsure) | 2 | 1 |
| found that aren't there | none (with 52 players, 38 pets, all orange snails named Snail, and their name tags on the frames) | none (another player fighting the stumps, his hits' sparks, her pet, ropes, vines) | none of these kinds (6 of the first map's Orange Mushrooms on rock, as before at this size) | none |

**What a look costs** (`bench-look` on the 17 saved frames, medians in ms; each pair of columns from runs back to back on 2026-10-20, the first 5 looks at each frame, the second 3 rounds of 3 alternating; offline, so the grab itself comes on top: 16.7 ms with mss, which waits for the compositor's next frame; with DXGI the wait for the screen's next frame, 8 ms on average at 60 frames a second, and copying it off the graphics card takes about 1 ms more than converting a saved frame):

| | at first | after the first speedups | the same, timed again | now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Eyes.look` (her tag, HP and MP, the ground, her dot, ropes, EXP) | 87.7 | 14.6 | 13.9 | 9.2 |
| `Senses.look` without monsters (the navigator's look placing her) | 88.7 | 16.0 | 17.0 | 12.9 |
| ... with the monsters in her band (a fight's look) | 180.7 | 48.0 | 48.4 | 31.8 |
| ... and the drops on her platform (the hunt loop's) | 199.6 | 62.6 | 62.4 | 43.0 |
| ... the whole screen and every drop in view | 562.5 | 229.4 | 237.1 | 162.9 |

Where it went: the capture was viewed as RGB in place, and every OpenCV call on it copied it first (8.9 ms for the half-size frame alone, now 0.9); her name tag was matched over the whole play area (46.0, now 3.4 near where she was); ropes were looked for over the whole screen with numpy's colour tests (31.4, now 8.6 where the map's can show); the monster search ran on one thread (the band 92.0, the whole screen 349.7; now 33.5 and 122.0 on 6); a monster's HP bar was read pixel by pixel (0.50, now 0.20). Then (the last two columns): each rope column was split viewed in place (8.6, now 4.3); the monster search's numpy work after each match held Python's lock (the band 34.1, now 22.5 with it in C; the whole screen 127.9, now 78.1); drops were searched strip by strip on 4 threads (see Where the time goes). Every answer is the same as before on all 17 frames. With the grab, the look placing her should take about 25 ms in game with DXGI (33 with mss) instead of 110; not measured there yet (`bench-look --live`).

**Capturing the game** (`gamelab/capture.py`, a shared module; `[capture] method` in config.toml, `"dxgi"` by default). mss copies the screen with GDI, which waits for the compositor's next frame: 16.7 ms a grab whatever the box's size, 17-46 ms after a pause, so a glance (two grabs) took 33 ms. DXGI desktop duplication (through ctypes, no new packages) is handed each frame as the monitor shows it, with when it was shown (QueryPerformanceCounter's ticks, the clock `time.monotonic` reads); the frame is copied into a texture of its own on the graphics card, and boxes of it are copied off the card as they're asked for. A frame comes only when the screen changes, so the last one is the screen as it is until another comes. Since 2026-10-27 a box's copy off the card can be waited for on a fence's event before Map, which otherwise waits by spinning a driver thread: 4 ms of CPU a frame less on a texture holding a saved frame, the frame 0.15-0.2 ms later (`[capture] fence`, false by default till it's tried live; The re-finds' GPU, twice as fast, below).
- A look waits for a frame shown after it began, as with mss (a look sees what came of the keys sent before it): up to 20 ms (`FRESH_WAIT_S`), a frame of the game's 16.7 ms and the ~2 ms a frame comes after the time it was shown; when none comes by then, nothing on screen has changed and the frame held is the screen as it is. It was 15 ms at first, shorter than a frame: against a duplication presenting every 16.7 ms with its frames coming 0-2 ms late, 6-18% of looks got the frame shown 1-3 ms before they began (now none, `tests/test_capture.py`). With nothing on screen changing, a 20 ms wait lasts 31 ms (the timer's ticks, below); a frame that comes ends it at once. A glance takes its minimap box and HP row from the newest frame, without waiting.
- Measured on this PC's desktop with the game not running (`bench-capture`: a 1920x1080 box of the 3840x2160 monitor, one corner of it changing 30-60 times a second; 100 rounds, medians): a look's capture, RGB, 12.4 ms against 24.5 with mss, of which the frame came 5.6 ms after the look began; a glance 1.0 ms against 33.7. With nothing on screen changing, a look's capture took 25 ms against 22 (with the 15 ms wait of then; with 20 ms, about 34 by the same ticks, not measured), as the wait for a frame that doesn't come ends on Windows' 15.6 ms timer ticks (a 1-15 ms timeout took 16 ms, 17-20 ms took 31). Copying the whole box off the card and converting it took 2.0 ms (3.8 copied first and then converted). The pixels were mss's exactly wherever the screen didn't change between the two grabs. Over 10,000 glances and 1,000 looks the process's memory went from 148.5 to 151.1 MB and was flat over the last 7,500 glances.
- The first frame after duplicating starts is black, with no present time: frames without one (also those where only the mouse pointer moved) don't count, and the first real one came 12 ms later even with nothing changing. Duplicating is lost on a UAC prompt, a mode change or a full-screen switch and is then started again (180-240 ms); anything else that fails falls back to mss, and DXGI is tried again 10 s later. A monitor can be duplicated only once in a process (a second DuplicateOutput was refused), so the process shares one grabber. Boxes are in the monitor's physical pixels: like mss, the grabber makes the process DPI-aware first. A game window across two monitors is grabbed with mss.
- Glances still start 63 ms apart at the soonest (`GLANCE_EVERY_S` in `perception/eyes.py`), the pace mss's two grabs and the navigator's 30 ms between glances gave: what the navigator makes of glances in a row (her dot standing still, so cutting a plan off its path and `recover`) was set at that pace, and the simulator charges it. It's judged in time now (Control: a route), so it would mean the same at any pace; without a feed glances keep this one, since the simulator charges a glance mss's 35 ms and can't say what a faster one would do, and with a feed every frame didn't pay (Continuous perception: Glances at the feed's rate).
- The elevated key player keeps mss (its Lie Detector watchdog included): it loads as little as it can. Not tried in game yet: `bench-capture` and `bench-look --live --capture dxgi` (or `mss`) measure it there.

**Capture checks: looks that aren't of the game** (from 2026-10-24; `perception/framecheck.py`, `localization/placecheck.py`, `Eyes.recover`, `Senses._take` and `regain`). At 16:46:50 a hunt on Tree Dungeon (`tour --loop --skill`) read her place off the map from its first look (x 950 on a map whose camera stops at 410, platform none) and for two minutes sent a plan off a rope every 5 s, 25 of them: nothing asked whether a look made sense. Every one of its 1,148 looks had read her dot without the map's minimap picture, with the first map's origin (Localization; the offline repro of two saved frames gives the telemetry's places to 0.1 unit), and why the picture was missing in that process isn't known: `mapdata.minimap_picture` swallowed whatever kept it from loading, and nothing logged it. At 16:48:44-48 the user moved the game window, and four looks were of a frame offset from the client area (+26,+26: the window's own title bar in the top rows; -5,+6); at 16:55:33 a look captured another program's window over the game. Now a look is checked before anything is read from it, one that fails is never handed on, and what's wrong is said in words:

Only a frame failing both anchors is looked at: of the 29,416 saved 1366x768 frames (20,782 distinct), 359 (245 distinct), 216 of them the fault (the 215 of the player's recording at 00:29:02-00:29:55 on 2026-10-26, as the capture shows it, black under the HUD: `tests/fixtures/capture/tree_002902_drawn.png`; and the frame of 23:40) and drawn, all at (-18, -85); none of the other 143 (30 distinct: black map changes, the drag of 16:48, 16:55:33, countdown frames shrunk from 1920x1080), with no frame known or at the insets of 100-300% (the review's scan, `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/winfix/review-detect/fp_lab.csv`, `fp_scratch.csv`); the cash shop, the login and character screens, a game window over both anchors aren't saved yet. 12.5 ms at most, on frames that fail both anchors only |

Both anchors are drawn by the game at the same pixels on any map; at 1920x1080 (and in the simulator) they aren't measured and aren't checked. Their cost on a good frame is 0.04-0.07 ms; a frame that fails also has the HUD's border searched 48 px each way to say how far it's off (about 5 ms, only then): the frames of 16:48 come out +26,+26 and -5,+6, as the minimap window and the quest box matched by hand had them. Across, the border's end nearer where it should be counts: something over one end (a game window over x 1080) only shortens it, and with the minimap closed too such a frame was "offset by (+0, +0)", which reopened the capture for nothing; it's the minimap now. A look costs about 0.3 ms more in all; a glance one more box (80 x 18 px), 0.03 ms to compare it, and the window's checks.

**When one fails.** `Eyes.look` raises `BadLook` (a `Problem`: its kind and why). `Senses` takes the look again 0.2 s later (`RETRY_GAP_S`), after `Eyes.recover`: the minimap's picture and her name tag are searched for afresh; when the capture itself may be at fault (the frame offset, or old) the duplication is opened afresh at the first such failure since a frame last passed, mss takes over for 10 s at the second (`Grabber.reopen`, `fall_back`), and the two again in turn every 5 s while they last (`CAPTURE_AGAIN_S`; going by the failures of any kind in a row, a drag that failed first as "moved" and left the capture lagging was never reopened); a window moving is waited out. While the window is unfit in a way only the user sets right (`framecheck.WAIT_KINDS`: another size, partly off the screen, gone, or minimized while waiting already), a look asks the window alone (`Eyes.window_wait`): it doesn't capture or bring the game to the front, where a hunt standing still on a resized window used to pull the game over whatever the user was doing twice a second; a game closed or crashed is waited for the same way, where it stopped the hunt. A look that fails isn't placed, the camera learns nothing from it, the other players are kept, and the listeners (her EXP and HP, the mini-map's telemetry) never see it. After 3 s of failing (`LOST_S`; the drag of 16:48 gave four bad looks in 4.1 s), `Senses.look` raises `LookLost`: the hunt loop stands still, sends nothing, takes a look every 0.5 s (`Senses.regain`) and hunts on when one passes, or ends at its time as before. Its own clocks move on by the pause (`Hunt._paused`: time without progress, the objective's and its trip's, the ground's and her spot's, and on a rope her time up there and the wait before another, Positioning), so it isn't booked as hunting time or as no progress (a pause of 125 s ended the simulator's hunt as stuck on the first look after it, and a shorter one dropped the objective at once); the game's own (respawns, drops) aren't moved. A navigator's trip stands still the same way (`Navigator.go`: the `nav` command, a trip to rest, the tour's stops), up to its deadline, or the hunt's end for the hunt loop's trip to rest, which then stops the hunt as a pass does (`stand_until`; before, a hunt could stand past its end by up to the trip's 180 s; its last trip, to stand by after its end, stands up to its own deadline), the deadline moving on by the pause, as the time its chains have stopped short of a monster does (`TripState.paused`; the escorted trips' `MEET_S`), a look taken before it not used; the climb from Tree Dungeon's floor to its top with every look failing from 4 s to 16 s stood still from 9.0 s, sent nothing, and arrived after (`tests/test_framecheck.py`); a trip the hunt loop drives a pass at a time pauses with the hunt. A pet check that meets a look failing its checks presses nothing on it and tries again 90 s later (`PetCare.check`; it used to stop the hunt); any other command stops with the reason, as a navigator's trip cancels the plans it sent on any error. A glance that fails (the window as above, or the title strip) has no dot and keeps the last HP read, so a running plan isn't cut on its account (its look after it is checked). In the simulator, every look failing from 20 s to 35 s into the hunt loop on Tree Dungeon (with positioning and the escorted trips, as merged): the first look failed at 20.7 s, no plan went out from then until they passed (a throw decided on the last good look went at 20.6 s, the next plan at 35.3 s), standing still from 24.0 s, and hunting on after (`tests/test_framecheck.py`). The log says it so, and the telemetry has each as an `event` (kinds `look`, `lost`, `window`):
- `a look failed its checks: the capture is offset by (+26, +26) px from the game's client area (the window moving while it was captured?)`, `... then: the game window moved while it was captured: (2446, 146) -> (2472, 172)`
- `the game window moved: (2446, 146) -> (2472, 172)` (between two looks that passed)
- `standing still: the game's client is 1396x1952, not 1366x768: waiting for it to be set back (it isn't resized here) (nothing is sent until the game looks as expected again)`
- `standing still: her minimap dot puts her at (950, -910), off the map (x -360..410, y -2070..460): the minimap's picture not found where it is, or another map`
- `the game looks as expected again (15.0 s after a look failed)`

**A client of the wrong size, or the game drawing off it, set right with Alt+Enter twice** (built on 2026-10-24 on `work/window-recover`, never merged; ported onto the perception service on 2026-10-26: `control/window_size.py`, `Senses.window_fix`, `window --recover`). At about 19:55 on 2026-10-24 the client was another size, the cause not known, and the user asked for the way they set it back by hand: "use alt + enter to enter full screen mode, then use alt + enter again to return to window-ed mode". On 2026-10-25 at 23:21 the game was full screen at 3840x2160 for about a minute; at 23:40 the client was the right size, 1366x768 at (2454, 107) (DPI 300%, the window 2436,22..3838,893), and the game drew its picture 18 px left and 85 up, at the window's corner (`tests/fixtures/capture/tree_234040_drawn.png`): the minimap's title strip cut off, the HUD's border on row 615, and "the capture doesn't show the game where its window is" on every look, a hunt standing still for ever. Alt+Enter twice set that right too. Both are faults `framecheck.FIX_KINDS` names (`size`, `drawn`).
- *Who sees it:* the perception service, which sends no keys: its frames say the client's size (`size`), the game drawing off its client (`drawn`, the table above), or a capture that failed outright (`capture`: mss refused mid-switch ended the frame loop, and the service with it; now the frame says so, the duplication is opened afresh or mss takes over as for an offset capture, and the loop goes on).
- *Who sends Alt+Enter:* a command that hunts (`hunt kill` and `clear`, `nav`, `tour`, `probe run`): its Senses hand every look with nothing to act on for such a fault to a `SizeFix`, which tries once the same fault, the window where it was, has stood 5 s (`STEADY_S`, a guess: never in the middle of the user's own drag), once more 30 s later (`AGAIN_S`) if the looks after didn't pass, then waits for the user (said once); 4 tries an hour at most, by any process (`HOURLY`, `lab/window_tries.json`). Any command's looks wait for the first try before LookLost (`SizeFix.pending`; a plan holding it off is waited for 10 s more at most, `HOLD_S`), where LookLost (3 s) came first and they stopped untried; the hunt loop (`tour --loop`, `--grind`) does so at her first look, then makes its tries while it stands still (`Senses.regain`; standing still set before her first look, `tour --loop` on a client drawn off ended untried). Before a try it looks for the game in play on the service's picture of the client (the HUD's three buttons, `framecheck.hud_seen`, 0.7 or more, as the pet does: Behavior: Her pet): below that (its login or character screen, where Enter types into a field or picks) no try, and the picture is looked at again 30 s on. A try is counted as its first Alt+Enter goes to the player (a try cut short, its process killed in the hold, is one too); one that brought the game forward but sent none (no picture to look for the Lie Detector on, the game not in front) isn't, here or in the hour's, the next 30 s on, 4 of them at most (`UNPRESSED`). A command that finds the client at a size the eyes have no calibration for as it starts (3840x2160, full screen) tries at once and waits while it isn't right, 180 s at most (`_fit_start`, `START_WAIT_S`, a guess: the two tries end within a minute and a half), then ends (`error: the game's client is still 3840x2160 after 180 s ...`), where it stopped at once with "not calibrated at 3840x2160 yet" (waiting for ever, it kept the pet's babysitter stopped, the pet unfed); its telemetry is recorded from before that. At 1920x1080 (the stretched window) the eyes get no fix: Alt+Enter sets the game's own size. `hunt look`, `map` and `watch` send no keys; the pet's babysitter makes one bounded try of its own (Behavior: Her pet).
- *One try* (`refit`): Alt+Enter through the player (Alt down, Enter tapped 50 ms later, Alt up 50 ms after it: `ALT_ENTER`, the explore steps' `alt+ 50 enter 50 alt-`), each a plan of its own, then a wait for the window to change (within 8 s, `CHANGE_S`) and stay as it is 1.5 s (`SETTLE_S`); from full screen none goes out sooner than 8 s after the player answered the one that put it there (counted from before that plan was made ready, a first that waited 2.5 s for the game to come forward had the way back 5.5 s after it) (`FULL_HOLD_S`, measured: at 23:41 the user's fix through `act alt+ 50 enter 50 alt- 3500 alt+ 50 enter 50 alt-` put it full screen with the first, the second, 3.5 s on, wasn't taken, and one more about 8 s after the first set it back at (2454, 107), drawn right; as built on the branch the second went once full screen had stood 1.5 s, 2.7 s after the first), and one from full screen that changes nothing is pressed again, 3 at most (`BACK_PRESSES`); then the client's size read. A game full screen already gets only the way back; the second goes out only once the first has put the game full screen (one that left it windowed, or changed nothing, would put it full screen and leave it so), and none after a first that set it right. On a fake window (`tests/test_window_size.py`): a game that takes no key for 4 s after a switch is set back with two Alt+Enters, one for 9 s with three, and one that never takes another is left full screen, said.
- *What holds it off:* the Lie Detector alarm up (said: a hunt's next plan or look raises it and she retreats, the pet goes on feeding); the Lie Detector on screen, looked for before each Alt+Enter on the service's picture of the client (below), and seen there the alarm is raised as the player's watchdog raises it (its file, the picture as its screenshot, the page): every command refuses from there, a hunt retreats, whoever is at the PC is told (only the watchdog raised it, and it didn't see the Lie Detector at another size); no picture, no Alt+Enter: none to begin with, and after one put the game full screen the look is asked again every 0.5 s for 8 s (`LOOK_FOR_S`), then the try stops with the game left full screen for the next try or the user (the way back went out unlooked: three Alt+Enters over 24 s with a game that didn't take them, and Enter can answer the quiz); a plan waiting for the player or being played (`client.busy`; before the way back from full screen it's waited for, 10 s at most, `BUSY_WAIT_S`: a food of the pet's in the hold ended the try with the game full screen); another process's try (a named mutex, `window_size.LOCK`, let go of by Windows when a process ends however it ends: the babysitter kills the pet's process when a hunt starts, where the branch's lock file stood 120 s; the pet sends nothing while another holds it: `window --recover` runs beside it); the game minimized, at the try's start or in it (switched away from full screen, the game minimizes: it isn't brought back over what the user is doing); or the game not in front once brought forward (and the player checks that again before every key: Alt+Enter in another window does something else); a plan played without its Enter is said. Alt is her jump key too: she jumps where she stands at each.
- *Through the switch:* the service never sends a key and makes no new run for it (the window at another size is a wait); its frames say `size` while full screen, `capture` for a copy refused (DXGI's lost access is duplicated again, as before), and are read as before once the client is back. With no run to look with (the service started with the game full screen: 3840x2160 has no calibration; run 0 from 23:01 to 23:22 on 2026-10-25) a full ask was dropped with the asks, the Lie Detector look got no picture ("no frame from the perception service within 1.0 s", three of three), and no Alt+Enter could go out from full screen, the tries counted all the same; now it's kept and answered then too (`Service._not_visible`: a real service and client on a test pipe, the picture three of three, at once). After a try that set it right a command's looks and glances are of frames shown after the window settled at the soonest (`Senses.settled`), with LOST_S afresh; a try that set the size right with the game still drawing off it is followed by one more 30 s on, then it's the user's (never a loop: only a look that passes starts it afresh).

A `full` ask that takes any size (`ServiceClient.full_frame(any_size=True)`) is answered, while the frames aren't fit to read for such a fault, with the client's picture as it is (`perception.frames.glimpse`: 1366x768 as it is, any other size brought to 1920x1080; 6.2 MB down the pipe, 12 ms to convert and shrink a 3840x2160 one). On the saved Lie Detector screens as the game's own view stretched to a client of 3840x2160, 2560x1440, 1600x900, 1396x1952, 1350x700 and 1280x720, so brought to 1920x1080, every form is seen at every size (1.08-1.43 of the threshold) but the old countdown, seen at 3840x2160, 1600x900 and 1396x1952 (1.01-1.02) and not at 2560x1440, 1350x700 or 1280x720 (0.76-0.86); brought to 1366x768 instead, the countdown was seen at none (0.70-0.71; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/winfix/build/ld_sizes.py`, `ld_sizes2.py`).
- *Said* (and in the telemetry, `event` kind `window`): `the client is 1350x700, not 1366x768: Alt+Enter twice` or `the client is 3840x2160, full screen: Alt+Enter to set it back`; `the client is 1366x768 again (Alt+Enter 2 times; the window settled 1.2, 1.2 s after)`; `... (Alt+Enter 4 times; ...): the window didn't change within 8 s of Alt+Enter`, or `...: the first Alt+Enter didn't put it full screen (a second would)`; `no Alt+Enter: the Lie Detector alarm is up` (or `a plan is waiting for the player or being played`, `the game is minimized`, `another process is setting it right`); `the Lie Detector is on screen (quiz): the Lie Detector alarm raised (the player's watchdog may not see it at this size)`; `no Alt+Enter: the game isn't seen in play (its HUD's buttons match 0.30, 0.7 needed: its login or character screen?)`, `... the screen couldn't be looked at for the Lie Detector (...)` (after a first: `... in 8 s: no Alt+Enter without that look`), `... the game was minimized meanwhile: it isn't brought back over what's in front`; `Alt+Enter didn't set it right in 2 tries: waiting for the user to set the client back to 1366x768` (or `no Alt+Enter could be sent in 4 tries: ...`); at a command's start `the game's client is 3840x2160, a size the eyes aren't calibrated for: waiting 180 s at most for it to be set back`.
- `python -m gamelab window --recover` makes one try by hand (not counted in the hour's), saying the client's size, place and DPI awareness before and its size and place after; at 1366x768, windowed and drawn right by the service's newest state, it does nothing unless `--force`. Only `FULL_HOLD_S` is measured; the rest are guesses, which a try's "the window settled A, B s after" sets.
- *Not done:* nothing of it has run in game but the user's own Alt+Enters of 23:41; the watchdog's other sizes take a player started again (the user's UAC click), and whether its GDI grab sees a full-screen game at all isn't known; the in-play check has met no login, character-select or cash-shop screen (none is saved: only the desktop, black, and the play area moved over the HUD, 0.25-0.52); the drawn check's window frame is matched only at 300% (further up than 48 px it needs none); a hunt that gave up waits for the user to its end, and the pet isn't fed meanwhile (its babysitter is stopped while a hunt runs).

**Diagnosing a run.** A command that acts says, as it starts, the game's client size and place in desktop px and the process's DPI awareness (2: per monitor), and the minimap picture it loaded (`the minimap picture of map 10002073: 67x183 game px`). If the map has a picture and it won't load (tried three times), the command stops saying why, where it used to read her dot with the first map's origin; a picture that failed to load is tried again, not kept as missing. Every `scene` record has `minimap`: where the picture was found (its corner, full-size px) and how well it matched (0.645 on `tree_135315.png`). Her name tag's full-size template is cut again from calibration's after 50 looks in a row without her tag (`nametag.RECUT_AFTER`; 14 at most in that day's tours), in case it no longer matches her. A box off the monitor (the window moved off it, the desktop resized) is a capture failure now, which falls back to mss, where it stopped the command.

**Offline tools.** `bench-look`, `bodies` and the feed run offline (`saved_world`), their eyes given the map's minimap picture (above), say at once of a saved frame whose look fails its checks why it does, and the command ends (`bench.refused`; it used to take the frame again for `LOST_S`), a refused frame handing on no HP. `bench-look --shrink` leaves the frames' own checks out: the shrink blurs their 1-px anchors.

**Not done.** The continuous feed (`watch`, `--feed`) reads its frames through `Eyes.look_at`, so a frame that fails the anchors or the picture, or puts her off the map, isn't placed (a look it serves has no place, and nothing acts on it), keeps the last good frame's HP and MP, and its EXP and HP aren't read for events (the 16:48:45 frame's 0% made a hit); the feed's child stops if the map's picture won't load, and the command's own eyes (which have it) take the looks then. But its frames aren't checked for the window moving mid-capture or for age, and a feed never makes `LookLost`. Several windows with the game's title aren't told apart (the first is taken). Whether there's a platform or rope under her isn't asked (a fall off a platform can have nothing under it for hundreds of units). The checks have run on saved frames and fakes only; on the first map and West Rocky Mountain II the anchors are the same pixels, but nothing was run there. (Since 2026-10-25 the perception service checks every frame as the command's eyes did, the window moving under a capture and a capture held 2 s included, each state carrying its frame's problem, and a look given none to act on makes `LookLost` after 3 s: The perception service.)

**To check in game** (no attacks: no key is sent; a look brings the game to the front, as any look does): `python -m gamelab hunt look --every 0.5 --seconds 90 --map 10002073` prints the client's size and place, the DPI awareness and the minimap picture loaded, then her place twice a second. While it runs: drag the game window by its title bar for a few seconds and let go (expect `a look failed its checks: the game window moved while it was captured ...` or `... the capture is offset by ...`, then `the game looks as expected again`, then `the game window moved: (x, y) -> (x', y')` and her place as before, never a place off the map); hold it dragging longer than 3 s (`standing still: ...`, then as expected again once let go); close the minimap window in the game and open it again (`the minimap window's title isn't at the top left`, standing still, back). If the desktop is resized (Chrome Remote Desktop from another device) and the client isn't 1366x768 any more, it says `the game's client is WxH, not 1366x768: waiting for it to be set back` and leaves the window as it is (`hunt look` sends no keys), and while it waits it doesn't bring the game to the front: another program clicked meanwhile stays in front. Each line goes to the telemetry too (`event`). **Alt+Enter** (keys this time: Alt, her jump key, and Enter, through the player; the game switches to full screen and back: only with someone at the PC watching the screen, the player running, no Lie Detector due, the perception service up): `python -m gamelab window --recover --force` with the client at 1366x768 should say `the client is 1366x768: Alt+Enter twice`, the game going full screen and back, then `the client is 1366x768 again (Alt+Enter 2 times; the window settled A, B s after)` and the client's place after; A and B, against `CHANGE_S` (8) and `SETTLE_S` (1.5), and whether the second was taken 8 s after the first (`FULL_HOLD_S`), say whether the waits want changing. With the game put full screen by hand (Alt+Enter), `window --recover` alone (`full screen: Alt+Enter to set it back`); a `nav` between two safe platforms started on it tries at once and goes on (`_fit_start`); a `hunt look --every 0.5` while it's full screen stands still and sends nothing; with `pet --every 1` running and the game full screen, the pet says `pet: waiting: the game is full screen (3840x2160)` once and sends nothing until it's back (`pet: the game looks right again`), and during a `window --recover` of the user's it says `pet: waiting: another command is setting the game's client right with Alt+Enter`. A player started again since 2026-10-26: with the game full screen, its log should say nothing new (no Lie Detector seen on the game's own screen at 3840x2160); at the next Lie Detector while it's full screen, `LIE DETECTOR seen` as at 1366x768. ## Her place from the scene, in the perception service (from 2026-10-30)

The user, 2026-10-29 ~22:15, of the localization prototype (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/loc2/combined: on the morning's held-out frames her feet within 3 px on 100% of the easy and the hard ones, where the service had 71% and 48%): "Please do that [her camera from the map's art drawn from the game data] and port the localization to C ... do that quickly as I can really benefit from it". The prototype's combined localizer (snap/c3_full/loc.py) is `localization/locate.py`'s `Locator`, its camera the map's art registered (camreg on mapart's picture, not the panorama stitched from the morning's frames, a third of the map), its plate and body cues the ported ones in C (Her place by her plate and her body), and the perception service places her by it:
- **Where it's used**: Senses gives it to eyes that look at frames themselves (the service's, saved frames'; `Senses._locator`, `locate.build`): at the game's own 1366x768, on a map whose art can be drawn (the game data copy here), for a character with her plate's model in her lab folder (`plate_1366x768.npz`; her pose bank `poses_1366x768.npz` for the body cue: calibration's, `localization.her_cues`), with config.toml's `[perception] scene` true (the default, `locate.ON`; false: as before). Not at 1920x1080, not in the simulator (its eyes have no name tag), not for a command's eyes (their states come from the service), nor on a map whose art can't be drawn: nothing changes there. Her plate's model and pose bank aren't tied to a map: on any map whose art draws it's used (the review's 10 maps, towns and fields among them). Whatever building it raises (a model file cut short, an allocation failing as a big map's art is drawn the first time: 0.4-0.5 GB at its peak for Ellinia, Lith Harbor and Kerning City) is said and gives her place as before, never the run for the map failing ("can't look at map"); whatever a look's `Locator.see` raises puts the locator away (said once, as before from then on), never the look failing. Only the latest map's art is kept in memory (`mapart._LOADED`; Tree Dungeon's 14 MB, Henesys 33, Ellinia 56).
- **A frame** (`Eyes.look_at`): her dot read first, then `Locator.see(frame, t, dot)`: the view (`camreg.Registration.see`), the cues cheapest first (her tag's full gray template about where the filter puts her, sure at 0.85, the play area's rows to the HUD's top when she's lost and every 30th frame (at 15 a second; 60th at 30) she isn't surely found; her plate's exact colours, her letters needed and her dot agreeing; her body against her pose bank in the box the filter's uncertainty gives, else across her dot's column), the filter (her x and its speed, y on her platform's line, under gravity in the air, steady on a rope; walls, walk-offs, landings, her dot a box she's in and an alarm). Her tag is then the plate's centre as matched (tag, plate) or where her feet put it (her plate model's offset, (+1.5, -16): measured at calibration, where `tag_below_feet`'s 11 put her 5 px low), the Observation's `feet`, `view`, `view_sure`, `located`. A frame whose view was never registered (none sure yet) is looked at as before (NameTag).
- **Placed** (`Senses._by_scene`): `where` her feet's map place (the view plus her place on screen, a unit a px), her platform the filter's, `how` the cue ("tag", "plate", "body"; "carried": none placed her, the filter's prediction, `tag_seen` False; "covered": so, under the Lie Detector, her stat window or in a portal's light, below), `mode` ("ground", "air", "rope") and `confidence` (the cue's score; carried, x0.8 a frame of 15 a second). Not found yet: her dot snapped as before, put on screen by the view (`how` "dot"). Off the map: not placed (placecheck).
- **The scene's px <-> map by the view** (`Scene.screen_x`, `screen_y`, `map_x`, `map_y`; `view` the map point at the frame's top-left), not by her tag and her place: every monster, drop and window placed through it is placed by the registered camera; `floor_y` her feet's row; `grounded` the filter's (a cue placed her, standing on a platform); a monster whose template knows its feet goes on the platform under them wherever the view is registered (`place`'s exact snap, before only with her standing). WorldState and `to_scene` carry `feet`, `view`, `view_sure`, `mode`, `confidence`; the 'scene' record's `her` has `mode`, `conf` and `view_sure`; the service's console line every 10 s says the share of frames each cue placed her in, carried and covered apart, the views registered and the locator's time a frame (`Locator.line`).
- **Counts in time**: the prototype's counts are of its 15 frames a second; at the service's 30 each is two (`Locator.k`, by the frames' gaps), and her vertical motion (rope against a fall) is read from every second measured place. After 0.5 s without a frame (`GAP_S`) she's placed afresh.

## Perception at 15 frames a second, one pass a frame (2026-10-30)

The user, 2026-10-30: "make perception output the 15fps whole screen only, no need for a separate 30fps existing tracking", "Perception should only give mob heading, speed should come from data-mined game files", and, asked whether her own place, the HUD and her touches should stay at 30 a second: "I meant everything at 15 fps". So the perception service looks at the game 15 times a second, and each frame gets one pass that reads everything off it; what the stack reads of the game, her place and HP as much as the monsters, is one frame's. (The design, its measurements and risks: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/p15.)

**What changed** (work/replan, on master 52d6195):
- *One rate* (`localization/rate.py`: `HZ = 15.0`): the feed's frames (`feed.HZ`), the service's (`service.HZ`), the rolling recording's (`control.recording.FPS`: every frame of the service's, where every other one of its 30), the simulator's feed (`SyncFeed`'s default). Glances are every frame the feed looks at (`senses.FEED_GLANCE_EVERY_S` 0, and a glance asks for no frame of its own: `Feed.glance`, `latest(..., ask=False)`): 15 a second, the pace they had at 30 frames a second (63 ms apart). What counted frames counts time: `tracking.MIN_SEEN_S` (0.2 s: 3 frames, where 5 at 30), `worldstate.BAR_EVERY_S` (0.2 s: every third frame, where every 5th at 30), `perception.deaths.EVERY_S` (once a frame, 15 looks a track a second as before). A lint (tests/test_rate.py): `service.HZ is feed.HZ is rate.HZ`, `recording.FPS == rate.HZ`, no other frames-a-second constant nor 1/15 or 1/30 of a second written into localization/, perception/ or control/.
- *One pass a frame* (`worldstate.WorldStep.step`): (1) her look (Eyes.look_at: her place by the scene or her tag and dot, HP, MP, EXP, level, the minimap, ropes) and the whole screen's search for monsters (MobDetector.detect_wide over the play area) at once, the search on a thread of the step's own (`HALVES`; it needs only the frame, and both are mostly C that lets go of Python's lock; only where the look frame is the capture itself, the game's own 1366x768, with the real detector); (2) her place, vitals and touches as before; (3) the detections placed on the map and matched to the tracks in one `MonsterTracker.update(t, found, view, her, players, read, dying)`, each detection's HP bar read where its track's is due (`_bar_due`, judged before the detection is taken; a new one's always) and the tracks that may be dying looked at (`_dying`, before her gains are judged, as before); (4) the drops: what a look asked for searched whole on its frame (scene.find_loot: her platform's, or every platform's in view; a pile just picked up never seen again, an item in two platforms' strips on the one it lies on), then `DROPS_STRIPS` (1) strip in view every `DROPS_EVERY_S` (0.2 s) by rotation, the one searched longest ago first, her platform's counted twice as old (every strip of Tree Dungeon's 12 in view searched again every 2.4 s, as `watch`'s schedule had every platform's every 2 s; two strips a frame, as the design had it, took the frame loop 0.25-0.35 cores more: Measured after it) (`WorldState.drops`: every strip in view, when it was last searched and what it had; for the loot design to come, read by the mini-map's scene record now; a state's `loot` is still only what was asked for). Each state's `monsters` are its own frame's detections, each with its track's id (`Monster.track`); `band_at` and `wide_at` are its own time; no state is given again later (`late` always False).
- *The tracker* (`localization.tracking`): one list a frame, the whole screen's detections, matched nearest first within the gate as before (10 + 1.3 x speed x dt + 25 units: 43.7 a frame on at 15), a walking track met by a detection facing the other way away from its platform's ends `FACING_COST` (8 units) farther; a track's place its detection's feet (no filter), its velocity its heading at its kind's speed from the game data (`monsters.walk_vx`: a move frame walks `speeds()[kind]` the way it faces, a stand or hit1 frame stands; `POSE_GATE_S` kept as a switch, off), from its first detection; `predicted` walks on and turns back at its platform's ends (MonsterTrack.at's), where it was clamped there. Which detection each track was is `matched`. A dying track no gain is on takes a detection only within `FADE_MOVE` of where it was, as its re-find did. `TRACK_SEEN` (attack.stance) 1: a track's speed counts from its first frame.
- *The feed* (`localization.feed`): an ask is for a frame at its time and the drops it wants (`to_ask`: never her band or the whole screen, every state has them; `band`/`wide` in an `Asks` are kept and change nothing); what's asked goes into the next frame due, the look waiting for it (`run`, `SyncFeed.tick`: HZ frames a second whatever is asked, since its review: The branch after its review; as first built, a frame asked for was taken at once and the next re-phased a period after it, 15.7-15.9 frames a second in the simulator's standard grind). `Costs` are the one pass's at 1366x768, the live size (capture 2 ms, her look 8.5, the whole screen 8.4 beside it, 1.8 more for the two at once, a bar 1.1, a death look 0.8, a strip of drops 3.8): a state is ready `Costs.of` after its frame; `COSTS_1366` is `COSTS` (the harness's `--costs measured-1366` runs as `measured`).
- *The service* (`localization.service`): its 10 s line and 'perf' record say each frame's pass (median, p90, p99, the most), her look's and the whole screen's in it, the monsters found and followed and the strips of drops a frame, a state's age as it goes out, the cores (`Perf`, `perf_line`); the watchdog watches the frame loop (a pass hung: the search is in it now); `SCHEDULE` and `HUNTING` alike; `perceive --wide-every` is gone. The ring's 16 slots hold 1.07 s of frames, a client's queue 4.3 s.
- *Consumers:* `navigator._placed` judges a glance at its frame's time (a glance can be up to a period and a pass old, about 85 ms, where 42); `fight.walk_on` by `walk_vx`; the 'tracks' records carry `pose`, their `vx` the game data's (a walk is x over time now, for analyses: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/p15/live_speeds.py).
- *Gone:* the re-finds (`_refind_all`, `_send_ahead`, near-first windows and memos, ONE_CALL, the GPU's AHEAD: MobDetector.refind, refind_all, native.c's rf_* and the GPU path are left unused, for a later cleanup), the searches' thread (`Searches`, `InlineSearches`, `Worker`, `SearchThread`, `Job`, `Found`, `search`, `came_back`, `merge`, `owed` searches, the late states), her band's own search and the schedule's whole screens (`BAND_EVERY_S`, `BAND_STAND_IN_S`, `WIDE_EVERY_S`, `WIDE_SHARE`, `ASKS_FIRST`, `Schedule.band_s/wide_s/loot_s/loot_wide_s`, `feed.MOBS_FRESH_S`, `WIDE_FRESH_S`, `ASK_ONLY_STALE`), the tracker's alpha-beta filter (`ALPHA`, `BETA`, `SPEED_CLAMP`, `POSE_VELOCITY`, `LONG_GAP_S`), `merge`, `searching`, `LATE_SEARCH_S`, `refound_seen`, `TimedSearches`.
- *Re-pinned* (each says why in its docstring; the scans' outputs D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/p15/impl/out/scan_*.txt, then scan2_*.txt for the drops' rotation's pace): `loop_tree_lie_detector_28` 9 (15 with the rotation as first built), `loop_tree_lie_detector_grind` 2, `loop_tree_grind_attack_key` and `loop_tree_attack_unbound` 10 (of seeds 1-10 10 alone: on 1-8 no 5 regular presses in a row went without effect in their 2 minutes, where on master 5 of 1-13 met all of it: her regular attack's doubt comes later on these seeds, to watch), `loop_tree_attack_misses` and `_seen` 1 (2 first), `loop_tree_attack_no_darts` 8 (of seeds 1-8 8 alone: on 5 her stars' test had nothing in reach to cast at), `hunt_kill_misses` 1, `loop_rival` 2, `nav_fight_across` 2 (1 first), `fight_step_wall` 1, `move_climb_down_nudge` 3, `probe_top` 2 (2 and 3 the only seeds of 1-10 where tests/test_probe.py's window-top test has a hit in the logs' top's world as well), `loop_lull_loot` 1, test_heading's knock test 6. `nav_tree_landing_no_shot` is expected to fail (test_sim's NO_LANDING_SHOT): on none of seeds 1-40 is the walker by her landing at her plan's look, so there's no shot to say there's none of (on master seed 2 alone of 1-6 met all of it).

**Measured before it was built** (the design's, read-only offline: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/p15, Idle priority on CPUs 12-23, another workflow's replay beside it):
- *Speeds:* the game data gives Tree Dungeon's Slime, Green and Horny Mushroom speed -20: 125 x 0.8 = 100 units/s (mapdata.mob_walk_speed's). Tonight's live thief run (02:03-02:48, the 'tracks' records, x over 0.5 s): walking medians 96.8 (Green, 9,610 half-seconds) and 98.2 (Horny); the user's own play 97.0, 98.0, 100.0; the whole screen at 1/15 s on the user's play clip (4,507 lossless frames, 11,948 detections) 100.0 for all three over 0.2 s windows, still in 29-33% of them.
- *Heading from one detection:* facing the way it walks in 99.2% of 5,358 walking windows; a move frame moving over the next 0.2 s 88.7%, a stand frame still 95.4%. Predicted from one detection by facing x 100 in a move frame (else still), turned back at its platform's ends: 0.6 / 12.6 / 28 units off a frame on (median / p90 / p99), 1.0 / 21 / 41 at 0.2 s, 4.0 / 37.6 / 68.7 at 0.5 s, 21.4 / 68 / 124 at 1 s, the best rule at every horizon (the chain's own velocity 0.6, 1.6, 8.3, 23 at the median; standing still 5, 16, 26, 39). Turns 0.52 a monster-second, 0.45 of them within 40 units of the end it can reach.
- *What the re-finds saw that the whole screen didn't:* 3.5% of the tracks re-found in a frame had no whole-screen detection over them (83 of 2,369; within 50 units of her 6.4%).
