## Motion planning on the whole state (2026-10-30)

The user, 2026-10-30: "Why motion plan still use the 30fps quick look? Since we are running whole screen perception at
15FPS now, should we simply drop the 30fps path and make motion planing work on the 15fps whole screen result now? and I
think ideally we probably want to regenerate motion plan at every frame so any hit/new spawn will cause motion plan to
react immediately" (the design: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan, its measurements in profile_priced_out.txt,
cache_trial_out.txt, stopgo_out.txt, recover_out.txt, plantime_out.txt). In steps on work/replan, each its own commit.

**The planner's monsters from the whole state** (`control/navigator.py`). Every state perception gives has the whole
screen's monsters, each with its track (Perception at 15 frames a second), and the planner took a part of them:
- *No second search.* A fighting trip's band look (the fights decide by her band) carries the state's monsters off it
  (`Scene.swept`, `Feed.look`), and the chains are planned by all of them (`trip_monsters`). Until now its frame was
  searched again in the tour's process over the rows the chain's platforms take (`Eyes.monsters`, 23 ms at 1366x768,
  `TRIP_LOOK_BELOW`), on nearly every plan look, without the feed's track ids or headings, and what was off the band on
  that frame went unread by the planner.
- *Speeds from the game data, headings from perception, for every trip* (`_walking`): each monster walks the way its
  track heads (`monsters.walk_vx`: its kind's speed from the game data the way a move frame faces, 0 standing or
  flinching; under `STILL_VX` it stands, and since the branch's review either way at its speed a while,
  `STAND_UNSURE_S`: The branch after its review), over what the tracker measured between two looks, with an escort too. Until
  now only without one, and only where the tracker couldn't tell yet: a fighting trip's monster seen once was planned for
  wherever it could walk either way at its kind's speed. Each planner's monster carries its track's id
  (`MonsterTrack.track`).
- *No quick look after a touch* (`POST_HIT`): the next pass looks with the monsters (the newest state's), where it took
  one without them and planned from the tracker's last monsters (`Tracker.last`, `TripState.quick`): live a median 1.2 s
  old (p90 3.3, the most 4.8; 39 of the thief's 449 chains of 2026-10-30, 8.7%), and the live tracks the look's own frame
  had left out. What the quick look was also for is kept: while her invulnerability after the touch lasts
  (`TripState.post_hit_until`: `Senses.invulnerable_until` less `IMMUNE_MARGIN_S`; `INVULNERABLE_S` from now where her HP
  dropped with no popup told), no fight starts on the way (`_shoot_on_the_way`, `_clear_the_way`, the shots first of
  `_meet`, `_shoot_ahead`, `_clear_landing` and `_last_shot`) and the trip's `until` isn't asked: that window is what lets
  her chains pass the monster that just touched her, and fighting from wherever a hit knocked her kept her fighting there
  (`nav_fight_across` ran out its 180 s). The hunt loop's "move on first" (`_owe_move`) is that window's.

Seeds re-picked (each docstring says why; D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/rp/out/scan_A*.txt): `nav_monsters_staircase` 2,
`loop_leaves_empty_ground` 2, `loop_tree_attack_no_darts` 3, `loop_tree_lie_detector_28` 8, `nav_tree_landing_shot_first`
3, `loop_tree_ore_waits` 1. `nav_tree_evade` no longer needs its spot and passes: planned from the newest state in the
window the contact rule's touch leaves her, the chain after it goes up past the Green Mushroom (touched once, on 19 at
2.1 s, where 8.2 s and three touches), on every seed of 1-16; it checks that now.

**Replanned at every state while a chain runs** (`REPLAN`; the user's "regenerate motion plan at every frame so any
hit/new spawn will cause motion plan to react immediately"). Every state perception gives (15 a second, each with the
whole screen's monsters) is a glance of the running chain's watch (`Navigator._watching`), and on it:
- *A monster coming into a leg still to come* (REACT's: one the plan didn't know, walked in or spawned; now wherever she
  is, not only with room to stop) has the chain replanned from where she'll be when new keys can act (`_splice_point`:
  `SPLICE_LEAD_S` on, 40 ms, the player's wait step and its last spin) against the newest state, all of it
  (`_state_scene`: the glance's state as a look with the whole screen, her memory's and the feed's out of sight), its
  route the trip's, its landings priced as the pass prices them, no wider takeoffs (`spread` off: a state's budget), and
  handed over in place of the running plan's rest (`_take_over`). Only from the ground, where the state has her on the
  platform the plan has her on then and within `SPLICE_DRIFT` (20 units) of where it has her, her start put where the
  state measured her: in a flight, or past a takeoff's key less `KEY_COMMIT_S` (the game's key lag: `KEY_LEAD`, a jump's
  `JUMP_LAG`, a drop's `DROP_LAG`, a walk-off's stop `STOP_S`), not yet: the next state asks again once she's down. (Built
  first to take over at the predicted landing, as the design had it: on the tower down from 6 a drop spliced at a
  landing she made late had its keys pressed in the air, and she ran to 29's end, the very thing `_queue_next` plans from
  a look for.) Only where nothing chains does she stop, as before (REACT's cut, with room to stop).
- *Every `BETTER_EVERY_S`* (5 states), the chain replanned so, and taken where the running chain stops short (for a
  monster, a move it can't predict, or cut off for length with nothing to follow on) and the new one goes the same way on
  past where it stops, unless where it stops the trip's pass would have her fight or end there (`_stop_calls`: the
  trip's `until`, the hunt loop's `Hunt._interrupt`, or in hunt mode a target in reach); or where the new one's route
  isn't the running one's and the route planner costs it `SWITCH_GAIN_S` less (`Planner.quickest` against
  `Planner.through` the running way's next move: the same estimates both, where a chain's own times against the route's
  estimates for the rest made every longer chain look 0.4-0.9 s "sooner"); `SWITCH_MIN_S` after the last switch at the
  soonest; never the same way over again (the same moves of the route, `_same_moves`: a replan one state later took the
  same route 99.2% of the time on the user's own play, its takeoffs moved by the flow's variety alone). `SWITCH_GAIN_S`
  and `SWITCH_MIN_S` are guesses.
- *A touch* still cuts the plan (the game knocks her about whatever is held), and the next pass plans at once from the
  first state that has her on the ground again (`KNOCK_REPLAN`, `_knock_landing`: from `KNOCK_AIR_S` after the popup,
  her knock's flight on flat ground by `physics.KNOCK_VX`/`KNOCK_VY`, moved there from the simulator's world; the scene's
  mode 'ground', else her place on a platform at the height the state before had it), a look of that very state, not
  once she's stood still and a look of its own (`recover`: 0.13 s median, p90 0.33, and its look's frame, live), with her
  invulnerability's window (`POST_HIT`).

Only a pass's own chain is replanned so: not an evade step's, a pass regardless or a hop (what they leave out on purpose,
the replan wouldn't). A chain cut off for length runs on into the next as before (follow's tail, `_look_ahead`,
`_queue_next`), a replanned one too. Each switch is said (the log's "replanned from ... (spliced)", a 'chain' and a
'replan' record: why, kind, its plan time, spliced or not, its legs, its planning ms) and counted (`Trip.replans`).

**Shot from along her platform** (`MEET_WALK`; the user's "in general you should kill all the mobs that are in the way").
With the whole state, what's in her way is seen, and more of it out of a star's reach from where she stands: on the
harness's standard grind (24 seeds) `MEET_S` fired 68 times where it hadn't, `NO_WAIT` 909 times against 419, touches
+19% (78.0 against 65.4, beyond 2 se) and EXP a minute -4.3% (within). `_meet`'s shot first now walks along her platform
to where her attack reaches it, `SHOOT_WALK` at most (`Escort.shot_place`, `shoot_from`: the landing's shot first's),
before a way around, a hop or a wait.

**The splice** (`control.client.splice`, `control.player`'s `Player.run`). A plan handed to the player as
`{running}.splice` (not a `*.json`: never a plan of its own) takes over from the running plan at its `at_ms` of that
plan's clock (at once if that's gone by when the player sees it): the running plan's keys from then on don't come, the
keys it holds then that the new one's `held` doesn't have are let go and those it has that aren't held are pressed, a
'down' of a key held then is left out, and its events play from then on, its clock's start the splice's time. The player
claims it (the file renamed), checks it as any plan (`validate`; no resize, no recording) and with the alarm up takes
only a kind that goes then (`alarm_refusal`); the alarm halts a spliced plan as any. It answers the running plan at once
with the problem `spliced` (`spliced`: the new id, its at_ms, how late it took over) and the new one as any, under its
own id (its own `.running`, `.cancel`, `.splice`). One whose time is at or past the running plan's end carries it on with
no key let go between (where the `end_ms` queue let go of every key between two plans). A splice the player never took
(the running plan over first) is withdrawn (`client.taken`, `unsplice`), and cancelling one not taken yet cuts the plan it
was for. The player says it takes splices in `lab/player.json` (`splice`, its pid: written as it starts, removed as it
stops; `client.can_splice`); a player started before this code writes none, and the navigator cuts the running plan and
sends the new one at once instead (every key let go for 15-35 ms). Live it needs the player started again, which takes
the user's UAC click. The simulator's player takes splices as the real one does (`sim.fakes.FakePlayer.splice`: seen
`SPLICE_SEEN_S` after it's handed over, the world's keys withdrawn from then on, `World.withdraw_from`).

Seeds re-picked with the replanning (each docstring says why; rp/out/scan_B*.txt): `nav_fight_up` 1,
`loop_tree_lie_detector_23` 2, `loop_tree_23` 3, `loop_tree_grind_lucky_seven_key` 2. Tree Dungeon's 42 goldens recorded

for, `nav_tree_landing_no_shot` not, expected to fail as before) and the hand-read ones read (`nav_tree_evade`'s contact

`nav_tree_landing_shot_first`'s shot first and "it's dying"; the Lie Detector's four: no splice with the alarm up, none in
them at all); 21 splices over the 42. Summed over them, the perception commit's traces / these: touches 1,008 / 1,063,
kills 953 / 950.

## Smarter looting: the loot sweep on the 15-a-second state (2026-10-30)

The user, 2026-10-30: "We should also tweak the look picking logic since we are very short on mesos and mob drops, we need to try to pick up all loots to keep the cash flow healthy", and "For loot, please be more intelligent and heuristic, before leaving an area you should try to pick as much as possible without too much impact on travel time, and in general you should kill all the mobs that are in the way, try not to hit by mobs just for picking up loots" (the design and its measurements: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/loot; this work's scratch D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/loot2). On work/replan, on top of the replanning (Motion planning on the whole state): her legs to drops are the navigator's trips, planned and replanned at every state against every monster as any.

**What the live runs said** (the thief's run of 02:03-02:48, the perception service's whole-screen view, against the user's own 5 minutes of play): she picked up 67% of the drops' worth seen (199 a minute; the user 70%, 306 of 437); she lost 100 a minute, 48% of it within 2 s of extra travel on her way while it lay there, 66% within 3; of what she lost, 47% waited on `PILE_CLEAR` (12-28% of those waits for the pile's own monster, drawn dying where it dropped them), 28% was known and never gone for, 15% yielded to something in reach; 15-24% of the piles' worth listed was the same drops counted by 2-3 piles; 12% of the drops lay past the 90 s `DROP_LIFE` the hunt loop left them at; half her departures from a stop (24 of 50) came within 3 s of a kill of hers, before its drops landed. Looting wasn't where her touches came from: 6.6 a minute on her drops against 11.3 the rest of the time.

**The sweep** (`behavior/sweep.py`, pure, as patrol.py is; as built on 2026-10-30: from 2026-11-01 no exchange of mesos for EXP, no price of her time, no `CAND_S` and no budget of its own, each pile within the seconds it may add to her way instead, "Loot as she kills" below; since 666c54b by her share of its worth, an itinerary within `MOST_S`: "The branch measured for the record against master 072e1ec (2026-11-01, the night)"): of the drop store's piles (`Hunt._spots`: each where its drops lie, what it's worth, its stand, when its drops land, how likely it is to lie there still), the set and the order that make the most of their worth at `MESO_EXP` (0.5 EXP a meso, the user's to choose: at 1.0 the break-even halves) and the guards' EXP, less her time at what it's worth (`_time_worth`: at a ground what she makes there, at a stop what staying gives, on her way the loop's rate or the best ground's, or more what's in reach now: EXP before loot), adding at most `BUDGET_MIN` (2 s) or `BUDGET_SHARE` (0.5) of her way's time, whichever is more, each candidate alone at most `CAND_S` (5 s) more (86% of what she lost live), the best `MAX_CAND` (8). Solved exactly in its travel (a dynamic program over subsets and the spot visited last; each set's quickest order weighed by its drops' survival at its arrivals) once a look for each way (`Hunt._sweep`), the itinerary she's on kept unless another is better by `KEEP_SHARE` (20%) and `KEEP_S` (0.5 s) of her time (`sweep.Sweeper`: patrol's two-pile flip-flop in loop_tree_grind_jump_key is the warning case). It's said in her log when it changes ("sweep: ..., then ...: +1.6 s on her way for 27 EXP's worth") and recorded (a 'sweep' record: its order, extra, value, budget, rate and why each candidate was left out: "cost", "budget", "no way", "expired", "unsafe: ...").
- *Where it runs* (the hunt loop's rules 5, 5b, 6, 8 and 10 gone into one, "sweep"; 6a, a valuable pile at once with nothing in reach, kept): travelling, the piles worth their time on her way to where she's going (`_while_travelling`); at a ground with nothing in reach, those worth a round trip from its spot (`Hunt._at_ground`; in a lull, nothing wanted left on the ground and a kill of hers there due back, her time worth nothing until the respawn and the budget that wait, `_sweep_terms`: rule 8's, lull loot; grinding, from the stop's place at what staying there gives: `Grind._at_ground`, `_stay_gain`); leaving it, before she goes, those on her way to the next ground (`Hunt._leave`: the best other ground's spot) or stop (`Grind._leave`: Patrol.choose's, peeked), the drops of her last kills there waited for where that pays (an expected pile's landing, `DROP_LANDS` after the kill, counts as time on her way).
- *A pile's trip* is an objective as any ('sweep': `_go_for`, its stops sharing the trip's budgets in passing as rule 5b's did), its itinerary's way on carried with it (`Objective.after`); every pass on the way the sweep is solved again from where she is (`_on_sweep`): the same pile first, on; another, a guard to shoot first or none, the objective under it and what the sweep has now. A trip to a spot stops for a pile the sweep now has on her way (`_sweep_calls`, the navigator's `until`).
- *Its stand* (`_stand`, at her arrival or when she's by it): each bunch of its drops seen (`looting.PILE_GAP`) walked to from the nearer end, a press of pick-up for each drop and one more (`PILE_EVERY_MS` apart); a kill's drops not seen yet, a walk over `SPREAD` (30 units) either side of where it died, pressing; a drop still where she stood twice can't be picked up (`looting.cant_pick`); `PILE_TRIES` (3) stands or trips at most; a telemetry event 'pick'. What's left the next look's drops show (until now a mop-up of its own, 0.3 s and a look between its rounds: `walk_piles`, `mop_up`, `collect` and `sweep_through` are the tour's alone now).

**No touch for loot** (`Hunt._guards`, `sweep.meets`): no pile is stood on where a monster that counts as a danger would meet her standing there, her body's box (`motion.bodies.HER_HALF`) against each one's (`monsters.touch_box`), and `CONTACT_MARGIN` (10 units) more, over the stand and `STAND_PAST_S` (0.5 s) more, from when she'd be there; each walking the way perception says it heads at its kind's speed from the game data (`monsters.walk_vx`: Tree Dungeon's three 100 units a second), turned back at its platform's ends (`sweep.bounce`), either way at that speed where its heading isn't known; seen on screen, or about though the look missed it (localization.unseen); never her own kill dying there (`ledger.dying`) nor a track the feed has taken for dead (`Ledger.dead`). One that would meet her and that a star from where she is hits (`_hits`; seen on screen, not one about) is shot first ('sweep: clear first'), its kill time (`Attacks.kill_s`) in the pile's and its EXP in its worth: "kill all the mobs that are in the way"; any other leaves the pile out for that look ("unsafe: a horny-mushroom at x 890 on 23"). The stand is checked again on the look she's there on (from now), and isn't made unless it's clear. Where nothing counts as a danger (the first map), nothing guards a pile, as before. `PILE_CLEAR` (a monster within 100 units of where she'd go for it, whatever its way) and the HP price of a pile's danger (`_pile_price`, `HP_EXP` a bar) are gone with the rules they served.

**The drop store** (`behavior/ledger.py`): a drop seen is in one pile only, the nearest within `LOOT_REACH`, and loose ones make piles of their own a `LOOT_REACH` of them from the left (`DropStore._sighting`); each pile keeps where its drops lay (`Pile.xs`: its stand covers them). Every strip of drops perception searched since the look before counts, at its own time (`Scene.strips`: the state's `WorldState.drops`, the rotation's strip every 0.2 s and the asked-for ones; a strip searched before a pile was last seen says nothing of it). How likely a pile is to lie there still is the live survival (`ledger.SURVIVAL`, the service's Kaplan-Meier of the thief's run, hers and others': 94/84/55/26% at 5/20/60/120 s for hers; `Pile.still`: at an age over at its age when last seen), where `DROP_LIFE` (90 s) left it; a pile under `SURVIVE_MIN` (5%) isn't gone for. Another's drops are candidates past its killer's ownership (`ledger.OWN_S`, 15 s) where `OTHERS_AFTER` waited 30 s (live, 30% of others' drops were gone by then). An expected pile is worth its kind's expected drops (`looting.expected_worth`: the live 0.64 drops a kill, 57% mesos at the middle of its kind's amounts, the rest its items by their rates: a Horny Mushroom's 23.5 mesos, a Green's 14.1, a slime's 8.3), where it was a bronze coin of the map's (33.4 on Tree Dungeon).

**The simulator** (the commit before: `sim/world.py`, `sim/harness.py`; with the default world the simulator credited her with 94% of her drops, master's crowd baseline, where live she picked up 67-71%): `--world map-drops` (`world.TREE_DROP_MIX`, `Realism.drop_mix`: 0.64 drops a kill, 57% mesos, by its kind's amounts, the rest its items by their rates, piles of 1, 2, 3 and 4 drops 61, 23, 8 and 8% of those with any, 20 units apart on alternating sides) and `--world drop-takers` (`world.HER_DROPS_LAST`, `Realism.drop_takers`: each of her drops taken by others at a life drawn from the live curve, never before `rival_owns`; until 2026-10-31, since then the live evidence's own and expiry passes: "Her drops, her HP and her backpack at the user's prices" and "The review's findings fixed" below). ## Where she stands to fight: her full box against theirs, back to the stop, her HP priced (2026-10-31)

The branch after its review earned 24% more EXP a minute than master in the harness's standard grind and was touched
29% more (above: "Not done"). Where the extra touches were (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/pos, the diagnosis: every touch
of seeds 1-8 on both sides recorded with the rule in force, her place, the toucher's and the world every 0.1 s): at any
one place she fought as safely as master (touches a minute on 9 24.3 against 25.8, on 10 22.0 against 24.0), but she
spent twice as long at the top of Tree Dungeon's tower (platforms 6-13: 129 -> 258 s a run), above all on 9, wedged 40-50
units between 8 and 10 (every place on it 0.32-0.57 by the danger model, where 10's stop is 0.22). Touches from a
monster on the platform just under or over hers went from 11 to 23 a run, which neither her fights (rule 1, the stance)
nor the sweep's guards counted; after a knock onto 9 she stayed 36.7 s a run and took 16.5 touches there (master 10.0 s
and 3.6), shooting what was in reach, where the hunt loop has its 'back to spot'; and the grind priced her HP at the top
at 0.07-0.15 bars a round of its loop (10, 7) where she lost 3 bars a minute on 10: her HP bar between looks netted her
pet's potions out and missed her trips, what she lost on 9 and 8 counted against no stop of the loop, a bar was 100 EXP
(the hunt loop's 250), her stays weren't net of it, and the stops sat on spawn points (7's 1 unit off its Horny
Mushroom's, 10's 11). The time at danger 0.3 and over, 33.8 -> 85.5 s a run, at the danger's touch rate there (24-27 a
minute, against 9-10 under 0.1), is the whole excess.

**What changed** (each by the danger model, attack.danger, nothing by a platform's name):
- *The sweep's guards count her full box against theirs* (`hunt.BESIDE_GUARDS`, `Hunt._about` with the pile's stretch):
  a monster walking a platform just under or over a pile's whose body meets hers standing there (`Danger.beside`: its
  floor less than its top under her feet, or less than her 65 over them, its platform's stretch within reach; the rule
  `Danger.walk` and her trips' bodies already had, now `danger.level`) guards it as one on the pile's own platform: shot
  first, or the pile left until a look sees it clear.
- *Back to the stop* (`grind.BACK`, `Grind._back_due`, `_back`): got to the stop, on another platform where the danger
  with the look's monsters is `BACK_MARGIN` (0.05, a third of a Horny Mushroom's touch) over the stop's place's, she goes
  back to it before she shoots from there, no shooting in passing on the platform she leaves, `BACK_TRIES` (3) a visit
  and `BACK_REST_S` (5 s) apart at the most (unbounded, a prototype sent her back 124 times in a run); the hunt loop's

## The independent check's findings fixed (2026-11-01, the night)

The independent check of 1ff93e6 (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/verify/verdict.txt: not to merge as it was) confirmed
eight findings. This round (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/loot2/fix) fixed five of them and three of its nits, each
with a test, on master 072e1ec. Finding 2 (the stop's 2 s sweep budget, piles about to expire) and 3 (the docs'
15-minute numbers) are left to the next stages: the user's answers of ~02:00 change them ("piles should be picked up
soon after killing"; Meat, 150 HP, 200-300 a run; her pets take what they walk over). Finding 7 (cut and resend
unmeasured since b9933ef) is a measurement for before the live grind.

- **A monster of no known kind priced at nothing** (finding 1, a regression against master). `Danger.taken` of a kind
  the map's game data doesn't have ('', which the landings' judge takes for a 'pig') is now the map's hardest-touching
  kind's, as `Navigator._toucher`'s stand-in is; 0 only with no kind known. With her own prices (a6a2c28) a meeting with
  one had cost nothing: no shot first, no wait at a trip's last landing. Master's flat `MEET_PRICE_S` priced it.
- **The pickup log's cut names** (finding 4). `looting._earned` reads an "earned" line with maplehelper's loot-line
  parser against the game's item names (`maplehelper.ocr.parse.parse_loot`, `ITEM_NAMES`). A cut name it leaves open
  ("Orange Mushro...") is the one priced drop it starts; a misread tab ("(Ete)") is the kind's. Every "earned" line of
  the live fixture (tests/fixtures/pickup_log_lines_2026-10-26.json) now comes out as its item, where the regex read
  "Horny Mushroo... x1 earned. (Etc)" as a kind of its own, never one she held: her cap top-up into a known-full Etc tab
  cleared it. An "earned" line after the last refusal says its tab has room only for a kind that didn't fit (stuck
  under her now, or refused). A top-up of a stack she holds needs no slot; until now such a line kept a tab from being
  learned.
  The simulator's log cuts names over 15 letters to 13 and "..." (`world.log_name`: Tree Dungeon's caps as the game cuts
  them).
- **FAILED_PICKS never reset in the grind** (finding 5). The row of items stuck under her is broken by an item of a
  stand of hers that the looks show gone from its pile (`Looter.on_look`). It starts afresh once it marks a tab full or
  a tab is tried again. Only a mop-up reset it before, and the grind's stands have none: three stuck items in a run,
  however far apart, marked every later one's tab full.
- **Rule 6a and EXP before loot priced items she can't take** (finding 6). They now go by the dearest drop she can take
  (`Hunt._dearest`, by `Pile.each`: what each drop seen is worth) and the pile's worth to her (`Hunt._worth`). With Etc
  full she had rushed a pile of a coin and an ore for the coin.
- **HELD_AGE for good** (finding 8). A pile holds an older pile's age (`Pile.aged`, `aged_xs`; `Pile.born` is what
  `Pile.still` goes by) only while a look still sees a drop where the older's lay; its own `since` is kept. Before, a
  pile whose own drops lay until 330 s in the simulator was given up at 241 s.
- **Nits.** `SPLICE_PHYSICS` checks the arrow as of the press's whole ms (`flow.ms`; at 0.4006 s it missed the 401 ms
  press). Her landings' EXP a second is kept within `fight.RATE_BAND` (4) of `RATE_PRIOR` either way, and is
  `RATE_PRIOR` where the hunt has none or one not over 0: before, a price went by 1 / rate without bound. The claim
  that Tree Dungeon's numbers price her landings "only until her max HP is read" is corrected (above and in fight's
  note): her EXP a second stays the live thief's wherever no grind loop sets one.

**Measured.** The standard grind (the harness standard, 12 seeds of 5 minutes against 1ff93e6, fix/ab.txt) is the same
to the digit: EXP a minute 338.8, touches 85.7, loot's worth 242.2 a minute, drops' share 0.948, hurt 56.0, at piles
12.7, potions 23.0; no deaths, falls or stops. None of the fixes changes a decision there: the map's three kinds are
all priced, no tab fills (the standard world drops no items), the loops' rates are inside the band, and no pile's older
drop goes while its own lie on. With her drops as live (`--world map-drops`) and `etc-full` or `fills-up` added
(fix/ab_etc.txt, ab_fills.txt) the same to the digit too: in `etc-full` she holds no stack, so no "earned" item line
comes, and the tab is learned once from the game's message (fix/probe, seed 1: one `cant_pick` a run); in `fills-up` no
item stays under her twice in 5 minutes (none). So the backpack fixes are checked by the tests alone. The 43 Tree
Dungeon goldens match (`golden check --jobs 4`, fix/golden.txt).

## Loot as she kills: her Meat, her pets, and the seconds a pile may cost her way (2026-11-01, the morning)

The user's answers of 2026-11-01 ~02:00: her pet's HP potion is Meat, "Usually 200 or 300 pieces of meat (150HP)"; piles
"should be picked up soon after killing. If a pile is about to expire, it probably means they aren't important enough
to get picked up anyway. I think a real human would bias route planning to pick up piles"; her pets have "pick-up skills
but not exactly item pouch/meso magnet. The pet will pick up whatever thing when the pet walks past those loot. But the
pet won't proactively go for the loot"; and of MESO_EXP, "I'm not sure about this currency conversion. My idea is just
picking up mesos and items as we kill mobs". The design (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/loot2/design: prototypes measured
in process) was built here (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/loot2/impl), each part measured paired, 12 seeds and 24 where
that was borderline, at 5 and 15 minutes, in a world with her real stock and her pets.

- **Meat from a run's stock** (`--world meat`: world.MEAT_HP, POTIONS). Her pet drinks Meat, 160 HP by the game data
  (item 2010003; 63 live rises of exactly 160 HP on 2026-10-30, the magician's pet), 80 mesos at the user's prices, from
  250 a run (the middle of their 200-300; the user remembered 150 HP). The crowd preset's 60 Orange Potions ran out
  within 15 minutes: in the design's runs (at 150 HP) the safety stop ended 7 of 12 of the tip's 15-minute grinds and
  none with Meat, which gave the tip +21.3 EXP a minute (se 8.0) and +17.3 loot (6.3) over its own 60-potion runs. At 5
  minutes the tip's runs are the same to the digit, but for its potions and cash. A world switch for now: master's code
  has no such world, so the harness's cached baselines of master can't pair with it as a default.
- **Her pets in the simulator** (`--world pet-loot`: Realism.pets, world.PET_SPEED ..., World._pets_step). Two Snail
  pets trail her on her platform and take what they walk over (the game data's pickupItem, no sweepForDrop), as her
  pick-ups, with the pickup log's line and her tabs (World._take). Their numbers are a coarse grid's against the
  perception service's 15 fps records (world.PET_SPEED's note): 31% of her pick-ups theirs, the share by her closest
  approach the live shape about 0.15 high, only 7% taken 45-150 units from her where live 23%. The outcomes show hers
  and her pets' apart (`her_value_per_min`, `pet_value_per_min`, `pet_share`), `drops_expired`, and the fit's tables
  (`taken_from`, `approach`). Checked against the design's prototype: the same runs to the digit (4 seeds).
  Correction: her pets aren't "Coffee" and "Snailail", as the last round read the golden clip: "Coffee" was the end of
  the player AnimalCoffee's tag over a snail, "Snailail" two "Snail" tags 14 px apart. Her pets are Snails named
  "Snail", like other players'.
- **A fresh pile by her left to her pets a moment** (hunt.PET_LOOT, PET_NEAR 100, PET_WAIT 4 s; `Hunt._pets_first` in
  `_candidate`). A pile of hers on her platform within PET_NEAR of her isn't a candidate until she's been by it PET_WAIT
  s, from its landing at the soonest; counted afresh once she's farther. (Off since d58224c, the loot review's finding
  1: its gain was the simulator's pets'; "The branch measured for the record against master 072e1ec (2026-11-01, the
  night)".)
- **Each pile within the seconds it may add to her way** (`Hunt._allow`, sweep.Spot.allow; behavior.sweep). No
  exchange of mesos for EXP in the sweep, no price of her time, no CAND_S, no flat budget. A pile may add ALLOW_FRESH
  (3 s) while it's FRESH_S (15 s, OWN_S) old or younger, down to ALLOW_OLD (1 s) at OLD_S (60 s) and after: no late
  trips for old far piles, nothing for their expiry. Where the danger at it is SAFER_MARGIN (0.05) over where she
  stands, ALLOW_OLD at most ("try not to hit by mobs just for picking up loots"). An itinerary stays within the sum of
  its piles' allowances (its guards' kill times not counted: EXP), and the hunt loop's budget where it has one (its way
  out; a lull's wait, every pile its wait too); of those, the most mesos likely still there, then the least time
  (since 666c54b a pile's allowance by the share of its worth she can take, an itinerary within `sweep.MOST_S`, 6 s,
  and a lull's danger cap kept: the record below). This
  replaces the independent check's finding 2: at a stop the 2 s budget never fetched a fresh coin 160 units off; now
  it's fetched while fresh, and not once old. PILE_HP, the grind's DROPS_IN_CHOICE and `_time_worth` went with the
  exchange (history in grind's comments). MESO_EXP stays for EXP before loot (`_loot_first`, rule 6a) and a bar of her
  HP's price (`bar_exp`: her touches, her landings); since b1ef776 for the latter alone (rule 6a's pile waits while
  something is in reach, whatever its worth or risk).

## A replan dropped as too late: its monster asked about again; the clock inside a replan (2026-11-01, the evening)

The latency analysis of the 15-a-second loop (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/crowd/explanation.txt) found the 15-45 ms
states to be the watch loop's "a better way" check asking the hunt about a made-up spot (`_stop_calls`, Hunt._interrupt,
92% of it `reach.shots`' jump-shot search), harmless in every test, and one weak spot never hit. Of its options the user
chose "a b and d": the spikes left as they are (no skipping the jump-shot search for that check), this fix, and a
cheaper search with the same answers (a later stage, as is their "add a bit jitter" to the jump attacks' two timings).

**The weak spot** (`Navigator._switch`, `_watching`, `_dropped`). `_switch` set `_replanned` before its deadline's
check (`SPLICE_LATE_S`: a replan the player would take more than 50 ms past its plan time 0, or past a takeoff's key of
the running plan, is dropped), so a "monster" replan dropped there left its monster marked reacted-to for
`REACT_AGAIN_S` (3 s): with no room to stop, she ran on into it while the log said "the next state asks again". Now a
late drop clears `_replanned` and leaves `_late` (its why, its ms, how late) for `_watching`, which says it with what
comes of it, one line for every path:
- a monster coming, room to stop: "dropped, she stops for it" (REACT's cut, the monster marked, as before), the cut's
  "plan cut short" next;
- a monster coming, no room: "dropped, the next state asks again", now true (not marked: the next state's `_coming`
  finds it again and `_switch` replans for it from there);
- a better way: "dropped, the next look for a better way asks again (0.33 s on)" (`BETTER_EVERY_S`; nothing else
  changes for it: nothing is marked by a better way's look).
(From the review of 2026-11-01 the next state asks again once in a row, `LATE_RETRIES`; dropped late again, the monster
is asked about again 1.5 s on, `LATE_AGAIN_S`: The reviews' findings fixed, below.)
A replan that ran with nothing to take (no route, nothing chains) still marks its monster (the review of 2026-10-30).
The 'replan' event's "dropped: too late" says its kind (`of`) and what came of it (`then`). Each state asking again
costs a replan's time again while the drops last (the one monster's drop below had room: she stopped).

**The clock inside a replan** (`fakes.Clock.reads`, `Scenario.think_reads`, the harness's `--think-clock K`). With
`--think K` the stack's computing is charged to the fake clock at the fakes' calls only (a look, a glance's wait, a
sleep, a plan sent or spliced), so a read of the clock inside the computing gives the last call's time: `_switch`'s
`late` was 0 however long it took, and `FakePlayer.splice` charged it only after the check (the splice then taken late).
`--think-clock K` charges it as it goes: at every read of the clock (`monotonic`, `perf_counter`, `time`) what was
computed since the last charge first, times K (the real `perf_counter`'s), the world and the feed's frames going on
meanwhile, as live. Exclusive with `--think`; not cached (`baseline.UNCACHED`); a result says `think_clock` only where
it's set. Off by default: every cache key and result as before.

**Checked.** The harness standard (12 seeds, `ab --base 666c54b`,
`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/speed/b/ab_default.txt`, 666c54b's seeds run into the cache first): every headline
difference zero, and all 114 keys of all 12 results the same to the digit (`default_same.txt`). The 43 Tree Dungeon

loop_tree_attack_no_darts and loop_tree_attack_misses); the new tests fail on the old navigator (the late monster never

## The jump-shot search cheaper, the same answers (2026-11-01, the evening)

The user's option d of the latency analysis: "make the search itself cheaper with the same answers". Four changes,
each exact (the analysis's probe, `crowd/probe/variants.py` and `shots_copy.py`, had them; made again in the code):
- **Sight lines by a grid** (`reach._Sight`, `_sight`, `SIGHT_CELL`). `sight_stop` and `clear_length` tried every one
  of a platform's floors and walls for every line (`_near_line`: on Tree Dungeon 182 floors and the 214 walls of its
  tower's group, 396 for each of its 19 platforms in it), 40% of the time of the 40 slowest searches. Now a platform's
  footholds are listed by the 64-unit cells their bounds touch (made once a platform, kept on it, anew for other floors
  or walls), and a line's are taken from the cells its box touches: the same ones, in the same order (59 us a line
  there, 4). The tower's floors share one x range, so the cells go across and down. The simulator's world's line
  (`World.sight_stop`, through `wall_between`) is the same code.
- **The monsters' places once a search** (`reach.shots`' `placed`). Both sides of each kind of jump try the same
  attack keys, so they asked `where` (`fight.walk_on`) for the same times again: 39% of those searches' time.
- **A jump's landing before its keys** (`reach.shots`' `lands`, `jump_lands_back`, `Shot.lands_back`;
  `stance.jump_room`; `fight.jump_cover`). `stance._jump_shot`, the only taker of a jump shot (the stance's two asks,
  `jump_hits` for the hunt loop's and grinding's in reach, the escort's `jump_reaches`), takes none whose jump lands
  her anywhere but back on her platform within `_stand_limits` however it goes, and that is the jump's (each side and
  kind's landing and its variants'), known before any key is tried. So `jump_cover` asks with `jump_room` (the
  uncrowded limits, the widest any ask keeps to) and a jump landing elsewhere has none of its keys tried (in the
  analysis's worst state every shot found was of a jump landing on the platform above). The shots kept are the same,
  field for field, in the same order; those left out no asker takes (`_jump_shot` uses `Shot.lands_back` itself, so
  the two can't drift apart). The analysis's warning (exact for the hunt's question only) was for its probe's crowded
  limits; the uncrowded ones hold for every ask.
- **A trip's question asks what's in reach only where it decides** (`Hunt._interrupt`). In passing, the first monster
  a star from where she stands hits decides it, the others' jump-shot searches not made; with neither her time in
  passing there left nor a spot's ground to shoot at from there, nothing in reach is asked (the answer was
  `_sweep_calls`' either way).

The 89 attack keys a start are still tried (the user's "you only need two jump attacks", at once and at the jump's
top, 40 and 278 ms, with "a bit jitter", is the jump-attack stage's: Two jump attacks, jittered, below); the first three

## Two jump attacks, jittered: at once and at the top (2026-11-01, the night)

The user, after the latency analysis: "You only need two jump attacks: one with jump and immediately attack, another with jump and attack at mid air peak", then "The 40 ma and 278ms thing, add a bit jitter to it so we still have some variation and can later on analyze if the jitter can show any pattern".

- **Two keys** (`reach.shots`; `KEY_FIRST_MS`, `TOP_KEY_MS`, `KEY_SLACK_MS`, `KEY_CHECK_MS`). Each jump and side tries the soonest key (40 ms after the jump key; a jump that turns her in the air, the turn's soonest, `turn_key_ms`: 120) and the top's (`TOP_KEY_MS = round(physics.APEX_S * 1000)`, 278: an attack starts `JUMP_LAG` after its key as the jump lifts off `JUMP_LAG` after its own, so keyed so it starts at her arc's top, 77 up), the sooner that surely picks the target winning (`Coverage.best`, the stance's order as before). Sure as before, the same pick 15 ms either side of the key and across the decide lag, now checked every 5 ms where the scan checked the two ends. From 2026-10-25 to now every key from the soonest to 480 was tried, 5 ms apart (about 89 a start; the user then: the timing "needs to be dynamic but preferably attack immediately after jump or at jump 2"); `KEY_LAST_MS` and `KEY_STEP_MS` are gone.
- **The jitter** (`fight.jittered`, `JITTER_FIRST_MS` 15, `JITTER_TOP_MS` 20). A jump attack's key is its base key plus a jitter drawn as it's carried out (`throw_act`, as its key plan is made), uniform to the ms over its window: the soonest's up to 15 ms later, never sooner (sooner than 40 the game may take the attack on the ground, unmeasured; sooner than the turn's soonest a turn in the air went the wrong way more often live), the game's own spread of a key (`KEY_SLACK_MS`: `body.Lags`' 7.7 ms sd, twice), her feet 7 units higher at the most; the top's 20 ms either side (her arc flat there: within 0.4 units of the top). Drawn from the hunter's own generator (`Hunter.jitter`: the system's live; `sim.scenarios.Sim.hunter` seeds it by the scenario's seed, so a simulated run is the same to the digit when run again), not in the search, which stays deterministic.
- **Still sure** (`Shot.window`). The search checks the pick over the whole room the jitter may take the key to, the slack about every key of it too; where it isn't sure all over that the window is narrowed to the keys about the key that are (a shot sure at its key alone is kept with no jitter, not dropped: dropping would lose shots the scan had at that very key, and the record says how much room there was). The window was the run of later keys that still picked the target (used by `Shot.text` and the 'jump' record alone); it's the jitter's room now.
- **Up close too** (`stance._from_here`, `_jittered_up`, `JumpPlan.room`, `JumpPlan.keys`). Most of her jump throws aren't shots: a jump in place at a monster too close for the ground's star (28 a 5-minute run on the hunt loop against 4.3 shots), keyed 40 ms after the jump key (120 turning in the air; after a tap first). A sure one gets the keys after its key, up to 15 ms later, whose attack surely picks the monster too by the stance's own check (`reach.air_sure`, `CLEAR_MARGIN` farther, every 5 ms), up to the first that doesn't (40-45 at a pig 95-105 off on her floor); its plan says 'close' (or 'tap first'). One not sure keeps the stance's own key. (From the review of 2026-11-01 each later key's line to it is checked too, `ROOM_LINE`, and one not sure is jittered over the whole of the soonest's room, `fight.JITTER_ALL`: The reviews' findings fixed, below.)
- **Recorded.** Her log's jump line says the key as keyed ("the attack 278 ms in (258-298), 77 up: pig +150, keyed at 285 (+7)"; "jump (close): a jump in place throwing right, the attack 40 ms in (40-45), keyed at 43 (+3): pig +105"). The 'jump' record: the key sent (`key_ms`), the shot's own (`base_ms`), the jitter (`jitter_ms`), the room (`window`), the turn in the air, her rise at the attack's start as keyed, the target's kind, dx and height, the jump's kind and side, where she lands, its number (`n`); after its keys a 'jump_keys' record (by `n`): whether they went, and the attack key as the player pressed it after the jump key (`pressed_ms`: `Actions.key_gap`, from the player's answer's 'sent', which `Actions.play` keeps now; the simulator's player answers with the plan's own times). In a simulated run each of her attacks as the world resolved it is a 'sim_attack' record (`World.on_attack`, `Sim._attack_told`: its key's time, plan, ground or air, her rise, the kind it picked, its outcome), so the run's telemetry carries its own outcomes. `sim.harness.attack_kinds`' `chosen` counts the 'close' and 'tap first' ones too.
- **The report** (`python -m gamelab jitter [FILES]`, `analysis.jumps.jitter_report`; by default the live telemetry). Each jump attack with jitter joined to its 'jump_keys' (not thrown: no outcome) and its outcome: the simulator's own in a simulated run's telemetry (its first jump attack keyed within 1.5 s of the record, as `attack_kinds` matches them), else the looks' (`outcomes`: a kill by its EXP gain, a hit by a bar lower, else nothing seen). By base key, jump kind, turn, close or shot, and 5 ms bin about a multiple of 5 (the soonest's 0 to +15, the top's -20 to +20): how many, kills, hits, misses, wasted, the share that hit, the targets' median distance and height; whether the jitter predicts a hit (a permutation test within each group with 2 hits and 2 not, and stratified over all of them: 2,000 shuffles, seeded); the player's presses against the keys sent. In the simulator the outcome follows its model of the pick, the one the search goes by, so a pattern there is the model's; the live grinds are where one means something.

**What the two keys change, on the exact stage's recorded searches** (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/speed/j`: replay2.py, old_shots.py, sum_replay.py, lost.py; option d's recordings of 3255623's code, the harness standard's 12 seeds and the hunt loop's 4, every search made again both ways, 3255623's search reproducing all 5,938 records): of 9,787 wanted monsters, 2,311 had a jump shot by the 89 keys (their soonest key 40 for 44%, 45-115 ms for 27%, 120 for 5%, 125-275 for 21%, after the top for 3%). By the two keys 115 of them (5.0%) have none (up 3.9% of those with one, forward 7.9%, back 7.5%; all Green and Horny Mushrooms; 62% of the lost shots were on her way down, 278 ms and later, 18% before 120); 1,117 have the same soonest key, 1,079 a later one (by 108 ms at the median, 218 at p90, 238 at most), none a sooner one, 1 a shot it had none of (sure at 278, between the scan's 275 and 280). The stance's own choice, asked both ways on the two keys' runs (rec2.py: every `stance._jump_shot` asked with the 89 keys' cover too, 16 runs): of 1,954 asks, 66.8% none either way, 13.9% the same shot, 18.2% the same jump at a later key (by 143 ms at the median, 233 at most), 0.7% a shot by the 89 keys and none by the two, 0.3% another jump at the same target (5 of 6 sooner: a jump forward at once where the scan had a jump in place turning, 445 ms in).

## The reviews' findings fixed, and the branch measured again (2026-11-01, late)

The two reviews of e7932ad (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/speed/review: the adversarial review of 666c54b..e7932ad;
`speed/adv`: the independent check of the record above) found one defect, in the jitter up close, and gaps; each is
fixed here or said why not. This round's measurements: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/replan/speed/fix (`out/` the runs in
process by `drv5.py`, the record stage's drv4.py with `--set MODULE:NAME=VALUE` switches; `tables.py`, `chosen.py`,
`same_runs.py`; the harness's own `ab` runs in `out/ab_*.txt`; `golden/`, `tests/`, `bench/`).

**The findings, one by one.**
- *A close jump throw's jitter room ignored its line* (the first review's finding 1, MEDIUM): fixed, 99506a4.
  `stance._jittered_up` widened the room (40 ms on, up to `JITTER_FIRST_MS`) by `reach.air_sure` alone; on a slope her
  floor, or one just over her, stopped the star of a later key where the key's hit (Tree Dungeon's 33 at x 126.9 at a
  Horny Mushroom 107 off: keyed 40 the world's star hits, 41-55 stopped). Now each later key's line too (`ROOM_LINE`,
  `_from_here`'s `clear`: `reach.wall_in_way` from her feet as its attack starts, at both ends of the decide lag as
  `air_sure`'s pick, to where the monster is then). On 300 of the world's close throws at a lone still mushroom on Tree
  Dungeon floors (`world_rooms.py`): room keys the world's star doesn't hit with 185 of 4,150 (22 throws) -> 0 of 3,490
  (with the line at the attack's start alone, 10 of 3,940); rooms whole (40-55) 236 -> 177. On the harness standard's 12
  seeds no run changes (with `ROOM_LINE` off the same to the digit): its close throws there have no later key whose line
  is stopped.
- *58% of her jump attacks neither jittered nor recorded* (the first review's finding 4b, the second's F2): fixed,
  7cb9e9d, d89ce8e and e8c1403. `fight.jittered`'s `JITTER_ALL`: a jump attack the stance keyed at its own key, with no
  shot and no room (a jump throw up close not sure, 'tap first' not sure, at a snail, a jump back, a jump up onto the
  platform above, `ESCAPE_UP`), is keyed over the soonest's whole room from the key her actions would press (40-55; 120-135
  turning in the air or a jump back's), never sooner, its plan not sure (`JumpPlan.sure` False), and recorded as the
  others ('jump' with `sure`, its kind 'unsure', 'jump back', 'tap first' or 'up onto N'). In the 48 standard runs every
  jump attack has its record now (2,393; 932 of 2,213 before). With `JITTER_ALL` off they are keyed as before and still
  recorded (their room the key alone, nothing drawn): 12 standard seeds the previous tip's to the digit on every key but
  the records' own counts (`out/same_off12.txt`; `random.randint` over one key still takes bits from the generator, so a
  draw there had moved the sure ones' draws after it: e8c1403).
- *The jitter analysis's gaps* (the first review's finding 4, the second's F1): fixed, 30bd23c and ba1e4b2. The window and the
  jitter were confounded (a room narrowed by the target's geometry gives no large jitter): `jitter_test` shuffles within
  each room alone (`_room`, with its base key, kind, turn and shot/close/unsure), `jitter_table` says each bin's share of
  narrowed rooms. The jitter is the press's (`pressed_jitter`), and a press more than `PRESS_OFF_MS` (5) off its key sent
  (her actions turning her in the air at their own key where the stance had her facing it, 76-80 ms off) isn't counted.
  A 'jump_keys' record goes with the 'jump' record just before it with its `n` (each hunter numbers its own from 1). A
  record with no target doesn't stop `outcomes`. The soonest's small jitter against the game's own spread of a key (sd
  4.6 ms against about 11-13, seen at the game's 30 ms steps) is not a defect but a limit: a pattern within 0 to +15
  shows only over many attacks (the module's docstring says so); the top's -20 to +20 is wider.
- *A late monster replan retried at every state* (the first review's finding 3, LOW-MEDIUM): fixed, 76adfef. The next
  state asks again `LATE_RETRIES` (1) times in a row; dropped late again, the monster is marked for `LATE_AGAIN_S`
  (`REACT_AGAIN_S` / 2, 1.5 s), then asked about again; the log says so. It never fires in the harness's runs (no monster
  replan was dropped late at 1x or 3x of its computing charged, here or in the bookkeeping stage): its tests alone.
- *The two keys' cost, grinding's share of her drops* (the first review's finding 2, the second's F3): measured, not a
  cost at 48 seeds. Against the jump stage's base 3255623 (`ab ... --base 3255623`, its seeds 13-48 filled; `out/
  t_prev_vs_325_48.txt`) the previous tip's share is 0.953 against 0.960 (-0.007, se 0.006): seeds 1-12 had it -0.028

  EXP cost of the two keys (-21.8 a minute on 24 seeds in their section): none measurable on 96 (next section).
- *Tests weakened* (the first review's finding 5): fixed, 270c87e: the ten `act[:2]` assertions compare the whole act
  less its room and target again (`test_attack.close`, `no_room`), or the act itself where the stance keys it unsure.
- *Nits*: the default save name (7a69c7a: "-think1.5", "-think-clock3", where such a run's save had gone over the

  `Map` says): native.c is master's unchanged, its DLL named by its source's hash, so a comment would have every

deaths, falls or stops. About 2 third-key attacks a run in the hunt loop (76% hit or kill), and the top's key from 1.8 a
run to 0.35: the jitter report's top would have few. On the 5,938 recorded searches made again (`replay/replay3.py`): of
4,595 targets with a jump shot by the 89 keys the two keys lose 279, and a third key wins back 25-39 of them (14% at

55-93 ms at the median against 148), for at most 5% more search (2.68 -> 2.81 s for all of them).

## Spawns seen as they fade in: every spawn point in view, every frame (from 2026-11-01)

The user, 2026-11-01: "it seems that it doesn't detect monsters that have just spawned because spawned monsters are
fading-in. Anyway we can improve that?" Of the three ways offered (a fade-aware check at the spawn points, a colour
gate that lets blends toward the background through anywhere on screen, the planner taking a point due a respawn as
maybe occupied), they chose the first and widened it: "Should probably always check instead of only checking when it's
due." and, of the second's false alarms, "Do you mean false positives? I'd like to avoid that." So every spawn point in
view is looked at on every frame, whatever the respawn belief says, by a check tuned for no false positive with a wide
margin (misses rather than ghosts), and nothing anywhere else on screen is loosened. The measurements, the mechanics and
the prototype: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/spawn-fade (measure, mech, proto); this build's replays: spawn-fade/integ.

**Why the whole screen found them late.** A monster the map spawns fades in from nothing to solid, linearly, in 0.817 s
(alpha 1.224 a second, p10-p90 1.201-1.256 over 223 births on 20.9 minutes of Tree Dungeon's lossless clips: the golden
clip of the user's own play and 14 Lie Detector alarm clips; HeavenClient's port fades in 0.32 s: this client is
slower), its feet on its spawn point, in its move/0 picture (194 of 206) or stand/0 (12), walking from the start. Every
pixel of it is the game's blend of its picture over the map's art, one alpha over all of it (the fit's residual 0.27-0.3
levels). The whole screen's search (perception.mobs) looks for a monster's own colours: its step 1 (the colour gate and
silhouettes) passes a newborn only at alpha 0.6-0.8, so it found newborns a median 7 frames, 468 ms, after they first
showed, at alpha 0.63 (Horny Mushrooms 552 ms, Green ones 400; step 2 alone, at the right place, would pass 96% at
alpha 0.3-0.4). The perception service's records of 2026-10-28..30 saw 878 newborns an hour come into view.

**The check** (`perception/spawns.py`, `gamelab/spawns.c`; `worldstate.SPAWNS`, `WorldStep._newborns`, `_handed`,
`_spawn_watch`, `worldstate.spawn_points`). Every spawn point whose window is in the play area and clear of the chat
box, the minimap and the quest helper (camreg.EXCLUDE), wholly or past the screen's top, left or right edge in part (the
rest left out of the fit, the art in its place: `SpawnWatch._shown`, `ONSET_COVERED`), on every frame of the game as
expected with her placed and the view registered on it (the scene's locator), after her look and while the whole
screen's search finishes on its thread:
1. *Empty test*: fewer than `EMPTY_COUNT` (20) pixels more than `EMPTY_LEVELS` (3) off the art on some channel: nothing.
2. *Onset fit*: the point's kind's `ONSET` pictures (stand/0, move/0) both ways, its feet within `BAND` (4) units of
   the point along its platform, `ROWS` (+-1) up or down: 108 hypotheses, every `STRIDE`-th (3rd) pixel of each picture
   weighted by its alpha (657 of a Horny Mushroom's, 538 of a Slime's). With D = F - B, G = A (S - B): a = D.G / G.G,
   R2 = (D.G)^2 / (G.G D.D), residual sqrt((D.D - (D.G)^2 / G.G) / n). The hypothesis explaining the most with
   `A_LO`-`A_HI` (0.015-0.95) and `MIN_USED` (40%) of its pixels left is the point's; a newborn where `A_MIN` (0.02)
   <= a <= `A_START` (0.8), 1 - R2 <= `U_MAX` (0.008) and the residual <= `RES_MAX` (1.5 levels).
3. *Follow*: each newborn from the next frame, every `FOLLOW` picture of its kind (stand, move, hit1), its feet up to
   `FOLLOW_SPEED` (180 units a second: 12 a frame at 15) the way each faces and `BACK` (3) the other, the same rule, its
   alpha no more than `DROP_A` (0.08) under the most it's been (found fainter than that, it's fading out, not in: let
   go, and its place not looked at for another for a whole fade, 0.82 s); until the whole screen finds a monster of its
   kind within `HANDOVER_DX` (15) across and `HANDOVER_DY` (8) down of it (`SpawnWatch.handed`: that frame's sighting
   is the search's, the watch done with it; one of another kind there has the frame's place, the newborn followed on),
   its best fit is solid, or it's unfound `LOST_AFTER` (2) frames.
Her box (`HER_BOX`: 40 either side of her feet, 85 up, 28 down) and the boxes of the monsters the frame before found
(`MOB_BOX`, the tracker's `matched`, not the watch's own newborns; at an onset not one within `ON_POINT` of the point)
are left out of the fits. The maps watched are `MEASURED`'s, each with its kinds (Tree Dungeon: its 15 Horny Mushroom,
14 Green Mushroom and 2 Slime points; on any other map none, its kinds Tree Dungeon's or not); only at the game's own
1366x768, with the scene's locator and the watch's C (else none: in numpy it took 13.6 ms a frame, 132 at p99).

| Constant | Value | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `FADE_PER_S` | 1.224 | the measured fade (223 births; 0.817 s to solid) |
| `EMPTY_LEVELS`, `EMPTY_COUNT` | 3, 20 | the prototype's empty test: a frame where nothing is drawn is the art to the level |
| `BAND`, `ROWS` | 4, +-1 | of 99 newborns caught before alpha 0.15, 82 started at the point's x exactly, all within 3 |
| `ONSET` | stand/0, move/0 | the newborns' first pictures (194 move/0, 12 stand/0); every stand and move picture found 12 more hidden starts at about 3 times the cost |
| `A_MIN`, `U_MAX`, `RES_MAX` | 0.02, 0.008, 1.5 | the rule over every point-frame of the clips (rules2.py): no false positive, the nearest negative (a solid, partly covered Horny Mushroom at a 0.94: 1 - R2 0.040, residual 17.7) 11.8 times past it; newborns' fits 1 - R2 0.0002-0.001, residuals 0.27-0.30 at alpha 0.05-0.6. R2 alone found 9 more births end to end, but 4 of its follows drifted onto something else: the residual holds the follow |
| `A_LO`, `A_HI`, `MIN_USED` | 0.015, 0.95, 40% | over 0.95 a solid monster, the whole screen's; a hypothesis with most of its pixels under her or another monster (or off the screen) isn't tried |
| `A_START` | 0.8 | the review: a solid monster by its point under a faint shade over the whole screen (5% black) fits as a newborn at a 0.94, 1.15-1.30 times off the rule; under 0.8 a shade must take 20% off, 4.7-5.2 times off at the nearest. The 48 onsets over 0.8 on the clips were all on traced newborns, 47 found at that point in the 20 frames before |
| `ONSET_COVERED` | False | a window reaching under the chat box or the game's windows isn't looked at: the rows over the chat box are drawn over now and then (its border, lines of text), newborns there fit 2.5-5 levels off (none found), and a solid Slime cut by it came 3.3 times off the rule; past the screen's top or sides every fit within 14 times of it was a newborn |
| `FOLLOW_SPEED`, `BACK`, `DROP_A` | 180/s, 3, 0.08 | a newborn's steps a frame (the median 5 units, p99 12, the most 16); `DROP_A` under the most it's been, not the frame before's (a picture fading out was followed all the way down, 0.08 a frame at a time) |
| `HANDOVER_DX`, `HANDOVER_DY`, `LOST_AFTER` | 15, 8, 2 | the prototype's hand-over (318 of 390 followed newborns handed over at alpha 0.69, 68 lost to cover at 0.29) |
| `HER_BOX`, `MOB_BOX`, `ON_POINT` | see above | her body and name tag, a mushroom's 56 x 52 pictures |

*The background is the map's own art*, the picture the camera registration holds (localization.mapart: Tree Dungeon's
is fixed art everywhere), not one learned: of the prototype's backgrounds, a running median of each point (a sample
every 0.5 s, the last 11, her and the monsters masked) found 199 births against the art's 252 and came within 3.9 times
of the rule on her passing (alpha 0.11, residual 2.4), and plates kept from windows unchanged for 0.6 s found 224 and
gave a false positive under a looser rule. The art can't be fooled by her standing on a point (the test: 6.6 s of her
on point 14, then the newborn there found 7 frames after she left, at alpha 0.098, as with nothing before it) and needs
no warm-up; where a map's art isn't its fixed art alone (mapart's `static`: animated objects, moving backgrounds) those
pixels are left out of the fit. A view one px off loses newborns and made no false positive (the prototype's shift.py).

**What the state says of a newborn.** Each sighting is a detection beside the whole screen's (`Sighting.mob`: its feet,
picture, facing and pose, its fit's share explained as its score, so the death watch doesn't look at it), with its alpha
(`Mob.fading`, `Monster.fading`; the scene records' monsters `fading`). The tracker (localization.tracking) makes it a
track at once, 'spawned' (its alpha in the event), with `Track.fading` (its alpha as of its last sighting, carried on
its fade's line once the whole screen has it, which finds them at 0.6-0.8) and `Track.solid_at` (when it turns solid: t
+ (1 - a) / FADE_PER_S; `Track.opacity(t)`; the 'tracks' records' `fading`). A newborn can be hit while it fades (its HP
bar shows from alpha about 0.36) but didn't touch her until it was solid (1 of her 34 touches on the golden clip came in
the 0.82 s after a respawn pass, against 3.9 at random; one clip, two examples frame by frame): for the planner to use,
nothing of it changed yet. A fading sighting is the track of a monster first seen since its fade began only, never an
older monster's (`FADE_SLACK_S`), nor (from the review) the newborn's before it at its point, and a track seen fading
isn't dropped as a flicker (`MIN_SEEN_S`): it's a monster, not scenery. The service's 10 s line and 'perf' record say
the watch's time a frame and the newborns found a minute (`spawns_ms`, `newborns_a_min`).
