Harness, preset `game`, 20 seeds of 20 minutes, leaving out the one run each where she fell out of the map through a corner (the loop's seed 13 before, the tour's seed 10 after): the hunt loop 123.6 -> 115.3 EXP a minute (better on 7 of 19 seeds), picking up 95% of its drops instead of 80%, with as much HP lost (2.5 bars); the tour 88.9 -> 86.2 (better on 7 of 19), 92% of its drops instead of 95%, HP lost 2.8 -> 2.5 bars. A seed's EXP a minute moves by 21-25% either way, so these means are good to about 5%. On the loop's seed 17, putting the jump's lag alone back to 55 ms undoes most of its change (90% -> 43% of drops picked up, 151 -> 158 EXP a minute, against 32% and 165 before): with lift-offs and attacks 12 ms later she attacked 11% less often there (1,013 attacks against 1,143) and picked up more; how isn't pinned down. All of this is the stack against its own model, not the game.

## Attack

- **Which attack a throw is** (`attack/choice.py`, `behavior/attacks.py`; `tour` and `hunt` `--attack choice`, the default from 2026-10-24). The user, out of MP and potions: "please try to use a mixture of regular attack and lucky seven ... I meant use lucky seven first but for finishing up a low hp monster, use regular attack", and "if MP amount is not enough to cast a single lucky seven, then use regular attack". So each throw, as its key goes out (every throw goes through `Actions`, whose attack key asks the hunter's `Attacks.key`):
  - the regular attack while her MP is under one cast (Lucky Seven's `mpCon` at her skill level in the game data, 14 at level 16: config.toml `[character] lucky_seven`, `mp` 623; 11 at level 10 and 601 until 2026-10-26: Her throws at the dead, below), her MP her bar's share less a px of it (1/104: so a cast is never pressed with too little, which in game throws nothing); no other reserve;
  - the regular attack at a monster whose HP left it takes about as fast as Lucky Seven would (`finishes`: its expected throws within `FINISH_SLACK` 0.25 of a throw of Lucky Seven's; a guess), Lucky Seven there being overkill: its MP and stars for nothing;
  - the regular attack with nothing seen in the throw's way; Lucky Seven otherwise.
  - **What a monster has left** (`choice.Left`) is a chance of each amount, not one number: its HP in the game data (`MapModel.mob_hp`: a Horny Mushroom 403, defence 10; a Green 233) less each of her throws at it, the attack's damage as drawn (the regular star 20-140 before defence, Lucky Seven two stars of 96-192 at its level 16, scaled by its damage in the game data at another: as the monsters' bars read them at level 25 on 2026-10-25, Her throws at the dead, below; until 2026-10-26 30-70 and 45-105, the simulator's, fitted to her kills when the bars over hurt monsters read empty on Tree Dungeon at 1366x768, 83 of 87 in the 20:57 run of 2026-10-24: Perception, Monster HP bars) or nothing with `MISS` 0.275's chance; a look that sees it alive once a throw has shown if it hit (0.6 s, `LANDS_S`: the server's damage, live on the bar 0.21-0.55 s after the key; 0.85 until 2026-10-26) rules out what that throw would have killed it with, and one that reads its bar between empty and full sets it. A bar up but read empty still says her damage shows (the game shows a monster's bar to whoever damages it): the chance all her throws at it missed is dropped (`Left.hit`, from review on 2026-10-25), once no throw is out that may have shown since and not landed (keyed 0.15-0.6 s before the look: `SHOWS_S`, `LANDS_S`). In the live tours of 2026-10-24 a bar was up on 28% of sightings 0.85-6 s after her throws at a monster near it and 9.5% of those with none, and those didn't go with other players by them (7.2% of sightings with another player on its platform, 9.7% without: her stars hitting another in their path than the one aimed at, and misreads), so a bar on a monster she hasn't thrown at isn't taken for others' damage, and it has its whole HP. In the simulator with the bars drawn empty, `Left.hit` took the all-missed chance (about a quarter) off 45 times in 5 minutes, and the choice still threw no regular attack to finish in 518 throws (seeds 1-3 of 10 minutes; her reckoning of a target's HP off by a median 96-98, against 86-98 before): Lucky Seven's two stars of 45-105 leave what a monster has left too spread for the regular attack to be about as fast, short of a bar's share. A throw takes the likeliest monster in its way that isn't likelier dead than alive by her throws, and is chosen by what that one has left if it's alive when the star lands. By the throws' average damage alone, two casts left a Green still walking with 16 HP and the regular attack went to finish it: in the simulator 17 of 25 such throws didn't kill, and the choice made 159 EXP a minute against Lucky Seven's 215.

- **Range** (`reach.py`): a star reaches 400 units to the near side of a monster's body: 200 for the claw (Lucky Seven's text: "within 200 range in front") and 200 more with Keen Eyes maxed, both by the skill data. On her level stars have hit slimes 408, 410 and 452 units off by their middle at the look before the throw (the last walking closer before the attack started) and missed at 421, 560 and 634 (`lab/range_probe.jsonl`); in the tours' telemetry none was hit at 445 or 472. So a pig is in reach out to 434 by its middle and a snail to 419 (460 for all, before). She throws as soon as the target is within 410 units, leaving room for it to walk during the half-second wind-up. Close up the claw swipes instead, for 9-11 damage against 30-70 for a star. Each attack takes one of the claw's two stab stances at random (stabO1 or stabO2), cuts that stance's box in the game data to 65 units ahead of her, and swipes the nearest monster whose body reaches into it, on her level or not (the client's routine: sources under the angle, below). The boxes reach from 12-20 to 65 ahead of her and from 15 to 30 above her feet, so a monster on her level up to 65 plus half its width off by its middle (a pig 99, a snail 84), and off it none whose feet are 30 or more above hers, nor one whose top is under 15 above them (walking, a pig more than 31 below her, an Orange Mushroom more than 40). So she counts on a star at a monster on her platform only from 12 units past that, by its size (`reach.claw_edge`): a pig from 111, an Orange Mushroom from 109, a slime from 105, a snail from 96. Before, the claw's swings' boxes were taken for it (73-102 ahead, as 90, on her level only: a pig from 136, a snail from 121), and before that 100 for every kind.
- **Other platforms, and the angle:** stars pass through other platforms (going down past her own platform's end: what stops a star, below), so targets on a platform up to 60 units below or above her are shot too (a pig 60 below hit, a pig 60 above killed). Off her level a star needs room sideways, and how much goes by the monster's body. From the ground the attack finds its target by a stepped search (`reach.search_band`), the client's own (where it comes from: below). It looks in 20-unit bands from 65 ahead of her out to 400. Band k's window reaches (65 + 20k) / 4 units (in whole units) above and below a row 28 above her feet, so from 12 - 5k to 44 + 5k above her feet (`reach.window`): one unit up and one down for every four ahead (14 degrees). The star goes to a monster whose body (its box in the game data) overlaps the first band any body does. Of those the client takes the one that entered the map first, which can't be seen, so any of them may take it (`reach.take_chances`; the simulator draws one per attack). So a monster off her level is picked only once its far side reaches the band whose window takes in its body (`reach.min_dx`, middle to middle, walking bodies):

  | | Snail | Slime | Pig | Orange Mushroom |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 60 above | 126 | 117 | 111 | 113 |
  | 42 above (predicted) | 46 | 37 | 31 | 33 |
  | her level | 46 | 37 | 31 | 33 |
  | 42 below (predicted) | 166 | 97 | 71 | 33 |
  | 60 below | 246 | 177 | 151 | 113 |

  60 above her the top decides it: with the logs' lower top (21, below) each kind would be picked only from 191-207, and 42 above from 131-147. With the client's, a monster 42 above has its feet 2 units under the first window's top, so it's picked as on her level. The 42 rows are the search's prediction, unchecked: nothing has been thrown 42 above her, and the only throws logged 42 below go against it (from 0 at 1, the shot log of 2026-10-18: pigs 124-125 off missed 3 times of 4 and an Orange Mushroom 91 off missed, where the search picks both, a pig from 71 and an Orange Mushroom from 33; what else was in front wasn't logged then; at 158-210, 5 of 5 hit). So between her level and 60 below her, her decisions keep at least to the old ramp (`reach.RAMP_BELOW`: 42 below, 126 for every kind, a snail 166 by the search) until `probe run below-42` settles it; on this map that's only 0 -> 1. A pig flinching after a hit (54 tall) is picked 60 below her from 111, one standing (38) from 171; 120 above her the last bands pick each kind from about 351, but she doesn't throw that high (60 is measured). On her level the claw swipes first, so she counts on a star only past its reach (`reach.shot_dx`: a pig from 99, a snail from 84), and on her platform only past the claw's edge (above). With one right under or over her, she steps along her platform to 40 past where a star picks its kind; before, any monster 60 below was thrown at from 150 (a slime needs 177, a snail 247, and an Orange Mushroom is picked from 113), and a pig 42 below from 126 (still so, by the ramp). From a jump the search doesn't fit (stars keyed 40 ms after the jump killed snails 36-66 units away, closer than it starts), so an attack from a jump keeps to the area (below).
- **Where the search and the claw's reach come from.** The game decides what an attack takes in the client, from data it has (ranges, bodies, the claw's boxes), and the game's own files hold only those inputs: a claw's afterimages have boxes for its swings and stabs (none for `shoot`), Lucky Seven's skill data has no range or box, only Keen Eyes a `range` (50-200), and no foothold or map has a flag for stars (local game data v779, all 14,662 images). Two readings of the client's code give the routine alike:
  - RustMS (github.com/neeerp/RustMS, HeavenClient at commit 946474460d4c, unchanged in today's master), a port of the decompiled 2025 MapleRoyals client, GMS v83, which its author calls AI-assisted; it has unit tests of its own. `ShotPath.h:20` `HEIGHT = 28` (the shot's row above her feet), `:26` `SPREAD_DIVISOR = 4`, `:29` `STEP = 20`; `:311-331` (`search_steps`): each step's half-height is its near edge's distance from her divided by 4, in whole units, about that row (its test: the first step for her feet at y 200 is y 156-188, 44 to 12 above them); `:335-339` (`in_step`): overlap is strict. `PointBlank.h:16` `MAX_REACH = 65`, `:20-26`: the claw's box has its front cut to 65 ahead, and the search starts where it ends. `Combat.cpp:1665-1676` (`find_whack`): the stance is picked first, with the weapon's close list (`CharLook.cpp:641-655`), which for a claw (`info/attack` 7) is stabO1 or stabO2 (`AttackStances.h:49`; the swings are the throw's own list), and the nearest monster in its box, by distance (`:1813-1842`), is whacked, with no gate for her level. `:1695-1720`: the steps are tried nearest first, and within one the monster that entered the map first wins.
  - meowdb's MapleStory Classic pages (this game; meowdb.com/msclassic/formulas/targeting and the Lucky Seven page, fetched 2026-10-20): its code has `{aimHeight: 28, divisor: 4, step: 20, starts: {ranged: 65}}` with a band's half-height `floor(start / 4)`, and its Lucky Seven figure 124 up and 68 down at the last band (385-400), drawn since the 2026-08-22 snapshot, before RustMS's code. It states no method. Its damage guide has a claw always stab at close range. It puts the nearest monster first within a band, RustMS the first to enter the map.
  - ohmi69's OSMS Data Explorer, read from this game's client binary, has the same constants (65 ahead, the row 28 up, a divisor of 4) and gives a claw only stabO1 and stabO2 up close (`lib/skill-range-viz.js:77`; `tabs/formulas.js:78-95`: the swings are what a throw plays), but draws a basic shot's target as a 1-unit line 28 up, which the logs refute (stars hit monsters 60 above and 60 below): it counts for its constants only.
  - Harepacker's v95 MapSimulator has the 28 too (`DefaultShootAttackPointYOffset = -28`).

  Confidence: 65, 20, the divisor 4 and the row 28: high (two lines of sources, for v83 and for this game). The top 44: medium, one code line plus one page with no method. The stab boxes cut to 65: medium-high in the sources (v83's code, two readings of this game). Map-entry order within a band: medium-low (RustMS and ohmi69's object order against meowdb's nearest).
- **What the logs say of it.** The shape is checked against the shot log (204 throws, 100 off her level), the 13 range-probe throws and 418 throws rebuilt from the tours' telemetry, over the monsters' frames and facings. They agree with it, and fit its floor (best of the grid, 4-16 within 2 log-likelihood). They lean to a lower top: fitted, 21 + 5k (95% about 16-28; 44 + 5k 6.2 log-likelihood worse), which `reach` had until 2026-10-20. Cleaned fairly (the kills credited to two throws set aside, and the shot log's hits logged in the same second counted once, not dropped), that lean is 2-5 log-likelihood. Taken as independent throws that would rule 44 out (the probes' scorer bounds a fit at 1.92), but its 10-14 throws 60 above her (150-191 off) are four episodes (3 -> 1 twice, 13 -> 12 and 22 -> 21), whose throws go together: all four leaning the same way comes by chance 1 time in 16 (p 0.06, one-sided), and in the shot log, without any one of them the lean is 1-3.5. Suggestive, not decisive; any top from 17 to 28 fits as well. So `reach` has the client's top, and `reach.SEARCH_TOP0` stays the one number to change (to 21) if throws from 13 at 12 find the lower one (`probe run top-60`, 30 throws: a pig 60 above hit from 111 with 44, only from 191 with 21; `top-120`: hits from about 350 with 44, none with 21). Too high a top has her throw at monsters above her that the star doesn't take; too low, skip them, and count on stars at monsters past them that they take. The claw's reach (65 against the 90 taken before) shows in two places: a slime with its near side 79 off took a star's damage, and a pig thrown at 122 then 74 off (near sides 88 and 40) lost a star's and a swipe's worth together, where the old reach has two swipes. The bar drops can't tell more (`probe run claw-edge` settles it). The order within a band fits random 0.4-0.7 log-likelihood better than nearest: noise.
- **What stops a star** (`reach.wall_between`, `wall_to`) **is checked on the attack's pick alone,** as the client does it. The claw and the star's search pick by the bodies, whatever the terrain; then one line, from her to the monster picked, is checked, and if terrain stops it the attack hits nothing: the star ends where it's stopped, and no other monster takes it. RustMS's port of the v83 client clears its targets and ends the shot at the stop (`Combat.cpp:1289-1307`); ohmi69's reading of this game's client removes a blocked target without filling its slot, and meowdb's page on this game says the same. So a monster the attack takes first whose star is stopped leaves those behind it out of reach (`reach.shielded`: one in an earlier band of the search; one in the same band takes only its share). A claw swipe isn't checked (the client's whack has no line). Until 2026-10-20 a walled monster was passed over, and the next one took the star.
  - **What stops the line:** the walls of the foothold group of the platform she last stood on, and only going in at their outer face: a wall drawn downward faces right, one drawn upward faces left (RustMS `ShotPath.h:382-445`, `blocked`: a line stops only going from a foothold's open side to its closed side; the v40 client's own collisions test walls so too, by a reconstruction of its physics). On this map every wall faces out from the platform it hangs from (the step between 2 and 4 faces 4, below it, and the basin's sides face its floor, 36), so a star thrown from a platform never meets the back of a wall of its group across its line: one-sided walls change nothing here. A floating block is one group (its floor and the walls hanging from its ends), and so are platforms joined by a step: 2 and 4, and the basin's 34, 35 and 36. The walls of other blocks never stop a star. RustMS's port also has the walls of group 0 stop a star from every group (`ShotPath.h:398`; the v40 collisions have no such exception): left out, and on this map group 0 is the basin, where it changes nothing. The game data has no foothold flag for it (in all 306 map images a foothold has its ends, its neighbours and `piece`, and `forbidFallDown` in 51).
  - **The logs** of 2026-10-18 to 10-20: from platform 4 no star reached a monster on 2, 60 above her behind the step wall: 0 of 3 in the shot log, all 4 kills of 40 throws on 4 in a sweep, and 0 of 5 in a tour's telemetry, the Orange Mushrooms on 2 in view with no HP bar for 4 s of throwing. In the same logs, stars 60 up past the side walls of the blocks above hit (19 -> 18 13 of 13 decided, 3 -> 1 15 of 19), and stars down past her own block's hanging wall hit 81% (14 -> 17). "Every wall blocks" contradicts the first of these, and a line from her to the target's feet can't fit both 4 -> 2 and 14 -> 17. On this map her group's walls rule out one pair of platforms, 4 -> 2 (at every x); 174 of the 306 maps have steps within one group.
  - **Which line** (`reach.LINE`). `'v83'`, the default since 2026-10-21: the v83 client's line (RustMS), from 28 above her feet at her own x to where the star hits the body (`reach.hit_point`: its top if it's below the row, its feet if above, the row if it crosses it; its x taken 1 unit inside the monster's platform, `reach._hit_on`, below), which her group's walls stop as above and any floor stops going down through it, the corners at footholds' ends as the client has them (`reach.sight_stop`). meowdb's page on this game says so too: shooting down through the platform she stands on is blocked, up through one isn't (it cites no test: on its Lucky Seven page the claim was tagged unverified on 2026-08-22 and by 2026-09-29 untagged and reworded, and the one in-game test the site gives on terrain is a note that walls stop Energy Bolt). `'level'`, the default until then: a level line 28 above her feet (higher in a jump) to the monster's x, which only walls can cross, as ohmi69's reading of this game's client checks a basic shot (the one source for it, and the one whose basic shot's target, a 1-unit line, the logs refute). The 299 decided live throws of 2026-10-18 to 10-20 give the same verdict by both: every throw down was made from near an end. The user, watching her hunt on 2026-10-21, saw the difference: "for targeting below your platform, your platform itself can block the thro[w] (this applies to both step down and standing on a higher platform trying to hit mobs on a lower one)". The two differ only below her: by the v83 line a star needs room past her platform's end, |dx| > e (28 + t) / 28, e her distance to the end and t how far below her feet the monster's top is (a walking pig 60 below: 1.5 e). From 2 at x 50 it stops every star at pigs on 4 under 254 off and slimes under 284; from 14 at x 690 at pigs on 17 up to 238 off, from x 706 under 215 and slimes under 241; from 25 inside her platform's end, none a star picks 60 below her. Where past the end the star gets through the user's report doesn't say: `probe run step-down` (from 2 at x 50) and `hanging-wall` (from 14 at x 706) throw at pigs and slimes from short of where the v83 line lets it through to about 55 past it. Her decisions, the spots (`spots.coverage`, tried every 2 units) and the simulator's world all keep to it, and where a floor stops a star from where she'd walk to, she walks along her platform to where it doesn't (`stance._clear_from`); the mini-map's band still shows only the walls. In the simulator the line is worth about 1% of her stars on the tour (Found offline: her own platform stops a star down past its end).
  - **Its height:** any from 1 to 59 fits the logs, and 28 is the client's own: the row a shot flies along and its search opens about (the angle, above). On this map no step is lower than 60, so the height changes nothing. The step-up probe brackets it: from 4 at 2 (a 60 step), jump throws (the line 26 higher) stopped and jump backs (44 higher) getting through would put it at 16-34.
  - **Her decisions:** she doesn't throw at a monster whose star is stopped, or at one behind one (`reach.can_hit` with the monsters around her), or walk along her platform for one but to where its line is clear and no monster the attack takes first has its own stopped (`stance._clear_from` with the monsters around her: from 14 at x 690 a pig on 17 at 880, in her floor's shadow, takes the stars at one at 1000, and from 729 on it's under 151 off and isn't picked, so she closes in to 736); at one behind a monster the attack takes first whose star isn't stopped she does throw: that one takes the stars until it's dead, then hers comes (it orders the kills, as a monster in her way on her platform is shot first), where a walled one dies to none of them and keeps the stars from those behind it as long as it stands there. With every spot near enough shielded so and she at the nearest, `decide` skips the target (it used to walk 0 units, a tap back and forth on the spot until the kill's patience ran out); spots don't count what's behind a wall or under her floor's edge; and a kill isn't matched to one, nor to one behind one (`fight._in_path`, `ledger.in_path`). A monster's x is taken 1 unit inside its platform's ends, so one at the foot of a wall rising from its own platform's end (the basin's sides) isn't behind it. `reach.WALLS_BLOCK = False` switches the rule off for her decisions: the probes that measure it do so for their run (`probe run step-up`, `step-down`, `hanging-wall`); the shot log and the probe log record its verdict either way.
- **A group** (`stance.py`): a star hits one of the nearest monsters in reach on the side she faces (the search's first band), so she throws toward the side with the most monsters in reach, and keeps working the side she faces while it has any. Turning after every throw spread the damage over both sides.
- **What an attack hits is picked when it starts** (`reach.in_area`), about 67 ms after its key like a jump's lift-off, from where she is then; the star that flies is only a picture. From the ground, the claw's stab comes first, then the star's search (above). From a jump, it's the nearest monster whose body (`localization.monsters`: the boxes of its frames in the game data) reaches into an area fixed to her feet: from 19 below them (fitted, 18-21) to at least 60 above, its near side within 400 ahead. A jump throw's attack key used to come 100 ms after the jump key (the macro's F1 combo), so she was 42-49 units up when it started (60 fps recordings), and the area's floor was about 30 above the platform: over a snail, which is 24-26 tall (33 while it flinches); slimes (40 at least), pigs (38) and Orange Mushrooms (55) reach into it. On 2026-10-19, of 45 jump-throws at snails 3-77 units away on the 168-unit platforms 3, 20 and 22, at most one hurt the snail, and pigs, slimes and Orange Mushrooms on the platform 60 above took the stars and died. Their EXP was taken for the snail's ("snail down"), and the snail, still alive, was then left alone as a dying one. Now the key comes 40 ms after the jump (`physics.JUMP_ATTACK_MS`): the attack starts about 26 units up, and the area's floor about 7 above the platform. In game on 2026-10-20, at a snail 20-60 units away on platform 22: keyed 100 ms after the jump, the star flew over it and did nothing; keyed 40 ms after, a star hit it for 78 and killed it. In a hunt loop afterwards, jump-throws at snails killed them. RustMS's port of the v83 client has no case for the air: from a jump the claw and the search would pick as from the ground, from as high as she is, and 21-26 up (the attack starts up to 11 ms after the jump's lift-off lag) that picks no snail 35-85 off: the stabs' boxes are then 36-56 above the ground, and the search's windows first take a snail 86-106 off. The kills above go against it; `probe run air` weighs the two, and the simulator's world has either (`sim.world.AIR_PICK`). (Until 2026-10-27; since, from a jump the star's search alone picks, and up close she goes by where a monster will be when her attack starts: Clearance and slopes, above.)
- **Too close:** she jumps away from it, turning toward it in mid-air to throw. A star leaves about 520 ms after the attack key, in the air or not (recorded at 60 fps), so the key goes in once she has turned in the air (120 ms after the jump key, `physics.AIR_TURN_LEAD_MS` 60 after the turn's arrow, where her attack still picks the kind: `reach.turn_key_ms`, 105 for a pig; 85 until 2026-10-26, and both live jump backs of 2026-10-25 threw the wrong way) and the star leaves as she lands; its target, though, is picked when the attack starts, about 40 units up and 16 out (`jb_k165` at 60 fps, the jump keyed 80 ms after the arrow; about 27 out by the engine with it keyed 150 ms after, as now), not the whole jump away. It needs 110 units of room behind her and no monster within 160 there; otherwise (cornered) she throws from a jump straight up. Each only if that attack starts low enough to pick the nearest monster's kind (`reach.air_hits`: how tall it is at least, 6 units into the area): a jump back's (floor 25 up) can't pick a snail, and she doesn't jump-throw at one either (`stance.JUMP_THROW_SNAILS`, off since 2026-10-21: in game they mostly missed; Found offline: snails from the ground): she steps back to 3 past the claw's edge (`reach.star_sure`: 99 for a snail; a star from the ground), and as much farther as it walks at her meanwhile, if her platform has the room (the 50 she keeps from its ends with monsters about: not to a short platform's far end, `stance.SNAIL_FAR_END`), else stabs it from the ground. A monster counts as too close by its size, as far as the claw would swipe it (`stance.close_to`; the hunt loop's close quarters too). It all follows from `JUMP_ATTACK_MS`: keyed 100 ms after the jump, a jump throw's attack couldn't pick a snail either, and she shot it from the ground (the claw swipes it, weak but always hitting: 5 swipes kill one). Under a platform within her jump height she doesn't jump to attack (on platform 20, five jump-throws at a snail put her up on 19); she steps away instead, or (cornered) throws from the ground. A kind that hits hard is kept further off by the map's danger (Positioning, below: a Horny Mushroom from 162 units, then a jump back, a step away or a throw, whichever leaves her the least danger); on the first map no kind is. (Until 2026-10-27; since, from a jump the star's search alone picks, and up close she goes by where a monster will be when her attack starts: Clearance and slopes, above.)
- **Spacing:** she steps away from any monster on her own platform within 110 units, or as far as the claw would swipe it (a pig within 111), unless that walks into another one or off her platform. With monsters on her platform she stays 50 units from its ends: a monster touching her pushes her 20-21 units on a wide platform, and 82 and 109 units on a narrow one, which knocked her off.
- **Facing:** she only taps an arrow to turn when she isn't already facing the target. Every tap also walks her a few units, and nine taps in a row once walked her off the end of her platform. A jump-throw that turns her jumps at once and taps the arrow in the air, 60 ms after the jump key (`physics.AIR_TURN_MS`, as the jump backs turn), its attack 120 ms after the jump key at the soonest (60 after the arrow, `physics.AIR_TURN_ATTACK_MS`, where the kind allows: `reach.turn_key_ms`; 85 until 2026-10-26, when 10 of 28 such turns went the wrong way live): by the engine she comes down 3.8 units on (2.7-4.3), where tapping first and jumping once the tap's walk had stopped (`actions.JUMP_THROW_TURN_MS`, 205 ms; still there for an attack that must come sooner, and with `actions.AIR_TURN` off) carried her 5.3 (1.8-7.0) and put the attack 245 ms after the tap; jumped 80 ms after the tap, 32 (12-53). A jump forward turns her with its held arrow: no tap. (Until 2026-10-27; since, from a jump the star's search alone picks, and up close she goes by where a monster will be when her attack starts: Clearance and slopes, above.)
- **Where to shoot a platform from** (`spots.py`): a spot on another platform she can stand on, either one no monster can reach or one only monsters not worth hunting reach (snails: she shoots those when they come close), with at least 30% of the hunting platform in reach. Of the spots about as good as the best, she takes the nearest: coming up from the basin she shoots 21, 18 and 12 from the platforms below them, and from above she shoots down, from near her platform's end, where her floor stops the least (17 from 14 at x 756; by the level line 716 had as much). With the map's danger, a spot on any other platform that scores better than hunting on the ground itself (its share in reach less its danger), and the ground's own safest place where there's none (Positioning, below; on the first map nothing changes). The spots for a platform depend on the map (and on what stops a star, which a probe can switch: `reach.WALLS_BLOCK`), so they're worked out once for each (27 ms a platform by the v83 line, every star's line to every 2 units of the platform from every 10 of the others tried at once, `reach._sight_clear`; 3.6 by the level line): the hunt loop's 16 grounds take 0.67 s at its first look.

In its log, "jump-throwing right at 278 ms, above (...)" is the stance, and "    jump (above): a jump in place throwing right, the attack 278 ms in (258-298), 77 up: ..., keyed at 285 (+7), ..." each one carried out ('passing': a jump forward on her way; 'reach': one out of reach otherwise); the attack choice's line after it names the target above, not "nothing seen in its way". After, `python -m gamelab.analysis.jumps` on the run's telemetry: how often each fired, and the kills and hits seen after. Watch for a jump that lands off her platform or up on the one above (a short kick), a jump forward into a monster or past where she was going, a jump in place right under a monster above (the stance no longer takes one: her body would meet it), and stars at monsters above that hit nothing (by the model, up close only with the attack at the top: "the attack 278 ms in"). After, `python -m gamelab jitter` on the run's telemetry: the jump attacks by jitter bin and whether the jitter predicts a hit there. From the ground, with `UP_BY_SEARCH` on: throws at monsters more than 60 above her that hit nothing (a pig 100 above her 271-357 off: picked there by the client's top, 44, not by the logs' 21) point to the lower top, what `probe run top-60` settles.

## Her throws at the dead, her MP, her damage and her air turns (from 2026-10-26)

The supervised hunt of 2026-10-25 23:43 (`tour --loop`, 340 EXP a minute; telemetry 20261025-234327-tour.jsonl, the perception service's 20261025-210747-perceive.jsonl) had her pet drink 25 MP potions in 11 minutes. Four lenses on it, each re-checked (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/analysis-1025/checked.txt), found where the MP went; branch work/hunt-a acts on the MP side (the scripts behind the numbers below are in D:/MapleHelper-scratch/hunt-ab/a/scripts).

- **No throws at the dying** (`ledger.dying`, `DIE_S`, `DYING_DX`, `GAIN_AFTER_KEY`; `Attacks.target`, `key`; `fight._targets`, `_shoot_at`; `Hunt._book`). 18 casts of Lucky Seven and 4 regular throws went at a monster whose kill had just been placed (about a tenth of the potions), 29 throws in all after the hunter had the kill. Three causes: a kill's gain shows 0.15-0.46 s after the key of the throw that made it, the server's, before the star leaves, so its monster is still drawn, dying, and the rule "one no longer seen" put 15 of 72 kills (10 piles) on a monster already hidden or gone; the dying monster stayed drawn 0.6-1.3 s, 14-25 units from where its kill was placed, and was taken from the path again, whole (a dying monster's bar reads None), with a new mark that the hidden fallback then followed for 1.8 s without the DEAD_LIKELY check; and the hunt loop made a new FightState at every new place or objective, which a kill's pile is, losing `dying`. Now a gain 0.1-0.6 s after a throw's key is that throw's kill, the first of its kind in its path, seen or not (`dead_one`, `Ledger._place`, with the gain's time: `Hunter.gains_told`); of the monsters of a placed kill's kind on its platform, the one nearest it, within 40 units, is the one dying there while its kind's death animation plays from the look that placed it (`MobBody.die_s`, the game data's die1 frames: 0.84 s for a Horny or Green Mushroom, 0.66 for a pig): no throw's target (the path worked out without it; the hidden fallback skips marks on it, and takes one not likely dead first, as the path does), no mark, not fought, out of the ledger's and her wounds' throw paths, and fight.kill waits for it to fade out; and the hunt loop's FightState keeps `dying` and its keyed throws across a new objective. At first every one within 40 units for 1.5 s: then, once the dead one was gone, a live one by where it died went unshot for most of a second, and grinding, finding nothing to shoot, went on (grinding, 8 seeds: 320 EXP a minute; the nearest only, 317; the animation and 0.15 s more, 351; the animation alone, 390). It's taken for the dying one by where it is alone: with the dead one unseen at the look (live, her looks missed 5-41% of the monsters within 125 units of her), a live one of its kind by where the kill was placed is, no target and out of the monsters about her (`fight._targets`' `visible`, `fight.dying_seen`) for up to its death animation. Kept among them instead (tried in the review of 2026-10-26: the stance's danger, its jumps' arcs, too close), the dead drawn there had her step and jump away from them, and on loop_rocky_bridge she fell out of the map (tour_hunt_basin, loop_rival, tour_hunt_other_spot and nav_fight_across_runs_out lost what they show, and test_retreat's sweep a seed): left out, as before. Replayed on the live hunts against the perception service's deaths and tracks (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/hunt-ab/review-a-measure/scripts/replay_check.py), of the 147 casts it would have taken off a target, 103 were at one the service saw die, 10 at one it still tracked alive 1-2.5 s later, 34 not known; and 48 of them had another monster in the path, which the star takes past the dying one (the throw goes at that one: no MP saved). Within 30 units instead of 40, 85 dead and 8 alive (25: 67 and 7): the same share, fewer of the dead (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/hunt-ab/a/review/replay_check_dx.py), so 40 stays.
- **A last look before the key** (`Actions.still`, `Hunter._still`, `Attacks.in_way`, `Feed.newest`, `pending_events`; `hunter.LAST_LOOK`). She decided each throw on a look 0.2-0.34 s after the key before, then waited out her lock blind: the look was a median 0.57 s old at the key, and 17 throws went out after a gain that showed before their key, 6 more before the hunter read it. Now once her lock is waited out, before any key of a throw or a jump throw, the feed's newest state (if of a frame after her keys' effect; nothing asked of the feed, nor waited for) and its events not yet drained: an EXP gain naming a kind in the throw's way (`aimed`, its target, its path; an unreadable one, any kind), as a copy of her meter tells them apart, drops the throw ("a kill came in before the key (horny-mushroom): the throw right is dropped, decided again", a telemetry event 'dropped'), and the next pass decides again. A jump back never is, and a probe's throw dropped so is none of the probe's (`probe._throw`: it scored one, for a star never thrown, until the review of 2026-10-26). On the way: `feed.fresh` compared a frame's time with a look's `after` strictly where WorldStep hands a frame what was asked within 1e-9 s, and a look waited out FEED_WAIT_S for nothing (simulator); now within 1e-9 s too.
- **Her stats and damage at level 25** (config.toml `[character]`, `maplehelper.config.Character`; `attack/choice.py` STAR, SKILL_STAR, SKILL_LEVEL, LUCKY_SEVEN_DAMAGE; `sim.world.LEVEL_25`). HP 774, MP 623 (her bars' numbers), level 25; her MP bar fell 2.345 px of 104 a cast (standard error 0.03) over 364 one-cast stretches of the hunts of 23:43 to 01:03, 14.05 MP: Lucky Seven's `mpCon` at 16 and 17 (13 at 14-15 would be 2.17 px, 15 at 18-19 2.50): 16. Off the monsters' bars with nobody within 200 units: the first bar 144 Horny Mushrooms showed after one cast, 231-346 dealt before defence (5-95%), 288 at the median, two stars of 96-192 to the unit (the most twice the least, as Lucky Seven's formula has it), which kills a Green Mushroom 91% of the time (live 45 of 53 Green kills opened with it took one cast); the regular star, 18 hits of 26-137, 80 on average: 20-140, as wide as the claw's star is by its formula at her first job's mastery. Lucky Seven's stars scale with its damage in the game data at another level (120% at 16). With them 'finish' fires from 49 HP left on a Green and 44 on a Horny (40 and 36 before), a regular star killing 76% of the time there; it rarely fires off a bar (none of 381 casts at a monster with its bar read was at 49 or less), mostly after a cast that likely killed ("the regular attack: green-mushroom ~27/233 HP if alive (48% dead); finishing it"). The simulator's Her on Tree Dungeon is LEVEL_25: those HP and MP, her stars drawn so with `spread`, 14 MP a cast (`Her.cast_mp`) and the 100-MP Blue Potions her pet drank then (`Her.mp_potion`: the first 20 drinks 95-100 MP each), where LEVEL_24 had 752, 601, 11 and 185.
- **Her MP under her pet's warning** (`Attacks._mp_read`, `_believed`, WARNING_STEPS, WARNING_S, MP_FIRST_S, MP_SHOWS_S; `Actions.throw`). Her MP bar read 0 for up to 0.6 s after each cast that took her under the pet's 5% warning (26 runs of 0 reads, each from 0.20-0.46 s after a cast's key, 24 ending in the pet's drink; no look ever read 4 or 5 px, the bar 6-9 px before each), while she still had 20-35 MP: 11 regular throws went out for 'MP 0'. A 0 read within 2 s of a read above 0 is now her MP as reckoned (the last read less her casts since) where that read, or the reckoning, is 9 px or less (from 7 px a cast's MP is still there, from 3 px not; from 10 px and two casts, 5.3: replayed, two of the live 0s came so), counted once a run of 0s in the attack summary ("her MP bar's 0 under her pet's warning not believed N times", apart from the regular attack's reasons; it counted looks, up to 6 a run, until the review of 2026-10-26). A cast's MP first showed 0.21-0.53 s after its key (it was believed from 68 ms on): a bar read off a frame shown at t is less the casts keyed after t - 0.21, and her reckoning stands where it's within the casts keyed from t - 0.55 to then shown or not; past that, the bar (a drink, her regen, a press that took no MP: believed less a cast at most). For a day a read inside 0.55 s of the last cast was believed only where it was lower: with a look 0.2-0.34 s after each key, nothing that raised her MP showed while she kept casting, her reckoning only went down, and she threw the regular attack for 'MP' with plenty of it (the review: replayed through the branch's own `Attacks` on the four live hunts at level 25, 91 'MP' throws, 45 of them with a cast's MP surely hers; master's rule, 85 and 32; in the harness 11.75 a run, every one with the MP). Her pet's drink shows about 0.3 s after the cast that brings it, and a drink shown between the look a throw was decided on and its key went unseen until the next look: the last look before the key reads her MP too (`Attacks.glance`, from `Hunter._still`). Replayed as built (the glance off the service's newest frame before each key: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/hunt-ab/a/review/mp_replay_glance.py), 39 'MP' throws, none with a cast's MP surely hers by the newest read (without the glance 48, 9 of them). In the harness none: her bar is drawn now at the server's time (`world.MP_SHOWS_MS`, 0.29 s after a cast's key, its pet's drink with it; drawn at the key, a look under 0.21 s after it showed a cast she took off as still to come, 2.4 such throws a run), and without the glance 1.25 a run. And `Actions.throw` asks its attack key before it tells the throw listeners, as `jump_throw` does: a ground throw's cast went off at the next throw, with that one's key time. Which frame the game draws under the warning isn't known (`perception.hud.mp_fill` finds no blue on its row: a warning flash?): one frame of a 0 read saved at a supervised run would tell.
- **The air turn** (`physics.AIR_TURN_LEAD_MS`, `AIR_TURN_ATTACK_MS`; `reach.turn_key_ms`, `TURN_KEY_MS`; `Actions.jump_throw`'s `turn_key`, `JB_THROW_MS`; `fight._turn_key`; `world.AIR_TURN_SAME_STEP`). 10 of the 28 jumps that turned her in the air threw the wrong way by her frames (36%; none of those 10 killed, 10 of the 18 that turned did), the attack 25 ms after the arrow; the ground throws that tapped first, 80 ms before the attack, turned on all 68 readable ones; both jump backs went the wrong way. Now the attack comes 60 ms after the arrow (120 ms after the jump key) where her air attack still picks the kind (a Horny or Green Mushroom, 51 tall, up to about 145 ms), else as late as it still does (a pig 105, a slime 110; a snail none, as before): a jump throw's turn in the air, a jump back's attack (its star now leaves as she lands, not just before: its target is picked as the attack starts, in the air), the turning shots her jumps' coverage tries (`reach.shots`: from each target's kind's own turn key, `turn_key_ms` of its height; for a day every kind's from 120 ms, and a pig on her platform had no turning shot until her way down, 430 ms in on a test map's floor, now one at 105 (a slime has none either way: at 110 its pick isn't sure 15 ms later, KEY_SLACK_MS); a plan's turning shot goes at its own key, `fight._turn_of`). The path a throw's kill is credited by (`FightState.aimed`, `fight.attack_gap`) is worked out where the attack goes: a jump back's at its turn key, where it was 85 ms (review, 2026-10-26). The simulator turned her as it saw the arrow, whatever came at that step (2 of 201 air turns went the wrong way in master's harness); now an arrow acted on at the same step as an attack's key turns her too late for it (25 ms apart one time in six, 60 never). How the game decides isn't known.

EXP a minute is level within the noise. Grinding: 0.0% seed by seed (se 4.1%, the median +0.6%, better on 12 of 24); leaving out the seeds stalled on either side, +0.5% (se 4.9%, 13 seeds). The hunt loop: 346.7 against 332.3 on average, -14.4 (se 21.7), seed by seed +2.8% (se 9.4%), the median -3.0%, better on 9; without the stalled seeds +3.3% (se 4.8%, 9 seeds). Every stalled seed (over 60 s with no kill or pick-up) is a rest that ran out its 120 s, and every such rest stalled one: a touch stood her up from the chair and her HP stayed where it was (`tour.Tour.rest` doesn't sit her down again; found in the review, left as it is). On the hunt loop 17 of the branch's 72 rests in 24 runs ran out so, against 11 of master's 91 (24% against 12%; grinding 10% both): most of its lower mean, and why its rests are touched more often isn't found. The branch's own changes show in MP: 4.8 and 6.0 MP less a kill (se 0.7 and 0.6; higher on 2 and 0 of 24 seeds), 0.6 and 0.9 MP potions a minute fewer (se 0.2 and 0.3), casts at a monster dead by then 55 and 67 fewer a run (45% and 51%), and no regular throw for 'MP' (the branch as first reviewed: 11.75 a run, every one with a cast's MP hers). The potions are relative: see below.

Her touches: on the whole 1.5 and 3.0 fewer a run that hurt (se 2.9 and 3.6), HP lost a minute level (+0.01 and -0.04 bars, se 0.04 and 0.05). On trips, grinding 2.0 fewer (se 2.0); the hunt loop 2.6 more (se 1.8, more on 12 of 24 seeds), 0.26 bars more HP lost on them (se 0.14, more on 15) and 16.5 s more on the move (se 6.6, more on 18): she travels more, at master's rate a second (0.20 touches a second on the move, 0.21 for master). The branch as first reviewed (e21f9b8, 16 seeds) had 4.2 more touches on trips (se 1.5) and 20 s more travelling. Counted rule by rule (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/hunt-ab/a/review/diag_trips.py, its 8 seeds), the trips it set off on toward a pile were 107 a run, against 60 with the last look switched off and 68 for master in the new world; after a throw dropped at its last look the next pass set off on its way 14 times a run, nothing in reach and 10 monsters in view, where the throw at the dead would have held her there its 0.85 s: the lock's time a throw at the dead no longer takes goes on the move. Tried in the review, none better: a hold that long after every drop brought the trips back to 60, not their touches, and cost 18% of her EXP; the last look kept out of rule 4's shots in passing, 4.3 more touches on trips (se 1.9; 16 seeds, the dying then kept about her, before her bar's lag); the dying kept among the monsters about her, 1.2 (se 1.9, 24 seeds) and 5.7 s, but stepping and jumping from the dead (above). How safely she travels is part B's (Cutting her touches), and whether the freed time should go on the move the hunt loop's.

What the harness overstates. It decides the next throw sooner after a key than live, a median 0.25 s against 0.35 (61% of its stances before the world's 0.29 s gain, 28% of 1,446 live: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/hunt-ab/review-a-measure/scripts/rv_timing.py, live_timing.py), so it drops 6 throws a minute at the last look where the live hunts' replay drops 0.7, and master in the new world casts at the dead 11-14 times a minute against 2-4 live: what the last look saves is the replay's, not the harness's. (Its kills come about as fast as live's, 10-12 a minute against 10-11, not twice as fast as said before the review.) Its MP potions are 1.7-2 times live's (3.0-4.0 a minute against 1.6-2.3): the misses (Noise.miss 0.275, fitted with the old damage) and the presses that take no MP (live 7% of casts; the world takes it on every press) aren't refit, nor the HP potions (LEVEL_25's pet at 45%; part B's world has live's 70%, and so has LEVEL_25 since Parts A and B together) or the detector's misses near her (part B's `--world near-misses`); its decisions' timing isn't either.

The branch's changes one at a time, as first built (grinding, 8 seeds; scripts/ablate.py: each switched back alone on the branch, 390.3 EXP a minute, 37.4 MP a kill, 67 casts at the dead a run): with no monster taken for one dying 385.6 (-0.4% seed by seed, se 3.3%), 37.8 MP a kill, 83 casts at the dead; with no last look 384.7 (-0.7%, se 3.7%), 40.3, 89; with the air turn's attack 85 ms after the jump key 355.2 (-7.5%, se 5.0%, 2 of 8 better), 35.9, 65; with a kill put on a gone one first, as before, 348.1 (-8.8%, se 8.5%), 37.3, 63. The MP is the dying rule's and the last look's; the EXP effects are within a standard error or two of the noise on 8 seeds (the review's hunt-loop ablations as noisy), and the air turn's rests on the world's rule for an arrow and an attack at the same step (`world.AIR_TURN_SAME_STEP`, built for it: 25 ms apart fails one time in six, 60 ms never).
