**After the reviews** (the same day: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/kplace/review-truth, review-behaviour and review-perception, each finding checked before it was acted on; the fixes measured in D:/MapleHelper-scratch/kplace/fix2: the service's frame step replayed again on the four recordings, the 00:20 Lie Detector's before/ too, its live gains' kinds told up to 0.3 s after the replay's change as the review's were, `replay.py`; scored by `score.py` and `heldout.py`, the review's judges, and `excl.py`; variants by tag, `k2`-`k5`; the harness and the goldens below):
- *A wrong binding stays in her body's way* (`fight.TOUCH_NEAR`, `TOUCH_NEAR_DY`, `FightState.touch`, `_unsure_by_her`; `Ledger.unsure`; the stance's `touch`). A bound monster whose death isn't seen yet is no target, but it may be a live one (on the review's replays 12 of the 103 bindings on named gains, 21 of 62 on gains of no kind known, let go 0.53-1.55 s on), and leaving it out of the fight's monsters left it out of the stance's danger too. One within 150 across and 80 up or down of her (17 of those 33 were) now counts for her body (the danger where she'd stand, her jumps' arcs and landings, an escape's ways), not as taking her stars or as a target; the drawn dead kept among every monster had her step and jump away from them (loop_rocky_bridge, 2026-10-26), so not all of them. It costs a jump now and then by a monster she has just killed (`loop_tree_safety_stop` at 1.63 s: a throw from the ground where the jump onto 22 was).
- *Her kill stands where her star landed, and a stray isn't it* (`tracking.MonsterTracker._stray`, `STAR_LANDS_S`, `STAR_FLIGHT`, `LANDS_SLACK_S`, `BOUND_LOST`, `Track.lands`; `update`'s strays). A bound track is re-found only within a track's reach with its walk stopped 0.2 s after her star lands on it (0.75 s after the key and her distance over 1,490 units a second, the simulator's model: 23 of 26 kills within 0.15 s of it), and once lost from sight 0.3 s by then, no farther than 35 units from its last sighting: a sighting farther off is another monster her window found, a track of its own at once, not a sign that the bound one lives. Its reach had grown as any track's while out of sight: at 23:14:41 (w2310-037) the green she killed, lost 0.25 s after the gain, was taken for a green 56 units on at 1.18 s and let go; at 00:58:28 (w0056-015) a horny 71 units on a frame after its last. Held to FADE_MOVE from her star's landing whether lost or not (the review's suggestion: `k2`), a track the filter had walked on past where its green stopped lost her dying kill to a new track, a target again (w0020-099), and wrong bindings to live ones walking on weren't let go (23:13:46's green); a walk stopped at the landing alone took 111 units at 23:14:41 (`k3`). With both, where her kill ends is right on 76 of the 85 (74 so counted as reviewed); 18 let go where 33 (13 for a sighting, 4 for another seen dying, 1 a throw told again: `binds2.py`).
- *A death seen too soon is no gain's* (`DEATH_AFTER_GAIN_S`; `_deaths_seen` after the binding, `_picks` passing over the seen dying). Another player's kill seen dying in her gain's frame, or one frame on, took her gain and made her victim a target again (review-behaviour/order.py); her own star can't have killed anything that soon (die1 begins 0.60 s after the gain at the median of the 106 of hers labelled, 0.35 at p10, under 0.17 on 2). A death seen less than 0.3 s after a gain isn't that gain's, and the gains of a frame are bound before its deaths seen are taken.
- *Her throw's way from her look* (`hunter._retell`, `RETELL_S`, `TOLD_KEEP`, `told_throws`, `facing_agreed`; `tracking.throw` told again at its key, `RETOLD_S`, `_retold`, `_taken_back`, `_picks`' `dead`; the 'retold' event, let_go's `why`). Her throws are told the way her keys made them, the stance's side; where the game had swallowed the arrow, she threw the other way and the gain was bound to what she hadn't thrown at (w0020-097, -102: the star's crescent on the other side). A look whose frame shows her facing otherwise than her keys, strongly (Actions.see's 'told otherwise', heading.Reading.strong: no frame read the wrong way on 2026-10-24 was), tells again that way the throws keyed since her last arrow, her last hit and the last look that agreed with her keys, 2.5 s back at most: a gain bound off one is let go and bound on that side, or to the one there whose death was seen meanwhile, taken for another player's then (w0020-097: its frame came 0.75 s after the gain, 0.09 s after her victim's death was seen: hers now). On the four recordings 5 of the 25 'heading' frames came after throws with no arrow or hit since, all strong, 6 throws told again (the others after an arrow; -102's too). In the simulator, turned without a key twice (tests/test_heading.py), the two throws that went the wrong way are told again, and only those; with every frame read the wrong way weakly, none.
- *A gain of no kind known* (`UNKNOWN_HURT_FIRST`). It goes on the nearest ahead of any kind as before, those showing a bar first (her throws hurt them): w0020-085's gain (26, a green's, its kind not read live) went on the unhurt horny 50 units ahead of her, where the green her stars had hurt was 255 ahead, and is right at once now (the review's judge takes the other green, 60 units off, for the dying one). On the labels nothing else changes with it, and on the whole nights' emulation, with the throws told again, tonight's throws at the dead left out 51 where 53, at live ones 77 where 79.
- *Another player's kills in her memory* (`Memory`'s `theirs`, `Ledger.theirs`, the event 'taken', `counts['taken']`; `patrol.Belief._take_events`). The feed's tracks found dead were her memory's 'killed' events, counted under none of the counts Belief reads the events by: each pushed one of her own kills before it out of what Belief read, and another player's kills were hers there. Now a dead track of her kill is 'killed' as her ledger's kills are, and another player's (the tracker's cause "other", a share) 'taken': its point empty, no refill timed from it, and by another player a monster taken (`gone_by`), as one looks forgot. In loop_tree_grind the share Belief learns another player takes of Green Mushrooms, master's 0.8, had gone to the prior, 0.5 (review-behaviour: memcount.py, runsc_fix.py); 0.77 now.
- *The death watch* (`DeathWatch.others`, `counts`, `MEASURED`). Only the kinds whose margins were measured are watched, Tree Dungeon's mushrooms (a live Slime there came to 0.58 of die1/0's 0.6, its die1 a fifth of a mushroom's pixels; other maps' kinds not until a recording of them is replayed so), and a fire whose window the other mushroom's die1 matches better is no death (the two score nearly the same on die1/0-1: on 80 labelled deaths the other kind's die1 came to 0.7 at the dying one's feet on 61; at 00:23:00 a walking horny's track, lost where a green died, fired at 0.819 where the green's die1 scored 0.974, and the horny was re-found walking 0.38 s later: no fire now; of the review's 549 fires 11 were matched better so). The other kind is matched on a fire only, about 0.25 a second. On the three labelled recordings 74 of the 111 deaths seen (73), 84 fires (83); 0.46-0.60 ms a frame on the pool (0.43-0.62), p99 1.6-1.9 ms, the worst 3.8 (eval_deaths.py, its frames' `deaths_s`). A slime's death is judged as before now, unseen: in `loop_tree_run` a slime she killed was still among her hidden ones 0.9 s on.
- *The simulator* (`SimMonster.ghost`). Where her kill dies, at her star's landing, is worked out on a copy of its motion: advanced itself, the monster was drawn off its own path from the kill to the landing on 18% of 2,000 such kills (a median 27 units, review-behaviour/simjump.py), the frames between evaluating its newer segment backwards. FakeDeaths watches the kinds the real one does.
- *The papers*: the telemetry's table names the new event kinds and keys ('victim', 'let_go' and its `why`, 'retold'; died's `seen` and `share`, the tracks' `gain` and `share`); the in-window counts here are the script's put right by eye as the review did, and 23:11's 032 was 23:14:18's; the 88% above is in-sample.

## In game, on Thicket Around the Beach II

- **Navigation:** 21 moves in a row across every move type without a miss, and a 17-move climb from the basin to the top. Chained, a 13-move route up took 19.0 s in 3 key plans with no misses (33.4 s one move at a time). Over 10 test routes, a move landed elsewhere about once in 15, usually a drop or a straight-up jump timed off; each time she replanned from where she was.
- **Hops on routes:** across 4 routes (45 moves), she hopped 4 monsters in her way, with no hits and no misses.
- **Shooting from other platforms:** from platform 14 at monsters on 17 below, from 3 at monsters on 1 above, from 11 at 12 below and from 15 at 18 below. Most kills took 2 regular throws.
- **Sweeps:** a 6-stop sweep made 7 kills (EXP +92) in 114 s with no rest needed. With long-range shots, all 9 stops in 350 s with a rest: 28 kills (14 at the stops, 14 on the way) and EXP 6,459 → 6,856; far kills' drops were collected 5-50 s later. After the jump-back timing change, a full 9-stop sweep made 28 kills (6 on the way), EXP 6,856 → 7,247 in 309 s, lowest HP 92%. In crowds it took 7-9 throws a kill: each star hits whichever monster is nearest in its path, so the damage spreads.
- **Loot:** recorded at 2 frames a second, the sweep after a fight picked up a slime's Squishy Liquid and two coins within 8 s, and the tour's loot collection picked up drops seen from another platform. With her Etc tab full, a Snail Shell stayed after she stood on it twice; she read the game's message in the pickup log and switched to mesos only.
- **Arrows right after an attack** (2026-10-21; the telemetry of the hunt loops and tours played that night): an arrow pressed within 0.62 s of an attack's key (at least: later ones up to 0.78 s weren't pressed) doesn't move her until about 0.79 s after it. From 00:15 to 00:48, of 13 chains sent within 0.35 s of the look after a throw (their first arrow about 0.3 s after its key), 6 first moved her 0.73-0.92 s after they went out and 2 never did, and 9 missed their move: held on, the arrow set her off about 1.0 s after the key, and let go sooner it did nothing. Twice a walk-off off 3's left end onto 4, the arrow held 0.5 s from about 0.3 s after the key (00:19:04 and 00:19:37), left her standing on 3, and the walk-off sent again went. Arrows pressed 0.575 and 0.66 s after the key were read as moving her at once (but see below: by when she went off the end, the one at 0.575 set off 0.07 s late). From 00:49 every plan's first arrow waits until 0.6 s after the key (`actions.ARROW_LOCK_MS`): in the five runs to 01:17 no chain went sooner than 0.45 s after the look after a throw, all seven walk-offs from 3 onto 4 set off within 0.41 s, and every move that missed was a jump (9 of them: Motion planning), where before it 11 of the 13 were, and 2 were those walk-offs. The 5-minute hunt loop right after it ended 3 chains elsewhere than planned or off their path, the one before it 12. But held back to 0.6 s she still set off late, and those misses were its own: of the walk-offs from 3 onto 4, her dot first moved 0.41 s after the plan went out (the median of 11), against 0.23 s (of 6) when the first arrow came later after the key. Timed better, by when her dot went off the end of its platform (less the fall to her dot's first drop, and her run to the end by the engine), the 17 walk-offs whose first arrow went out 0.59-0.62 s after the key were acted on 0.75-0.88 s after it by her dot (median 0.81: 0.21 s after the plan went out, where an arrow with no attack before it is 0.09 s, the median of 73 walk-offs), so about 0.79 s after the key by the game's clock, 0.12 s late; the 3 whose first arrow went 0.79-0.82 s after the key were acted on at once (0.03-0.09 s). The press read as at once at 0.575 s was the walk-off at 00:19:14 (0.56 s after the key by this reckoning, the throw's key 0.13 s before the look after it): it set off 0.07 s late, and its dot first moved only as she fell. So she moves from about 0.79 s after the key, wherever up to 0.62 s the arrow went down; from 0.63 to 0.78 s no arrow was pressed, so whether one then is swallowed isn't known. **To check in game:** standing on open ground, `act f 650 right+ 500 right- 600 --record`, and the same with 700 and 750 for 650 (twice each, and left): she should start moving 66 ms after the arrow if it isn't swallowed, else about 0.79 s after the key; if 650 isn't, `actions.ARROW_LOCK_MS` can come down to it. Of the 10 chains that set off right after a throw for the jump from 16 up onto 14 (for the rope to 6), 8 came down short of 14 and fell to 25 (taking off 15-30 units short where tracked: the jump key went at its planned time) and one overshot onto 17 off a step back gone late; the 18 sent with no throw in the 1.5 s before all landed. (In the logs these read as rope grabs toward 6 that dropped her onto 25: 00:34:11, 00:46:42, 01:05:40, 01:05:58, 01:24:47, 01:44:06, 01:44:27, 01:48:40.) The first arrow now waits until 0.8 s after the key (Control), and the simulator acts on a swallowed one at about 0.79 s (`world.ARROW_HELD` 0.77 and the wait for the step; 0.835 at first, fitted to the dot's first move: with it, held back to 0.6 s the chains onto 14 were mostly cut short on 16 rather than falling to 25 as in game).
- **Jumps from standing** (2026-10-21, 34 jumps from platform 34 keyed 0-160 ms after the arrow): the game moves her in 30 ms steps, and a jump three steps into a run leaves at 126 units/s and lands 13 units short; from 150 ms after the arrow a jump leaves at full speed but for at most 5% (none of the 10 keyed 130 ms or later left short; of the 8 keyed 100 and 120 ms after it, 6 did). The kick: all 4 at 40 ms and 3 of 4 at 60 left at full speed, not reliable enough to plan on. Motion planning has the tables.
- **Respawns, and how full the map is** (the telemetry of 2026-10-19 to 21, offline: Respawns and drop life): a platform she emptied was mostly still empty 12.56 s later (of 77, watched without a gap over 2 s, 80% weren't back, 23 watched that long; past 30 s too few were watched to say; in the simulator about half were back within 5 s), and the platforms in view had a monster at 26% of their spawn points (the basin 12%, and none 45% of the time). Drops lay over a minute (95% at 60 s); how much longer, no hunt has shown.
- **Not yet checked on its own:** placing her from the minimap dot and the camera when her name tag is hidden.

## In game, on Tree Dungeon, Forest Up North II (map 10002073, from 2026-10-24)

The third map, "supposedly better for exp hunting", with many more other players: Horny Mushrooms (15 spawn points, HP
403, EXP 41, a touch's PADamage 110), Green Mushrooms (14, HP 233, EXP 26, PADamage 54) and two Slimes on the floor.
It is a tower 530 units wide (x -220..310) between two walls of foothold group 0, from the floor (33, y 248..225) up
to 6 (y -1628): shelves of group 0 against either wall (left 7, 13, 15, 20, 22, 29, 31; right 6, 12, 19, 24, 28) and
floating platforms of other groups between them, none with a wall; platforms 0-5 are wall caps above the VR, never
reached. Two exits (`out00` at 282 on 28, `out01` at 281 on 12) lead to 10002070. The map is 770 wide, so the camera
can't move across (Localization), and its minimap window shows 112 of its picture's 183 rows, scrolled with her. She's
level 25 (HP 774, MP 623, Lucky Seven at 16: 14 MP a cast; level 24's HP 752 and MP 601 until 2026-10-26: Her throws at the dead), with West Rocky Mountain II's keys and pet. The read-only study of 2026-10-24 has the rest
(`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/map3/study/ONBOARDING.md`: structure, grounds, stands, monsters and drops, crowding, the 20
native frames hand-labelled). Its monsters and drops as the stack sees them are under Perception (learned gates, kinds
that share a body, drops per map); its motion and the simulator there are below.

**The motion** (offline, from the game data and the planner: 175 moves, 74 jumps, 39 drops, 36 walk-offs, 13
jump-ups, 7 climbs, 6 climb-downs; every place gets to every other but the caps):
- **7 (two Horny Mushrooms) is reached:** the running jump off 8's left end (x 22), 45 up and 28 across, lands only
  from takeoffs at x 24-48, 2-26 units in from the end (the study's brute force); the jumps off an end looked for
  nearer the end (`route.END_LOOK`, West Rocky Mountain II's 17 onto 16) run from x 57, take off at x 37 (15 in) and
  land at -32. 25 -> 29 is found the same way. In the simulator 10 -> 7 by 9 and 8 arrives in 4 s
  (`nav_tree_top_cluster`).
- **The rope at -8 from 30** hangs 94.3 above 30's floor: 0.7 inside `physics.ROPE_REACH` (95, a guess from the start;
  the highest grab tried in game was 69 up) and 12.3 beyond HeavenClient's (`Ladder::inrange`: a point 5 above her feet
  on the rope, 82 at the top of her jump, `physics.GRAB_SURE`). It was on every way up from the bottom. A climb up a
  rope beyond a sure grab now lands half the time (`route.GRAB_CHANCE`, each miss 3 s), so the ways up go 30 -> 29 (a
  running jump) and up the same rope from 29 (36.8 up): 2.7 s against 2.4. Missed, the jump for it passes up through 29
  (58 above 30 there) and lands her on it; in the simulator with HeavenClient's reach (`Realism.rope_reach`) she does,
  and goes on up from there (`nav_tree_rope_miss`). No other climb on the three maps is between the two reaches.
- **Its floors slope** (most floating ones 17-19 units over 188, 0.1 a unit; the floor 33 rises 248 to 225 to the
  right): a step onto a floor rising the way she flew went through it, by the engine's landing check (Motion
  planning: now as HeavenClient judges it). Knocked right off 30 she came down through the floor and out of the map;
  of six 5-minute hunt loops from 28 four fell out, two inside the tower; none of those now.
- **The tower's walls** (group 0) don't stop her off a floating platform's outer end or a rope, by the client's
  movement as reconstructed (`body.OWN_GROUP_WALLS`; off a rope, none: `body.ROPE_GROUP`): knocked off 11's left end
  (13 from the wall), 23's (23), 25's right end (34), 10, 26, 17 or 8 toward the wall, or off the rope at -192 (28 from
  it), she falls past it and out of the map. Whether the game stops her there isn't known: `Realism.zero_walls` has
  group 0's walls stop her whatever her group, off a rope too, and the harness runs both (`--world zero-walls`).
  HeavenClient has neither rule: a wall stops her if it's chained to the foothold below her (its prev or the one
  before, `FootholdTree::get_wall`), whatever its group; that's a third reading, not modelled.
- **The exits:** no plan holds up within 60 units of a portal, nor on a platform up to 125 above an exit
  (`MapModel.portal_near`: flow and the mover's climbs; by one, the mover's climbs press up only after the jump's key,
  `mover.PORTAL_UP_MS`, which helps only if the game takes a portal on the ground alone), and no rope hangs near either
  exit. HeavenClient takes a portal while up is held with her feet from 100 above it to 25 below and 25 either side,
  on the ground or in the air (`Stage::update`, `Portal::bounds`, read 2026-10-24; `mapdata.PORTAL_BOX`), and so does
  the simulator: there it takes her out of the map and ends the run (`world.SimLeftMap`). One harness run of an
  earlier build did, a chain played on after a knock the stack didn't see (Harness baselines, below).
- **Trips** (the planner's seconds, from the middle of each, risks included; from her spot on 28 at 247 to the top
  stand on 8 at 137, 27.1 s; from the mid portal's shelf 12 at 160 to 7, 9.5 s):

each monster back 8.8 s, 17 s or 30 s after its death); with `Realism.shared_exp` (off) a kill of

44 labelled in plain view it found all, none as the other kind (Perception: Kinds of one shape). Its drops: in the

doesn't look for), drawn where they lie and named as that detector names them; what she picks up is weighed by the
map's worth either way (a bronze coin 33.4, not the first map's 15: so the harness's mesos a minute there are 2.23 times
what they were before the two met, her runs otherwise the same to the field on the two seeds of each run tried). Her MP
and Lucky Seven's are modelled with the harness's `--attack` (Attack: which attack a throw is); by default the sim
throws the Lucky Seven key as a star, and with `--world lucky-seven` every attack as live Lucky Seven, 3 stars a cast.

## Screen size: the game at its own 1366x768 (from 2026-10-23)

The game lays out a 1366x768 view, one game px to a map unit, and stretches it to its window. Until 2026-10-23 that
was a 1920x1080 client area on this PC's 4K screen, the view stretched 1.40625 times with bilinear filtering, and every
template, calibration and pixel constant was made on that picture. Since then the game is set to its own 1366x768
(Options, Graphics, Resolution "1366 x 768", windowed: `GetClientRect` 1366x768), drawn pixel for pixel ("run
detection on the native resolution, it's both more accurate and less resource consuming").

**The geometry** (`gamelab/screen.py`). A `Geometry` is a client size and how much a look shrinks it: `stretch` (screen
px per game px: 1.40625, or 1), `frame_scale` and `units_per_px` (a look frame's px per map unit and back: 0.703 and
1.42 at 1920x1080 half size, 1 and 1 at 1366x768 full size), `px` and `fpx` (a px measured on the 1920x1080 window, at
full or half size, in this geometry's px), `to_game` and `from_game` (where a game px's middle is on screen), and a
`suffix` that tells the files made for a size apart. It's worked out from the client size where frames are taken (the
commands make their `Eyes(geo=...)` from the game window's size as they start, a minimized game restored first by those
that bring it forward anyway and waited for by `watch`; `ScreenFrames`; a saved frame's own size) and goes with what's
read: `Observation.geo`, so `Scene`, and `WorldState.geo` over the feed's pipe. A capture of another size than the eyes
were made for is refused (as one not 1920x1080 was: run the command again), and the feed marks such frames not visible.
Nothing that reads the game uses the 1920x1080 window's numbers any more (`GAME_SIZE`, `SCREEN_SCALE`, `SCALE`,
`UNITS_PER_HALF_PX` are the simulator's, which draws its world at that size). `tests/test_geometry.py` checks that
outside the simulator no module imports them, no call leaves a `geo` at its 1920x1080 default, no module makes numbers
of its own from STRETCHED's, and no `*_PX` constant is used but through a geometry's conversion, except where each says
why (13 places): the import check alone had let `map` place her with 1920x1080's Localizer, `bodies` keep its own units
per px and the looting compare her ground with 6 px unconverted. At 1920x1080 every conversion is exact (`px(n)` is `n`
to the bit), so all of it is as it was: the full suite, the saved screenshots' tests, and the 86 golden traces.

What goes by it:
- **Her name tag** (`nametag.py`): matched at full size as before, with a template made at that size. Each client size
  has its own calibration (`paths.calibrated`: `calibration_1366x768.json`, `tag_template_1366x768.npy`,
  `tag_template_full_1366x768.npy`; 1920x1080's are the files they always were), and the search near where she was
  is converted (171 x 85 px). The 1366x768 template was made offline from the 31 saved frames: her tag's box is
  see-through and the clouds behind it move, so it's the median of the 31 (15 x 55 px, `tests/fixtures/native`). It
  matches every one of them at 0.92 or better where her tag is, and nothing else above 0.39 (the party list's
  "BugBaby" is another font); on the 17 bench frames shrunk to 1366x768, at 0.77-0.88.
- **The minimap** (`minimap.sizes`): its box (0, 68, 213, 213), the dot's and the markers' sizes and the ring
  converted (areas by the stretch's square). At 1366x768 the markers are their pictures: her yellow core 6 x 6 (24 px),
  another's red 5 x 5 (21 px), and her dot's middle comes out on the half pixel ((94.5, 172.5) on all 31 frames).
  There a portal's inner ring (4 x 4, hollow: 8 px) passed as a buddy's core at both of this map's portals on every
  frame (at 1920x1080 the filtering had blurred it into its dark), so a core must fill 70% of its box (`MARKER_FILL`:
  21 of 25), not asked at 1920x1080. Every other player's marker on the 31 frames is found (one to three at once, two
  touching; by eye on the enlarged minimaps) and nothing else; the game's six player markers pasted at 14 spots each
  are found where drawn (within 0.2 px), the 25 others (NPCs, portals, shops, runes) never.
- **HP and MP** are fractions of the window, which hold (row 756, the HP bar's red from x 503 to 607).
- **Her EXP number** (`exp_number.py`): the reader's model takes the geometry's stretch across and down (1 and 1:
  every glyph its picture) and the box read follows from it (`read_box`: (748, 738, 847, 750), 99 x 12 px; its size
  says which window it's from). All 31 frames read 31,736 [92.47%] at level 23, every cell within 0.69 levels of its
  glyph and every other reading 22.7 or more off (at 1920x1080 0.68 and 14.1); the reader's own drawing reads back,
  and the number one game px off its place doesn't. 2.8 ms a reading, against 7.9.
- **Ropes** (`terrain.py`): widths, lengths and the closing and opening kernels converted (6 x 2, 22 x 1). This
  map's rock passes for rope at this size, crisp: over the whole screen 2-8 ropes a frame on the 31, of which two are
  real (x 941 and 1174, the ropes at map x -536 and -303). A look searches only where the map's ropes can show, and
  there one or both of the real ones were found on 30 of the 31 frames (both on 23), but on 15 with rock or a rope's
  pieces beside them, mostly in the column of the rope at x -414, which isn't drawn there; the median of what they
  say kept her at -792 on 30 of the 31 (once her platform's end put her at -779). Not seen on the first map at this
  size.
- **Monsters** (`mobs.py`, `sprites.py`): the game's own sprites as they are, pixel for pixel and with their own alpha
  (`sprites_x1` beside the 1920x1080 ones, with a `scale.json`: `mobs.picture_scale`; each picture's INDEX entry says
  `"alpha": "game"`, and pictures made before it, their alpha cut at 128, are made again). Step 2 matches only the
  pixels the game draws as they are, the opaque ones: a slime is see-through (11,464 of its 17,927 pixels drawn are
  half opaque), and on screen those are partly what's behind it. Drawn as the game draws it on this map's frames
  (396 times), its frames scored 0.96 or more with them (median 0.98) and 1.000 without; on the same frames without it
  the best anywhere near scored 0.46 with them and 0.40 without. The screenshot cut-outs aren't used at this size:
  they're of the stretched window, and shrunk back they're neither (on the 17 bench frames shrunk, a snail's cut-out,
  with the grass it stood in, took the place where the snail's own frame scored 0.93). What matching them against the
  sprites says of them (`cutouts.json`, in their own px) still goes for any window that stretches the game. At this
  size a map's detector holds its own kinds alone (`MobDetector(kinds=)`), whatever `sprites_x1` holds from other
  maps: on West Rocky Mountain II, none of whose monsters had a colour gate then, it found nothing (on a checkout that
  hadn't built the first map's sprites it had stopped every look with "no monster templates"; at 1920x1080 the
  cut-outs and the sprites folder, every kind in them, as always). The search goes coarse to fine and re-finds a
  monster as the frame its animation went to (below); its re-find window and bands are converted, and a band with no
  rows finds nothing (shrunk for step 1, OpenCV had refused it).
- **Drops** (`loot.py`): the game's item pictures as they are (`loot_x1`; every one opaque, alpha 0 or 255, but the
  Fragment of Magic's glow: Perception, drops of each map), searched at full size. Drawn on screen pixel for pixel, a
  drop's colours are its picture's to the pixel, so its shape is matched on brightness alone (one channel instead of
  three: `LootDetector.gray`; its px drawn partly see-through left out) and its colours are checked as at
  1920x1080 (by 24 at most, on average). On the 17 bench frames shrunk it found the same 11 drops as in colour (scores
  0.81-0.95, in colour 0.83-0.95) and as 1920x1080 (0.68-0.85), each within a unit of where 1920x1080 put it, and every
  platform in view took 78 ms against 112 in colour (73 at 1920x1080); on this map's 31 frames it found none, as in
  colour. Coarse to fine wasn't kept for drops: OpenCV's masked match costs about 0.2 ms however few places it scores
  (a 27 x 27 picture over a window its own size), so checking each spot found at the smaller scale cost what the
  first pass saved (6 strips drawn on, 33-35 ms at full size against 34-35 checked with OpenCV's match and 41 with
  numpy's, one place each).
- **The rest:** the feed's ring holds frames of the look's shape (`feed.frame_shape`, 768 x 1366); the Localizer's
  origin moves to the same game px (`use`: one minimap px is 16 units at 1366x768), and the camera, ropes and platform
  ends on screen, the loot strips, the ground under her, the mover's rope line-up, the mouse nudge, the feed tracker's
  screen edge (`View.edge`, 34 px) and how far another player's dot may move between looks go by the look's geometry,
  and `map` places her dot by it too (with 1920x1080's Localizer it had put her at (-1319, 1897) on `n28_000.png`, where
  Senses puts her at (-880, 2697)). Recordings keep their client size and scale (`Recording.geo`,
  `recordings.file_geometry`; the older ones were 1920x1080 at half size), and what reads them reads them at it:
  `bodies` (each recording with a detector of its own size: with 1366x768 screenshots it had searched the half-size
  recordings with the 1366x768 detector and found nothing), and `combo`, `lock`, `track` and the physics check, whose
  jump lift, jump straight up, claw swing box and camera strips are converted (not yet checked on a recording made at
  1366x768: none exists). calibrate makes a calibration for the size the game is at, says the pictures it wrote
  (`calibrate_crop_1366x768.png`, where it had pointed at 1920x1080's old `calibrate_crop.png`), its crop covering the
  same part of the game (569 x 284 client px) and recordings shrunk as looks are (full size at 1366x768).

**Coarse to fine** (`mobs.SEARCH_SCALE`, `FINE_GATE`, `FINE_TEMPLATES`, `FINE_SLACK`). A monster search at full size
cost half again what it had at 1920x1080 half size (below): step 1's colour tests and silhouette matches on twice the
pixels. Now step 1 always works at the 1920x1080 window's half size, 0.703 px per game px, where everything it goes by
was measured (its thresholds, `MIN_COVER`, `MIN_BODY_PIXELS`, `MAX_CHECKS`, the colour gates, the whole screen's
bands): at 1366x768 the band or the screen is shrunk 1.42 times for it (area averaged, 1.7 ms for a fight's band),
and the colour gates see about what they saw on the stretched window (the learned gates, Perception, made on its
half-size frames, included). Step 2 then works at full size, with the game's own pictures:
- **Several frames a place.** Blurred, a monster's frames were alike, and the one whose silhouette matched best was
  good enough to check. Crisp, they aren't: drawn as the game draws them, a snail or slime checked with that frame
  scored 0.43-0.55 where its own frame, a few spots down at the same place, scored 1.000, and 16 of 120 were missed.
  So at each place step 1 picked, its best 6 templates (4: 112 found) are checked, each at its own spot
  (`mobs._places`; spot by spot in Python it took 4.4 ms a band, with numpy 1.1).
- **A gate first.** That's only where the place's best template scores 0.55 at step 1's scale, as step 2 went at
  1920x1080: of 337 monsters drawn, 331 scored that there (333 at 0.5, 329 at 0.6), and this map's rock gave 2.8
  places a frame that did (10.2 at 0.5; 1.1 at 0.6).
- **In small windows:** each template is looked for 4 px around its spot. Of the 189 matches scoring 0.85 or more,
  all were within 3 px of it; in windows of 11 px templates slid onto the monster beside theirs, and an Orange
  Mushroom's frame scored 0.61 on this map's rock.

At 1920x1080 half size the look frame is step 1's (`MobDetector.search` 1) and the search is as it was, to the bit:
the suite's comparisons with the search as it was (`old_detect`, on made-up frames and four saved screenshots) and the
saved screenshots' tests; and the 86 golden traces are byte-identical.

What the search makes of the first map's monsters at this size (`bench-paste --full-step-1`: every frame of the four
kinds, both ways, drawn twice onto West Rocky Mountain II's 31 frames, 120 in all; the same scenes stretched to
1920x1080 as the window did, bilinear, and looked at as before, its cut-outs and its sprites; whole-screen searches):

| | 1366x768, coarse to fine | 1366x768, step 1 at full size, one frame a place | 1920x1080, half size |
|---|---|---|---|
| found by the whole screen's search | 114 of 120 | 111 | 116 |
| ... by a fight's band around each | 119 | 120 | 119 |
| as the frame and facing drawn, of those the game's sprites matched | 112 of 114 | 99 of 111 | 69 of 102 (14 by a cut-out, which says no frame) |
| feet against where drawn, across / down (mean; at most), units | 0.0 / 0.0; 0 / 3 | 0.1 / 0.2; 3 / 6 | 0.6 / 1.1; 4.5 / 9.1 |
| scores | 0.61-1.00, median 1.00 | 0.66-1.00, median 1.00 | 0.62-0.98, medians by kind 0.84-0.91 |
| found that weren't drawn; on the 31 frames as they are | 0; 0 | 0; 0 | 2 (slimes); 3 (an Orange Mushroom, snails) |
| the whole screen; a band (ms, medians, other work sharing the CPU) | 85.6; 26.6 | 105.3; 26.8 | 78.1; 22.0 |

(A look frame's px is put in the game's picture by its middle, `(x + 0.5) * 1.42 - 0.5` at 1920x1080 half size,
`pasted._game`: by its edge, as at first, the first map's sprites found at 1920x1080 stood 0.27 units left and 0.19 up
of where they were drawn on average, by the middle 0.06 left and 0.02 down; and the cut-outs' matches, which had
counted as the wrong frame, are counted apart. The means and the counts found are as before.)

The 6 missed: two Orange Mushrooms and four slimes whose own frame wasn't among their place's 6 or whose place was
crowded out; and at either size a monster drawn across two of the whole screen's bands is found only by the band
around it (they overlap by 43 rows at this size, 30 half-size rows at 1920x1080, and a pig is 64 and 32 tall; the
perception track's bands overlap by the tallest template). Drops, the same way (`bench-paste`, 32 drawn): all 32 at
1366x768, scoring 1.00 and none on the frames as they are; 27 at 1920x1080 (0.68-0.97: two Leathers, a Pig's Head, a
Pig's Ribbon and a Slime Bubble missed). On the 17 bench frames shrunk (as the game would draw them there but for what
the stretch had blurred), 33 monsters were found by one search or another: 31 coarse to fine (missed: a slime half
behind her on `z2_shoot3.png`, one on `z2_shoot1.png`), 31 with step 1 at full size and the cut-outs, as before (the
one on `z2_shoot1.png` and one on `closeup.png`), 33 with step 1 at full size and the sprites alone, and 28 at
1920x1080 (those three, and the snails in plain view on `stand.png` and `sit.png`). Where 1920x1080 found them, the
feet came out 0.5 units apart across on average (at most 1.4). On this map's 31 frames as they are, none of the first
map's monsters was found at full size (at 1920x1080 half size, the stretched frames, 3).

**Re-finding a monster** (`MobDetector.refind`, `mobs.REFIND_GOOD`, `REFIND_NEXT`, `_next_frames`). The feed
re-finds every monster it follows in each frame with the picture that matched it last, and a hidden one with that
alone. Blurred at 1920x1080, a monster's frames were alike and that one mostly did; crisp at 1366x768, once the
animation steps on it seldom does. So at a look frame finer than step 1's, where it scores under 0.9, the frames it
most likely went to are matched in the same window in turn (its pose's next and the one after, the other poses' first:
standing, walking, the flinch; then the rest; 4 at most) until one scores 0.9, the best kept. `bench-paste`'s re-finds,
on the 31 frames (the first map's standing and walking sprites, both ways: each found, then drawn where it stood as
what it may show next; the fallback, a live track's, to the kind's whole set in the window; medians, other work
sharing the CPU):

| | 1366x768 now | 1366x768, the last frame alone (before) | 1920x1080, half size |
|---|---|---|---|
| unchanged: found again (feet within a unit); ms | 52 of 52 (52); 1.7 | 52 of 52 (52); 1.9 | 52 of 52 (42); 0.9 |
| its pose's next frame: found (within a unit), going on to the whole set; ms (at 90%); found without the fallback | 50 of 50 (46), 0; 3.2 (3.9); 50 | 49 of 50 (39), 27; 5.1 (19.5); 23 | 49 of 49 (28), 10; 0.9 (4.3); 39 |

times, at 0.9 182, at 0.8 168; 0.9 because a monster with her or another over part of it would take all 4 matches
every frame at 0.95.

## Probes to run

What a star hits still has open questions that only the game can settle (see Attack): the search window's top and floor, the search between her level and 60 below her, how an attack from a jump picks its target, what stops a star (that her own platform stops a star down past its end, and the step wall one up to 2, the user saw on 2026-10-21; where it gets through, and how high its line runs, are left), and how far the claw swipes. Each is now between reach's answer (the client's routine, or the logs' where the sources don't reach) and one other. `python -m gamelab probe run NAME` puts one of them to the game; none has been run in game yet (built and tested in the simulator only). The player must be running, as for `hunt`. `probe score` weighs both answers on the log (below), and once one is decided, what the second column names goes its way.

| Command (her place -> theirs, what it throws at) | Decides: reach's answer / the other | Expected by reach's | By the other |
|---|---|---|---|
| `probe run top-60` (13 at x -14 -> 12, 60 above her: pigs and Orange Mushrooms 110-200 off) | `SEARCH_TOP0`: 44, the client's / 21, the logs' fit | Hits from 111 (Orange Mushrooms 113) | Hits only from 191 (193) |
| `probe run top-120` (15 at x 76 -> 12, 120 above: 340-420 off; whole-screen looks) | The same | Hits from 351 | None |
| `probe run claw-edge` (21 at x -225, her level: pigs and slimes 95-160 off; with up to 2 others in front, the snails on 20 and 22) | `CLAW_FAR`: the stabs cut to 65 ahead / one box to 90 ahead, her level only (reach's until 2026-10-20) | Swipes (small bar drops) out to 99 off a pig, 93 off a slime; stars beyond | Swipes out to 124 and 118 |
| `probe run claw-down` (3 at x 716 -> 4, 60 below: pigs within 95 at the pick, Orange Mushrooms 60-125; 80 throws) | `claw_takes`: the stabs, 15-30 above her feet / the throw's swings, 17 below to 62 above | No hit at a pig; stars at Orange Mushrooms from 113 | A third of the throws within 99 swiped |
| `probe run below-42` (0 at x 1222 -> 1, 42 below: pigs 60-160, Orange Mushrooms 100-160, snails 130-220) | `RAMP_BELOW`: the search alone / the old ramp; and `claw_takes` | Pigs hit from 71, Orange Mushrooms at any distance, snails from 166; no swipe | The ramp: every kind from 126. The swings: a third of the throws at pigs within 99 swiped |
| `probe run step-down` (2 at x 50 -> 4, 60 below: pigs 200-310, slimes 230-340; 40 throws) | `LINE`: the v83 line / a level line | None under 254 (pigs) or 284 (slimes): 2's own floor stops the line; hits beyond | Hits |
| `probe run hanging-wall` (14 at x 706 -> 17, 60 below: pigs 180-250, slimes 190-290; 40 throws) | The same | None under 215 (pigs; on 17 from 189) or 241 (slimes; from 183); hits beyond | Hits |
| `probe run step-up`, with `--style jump_throw` and `jump_back`, each with `--x 260` too (4 at x 500 -> 2, 60 above, behind the step wall: 200-400) | `SHOT_H`, fitted; her own group's walls stop a star / no wall does (the logs had it, and the user saw it on 2026-10-21) | No hits from the ground (the line 28 up) or jump throws (54 up), hits from jump backs (72 up), by either line | Hits from all three |

| `probe run floor` (14 at x 824 -> 17, 60 below: Orange Mushrooms 90-150, pigs 120-190, slimes 130-200) | `SEARCH_FLOOR0`, fitted (no other answer) | Orange Mushrooms hit from 113, pigs from 151 (171 standing), slimes from 177 | |

Where the probes stand is chosen so their throws tell the answers apart under the client's pick:
- **step-down and hanging-wall** throw where the two lines differ and about as far past it, 40 times: that her own platform stops a star down past its end the user saw in game, and what's left is where it lets one through, which the hits by distance in `probe score` show (and about half their throws are where the lines differ, as all 20 were before 2026-10-21). By the v83 line a star needs room past her platform's end, so from 2 at x 50 (169 from its end) the lines differ at pigs on 4 out to 253 and slimes to 283; an Orange Mushroom is clear from 199, and all of 4's are 201 or more off, so none is thrown at. hanging-wall stands at x 706 (25 inside 14's left end; from x 730 the lines differed only at pigs 166-178): pigs differ at 189-214, slimes at 183-240, and no Orange Mushroom can be close enough.
- **claw-down** throws at a pig only where it will be within 95 when the attack picks (`Probe.at_pick`, `probe.x_after`: one seen walking goes on at its kind's speed the way it faces for the time from the look to the pick, turning back at 4's end). A pig on 4 is never closer than 81 to her place (4 ends at 669), and the swings reach one to 99, so the throws that tell the answers apart are at a pig in the last 18 units of 4, where it turns, and walking 125 units/s (the game data's) it goes 20-26 units from the look to the pick. Where she stands moves that: with the game's errors (the harness's preset `game`) she stood 704-720 on seeds 1-8, within the 20 she keeps to, where a pig comes within 69-85 of her. Thrown at by where the look had it (88-100 off), it was within 97 at the pick on 13-37 of 40 throws there, and 40 throws decided the stabs on 1 of the 8 seeds, the swings on 2; by where it will be, 63-74 of 80. Orange Mushrooms out to 125, where their stars from 113 show how often a hit is seen. It needs 80 throws: with the stabs nothing at all is hit within 99, and a run of no hits only slowly rules out a swipe a third of the time (with the game's errors, 40 decide the stabs on all 8 seeds and the swings on 4, 80 both on all 8).
- **below-42** throws at Orange Mushrooms only from 100. One 42 below reaches into the stabs' boxes in its taller frames (58-67 units: half its standing and a quarter of its walking), which the scorer, by its walking body (55), leaves out; past the boxes' reach (97) it tells the ramp from the search and nothing else. Pigs (54 tall at most) never reach the stabs from 42 below.
- **step-up** is left with the line's height (the user saw the step stop her stars on 2026-10-21, as the logs had it), and can't tell the lines apart: the v83 line to a walking body on 2 ends at its feet, 60 up, so it meets the step wall below its top corner whatever the distance, as the level line does from the ground and from jump throws, and clears it with it from jump backs. Only a body lifted off its feet right behind the step's edge (a pig's third walking frame lifts 4; 281-315 off from x 500) would take the v83 line over the corner: a few hits there from the ground would point to it. Nor, since the star's hit point is taken on the monster's platform (`reach._hit_on`), does a body hanging over the step's edge at the far end of a star's reach (from 4's right end, 368-410 off) take it past the wall. Nor can any probe here tell one-sided walls from walls that stop a star either way: every wall on this map faces out from the platform it hangs from.

**How a probe throws:**
- The navigator takes her to her place, keeping clear of monsters, and she keeps to it, facing the way she throws: knocked off, or carried off by a jump back, she walks or goes back, her last walk the way she throws (from 12 behind her place at least), so no throw turns her. A turn's tap walks her 7 units on: from x 30 on 22 (`air`) her throws after the first came from 38, where the snail came back within reach of her. Nor does she walk or throw from a look a touch's knock may still be moving her in (`Hunter.knocked`).
- She throws the regular attack only when exactly one monster is in front of her (within 420 units by its middle, from 140 above her feet to 140 below; behind a wall or not, since a walled one the attack takes first takes it and the star stops at the wall), and it's one the probe throws at, in range sideways (for claw-down, where it will be when the attack picks). `--crowd N` also throws with N others in front, for a busy ground (the scorer weighs every monster in front); claw-edge does with 2 of its own (`Probe.crowd`), for the snails on 20 and 22, 60 above and below her: in game it threw none alone (below). A jump back's range ends 27 units nearer (`probe.JUMP_BACK_OUT`, the engine's): she's that far out when its attack picks, and from 4 at 2 Orange Mushrooms 387-394 off at the look were past a star's reach by then.
- After each throw she waits for its star's evidence before the next: every look until 0.9 s after the star was due, or up to 2.5 s while the target is hidden under its damage numbers. So a hit is never another throw's, and a monster hit by one throw has stopped flinching when the next attack picks.
- Her own platform's monsters (`probe._keep_clear`): one of a kind it doesn't throw at that comes within 150 of her (`fight.IN_HER_WAY`) is fought off first (`fight.clear` on her platform, up to one kill). One it throws at, on her platform (claw-edge, air), closer than its range starts, is stepped away from (`probe.GIVE_WAY`), up to 60 from her place and never within 90 of her platform's end, and where she can't step, waited out: fighting those off cost claw-edge nearly all its throws in the simulator (below). Either way no probe throws while one of her platform's monsters is in her way (`probe.in_her_way`, `choose`), whatever its crowd: one that close in front takes the attack itself, and such throws told nothing (below). A probe that stands where monsters spawn and throws at another platform's (`probe.clears_first`: step-down from 2, step-up from 4, claw-down from 3) clears her platform first (every monster on it in reach, 8 kills or 30 s at most), and again whenever one of its monsters is in front of her or in her way, and waits for a throw between clears. A run that fights 120 s without a throw (`probe.FIGHT_MAX_S`) stops and says so: her platform's monsters come back faster than she clears them, and she'd fight its whole time (as step-down did in game, below). The report counts the fights and their time.
- `--x`, `--dx LO-HI`, `--style` and `--throws` change a probe. `--walls on|off` sets whether her decisions keep to the wall rule during the run (whether a target behind a wall, or behind a monster the attack takes first that is, is thrown at, and the fights); the probes that measure it set it off.
- The player, the Lie Detector watchdog and the alarm work as for `hunt kill`: `probe run` is refused while the alarm is up, and every key goes through the player. Waiting for a lone monster she can go minutes without a key, the moment the alarm is otherwise noticed, so the probe also checks it before every look (a look brings the game to the front). `probe list` and `probe score` send nothing.

**The log** (`lab/probe_geometry.jsonl`, one line per throw) keeps where she and every monster in front of her were at the throw, and at the first look after it (about when the attack picked its target), each monster with the way it faced and its pose as the look read them. For each of those monsters it keeps its HP bar before the star could land, the bar in every look after, the looks it wasn't seen in, and whether it was gone at the end. It also keeps her EXP gains and the wall rule's verdict.

**`probe score`** (or `probe score FILE`) reads the log with the map's game data. A monster showed a hit when its HP bar came up or dropped, or when it died (her EXP up, and it the one gone): the claw's if it took under 20 HP's worth of its bar (a swipe does 9-11, a star 30-70: 16% of a pig's bar, 14% of an Orange Mushroom's, 17% of a slime's, 44% of a snail's, by their HP in the game data), else a star's. It showed none when it was seen with its bar as before 0.3 s or more after the star was due. While it was hidden, nothing can be told. Each answer is reach's model of the attack with one piece changed (`probe.Model`), and gives every monster in front at the pick its chance of the claw's swipe and of a star that gets to it, as the simulator's world picks: the claw's stance, one per attack, the nearest in its box; else any monster in the search's first band as likely; from a jump the area, or the search from as high as she is; then the line to the star's pick alone, the star lost if it's stopped (`probe.chances`). A monster the look after the key saw walking is as likely anywhere it walks from 40 ms before that look to 40 ms after it (`probe.placings`, `PICK_SLACK_S`): that look isn't taken at the pick, and its frame is older than its time, by how much isn't measured in game. Its likelihood is that of every monster's hit or none, with the two hit rates fitted (a monster taken shows a hit at least 30% of the time, one not taken at most 20%: without those bounds a run of hits fits "not taken" as well as "taken"; and neither rate within 5% of 0 or 1, since a hit or none is read wrong now and then too), and of every hit's size, read wrong 5% of the time. So a single "none" where every other throw hit weighs at most 2.9 (log 0.95/0.05), under what decides; with the rates allowed to 2% of 0 and 1 it weighed up to 3.9, and below-42 was decided in the simulator on one or two throws. Then:
- **Each question**, over the throws of the probes that ask it (the second column): both answers' log-likelihood, on how many throws they have the attack take something else, and the answer decided once it fits 3 better than the other (about 20 to 1) on 5 or more of those throws (`probe.DECIDE_THROWS`). Where they have it take the same on every throw, it says it can't tell.
- `SEARCH_TOP0` and `SEARCH_FLOOR0` fitted to every throw from the ground (the values within 1.92 of the best, and how reach's value and the logs' 21 do), and `SHOT_H` to every throw (a jump raises the line by `reach.air_rise`), each by the line in force (`reach.LINE`, or `probe score --line level|v83`, the questions but `LINE` and the score's header going by it too): a throw whose star the line stops took nothing, so its miss says nothing of the window. Until 2026-10-21 `SHOT_H` was fitted by the level line whatever reach had: where only a floor stops the line, nothing bounded it.
- The claw probes: the target's hits by how far off it was, each the claw's or a star's.

**Checked in the simulator** (`tests/test_probe.py`; scenarios `probe_top`, `probe_step_up` and `probe_air`: these runs and scenarios went with the first map's tests on 2026-10-31, test_probe.py keeping the probes' rules on made-up maps). Every probe was run in a world with reach's answer and in one with the other (the simulator's world goes by `reach`, so the other claw is `reach.CLAW`, the other line `reach.LINE`, the other air pick `sim.world.AIR_PICK`), 20 throws each (claw-edge, step-down and hanging-wall 40, claw-down 80, as in game), at a lone monster walking its platform. | top-120 | `SEARCH_TOP0` | 29.1 (17); 20.2 (15) | 3.4 (15); 2.6 (10): seed 5 undecided |

Moved back by the looks' times instead (4 units), it leaned 14.7 that way; taken as anywhere from 40 ms before the look to 40 ms after it, the old box is decided by 5.3. Before monsters walked the game data's speeds (pigs 70 units/s), three runs were left undecided, on 1-4 throws; at the rebase, five, and one leaned the wrong way. below-42 also asks the claw off her level, but its few throws at pigs within 99 lean the stabs' way by 0.8-2.6 in reach's world (decided on none), and decide the swings in a world with them on 2 of the 8 seeds (seeds 5 and 6; seeds 3 and 7 lean 0.2-0.8 the stabs' way), on none the other way: claw-down's 80 throws decide it on all 8. With the game's errors (the harness's preset `game`: stars that miss, walks that stop early or late, lags spread, lost taps, her dot to whole pixels, hit monsters hidden 1-3 s, sightings missed) 140 of the 160 runs are decided (145 before step-down and hanging-wall threw past where the v83 line lets a star through, 2026-10-21: their 32 runs decide 25, the level line's world on step-down only 4 of 8; 129 before the slack, claw-edge's 40 throws and claw-down's throws by where a pig will be), none the other way, and four lean it, by up to 2.0 (below-42 in reach's world on seed 4; step-down on three, by 0.2-1.5; four by up to 2.9 before): in game a probe may take more throws than these, and `probe score` reads every run's in the log. `tests/test_probe.py` runs claw-down with them in both worlds. ## Found offline, not fixed yet

None left from the refactor (each fixed below). Found since (2026-10-20, in the harness's runs):
- **A rest trip could end hanging on a rope, and the rest waited there** (gone with the rests on 2026-10-26: No resting: the safety stop). In the harness (`loop-grind`, crowd, zero-walls, the feed, seed 9, 2026-10-25) a rest trip from 28 (walk_off to 30, jump to 29, climb to 27) grabbed the rope at x -8 at 180 s and she stayed on it: "resting on platform 27" with her HP at 48% for the remaining 420 s (the chair does nothing on a rope), 373 s stuck, EXP 37 a minute against 155 at the base. Not fixed (the rest's, not the attack's: Attacks from her jumps).
- **A rest that a touch stood her up from waited out its 120 s** (gone with the rests on 2026-10-26: No resting: the safety stop). `Tour.rest` sits her down once (`Actions.sit`) and looks every 5 s until her HP is back or 120 s are up (`REST_SECONDS`); a touch's knock stands her up from the chair (the simulator's world does; in game unmeasured), and a chair pressed while she still slides does nothing, and it never sits her down again. In the harness (hunt loop, Tree Dungeon, crowd, zero-walls, the feed, 2026-10-25) a rest onto 25 at x 272, under 24's end, had a Green Mushroom on 24 touch her 2 s after she sat (seed 11: her HP at 74% for 120 s), and a rest trip that timed out rested on the floor among its monsters ("couldn't reach a safe platform (timeout); resting here", `loop_tree_run` on seeds 4 and 6, past the run's 600 s). It's most of the seed-to-seed spread of the hunt loop's EXP: over seeds 1-16 of 10 minutes, 42 s a run stuck at the base and 71 on work/jump-attack, and with the rest giving up once two looks show her HP not rising (an experiment: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/ov-jump-fix/exp3.py) 1 s either side, the two equal (+0.1%, SE 4.3%). Not fixed (the rest's, not the attack's).
- **The simulator can knock her out of the map at the basin's right corner.** A touch's knockback from the air near the right end of 36 (x 951, where the wall up to 35 meets the floor) carried her past the wall's bottom end, which `physics.fly` lets her slip under at the corner: her arc crossed x 951 just below y 576, past 36's end, with no floor below. She then fell forever at x 1479 (hunt loop, seed 10, 128 s into the run: 13.8 EXP a minute instead of 124-126). The simulator now flies her by the engine (`body.fly`), which lands a step that goes through a platform's surface before its end, so that corner holds (Motion planning: its arcs and the planner's).
- **Then the navigator never gave up getting off a "rope".** Placed off every platform, it logged "on a rope at x 1477: getting off" every 5 s for the rest of the run, and the hunt loop's own backstops (`STUCK_S`) never ran, since the trip never returned. The simulator now ends the run when she falls out of the map (`SimFellOut`, which the harness counts as a death), so it no longer gets there; in game a misread position could still do the same.
- **In the simulator the basin's cliffs let her through, and nothing is under them.** In the air from another block (27, 31, 33 and the others over the basin), the walls rising from 36's ends to 34 and 35 are another foothold group's and don't stop her (`body.OWN_GROUP_WALLS`), and past them nothing is under her: she falls below the map's lowest floor (`SimFellOut`, which the harness counts as a death). Whether the game lets her through them is unmeasured: the six telemetry flights through another group's wall all went through the hanging walls of floating blocks, none through a cliff with nothing under it (and through one, players would fall out of this map). So is what the game does with a fall out of the map. At the merge it ended 3 of 60 harness runs over seeds 1-30 (tour seeds 5 and 25, loop 19). The stack keeps clear of it now (Fixed since: the drops, the chains, the knocked jumps, the walk-offs), and none of the 60 falls out, nor any of 1,056 scenario runs (seeds 1-16). Taking a wall with nothing under its far side as stopping her whatever her group would close it in the simulator, but would rest on nothing measured either.
- **Knock-offs rose with the claw's edge by size**: fights ending with her knocked off her platform, tour 93 -> 113 in 10 runs of 20 minutes, hits pushing her off one 15 -> 20 (loop 8 -> 14), with jump backs +23% and jump throws +25%. At the branch's head it's 103 (93 at master; a run has 1-30, so about 10 either way is noise). `nav_fight_up` arrives on 30 of seeds 1-48, 39 at master: all 18 failures run out of time after a touch knocks her off 3 or 4 (or off 18, 20 or 21 on the way back up), in jump throws, jump backs and throws at pigs, slimes and snails within about 90 of her. Not mitigated: whether she's knocked off more in game is to be counted there (on 3, 20 and 22, with pigs and slimes 100-136 off). With both tracks (her body by the engine, monsters pushed back by hits), `nav_fight_up` arrives on 43 of seeds 1-48; the 5 others run out of time. With the review's fixes, 36 (38 without the waits for her to land and for a knock to end): the 12 others run out of time at 180-194 s, 10 of them knocked off 3 or 4 and climbing back from 32 or the basin, which took 164-180 s on the seeds that went that way and arrived at the merge.
- **Looks in mid-jump forget drop spots with the drops still there.** A look's loot strips are put just above the ground of the platform her position is put on, and in mid-jump that's the one under her (`pose.where_dot` puts her y on it), so they sit as high above its ground as she is and find nothing; two such looks 1.5 s apart forget a pile (`DropStore.on_look`, `Looter.remember`). It's what most of the hunt loop's lost drops came to: in the basin (seed 2), 357 of the 359 piles forgotten with drops on them were forgotten by looks in mid-jump, and 152 of the 204 drops that lay their whole life on 36 had such a pile. It got worse on this branch as jump backs and jump throws grew: the loop's drops share 84% at master, 72% now, nearly all of it on 36 (seeds 2, 4, 6, 8). `looting.STANDING_ONLY` (off) lets only a look that shows ground under her feet see a spot empty. On, the loop picks up 92% of its drops but makes 7% less EXP a minute (8 seeds; two runs fell out of the map), as it then goes for piles in the basin that monsters always guard (seed 4: 7 of its 10 pile trips there ran out their 60 s); the tour is about the same (87.4 EXP a minute, 94.6%). The hunt loop's pile rules should weigh that before it's switched on.
- **The simulator's attack picks by each kind's walking height, not by the frame a monster shows** (`World.top`: a pig 46 tall, as the decisions have it). By its frames a pig standing 60 below her (38-40 tall) would be picked from the ground only from 171 units sideways, not 151, and from a jump not at all, where in game pigs 60 below were hit; and a slime mid-hop on a platform 60 above (its feet lifted 16) only from 177, not 117.
- **A drop planned a few units from another platform's end below.** A drop goes from the middle of where her platform overlaps the one she lands on, but another may lie under part of that overlap: 11 -> 20 drops from -45, 6 units from the end of 12, which is between them. Flow then can't chain it (its spot lands on 12), and the mover drops within 20 units of the move's spot: in `nav_drops` (seed 1, where the route's weights come out otherwise since the drops moved) she landed on 12 and replanned. The middle of the stretch that lands on the platform (a drop falls straight down: `platform_below`) would hold.
- **On a rope, the escort threw at monsters "in reach" for the rest of a tour** (harness, tour seed 28, with her decisions on the v83 line, `reach.LINE = 'v83'`, in a world with either line). A chain capped at its length mid-climb (from 17 by 14 and 6 up to 3, `chain ended: long`) left her on the rope by 6, and the escort (`FightOnTheWay`, `navigator._shoot_on_the_way`), from a look that put her on a platform, threw again and again: the last 260 s went by without a kill, since the world takes no attack on a rope. It's the escort's, not the line's: with the level line that seed never got there. With her decisions on the v83 line, the default since 2026-10-21, that seed makes 121 EXP a minute, its longest stretch without a kill or a pick-up 24 s, and none of seeds 1-30 has one over 60 s (the escort's bursts are capped per platform, `ON_WAY_TRIES`).

- **Chained jumps miss more on the game's steps** (harness, preset `game`, 10 seeds: What the game's steps changed, in Motion planning). Landings elsewhere with no touch near: tour 14 in 377 chains, against 6 in 317 on the 5 ms engine. A chain is planned open loop from one look: on tour seed 9 a step back on 19 held 189 ms went 41.5 units, not the 35.8 planned (the release seen 60 ms late: walk jitter and the lags' spread), the jump off 19 landed 7 units short on 18, and the run on to 18's jump up onto 16 took off at 439, where from 440 on she'd have landed on 16 (planned 451): she fell to 32. On the steps a takeoff is also up to half a step's run (2.2 units) either side of the mean, and a run on from a landing waits up to a step. Route jumps keep 12 units of slop either side of their takeoff, which errors that add up over a chain's legs can use up. Since step 2 of the live fixes (Chains on the night's live misses, below) a chained jump takes off only where it lands with 8 units of slop at its real takeoff: 7 such landings in 384 chains of the tour's 10 seeds, 3 in 175 of the loop's.

Found since, not fixed (the simulator's physics):
