The same seed with blocking looks never got there. In game a map's sides are walls of their own. It happens at both ends of the basin, and which runs meet it shifts with any change to what she does: in the hunt loop with the feed, seeds 8 and 12 once the tracker gated its poses, seed 6 with the looks' newer costs; there she hangs "on a rope" outside the map (x -492 or 1477), "getting off" every 5 s for the rest of the run (264-673 s without a kill), which the harness counts as `stuck_s`. Comparisons in this README leave such seeds out, on both sides, and say so.

Fixed since, each a deliberate change to the scenarios that pinned it (re-recorded, and their `expects` changed to pin the fix):
- **Falling out of the map by the basin's cliffs** (harness, both tracks; the simulator's cliffs: Found offline). At the merge 3 of 60 runs over seeds 1-30 fell out (tour seeds 5 and 25, loop 19), each in the air above 36 from another block, by one of its ends. Fixed one cause at a time (each fix changed the runs, and others fell out until all were in), none of the 60 falls out now:
  - A drop goes from the middle of the overlap with the platform she lands on (`route._drop_moves`), not with whichever platform came first: 27 -> 36 dropped 6 units from 36's left cliff (from 27's overlap with 2, above it) and 33 -> 36 6 from the right one, and a touch's knock as she came down took her through (tour 25, loop 19). 27 -> 36 is gone (only 12 units by the cliff land her on 36).
  - No drop comes down within 70 units of a cliff (`route.KNOCK_CARRY`): knocks carried her 58 and 62 units off drops from 31 at 185 and from 33 at 907 (loop seeds 11 and 12). 33 -> 36 drops from 881.
  - No chain is planned from a look of her in mid-jump (Control: a route): loop seed 30.
  - No jump is keyed from a look a knock may still be moving her in (Behavior: a fight). On tour seed 5 a jump throw so keyed went in once she had landed on 34 and slid on (the turn's 205 ms wait let it: such a jump key isn't always lost in the air), took her up onto 31 0.4 units from its end (that nothing was overhead was checked 55 units back, where she was at the look), and the next throw's turn tap walked her off it. In `loop_run` the jump keys lost in the air went from 21 to 9: those left come from a touch after the look, in the plan's lead-in, which no look shows.
  - A walk-off has its run-up (Control: one move at a time): knocked onto 31's end, she was sent back down to 34 from 0.4 units in and left at 35 units/s (tour seed 3).
- **Shooting down at a snail 60 below** (both tracks). The decisions counted a snail on a platform 60 units below, 150-270 units off, in reach, where the simulator's attack area couldn't pick it: in `nav_fight_basin` on seed 6 she threw 72 stars from platform 30 at a snail on 33 and none hit, and on the physics track 6 of the 7 seeds of 16 that ran out of time did that. From the ground both now go by the star's search (Attack: other platforms), which picks a snail 60 below from 246 units off, and `nav_fight_basin` meets all its checks on all of seeds 1-16. Which is right in game is unmeasured (a pig 60 below was hit in game).
- **The probes keep their geometry** (`probe_air`, `probe_step_up`, both tracks). `probe_air` failed "every one kills the snail" on 6 of seeds 1-16 and `probe_step_up` "jumping back, every star does" on 3, none on the attack track. A run starts with her facing unknown, so the first throw turned her, and the turn's tap walked her 8 units on toward the snail's spawn, where it came back within reach of her (261 touches over the 16 seeds, 77 on the attack track); a knock then had the next jump throw keyed mid-knock, its jump lost. And a jump back carries her 25 units out by the pick, past a star's reach of targets at the probe's far end. Now she faces the way she throws at her place, doesn't throw from a look of a knock, and a jump back's range ends 25 nearer (Probes to run): all 48 runs of the three probe scenarios on seeds 1-16 meet their checks.
- **Resting at very low HP now reaches a safe platform** (`tour_rest_hp_low`). After a stop ended on "HP low" (below `--low-hp`), `Navigator.go`'s first health check ended the trip to rest at once, so she sat down where she was, among the monsters, and in the simulator died there. The trip to rest now checks only for potions (`Hunter.drink_if_low`): she drinks on the way, shoots what's in her way, and rests on the safe platform.
- **Drops noted during a loot trip are kept** (new scenario `tour_collect_loot_on_the_way`; `tour_run`, `tour_hunt_from_safe_spot`). `Tour.collect_loot` set the remembered drops to the rest of its list after each trip, so the drops of monsters shot on the way were forgotten (only a later whole-screen look found them again). They're now remembered for the next collection (or a fight's sweep) rather than gone after in the same one: going after them at once, every kill on a trip made another trip, and in the simulator three tour scenarios ran out of time shooting respawns. Collections are also capped (`LOOT_SECONDS`, 180 s: no trip starts later than that into one), because where respawns guard the drops, as on 18 below platform 16, going back for them never ended. In `tour_run` one trip now goes to a kept drop first; in `tour_hunt_from_safe_spot` the last collection goes after the kept drops on 18 until the cap (115 s more, 6 more items picked up, 15 more kills).
- **Kills made shooting a monster in the way of a move count in the trip's kills** (`nav_fight_basin`: 16 -> 18, all of the world's 18; `tour_run`: 74 -> 76 on the way). `FightOnTheWay.clear_way` now returns its kills, as `shoot` does.
- **`tour --seed` seeds the navigator's route choices too**, not just the sweep order, as the simulator does (no scenario goes through the command; a test pins it).

Fixed on 2026-10-19 as step 1 of `docs/hunt-modes.md`, one change each, before the new hunt loop, so it isn't credited with them:
- **The report adds up HP lost** (`tour_hunt_basin`, `tour_hunt_noisy`, `tour_run`): `Report.add` left `damage_taken` out, so every stop said "HP lost: 0%".
- **Every kill counts**: the trips to rest and to stand by, and the fights guarding drops, now add their kills to the tour's `on_the_way` (`tour_rest`: 0 -> 7 on the way; `tour_run` now reports all 114 of the world's kills).
- **No jump or attack inside the attack lock**: every plan that presses jump or attack is held back just enough that the key comes after her last attack's 730 ms lock (`Actions.hold_back`, used by `Actions.play`, so the mover's single moves too, and by the navigator's chains). Pressed inside the lock, a jump is ignored. This happened in 4 scenarios, by 2 to 494 ms (`nav_fight_up`, `nav_fight_across`, `tour_hunt_from_safe_spot`, `tour_hunt_platform_12`). In `nav_fight_across` the timing then differs enough that she isn't touched on her way to 18.
- **The mover's walks press pick-up** (the walk to an x after a trip, the walk before a jump up or a drop), as `Actions.walk` does, every 150 ms and through the slide after. Walks last about 0.2 s longer. 17 scenarios changed; `tour_run` picks up 189 items instead of 152, and the basin ends `tour_hunt_basin` with no drops left. `nav_monsters_staircase` moved to seed 1, because with seed 3 no monster was in her way to hop any more.
- **A trip to drops gets there** (`tour_hunt_basin`, now pinned to have no "couldn't get there (timeout)"). On the platform she's going to, the navigator no longer fires bursts at whatever is in reach (a loot trip to the basin's own drops used to spend its whole 60 s on that). It only shoots a monster between her and the x she's sent to (`clear_way`, at most 3 fights in a row), then walks there. 8 scenarios changed. `tour_hunt_from_safe_spot` now needs just over 400 s, so its limit is 600 s.

In the simulator's game-like world (`python -m gamelab.sim.harness`, preset `game`, 10 seeds of 20 minutes), these fixes took today's tour from 90 to 85 EXP a minute. It now picks up 95% of its drops instead of 94%, and loses less HP (2.6 instead of 2.8 bars). Its loot trips run out their 60 s 31 times instead of 64, but clearing the way to a drop now hits its 3-in-a-row cap 52 times instead of 11.

**The hunt loop in the simulator** (`tour --loop`, step 5 of `docs/hunt-modes.md`; not tried in game yet). Against the fixed tour above, preset `game`, 20 simulated minutes a seed:

| | tour | loop |
|---|---|---|
| EXP a minute, 10 seeds (20 seeds) | 84.8 (85.7) | 114.2 (117.7) |
| better on | | 9 of 10 (19 of 20) seeds |
| worst seed | | -35% (seed 7, both) |
| drops picked up a run | 185 (195) | 250 (266) |
| share of her drops picked up | 95.3% (95.6%) | 95.2% (95.8%) |
| HP lost (bars of 1.4%) | 2.6 (2.7) | 2.5 (2.5) |
| deaths | 0 | 0 |

With `--think 1` (the stack's real computing time charged): 80.8 -> 116.8 EXP a minute, better on all 10 seeds, 95.8% of drops: it passes the whole bar. With the knobs on, it misses one point: seed 7 (start on platform 24), 48 EXP a minute against the tour's 74. There it hunts 17 from the spot on 16, which pays best by the rate rule, but is knocked off it again and again, and the climbs back and the trips for piles on the way keep it from judging the ground (leaving is decided only when no other rule fires). Seed 7 swung between 44 and 85 EXP a minute across variants of the loop that differ in nothing it should care about; the share of drops picked up also moves by about 3 points between such variants (one started 0.2 s later). In the crowded `plain` world: 133 -> 208 EXP a minute and 336 drops a run against 299, but only 69% of its drops: with monsters always in reach, shooting comes first and piles are gone for only when about to vanish or when the ground empties.

**`--rest-avoid`** (step 7; `python -m gamelab.sim.harness rests`): 40 trips to rest at 28% HP from the hunting grounds, preset `game`. Keeping clear of monsters, she lost 1.6% HP a trip instead of 6.2%, and got there in 6.1 s instead of 28.5 s, with no deaths either way. The trips that shoot their way through made 120 kills on the way; the avoiding ones made none. It stayed an option, never checked in game, until the rests went on 2026-10-26 (No resting: the safety stop).

**Jump-throws at snails** (found in game on 2026-10-19, fixed on 2026-10-20; see Attack). On the 168-unit platforms 3, 20 and 22 a snail cornered her and she jump-threw at it: of 45 throws at most one hurt it, and the stars hit pigs, slimes and Orange Mushrooms on the platform 60 above. The simulator hid it: it resolved an attack when its star left (she had landed by then), from wherever she was then, hitting anything on her level at any distance. Now:
- `stance` decides close quarters by the nearest monster's kind: a jump back or a jump throw only if its attack starts low enough to pick that kind (`reach.air_hits`, from `physics.JUMP_ATTACK_MS` and `JUMP_BACK_ATTACK_MS`). A snail is shot from the ground: from 125 away if she can step back that far (a star), else from where she is (the claw swipes it). Checked in game on 2026-10-20: an attack keyed 40 ms after the jump hits snails (a star for 78, the snail dead), so `JUMP_ATTACK_MS` is 40, and cornered by a snail she jump-throws again.
- A fight's targets in the path of a jump throw (what a kill is matched against) come from her height when the attack starts: the platform above as far as a star reaches, and not a snail beside her. EXP from up there was taken for the snail's: on 2026-10-19 "snail down" was logged 3 times while the snail lived on, and the snail, then left alone as a dying one, twice ended the fight that way.
- The simulator picks an attack's target when it starts (`World._aim`), by the monsters' bodies: on the ground the claw's swing first, then the attack's area, from where she is then, in the air or not; hit monsters flinch taller for 0.6 s. New scenario `fight_snail_short_platform`: with the old decisions in this simulator it passes on none of 30 seeds (on 22 the snail is still alive after 15 s, on 11 "snail down" comes while it lives), with the new ones on 18 (on the others the snail walks into her first, and a touch knocks her off the end of 22).
- In the simulator's game-like world (preset `game`, 10 seeds of 20 minutes): the tour 84.8 -> 83.9 EXP a minute (152.9 -> 142.0 kills a run), the hunt loop 114.2 -> 115.4 (190.0 -> 187.0), its worst seed (7) 48.5 -> 80.7. Far fewer snails die (in the 10 runs, tour 211 -> 117, loop 78 -> 29), and stars that went over them hit the monsters above instead, which give more EXP. The claw swipes more often (tour 966 -> 1,642 swipes): by the game data its swing reaches into bodies up to 110-125 off by their middle, where `stance` and `decide` count on a star from 90-100 units. HP lost a run 2.6 -> 2.8 bars (tour) and 2.5 -> 2.6 (loop); drops picked up 95.3% -> 93.7% (tour), 95.2% -> 94.9% (loop).
- Left as it was: the ledger (`behavior/ledger.py`, `in_path`) still matches kills against a throw's path from the ground, as it isn't told which throws were jumps; and `stance`'s and `decide`'s distances for a star (90-110) are still inside the claw's reach for slimes, pigs and Orange Mushrooms.

**Stars from platform 4 at monsters on 2** (found in the live logs of 2026-10-18 to 10-20, fixed on 2026-10-20; see Attack). On 4 she threw at Orange Mushrooms on 2, 60 above her behind the step wall joining the two, and no star got there: 0 of 3 in the shot log, 0 of 5 in a tour's telemetry, all 4 kills of 40 throws on 4 in a sweep. About 1.2-1.5% of her live throws went that way (5 of 419 in the telemetry, 3 of 204 in the shot log). The simulator hid it: its stars went past every wall. Now:
- `reach` knows what stops a star, and every decision goes by it: `stance` and `decide` (and their walks along her platform), `pick_target`, the spots (`coverage`: a spot on 4 at x 244 had 40% of 2 in reach by distance, now none), the fight's far targets, the hunt loop's rules (shoot, in passing, back to spot, better spot, a trip's interruptions), the tour's stop on the way, the escort, and kill matching (`fight._in_path`, `ledger.in_path`). `hunt look` says "behind a wall", and the mini-map's reach band stops at the wall.
- The simulator's world stops the star there too (`World.nearest_in`, by the group of the platform she last stood on), the claw's swing as well. New scenario `fight_step_wall`: on 4 at x 520 with Orange Mushrooms on 2 and nothing on 4. With the old decisions in this world she threw 23 stars in 20 s and hit nothing; now she throws none and moves on after 1.7 s.
- The shot log keeps her x, the target's x, her group and the rule's verdict (`clear`), so the probes can be scored from it. A monster seen past its platform's end is placed at the end (`Scene.place`).
- In the simulator's game-like world (preset `game`, 10 seeds of 20 minutes), against before: the world's rule alone took the tour from 89.5 to 88.4 EXP a minute and the hunt loop from 122.4 to 120.8; with the decisions too, 87.5 and 122.1. In each, 9 of 10 seeds are the same throughout. The one that differs is a run that met 4 -> 2, diverging from there (tour seed 8: 104.3, then 92.8, then 83.5, where she went up onto 2 instead and was knocked back down 10 times; loop seed 7: 71.9, 55.4, 68.5). On this map the effect is within noise; on maps with steps it should be larger.
- Not measured in game yet: the line's height (anything from 1 to 59 fits), its height in a jump (a jump throw's attack starts 26 up, its line under the 60 step's top; a jump back's 44 up, over it), whether the claw's swing is stopped too, and whether it's a level line at all and not one from her to the target's feet (they differ shooting down from 2 at 4 from far left of the step, and down past her own block's hanging wall).

**The star's search, and the angle off her level** (from the game data, meowdb and the live logs, 2026-10-20; see Attack). Off her level she judged a star's reach by one ramp for every monster (150 units sideways 60 below her, 200 above), and the simulator by a box. The logs fit the client's search by bands better, and by it the room a star needs goes by the monster's body (60 below her, an Orange Mushroom from 113 units, a slime from 177). Now:
- `reach` has the search (`search_band`, `min_dx` and `max_dx` by body, `body_of`), and her decisions go by it with each monster's kind (`can_shoot`, `can_hit`, `shot_dx`): `stance` and `decide` (with their steps away from one right under her, and a walk to one band past where a star picks it), `pick_target`, the fight's far targets, the hunt loop's rules, the tour's stop on the way, the escort and `hunt look`. Kill matching too (`fight._in_path`, `ledger.in_path`, `reach.ground_pick`): from the ground what the claw (on her level) or the search can pick, in the order it takes them; from a jump the area to 400 by a body's near side. Spots go by a pig's body (12 from 13: 60% -> 63% in reach).
- The simulator's world picks by it (`World.nearest_star`), the claw only on her level, and its stars reach 400 to a body's near side from the ground or a jump (434 for a pig by its middle; 494 before).
- Step 1's walls fit with it. Of her throws from 4 at monsters on 2 (60 above, 286-392 units off), the search alone picks one on 2 every time; with the walls, none. On the research's fits rerun against `reach`, the search scores -55.52 (shot log, off her level), -42.49 (telemetry, the nearest monster in front), -82.22 (telemetry, the whole pick) and -64.06 (her level); with the walls, -54.09 on the shot log (its 3 misses from 4 at 2) and the same on the rest, since the walls change no other pair. On the terrain research's scoring (did a throw from the ground hurt anything, 195 decided throws): the old rule -116.70, with the walls -116.40; the search -116.44, with the walls -116.24.
- In the simulator's game-like world (preset `game`, 10 seeds of 20 minutes), against before: the world alone (her old decisions) took the tour from 87.5 to 85.9 EXP a minute and the hunt loop from 122.1 to 111.3; with the decisions too, 85.2 and 121.4 (better on 3 and 5 of the 10 seeds; in the new world against her old decisions, on 4 and 5, with 3 of the loop's the same). HP lost 2.64 -> 2.62 bars (tour), 2.51 -> 2.42 (loop); drops picked up 95.9% either way (tour), 83.9% -> 79.8% (loop, nearly all of it seeds 2 and 4, where monsters are always in reach). Attacks that hit nothing: tour 666 -> 869 -> 786, loop 917 -> 1,114 -> 1,072. Most of the rise is stars at targets 400-470 off by their near side, aimed at within 410 by their middle and walked out of reach by the time the attack started: the shorter range makes the world harder, and the decisions win back part of it. Aiming within 400 instead would cut those by another 4-5% (tour 87.7, loop 121.2 EXP a minute); it's left at 410, where the range probe hit slimes at 408 and 410, until it's measured in game.
- `tour_run` moved from seed 8 to 6, and its limit to 1200 s: the basin's respawns make it chaotic (470-1190 s on seeds 1-16, before and after), and on seed 8 one EXP gain came in as the stop's fight ended, unplaced.
- The shot log is `lab/shots2.jsonl` from now on (`hunt shots` sums up both). The old one made every throw in flight at a kill a hit (its hits 60 below at 91-148 were mostly that). Now a kill is the last throw due before the target died (its HP bar gone after it had one) or else vanished; those due before it are undecided, those due after it missed. A star is due from when its key went down (held back to the end of the attack lock, up to 0.7 s after it was decided), and each throw keeps every monster in front of her at the throw and at the next look, about when the attack picked its target. A throw is scored from the last HP bar seen before its star was due, not the bar at the throw: keyed before the star ahead of it landed, it was credited with that one's hit (`hunt_kill_misses`: its second throw, a miss in the world, was logged a hit). In `hunt_kill_far` the log now reads hit, hit, hit, miss, miss, as the world has it (five hits before).
- Not measured in game yet: the windows' top (`SEARCH_TOP0`), the range to a body's near side, whether the search goes by each monster's frame (a slime's hop lifts its body 10-17; a pig stands 38 tall, walks 46), and how an attack from a jump picks its target.

**The claw or a star, by the monster's size** (from the game data and the simulator, 2026-10-20; see Attack). `stance` and the hunt loop took a monster on her platform as too close for a throw from the ground within 100 units of her by its middle, and `decide` within 110, whatever its kind. But the claw swipes any body that reaches into its swing, so pigs, slimes and Orange Mushrooms 100-124 units off were swiped (9-11 damage) where she meant to throw a star. Now:

Her step back for a star at a kind a jump's attack can't pick goes to 3 past it (`reach.star_sure`: a snail's is 124, as before), and `decide` walks to 20 past it (it was 150 for every kind).

HP lost 2.62 -> 2.52 bars (tour), 2.42 -> 2.13 (loop); drops picked up 95.9% -> 94.4% (tour), 79.8% -> 76.6% (loop). It doesn't pass the harness bar (the seed count, and the drops share). Those of the basin's fights end sooner or kill more (`tour_hunt_noisy` its 14 kills in 109 s instead of 272; `nav_fight_basin` 26 kills on the way instead of 20).

**A kill her EXP told of as a fight ended went uncounted** (simulator, 2026-10-20). A fight tells its kills apart from her EXP gains look by look, but the looks of a sweep for drops count gains too, and when that brought the fight to its kill count it ended without telling the last one apart: the kill was missing from its kills by kind, which a tour's stop sums up (in one `tour_run` of 161 kills, 34 gains came that way, and the 2 of them at its stops were missing; the escort counts by gains, not kinds). Now `fight.clear` tells those apart from its last look when it ends, and those seen by the look it ends on (knocked off), and then those its sweep after the fight sees, counted but with their drops left: left to the tour, they sent it on loot trip after loot trip (`tour_run`: 16 instead of 6, 1185 s instead of 708). `tour_run`'s "every kill counted" holds on 13 of seeds 1-16 instead of 5; the rest are 1-2 kills short of 150-215. 8 golden scenarios changed by a kill's log line ("pig down at x 805") and the sweep of its drops, and from there on (`nav_fight_across`, `tour_run`, `tour_rest`, `tour_rest_hp_low`, `tour_hunt_noisy`, `tour_hunt_basin`, `tour_hunt_platform_12`, `loop_basin`); with those seen by the look a fight ends on, `nav_fight_up` and `tour_hunt_platform_12` by one more such line; with those of the sweep after it, 15 more by such a line and nothing else (`fight_snail_short_platform`'s report now has the slime its sweep saw die: "1 snail, 1 slime", 2 EXP gains as before).

**Kills fade out as long as their death animation runs** (game data, 2026-10-20). A killed monster plays its die1 frames where it died, the last one fading it out: 1.26 s for a snail, 0.84 for a slime, 0.66 for a pig or an Orange Mushroom. The fight left whatever it saw where a kill had died alone for 1.2 s whatever the kind, and the simulator showed every kill for 0.8 s. Now both go by the kind (`MobBody.die_s`: the death animations are read with the map and kept in its cache under their own key, so older code still reads it; `fight.fade_s`, `SimMonster.fade`), so a pig walking up to where one has just died is shot at half a second sooner. 19 golden scenarios changed besides `nav_fight_up`, as a ghost shows longer or shorter and she turns to a live one sooner; each still shows what it's there for. `nav_fight_up` moved from seed 10 to 3: on some seeds a touch knocks her off 3 or 4 down to the basin and the trip runs out of time, more often since the claw's edge (she arrives on 38 of seeds 1-48 with the decisions of the star search, 34 with the claw's edge, 30 with this too, seed 10 no longer among them). In the simulator's game-like world (preset `game`, 10 seeds of 20 minutes), against the commits before it: the tour 88.7 -> 87.5 EXP a minute; the hunt loop 126.6 -> 115.5, all of it seed 10, which fell out of the map (see Found offline) - without it 126.9 -> 126.8. HP lost 2.58 -> 2.47 bars (tour), 2.12 -> 1.95 (loop); drops picked up 95.2% -> 94.4% (tour), 76.7% -> 68.4% (loop; 74.4% -> 69.5% without seed 10, from seeds 7 and 9). Against the star search (before the claw's edge): tour 85.2 -> 87.5, loop 121.4 -> 115.5 (121.3 -> 126.8 without seed 10), claw swipes 1,310 -> 861 and 1,831 -> 1,046, HP lost 2.62 -> 2.47 and 2.42 -> 1.95.

**The shot log gave one throw's hit to another** (simulator, 2026-10-20). A bar drop was a hit for every throw past its due time, however late the look, and the fight looks once a throw, right after each key: the look that should have shown a throw's miss often showed the next one's hit (`hunt_kill_misses`: its sixth throw, a miss in the world, was logged a hit). A kill went to the last throw due before the target was seen dying, but the simulator shows a star's damage at its release (520 ms after the key) whatever the distance, so a far throw that killed wasn't due yet and was logged a miss. Which of the two the game does isn't measured: a star is seen flying up to 0.6 s to its target, but the bar may follow the attack's message to the server. Now:
- A throw's damage can show from 0.47 s after its key to 0.3 s past its due time. A bar drop is a throw's hit only if no other throw's can have shown since the look before it, and a kill is the last throw's that can have landed only if that one alone can, or it was due by then; else they're undecided. Seen with its bar as before 0.3 s past its due time (0.9 s before), a throw missed.
- A throw's pick is the first look after it that places her, whether or not the target is in it (hidden under its damage numbers, it was noted at the next look it showed in, once 1.7 s after the star was due), with its time from the key. Each line keeps the target's bar at every look until it was scored and the throw's key time, so a scorer that knows the game's timing can tell the undecided ones.
- Over seeds 1-12 of the four `hunt_kill` scenarios, with hit monsters hidden for 1-3 s and without (the 63 runs that log every star the world throws, 279 throws): before, 253 right, 15 misses logged as hits, 2 kills as misses, 9 undecided; now 211 right, none wrong, 68 undecided. Of those, the 19 from the runs without hiding are all told right from their bars by the simulator's timing; the other 49 landed while the target was hidden, and nothing tells those apart.
- Golden: the shot logs of `hunt_kill`, `hunt_kill_far`, `hunt_kill_misses` and `hunt_kill_tag_hidden` (in `hunt_kill_misses` the miss logged a hit and the hit after it are undecided, and a miss that was undecided is a miss).

**What stops a star, checked on the pick alone** (cross-validation against public readings of the client's code, 2026-10-20; see Attack: what stops a star). The simulator's pick passed a walled monster over and gave the star to the next, walls stopped a star going either way, and the claw's swipe was stopped by them too. Now, as the client does it:
- The claw and the star's search pick by the bodies, whatever the terrain, and the line to a star's pick alone is checked (`World.sight_stop`). Stopped, the attack hits nothing: the star ends there (the world's log says at which wall or floor), and no other monster takes it. A swipe isn't checked: the client's whack has no line. Her decisions take a monster as out of a star's reach when one the attack takes first has its star stopped (`reach.shielded`, through `reach.can_hit`'s `others`, the monsters around her: in `stance`, `decide` and `pick_target`, the fight's far targets, the hunt loop's rules, the tour's stop on the way, the escort and `spots.spot_for`), and kill matching does so too (`fight._in_path`, `ledger.in_path`). `hunt look` says "behind one behind a wall" for such a monster.
- A wall stops a star only going in at its outer face (`reach.faces`: a wall drawn downward faces right, one drawn upward left; `reach.clear_span` and the mini-map's band, for which the page now gets each wall's face). On this map every wall faces out from the platform it hangs from (a test checks all 105), so this changes nothing here.
- The v83 client's line is there behind `reach.LINE = 'v83'`, for when the probes find it: `reach.hit_point`, `reach.sight_stop` (every floor of the map, `Platform.floors`, and the footholds joined to each one's ends, `Segment.prev` and `next`, from the map image, for the corners), `reach.clear_length` for `spots.coverage`. Where a floor stops the star from where she'd walk to, `stance` and `decide` walk her along her platform to the nearest place, 10 units apart, from where it doesn't (`stance._clear_from`; a wall of her group stops it from all of them, so the level line changes nothing there).
- With the level line none of it changes what she does on this map. In the harness (preset `game`, 10 seeds of 20 minutes) every seed gives the same EXP, drops and HP as before: the tour 96.4 EXP a minute, the hunt loop 130.3. Of the 66 golden traces one changed, `probe_step_up`, where the world's log now says that the 6 stars thrown from the ground at an Orange Mushroom on 2 stopped at the step wall (x 219), not "no hit". Only 4 -> 2 is walled here, and from 4 a monster on her side of the wall comes first in the search: over the 10 seeds the tour's world stopped 1 star of 6,264 at the wall and the loop's 2 of 8,240, and before, those hit nothing either.
- What the line is worth here, in the simulator: on the tour, over 30 seeds, 95.3 EXP a minute with the level line in the world and her decisions, 95.9 in a world with the v83 line and her decisions on the level line, 95.2 with both on the v83 line, and 93.2 with her decisions on the v83 line in a level world (a seed moves 20-25% either way, so these are good to a few percent). So on this map the line is worth under 1% of her stars, whichever it is.

**Arrows right after an attack** (found in game on 2026-10-21, fixed the same night; see In game, and Control). Every plan's first arrow waits until 0.6 s after her last attack's key (`actions.ARROW_LOCK_MS`, in `Actions.hold_back`), and the simulator's `Realism.lock_arrows` does what the game was seen to do (`world.ARROW_LOCK`, `ARROW_HELD`): an arrow pressed within 0.55 s of the key of an attack the game took is seen 1.0 s after the key if it's still held, and else never (the world's log says which). Before, it kept her still for the whole 730 ms lock whatever was pressed when, and no preset had it; now preset `game`, the two noisy scenarios and `nav_walk_off_after_kill` do.

What stood out, and what was done about it, each giving the same answers as the code before (the checks are named with each) and timed back to back with it (the stack's rows re-measured after the review, the planner's two speedups undone and the C off for "before": the first table had 3.6 s for all of the hunt loop's computing, the sleeps' and searches' share alone, and a different run's percentiles):

| ... before a sleep or a search: 99th percentile; longest | 30.2; 86.4 | 1.9; 6.1 |

With the physics and attack tracks (the perception track rebased onto them, 2026-10-20: her flight by the engine, `body.fly`, and the monsters at the game data's speeds), the stack's rows again (`sim.latency`, preset `game`, 5 seeds of 10 minutes, the C on and off, the same hunts either way): the hunt loop (6,094 looks) before a key plan p99 2.7 ms, at most 4.6 (5.3 with the C off), before a sleep or a search 2.3 and 3.5 (4.3), all of it 6.0 s (of which the sleeps' and searches' 4.4); the tour (3,621 looks) before a key plan p99 2.2, at most 6.1, where with the C off it was 5.5 and 164: chains planned on the move fly landings the planner hasn't, 1 ms each in Python. Before a look at most 43 ms either way (planning its sweep).

What each was (medians in ms; bench-look's 3 rounds of 3 looks at each frame, alternating with the code before):
- **The hunt loop's choices.** After most looks, its rate rule and the mini-map's 'hunt' record worked out where she'd stand to shoot every other hunting ground (3.6 ms a ground) and a route search to each (0.7 ms each): 30-60 ms between a look and her next keys. The spots depend on the map (and on the wall switch probes use) and are kept; the route times come from one search to every platform (1.6 ms), kept for the last 256 places (Motion planning, Behavior).
- **Ropes** (8.6 -> 4.3): each column was split viewed in place, and the shapes made over the whole column (Perception).
- **Monsters** (her band 34.1 -> 22.5, the whole screen 127.9 -> 78.1): on 6 threads the silhouette matches alone took 12 ms of the band; numpy's work after each match held Python's lock, so the threads took turns at it, 18 ms more. It's in C now (below). Every band of the whole screen's matches on the pool together, instead of a band a thread, was tried and not kept: no better (101 against 105 ms with the CPU busy).
- **Drops** (her platform 8.5 -> 6.0, every platform in view 88.9 -> 53.8, on the 30 saved screenshots that place her): strip by strip, each strip waited for its slowest template; now every strip's templates go to 8 threads together.
- **Her flight** (0.85-0.95 -> 0.019 ms): the engine's (`body.fly`), stepped 5 ms at a time in Python; the planner flies thousands (3,128 different landings) to build the map's moves, and a chain planned on the move could try dozens it hadn't before. In C now (below).
- What's left of the stack's own computing is small: in the simulator (with cProfile's overhead) planning a route 0.5 ms (median; at most 11), a chain 0.4 (at most 4), placing a monster seen 0.09, a look's placing 0.1, `stance` 0.04, the ledger's and drop store's bookkeeping after a look 0.01-0.02 (at most 0.9), a telemetry record 0.007.

**Python or C.** Two pieces are in C, `gamelab/native.c`, called through ctypes (which lets go of Python's lock for the call); `gamelab/native.py` builds it with MSVC 2022's Build Tools the first time it's needed, into `gamelab/build/` (git-ignored, named for the source's hash; `python -m gamelab.native` builds it now), and without the compiler, or with `native.USE` off, they're done in Python as before: the same answers, slower. The two are the monster search's step-1 bookkeeping and her flight: loops that numpy and OpenCV can't do without Python's own work, the first between OpenCV's calls, the second a simulation step by step. Each does the Python's arithmetic in the Python's order (IEEE double and float, `/fp:precise`, no fused multiply-adds), so the answers are the same to the bit: on all 31 saved 1920×1080 screenshots and 2,000 random inputs for the search, on 172,000 random flights (platform, x, time and speed at landing), and in tests that compare them with and without the C. The golden traces and the harness's runs (the loop and the tour, 20 seeds each, with blocking looks and with the feed) came out exactly as before; since the merge, the flight in C is the engine's (`body.fly`), and all 73 golden traces come out the same with the C off, as do `sim.latency`'s hunts. The elevated key player never loads it. Left as they are, with the numbers why:
- the silhouette matches (OpenCV, 0.48 ms each on one core, 79 for a band, on the threads): a direct loop in C wouldn't be faster than OpenCV's;
- the masked colour checks (30 a band, 0.39 ms each, OpenCV letting go of the lock: about 5 ms of the band's 22): in C at best 4 ms faster, and not OpenCV's scores to the bit (its masked normalised match goes through Fourier transforms), so a monster scoring near the 0.6 threshold could come out differently (since 2026-10-26 in C all the same where the CPU has AVX2, worked out exactly, the re-finds' too: OpenCV's scores within 1e-6 of it on a crowd's frames, the states the same on 41,113 saved frames but for one score's third decimal; see Perception's hot paths in C);
- her name tag (3.5 ms near where she was; the whole play area every 30th look, 36 ms): OpenCV's match takes as long on 1 thread as on 12, and matched in pieces its scores differ by up to 1e-4 (since 2026-10-26 looked for nearer first, 1.6 ms: CPU; the whole play area matched in 4 bands at once since 2026-10-26 as well, the same answers on 3,050 frames: Perception's hot paths in C);
- the Lie Detector check (the player's, 67 ms 4 times a second): the elevated player loads no DLL, and as little as it can (since 2026-10-26 its looks match around the forms' places: CPU);
- the GPU (onnxruntime with CUDA is installed, the onnx package isn't): one batched convolution could take the silhouette matches off the CPU, about 0.4 of the feed's 1.0 cores. Not built: its scores would differ from OpenCV's by about 1e-5, so some spots could change places; the model would have to be written by hand; and nothing shows yet that the CPU the feed takes costs the game frames (it runs at below-normal priority). If it does (`check` on a recording made with `watch` running), the cheaper knobs are the feed's schedule (`worldstate`): her band 5 times a second, the whole screen once a second, and for `watch` the drops on her platform every 0.5 s and in view every 2 s.

**The kernel's page zeroing** ("System" in Task Manager, which the table above leaves out). Each fresh page a process touches is a page fault, and Windows hands it a page zeroed by its zero-page threads (12 threads of the System process, pid 4, at priority 0, one start address: `review-numbers/systhreads.py`). Over 43 minutes with the game closed (gamelab at 0.02 cores), System was 6.5 cores on average and 11 at the peak, following the page faults (r = 0.91 over 12 windows of 5 s, about a core for 100,000 faults a second: `corr.py`; a controlled test, a fresh 6 MB array 100 times a second against one reused, three paired 10 s phases: +1.39 cores, `zerotest.py`; measured on a busy PC, maybe less on a quiet one). Most of it was the background jobs' (a `pytest` worker faults 74,000-333,000 pages a second: a `-n 4` job is about 3-7 System cores, on any CPU, which idle priority and the CPU affinity don't hold: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/cpu/APPLY-ops.txt caps the workers while she plays). Of gamelab's, faults a second (from outside the process, psutil; `review-numbers/faultrun.py` around each bench):

| | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| the player's watch (4 looks a second, `apply/ld/wd_paced.py`; live a grab's 4 MB more a look, 4,100 a second more either way) | 137,000 | 18,500-19,400 |
| `perceive` hunting at 30 (`apply/perc/prof_service.py`) | 25,700-34,700 | 27,700-37,000 (the same frame work) |

**The player's Lie Detector look** (`perception/lie_detector.py`, `control/player.py` Watchdog). Each form has always shown at one place (its template's top-left at 1920x1080: the countdown at (910,323) and its second window's title at (1648,589), the notice at (1458,680), the board at (432,124), the quiz's warning at (598,566), the quiz at (604,470), the Truth Booth's timer at (776,40); on every recording and fixture of 2026-10-18 to 26 that showed it, both sizes, the same pixel). So 7 looks in 8 match each form only within 48 px of its places (`near`: on the very pictures the whole frame's look matches, the frame stretched to 1920x1080, halved, grey), and every 8th look (`WHOLE_EVERY`, the first too) the whole frame (`scores`, as before), for a window anywhere else: seen within 8 looks of its first showing, 2 s (the notice comes 10 s before the mini-game, the quiz's warning 30 s before the quiz). `near` is asked only of a frame of the game's own size, 1366x768, with its picture where it belongs: either capture anchor in its place (the minimap's title strip, the HUD's border: `framecheck.anchors_off`, 0.04 ms; `Watchdog.in_place`). Every other look is of the whole frame: while a cycle is in progress (what it records is as ever), on a frame of any other size (a client of 1920x1080, or of another size brought to it: no anchors are measured there), and with neither anchor in its place, as when the game draws its picture off its client (2026-10-25 23:40 and 2026-10-26 00:29: 18 px left and 85 up), where every form is off its places too. The watch's thread sets OpenCV to one thread (it had that only from ultralytics' import, the YOLO shadow's, seconds after the start: its 24 threads cost 0.17-0.24 cores more with the whole frame's look, 0.13 with this one, for no faster a look), the countdown's yellow gate counts its pixels (`cv2.countNonZero`: 0.26 ms at 1920x1080 against the sum's 1.3; the same count), and the stretched frame, its half and its grey are made into pictures the spotter keeps from look to look (`LieDetectorSpotter._kept`, a thread's own: 8 MB of fresh memory a look before, 2,000 page faults). ## Perception's hot paths in C: 30 frames a second in a crowd (2026-10-26)

The user, 2026-10-26: "I found yesterday the hunt/grind frequently lags a bit seemingly due to late perception. That's why I proposed a full port to rule out python GC that can fire once in a while." What lagged was the frame loop running out of CPU, not Python's garbage collector (the planning step, D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/plan: live, 30 frames a second asked made 14.6 at the median while hunting, the frame period 27 ms and 9 more for each monster followed, 80% of the 1,053 s the hunts waited on perception; on the service's frame loop replayed, 207 collections in 1,622 s, 0.0037% of the time, the longest 4.2 ms; the long stalls live froze two processes at once, which one process's collector can't). Of the re-finds' time 89% was inside OpenCV's masked `matchTemplate`, C++ already, and the Python around it about 10 ms of an 80 ms step: so not a port, but that one match done otherwise, and each frame's re-finds at once.

**What changed** (the same answers as before, but for the masked match's last bits, below):
- *The masked colour match in C* (`gamelab/native.c`'s `mm_*`, through `perception/match.py`): OpenCV's TM_CCOEFF_NORMED with a mask worked out exactly, in integers (int64 sums, one rounding at the end), with AVX2 where the CPU has it (checked at run time; the build flags as before, so the other C pieces' answers stay the same to the bit). Without AVX2 the masked match stays OpenCV's: the same integers in plain C took 3.4-3.7 times OpenCV's time over the frame loop's masked matches (5.4 s against 1.6 on the crowd's 1,293, 5.2 against 1.4 on the 1,601 with the drops'; a re-find's window 7.3 ms against 1.8), and on 01:01's frames, the searches inline, the step took 103 ms (median) in plain C against 47 with the C off altogether and 19 with AVX2 (master 74: D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/pnative-finish/simd_bench.py, review-native-correct's `bF2c`, `bF2n`, `bF2`); `native.prepare_masked` makes nothing ready then, and the plain C is only the tests' (against AVX2). Each template is made ready once, as its detector loads it (`match.prepared`: its sums, its rows as int16 and its mask's runs, kept while its arrays are), and each thread keeps its scratch memory from call to call. A re-find's pictures go in one call each (`match.best_matches`, the window loaded once): its last template's, then its animation's next frames up to the first scoring `REFIND_GOOD`, the rest only if the caller goes on, `MobDetector.refind` taking their answers in turn as before. The step-2 checks, the gates and the twins' checks (`_match_at`: `match.best_match`) and the drops' strips (`loot`, on brightness at 1366x768) go through it too. A picture it doesn't take (another dtype, a flipped view) goes to OpenCV, and everything does with the C off (`native.USE`) or not built.
- *A frame's re-finds at once* on a pool of 4 threads (`worldstate.REFIND_THREADS`; the real detector's only: the simulator's fake re-finds are Python and stay on the frame loop's thread), each with its HP bar's read if it's due, placed in turn by the frame loop, so the states are one thread's. The detector counts its fallbacks under a lock (`MobDetector._counting`: `+=` from several threads could lose one).
- *The ring of look frames* holds 16 (`service.RING_SLOTS`; 8 before). A look's frame is copied out of it as its state is taken, and at 30 frames a second 8 held 267 ms: on the crowd's replays a look's frame was overwritten 86-88 ms after the look had its state at the soonest (whole-screen looks, their frames 254-268 ms old then; master's 153-324 ms at its 11-14 frames a second: the review, D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/review-native-correct). 16 hold 533 ms, what 8 held at the 15 a second live made; 50 MB of shared memory at 1366x768. A frame gone all the same comes out black, as before, but counted now (`ServiceClient.lost`, said on the command's last line), and her heading's pictures never learn a black box (`Heading.add`).
- *The service says whether the C is in use* (`native.state`): as each run starts, `perception: gamelab's C pieces in use, the masked match on AVX2` (or `off (why)`, or the masked match OpenCV's for want of AVX2), in the run's `session` record too (`native`), and on every 10 s line while it isn't all in use: a DLL that couldn't be built would otherwise show only as fewer frames a second.
- *Her name tag's whole play area* (every 30th look, and when she isn't near where she was) is matched in 4 row bands at once (`nametag.BANDS`): 12.5 ms against 24.3 (the planning step's `tag_split.py`: the median of the first 1,500 of 01:01's 3,050 frames; 9.9 against 17.0 the rest), the same answers on all of them; in the replays below her tag's look at its 99th percentile took 13.9 ms against 29.2.

**The scores.** OpenCV sums in float32 (its correlations go through Fourier transforms), so its scores aren't these to the bit: on the frame loop's own masked matches of 60 frames of a crowd (01:01 [700:760], 1,293 of them, and 1,601 with the drops') within 9.5e-7 of these in colour and 2.5e-5 on brightness, the best place and the 0.55, 0.6 and 0.9 thresholds' decisions the same on every call (`pconst/pnative/cmp_calls.py`). Where a window is a few levels from flat its float32 sums lose more digits: on the first map's pictures drawn on West Rocky Mountain II's frames (12,693 matches: `tests/test_native_match.py`, `pnative/diff_where.py`) up to 1.1e-5 in colour and 1.0e-4 on brightness, at scores of 0.24-0.32 (a strip's spread 3 grey levels), within 3e-5 wherever either scores 0.5 or more, the best places and the drops' peaks the same. A flat window scores -1, as OpenCV's NaN did. A match took (one thread, best of 5): a re-find's window 0.45 ms against OpenCV's 1.57, a step-2 check 0.05 against 0.58, a drop's strip 0.28 against 0.68: about 4 times as fast over all of them (4.2-4.7x on the crowd's 1,293, 3.5-3.7x on the 1,601 with the drops': the reviews' re-measures and `pnative-finish/simd_bench.py` on an idle machine; 4.5x said before was too much). Batching a re-find's pictures saved less than the planning step thought (about 25%): 4% of the re-finds' wall on 200 frames of the crowd (`pnative/n2_bench.py`), the window's loading being small beside the dot products, which are now most of a re-find (1.74 of 2.78 s on 150 frames, one thread: `pnative/prof_refind.py`). Since the evening of 2026-10-26 a re-find's window's dot products go by transform, every place at once, the same scores to the bit (A cheaper masked match).

**Measured** (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/pnative, the reviews' in `pconst/review-native-correct` and `review-native-numbers`, the finish's in `pconst/pnative-finish`; offline: no game, no keys, no capture, nothing attached to the live services; master 4ac1b2b exported to `pnative/master`, 7397dad to the reviews' folders; every job at idle priority on CPUs 12-23 through `bg_quiet.cmd`, other agents' work on the machine at times, its load in the tables).
- *The states as master's:* the step with its searches inline at the hunting schedule, the frames 1/30 s apart, her throws at seeded times, on every frame of both Lie Detectors' `before/` (2026-10-26 00:25 and 01:01, 3,048 each), with the drops searched (her platform every 0.2 s, every platform's every second) and without, the re-finds on 4 threads and on 1: in each of the 6 comparisons 0 of 3,048 frames' states (and late states) differed, 18,288 in all, the counts the same (00:25: 26,370 re-finds, 5,644 of them falling back; 01:01: 22,205 and 4,555). The step with its searches inline took 85-110 ms (median) for master, 19-23 for the branch, 32-34 with its re-finds on 1 thread (`ident.py`, `ident_cmp.py`, `ident/all.txt`). Rebased onto master 7397dad (her throws' and the unseen monsters' work: a track's `owed`), against that master's export: 0 of 3,048 again, 01:01 without the drops and 00:25 with them (`ident/rebased.txt`). The correctness review's own comparison (`review-native-correct/ident2.py`, `cmp.py`: 14 comparisons over 5 folders, both Lie Detectors' `before/` and 2026-10-25 00:55's, 2026-10-24 23:51's, the recording 2026-10-25 00:29's; 41,113 frames, with the drops and without, the re-finds on 4 threads and 1, the C off, plain C, and two threads hammering the same detectors and the match beside the step) found one frame that differed: frame 520 of 00:55's, one green mushroom's score 0.99 on master and 0.991 here, its place and every track the same. The C's score there is 0.990500093 (exact), OpenCV's float32 0.990499973, either side of the third decimal's rounding (`flip.py`); with the C off, no difference. A re-find goes by rounded scores (`REFIND_GOOD`, the best of a few pictures), so such a flip at 0.8995, or between two pictures 1e-3 apart, could steer which pictures it tries next or which one wins: about once in 10,000 sightings, harmless, the C's being the exact score. So: the same states but for a rare rounding of a score's third decimal; a difference live isn't by itself a bug. ## Perception at one pace, and the rolling recording in it (2026-10-26)

*The one pace since 2026-10-30: 15 frames a second, everything once a frame (Perception at 15 frames a second, one pass a frame); the recording keeps every frame.*

The user, that morning: "I found yesterday the hunt/grind frequently lags a bit seemingly due to late perception. That's why I proposed a full port to rule out python GC that can fire once in a while"; "Run the perception at the same rate between hunt and idle. The idea is perception is running as a constant thing and hunt is only a consumer of it"; "The recording should probably just take frames from within the same perception process to have a rolling window copy of things in memory, match fps or fps/2." The plan (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/plan`: its report, scripts and runs) found what lags: the frame loop out of CPU on the monsters' re-finds (live, 30 asked made 14.6 a second; the frame period 27 ms and 9 more a monster followed: 80% of the 1,053 s the hunts of 2026-10-25 and 26 waited on perception), not Python's garbage collector (the service's frame loop replayed: 207 collections in 1,622 s, 0.0037% of the time, the longest 4.2 ms; the live stalls froze two processes at once, which one process's collector can't), and nothing a port would mend (89% of the re-finds' time is OpenCV's masked `matchTemplate`, C++ already). A native masked match and the re-finds on a pool of threads made 30 a second with the same states: another branch (work/perceive-native). This one is the rest: one pace, the recording in the service, and what the loops wrote themselves written by threads beside them.

**One pace** (`localization/service.py`). 30 frames a second (`HZ`) whoever is attached, her band searched every 0.2 s and the whole screen every second (10 times a second since 2026-10-28, 15 since that evening: The whole screen 15 times a second); what a command asks is searched on the next frame besides and changes neither (its hello wakes nothing; `Hello.fast` only holds the map). `IDLE_HZ`, `ACTIVE_HZ`, `IDLE` and `ACTIVE` are gone. The drops are searched at `watch`'s rates (her platform's every 0.5 s, every platform in view every 2 s: `SCHEDULE`) while no command that hunts is attached, for the mini-map, and when asked while one is (`HUNTING`): a hunt asks for those it wants on the frames it takes, 55% of the tours' looks, published as any. Searched on schedule during a hunt too (as first built), they cost 0.20 cores (1.86 against 1.67) and a look with her drops waited 31 ms longer (median 177 against 146; her band's 150 against 139), with 0.6-0.7 collections a second against 0.05-0.1.

The service's real frame loop replayed (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/build1/replay`: `replay1.py`, from the plan's `replay.py`, on the crowd's saved frames [700:1300] of `lie_detector/20261026-010145/before` and the quiet ones [0:600], 30 frames a second asked, a minute after 12 s, a fake tour attached as the tours ask, or none; its own pipe, shared memory, recorder folders and mutex; master's code from `D:/MapleHelper` run the same way, read only; every run at Idle priority on CPUs 12-23, the machine 59-95% busy with other work, so the frame rates are the CPU's as much as the code's; `pooled.py`, runs pooled):

| | frames a second | cores | step ms (median/p90/p99) | page faults a second |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| master between hunts, the crowd (10 asked, `watch`'s searches; the recorder its own process besides, 0.09-0.20 cores) | 9.9 | 1.22 | 68/101/143 | 23,500 |
| this branch between hunts, the crowd (30 asked; the recording in it, 0.07 cores) | 11.4 (3 runs: 10.1-12.1) | 1.87 | 84/126/164 | 16,000 |
| master between hunts, the quiet frames | 10.0 | 0.74 | 27/49/67 | 23,500 |
| this branch between hunts, the quiet frames | 24.4 | 1.70 | 32/57/82 | 21,100 |
| master hunting (30 asked; the recorder besides) | 11.6 (the machine 59-69% busy) | 1.64 | 83/124/160 | 40,400 |
| this branch hunting, the recording in it | 10.9 (71-88% busy) | 1.72 | 87/130/162 | 16,600 |
| ... the recording off and on, alternated, 3 runs each (the drops then on schedule) | 10.8; 11.0 | 1.86; 1.90 | 89/133/176; 86/129/180 | 28,800; 18,400 |

So between hunts it looks 1.15-2.4 times as often for about 0.7 core more (the numbers review's replays, pooled: in the crowd 12.5 frames a second and 1.82 cores against master's 9.9 and 1.09; master's own code at 30 a second with this schedule, 12.7 and 1.74: the cost is the pace and the schedule asked, not new code), its frame loop saturated in a crowd as it is hunting (its steps 76/115/155 ms against master's 61/95/133 at 10 a second, its frames 23% fresher at the median), until the other branch's native pieces are in. There the frame loop alone made 29.9 a second for 1.45 cores between hunts, but without the drops searched on schedule (their pool's 0.19-0.24 cores in every run between hunts here) nor the recording (0.06-0.10): about 1.7-1.75 cores with both branches, +0.65 over today's service, +0.45-0.65 once the old recorder's process is counted as retired; to be measured. Hunting it's as before: the recording's 0.07 cores against the recorder's process's 0.09-0.20, and the frames a second and the step within the machine's swing. A hunt's looks (the fake tour's wait from its key's effect to a state, median/p90): master's 143/221 ms, this branch's 155/250, the machine busier for the branch's; recording off and on 168/287 and 155/299.

**The recording** (the rolling recording: In the perception service). On the replay: 0.067 cores for 10.6 frames a second kept (about 6.3 ms a frame: the frame loop gave 11), none dropped or late. The long run (330 s, the crowd, the fake tour): 3,113 frames over 300.8 s at the end, 1.22 GB, 286 of them whole; decoded, 3,069 frames were the very frame fed (by the state's number: 44 came before the measurement's rows), none other. A `save-recent` of 300 s asked 305 s in was answered 31 s later, 3,170 frames (527 MB of JPEG), each the JPEG of the frame fed, pixel for pixel (`verify_save.py`). Every frame of the saves was the JPEG of the frame fed. Writing a save beside the frame loop, as first built, cost it more than it seemed: see Saves beside the frame loop, below.

**Writes off the loops** (`telemetry.py`). A record is made into its line where it's emitted and written by the recorder's thread every 0.2 s (`FLUSH_S`), so a write held up by the disk holds up no frame loop or hunt (the plan put 1.7% of the hunts' waits on whole-machine stalls, plausibly the SSD's synchronous writes, not proven); past 50,000 records waiting the newest are dropped, counted; a write that fails stops it, said once; `flush` waits for what's emitted (a reader following the file sees a record 0.2 s late at most). The service's console (`print`, `_log`) goes through a thread of its own the same way (`console_in_background`; the watchdog drains both before it ends the process). The commands' consoles are as they were.

**Garbage collection** (`gcstats.py`, shared). Every collection timed (`gc.callbacks`): the service's console line every 10 s ends with them ("GC 4 (gen 0, 1, 2: 4, 0, 0), 1.6 ms, the longest 0.7"), and a `gc` record goes into telemetry once a minute, the service's and each command's that records (`report_every`): a lag can be told from a collection live. Each run made, everything there is goes into the permanent generation (`gcstats.freeze`: the run before collected first), so no collection goes through the map's templates, the models and the modules again: 47,600-48,200 objects in 14-31 ms on the replay. There, 0.05-0.7 collections a second, at most 0.25 ms of them a second, the longest 0.99 ms, none of the oldest generation (master's 1.37).

**Held frames** (`perception/frames.py`). A frame the capture still holds from more than 0.5 s before the look asked for one (`HELD_S`: DXGI waits 20 ms for a new frame, and the game draws one every 16.7 ms in front) keeps its own time, where it was stamped as now and acted on; said once (a `held` event) until frames come again. Short of `STALE_S` (2 s), where such a frame becomes a problem as before. The plan put 0.3% of the hunts' waits on one such stall (01:21, "the capture's newest frame is 2.1 s old"). Those held 50-500 ms (`HELD_COUNT_S`) are still stamped as now, but counted: the service's line every 10 s says "N frames held 50-500 ms (the longest M ms), stamped as now" when there were any (the correctness review: how often they come wasn't known; if often, `HELD_S` comes down to them).

**The capture's pictures** (`frames.Pictures`). A frame is converted into one of up to 24 pictures kept from frame to frame, never one somebody still holds (its reference count is the list's alone), where a new 1366x768 picture a frame was 770 page faults, which Windows' kernel zeroes (README, CPU): on the replay, hunting, 28,800 faults a second against 39,700 with new pictures (2 runs each), with the recording on 16,000-18,400 (the encoder's memory reused, plausibly: not looked into).

**The states.** Nothing of the world step changed: `states_dump.py` stepped master's code and this branch's on the same saved frames ([700:1300] and [0:600] of the crowd's folder, at 1/30 s, the searches inline at the service's schedule: 1,200 frames and their 1,440 states, the late ones among them, the same to the character, master's frames converted into new pictures and this branch's into the kept ones, the same to the byte; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/build1/states`). The service's states differ from master's only by its pace and schedule between hunts: three times as many frames, her band and the screen searched as often as hunting (0.2 s and 1 s, against 0.5 s and 2 s), the drops as before; hunting, none.

**After the reviews** (the same day: `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/review-constant-correct` and `review-constant-numbers`, their findings each checked before it was acted on; the fixes measured in `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish`, its `replay/`: the reviewers' `replay1.py` with the fixes' settings, the crowd's frames as above, the fake tour, 60 s after 12 s, every run at Idle priority on CPUs 12-23, the machine 14-77% busy; `old` is the branch as reviewed, its `control/recording.py` and `perception/frames.py` loaded in place of the new ones):
- *No other program's window in the recording.* The service's checks looked at `COVER_GRID`'s points only, where the recorder also asked `window.over` before and after each grab: a notification between the points was kept (the review's `privacy_demo.py`: the recorder's check said "covered", the service's frame went into the ring). Now its screen frames ask it too while the recording runs, before the shot and after it (`ScreenFrames.cover_check`, `Frame.over`): such a frame is a "covered" gap, the window named in the log (`privacy_demo2.py`: 0 frames kept, one gap). The walk up the z-order keeps Python's lock through its calls (`frames._over`, user32's reads of every window above the game: none sends a message), and the recording's own looks use it too (`GameWindow(over=)`): through `window.over` the two walks of a frame took 1.75 ms of the frame loop's interval (its search threads taking the lock at each of some 560 calls, 277 windows above the one asked, the worst this PC has; the interval less its measured parts, median 1.9 ms against 0.1 as reviewed), with the lock kept, 1.2 ms on that worst walk (the final pairs: 1.31-1.33 against 0.10), most of it the walk itself (0.47 ms a walk in a process alone, 0.60 through window.over; with 3 threads of Python churning beside it, 0.35 s against 9.7: over_same.py, its answer the same as window.over's on all 84 windows and boxes tried); live, the game in front has only this PC's topmost windows above it (the window in front had 44, 1 of them shown: 0.077 ms a walk, 0.096 through window.over; above_front.py), so about 0.15 ms a frame.
- *Never under 10 frames a second* (`recording.FLOOR_FPS`): the recording kept each frame the loop made, which in a crowd is fewer than the recorder's 10 (the review: 11.7% of the hunts' live 10 s lines said 7-10; on its replays 27% of the seconds held fewer than 10, the fewest 5). Now under 10 in a second, it grabs its own until the loop gives 12 a second over 2 s. Hunting, 3 pairs alternated: the frame loop as before, 13.99-14.11 frames a second against 14.07-14.29, 1.51-1.52 cores against 1.51-1.53, its steps 68-69/91-93/117-123 ms (median/p90/p99) against 67-70/95-97/121-126, the looks 118-120/169-189 ms against 106-117/167-190; the recording 13.4-13.6 frames a second kept against 12.8-13.0, under 10 in 0-0.8% of its seconds against 1.7-5.0% (the fewest 8-10 against 8-9: the second in which the floor is taken), its own grabs for the floor 0.7-1.4 a second, 0.05 cores as before (`a_fin*`, `a_old4-6`, the machine 14-15% busy). The first 3 pairs (`a_new*`, `a_old1-3`, 22-30% busy, the walk through `window.over`): 13.3-13.5 frames a second against 13.8-14.3, the recording 13.3-13.6 kept against 12.7-13.0, its own grabs 2.5-3.2 a second. Between hunts, 2 pairs: 13.3-13.4 kept a second and never under 10 against 13.0-13.1, 2.5% of the seconds under 10 (the fewest 8); the frame loop the same, 14.2-14.5 frames a second against 14.4-14.5. Asked 8 frames a second (under the floor all the time; the look at the window as `GameWindow.check` makes it, twice a grab, through `window.over` then): 15.0 kept a second, its own, for 0.14-0.15 cores, against 8.3-8.7 kept and 0.04 cores without the floor (its steps the same within the machine's swing: 72-78 ms against 69-85, 14-58% busy).
- *Picked by a token bucket* (`recording.BURST`): the review counted 78-94% of a loop at 12-16 a second kept where the code said every frame (a due grid); the bucket keeps 0.1-0.2 a second more on the same frame times, as many as the loop makes when it's slower, less its swing from second to second (`cadence_rules.py`, 77 runs).
- *Saves beside the frame loop.* Written in the service, a save shared its Python lock with the frame loop: a 120 s save during a hunt (1,620-1,650 frames in 10.0-10.8 s) made its steps wait 18-20 ms (median) against 1-2 outside it, 9.0-9.7 frames a second against 13.0-14.3, step medians 92-105 ms against 66-75, the writers at the lowest thread priority and at normal alike (`s_p2*`, `s_p0*`, 2 runs each alternated, the machine 16-32% busy: not a priority's starving, as the review's one pair at 100% busy suggested, but the lock). Now a save is written in a process of its own (`rolling.write_part_apart`, `control/partwriter.py`: the moments handed down its stdin as they're kept, the part written there below normal priority, as `gamelab recorder` wrote it; written in the service only if that process fails, said in the log): on the quiet machine (16% busy), during a 120 s save (1,620-1,650 frames in 10.2-10.8 s), written apart the frame loop's steps waited 3-4 ms (median) against 19-21 written in the service, it made 9.6-10.7 frames a second against 8.4-9.3 (13.6-14.0 before the save in all four), its step medians 87-102 ms against 93-114 (69-73 before; `d_apart4-5`, `d_in4-5`, alternated). What's left is the CPU's: the save's threads beside the frame loop on the replay's 12 CPUs, 6 cores' two threads each, as the old recorder's own process was (the numbers review's same save in a process of its own: 12.0-12.4 frames a second to 9.8). Live the save's process isn't kept to those CPUs, and its threads, at the lowest priority in a below-normal class, give way to the frame loop's (with its writers at normal priority, the frame loop's own in an Idle replay, `d_apart2` at 54% busy: 11.4 frames a second to 8.0, the wait 4 ms to 10).
- *GC's callback takes no lock* (`gcstats.py`): a collection that started inside `take` (its new window made under the lock) hung the process, the callback waiting for the lock its own thread held (the review hung it with the collector's threshold at 1 and 50; never seen at the default). Now the window is made before the lock, and the callback takes none: the review's `gc_deadlock.py` went through 200,000 takes at both thresholds (`gc_deadlock_fixed.out`).
- *The babysitter hands the recording over only once the old recorder has nothing left to write* (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/babysit3.ps1`): it force-stopped it as soon as the service waited, an alarm's clip or `before/` still to come; now not while an alarm is up or one began in the last 5 minutes, nor with a `save-recent` asked or being written, nor while its status says clips or saves are to be written (`pending_clips`, `saves_waiting`, new in the status).
- *The recording's own moments after 0.25 s without a frame* (`OWN_AFTER_S`, 0.5 as built): a stall of the frame loop's leaves it a quarter of a second.
- *Not changed:* a difference bigger than the whole frame on a camera pan stays a difference (keeping those whole saved 3-5% for 65% more CPU: The rolling recording); the recording still dies with the service (put to the user: `APPLY-ops.txt`); the memory figures are as measured below (Memory and disk).

**Tests:** `test_service` (one pace, the drops' schedule by who's attached), `test_service_recorder` (the difference chains read back bit for bit, a chain going whole and a save from a whole frame, a moment of its own between two frames, the frame loop's frames every other one by the bucket and never waited on, every one of an irregular loop slower than 15 a second, only the game's and none not asked about, a window over the game a gap that breaks the chain, its own grabs under the floor and back, its own moments while there's none, an alarm's `before/` and clip and `save-recent` written apart, a part written apart the same as here and written here when its process can't start, the mutex and `waiting.json`, the service feeding it and turning its screen frames' cover check on), `test_screen_frames` (a held picture never written over, a held frame's own time, the cover check before and after the shot, the holds of 50-500 ms counted), `test_writers` (a stalled disk or console holds up no emit or print, the bound, a full disk, the collections counted, a collection inside a take that never hangs); the tests that follow telemetry as it grows flush first; the recorders' mutex is each test's own (conftest).

**To put it live** (the user at the PC, between hunts, right after a Lie Detector is answered: the old recorder's 5 minutes go with it; this branch merged first):
- *The babysitter:* `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/babysit3.ps1`, babysit2.ps1 with the recording handed over (its header: the rules and the steps; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/APPLY-ops.txt`). Dry run first (`-DryRun -Once -Explain`: it names the recorder's pid as the one recording, and would start nothing), then stop babysit2, stop `gamelab perceive`, start babysit3 detached through WMI: it starts the new service within 5 s, which finds the recorder holding the mutex and says it waits, babysit3 stops the recorder within 5 s once it has nothing left to write, and the service records within 10 s of that. Rollback: stop babysit3, `perceive --no-record` (or the code before), babysit2.
- *Checks* (read only): `recorder --status` says "running", the service's pid, "its frames: the perception service's frames, 15 a second asked", about 15 frames a second and 0.07-0.13 of a core; `save-recent --seconds 20 --name check` writes about 300 frames, `sheet FOLDER` the game in every tile, and each line of its index a `seq`; perceive.log's line every 10 s says "(asked 30)" with or without a hunt, "recording: N s kept (X GB)" and "GC ..."; Task Manager: the service's private bytes after 5 minutes about 1.1-1.6 GB more in a crowd (up to about 2.7 on noisy frames, 2 while the floor's whole frames fill it; never past the 4 GB cap and a save's 155-270 MB) and no `gamelab recorder`; with a small window over the game (a notification), "not recording: covered" within a second; `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/cpu/fix/live_check.py 600 --every 60` over a hunt and a wait between hunts: the service's cores and faults against the table above; at the next Lie Detector, `before/` and the clip as before, 15 frames a second.

**Not done.** Live, nothing of it has run. The other branch's native pieces are what make 30 a second affordable; without them the service saturates between hunts too, and in a crowd the recording leans on its floor (its own grabs, mss, as the recorder's). The commands' consoles are written as before (only the service's goes through a thread). A client at another size is recorded through the recording's own grabs (mss), as the recorder did, not the service's frames. How often the capture holds a frame 50-500 ms is for the live line to say. `frames.py` may overlap the window-recover work (work/window-recover).
